prs.body:
Under OpenAI's base theorem and the retained analytic and fixed finite-alphabet multitape interfaces, this gives

**κ = 409953/10000000000 = 4.09953 × 10⁻⁵ > 2⁻¹⁵**, for `T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1−κ))`.

The exponent saving is **6.6006360% above #36** and **1.6202070% above #41** (`κ=4.034168124e-5`). During final verification, Rohan Arun’s #42 published the same broad fixed/alternating composition at `4.099494519e-5`; our different carrier matching gives a further **0.0008654970%** improvement. Exact lower bounds also exclude its full network at our new bit saving. These compare asymptotic exponents, not practical runtimes or global optimality.

### Construction

Compose RaD / hipotures's alternating changed DAGs from #41 with original envelope labels, both fixed `I+J` bases from #32/#35, copied centers from #36, and reversed corners/balanced assembly from #34/#37. Recompute the entire fixed profile for each changed DAG and use descending donor traversal for the actual carrier matching. The resulting local role counts are `R23=36685`, `R25=48479`; `m=575`, `W=178378409`, total child rank `102565738275`. All **4,073,300** paid endpoint corrections remain.

The full data profile is certified at the actual fixed bases for **4,073,290** source pairs. Ten failed primary-prime tests retain a conservative **47-singleton +481** fallback. No pair is discarded and modular zeros are not treated as rational zeros. Exact all-weight rank cuts prove the ordered zeros; successful modular pivots prove rational nonvanishing.

### Finite proof and verification

The independent compiler reconstructs every physical role and rational frame incidence. The complete formal dirty basis is tested in both orientations: **40,227** basis vectors at h23 and **53,079** at h25. Every auxiliary is restored. The fixed profiles reconstruct **68,462 +92,107** transition matrices with rigorous bounded-minor CRT certification. Exact rational moments reject the complete #40 and #41 networks at the new bit saving `40997/10^9`.

**`make verify` passes**, including 184 tests, the 14 focused adversarial controls, fresh graph/profile/physical-timeline/data-pair replay, and 18 historical patch checks. Both moments, all 47 strict assembly constraints and seven margins pass. Bit moment gap exceeds `2.8072e-11`; final absorption gap exceeds `1.9314e-11`.

prs.title: Add Gaussian parity proofs and mixed-center community integration
prs.body:
This adds an exact arithmetic and precision integration for the community's actual mixed-center producer. Starting from arbitrary dirty scalar ports, subtracting old/new values before division and collecting the side corrections produces an integer-only reference decoder. The completed-child denominator certificate is then applied to the pinned 29-class PR46 profile. The result includes a paper, 168 Lean theorem declarations, executable interfaces, source-pinned audits, and provenance.

The new standalone package is [`research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/`](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/tree/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis). The earlier 69-theorem package in `research/gaussian-parity/` is retained unchanged.

Entry points: [paper PDF](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/community-parity-synthesis.pdf), [LaTeX source](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/community-parity-synthesis.tex), [reproduction/interface README](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/README.md), [formalization map](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/FORMALIZATION_MAP.md), [community ledger](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/LEDGER.md), and [provenance](https://github.com/alejandrozu/integer-mult-bounds/blob/gaussian-parity-certificates/research/gaussian-parity-synthesis/PROVENANCE.md).

## Combined result

The source inventory covers all 46 PRs available at the start of this run, with pinned heads and 5,380 cumulative changed-file records, plus Swapnil Jain's separate Round 6 work. The concrete integration targets PR46 at `71b6c960c89295e952522dd44111df9cfc51ae90`, which retains the mixed-center/copied-center chain, changed-DAG and fixed-basis work, reversed geometry, PR44's weighted matching, and direct rational data recovery. These overlapping contributions are not treated as independently additive improvements. The inventory does not claim every community build was executed.

- **Exact dirty-port scalar decoder:** for the actual h28,d19 producer, `sum delta B - 2 sum delta D = -32 T`; the remaining collected numerators are `2 X`. The fused reference schedule needs zero additional fractional bits versus six in the explicitly compared generic old/new reference schedule. Gaussian quotient calls decrease from 26,268 to 3,286 in those schedules, excluding the optional image check and physical frame costs. These are reference-arithmetic counts, not measured runtime or optimality claims.
- **Complete image guard and usable adapter:** local divisibility is insufficient. `checked_fused_delta` checks `P(Q delta)==delta`, rejecting locally divisible off-image examples. `mixed_center_adapter.py` connects canonical, heterogeneous Gaussian tags to the actual integer producer/decoder at an explicitly promised common input grid. All center and side ports must share one phase frame; matching phases within individual roles is insufficient.
- **Actual-profile precision certificate:** the 29 complex child classes have old completed-child charge `421548223824*f`. Their certified charge is `(421548223824*f + 1142904672*(f mod 2))/2`, bounded by `211345564248*f` for every natural parallel width. This reduces that component by **49.864439629%**. Scalar E, global guard, unfinished recursion, tape/memory costs, normalized H0 output and the multiplication exponent are separately charged and unchanged by this certificate.
- **Formal tensor execution:** `GaussianTensorExecution.lean` defines and executes the full finite recursive C tensor in every dimension. This closes the earlier written-only execution link for that finite tensor algorithm; it does not certify physical frame/tape compilation.

The mixed-center inverse identity and Gaussian parity principles are inherited mathematics. The contribution is their combined exact dirty-difference implementation, guarded concrete producer integration, all-dimensional finite tensor execution proof, and source-linked actual-profile accounting.

**Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales** is the author and human developer. This research began in an earlier **Archivara** exploration of parity-aware integer multiplication. Alejandro subsequently developed the line personally with multiple AI tools, most recently **GPT-6.1**, as recorded by the author. This synthesis, paper, Lean proofs, controls and submission preparation involved substantial **OpenAI Codex** assistance.

The earlier exploration supplies the parity motivation. The arithmetic used here has independent proofs; this submission does not inherit its broader separation, carry-saving or benchmark assertions.

The package credits OpenAI's pinned manuscript; Douglas Colkitt/CrocSwap; icekylinx; Zhihao Chen/jacklightChen; RaD/hipotures; Aurel Prosz/Paureel; James Chang/jamesyc; Dominik Scholz; Rohan Arun; Chafik Boukhalfa/chafreaky; Swapnil Jain; and the contributors and AI disclosures retained in the upstream NOTICE and complete ledger. The local identity is unchanged: at sorted position i, prefix plus suffix sums every original input except the one at permutation position i. Restoring the original index is therefore essential. Every addition remains disjoint, and every globally shared output is checked exactly.

| 23 | 5,749 | 6,002 | 36,432 |

and **47,461** (h=25).

prs.title: Skip-prefix strips: conditional κ = 4498144/10^11 > 2^-15
prs.body:
**κ = 4498144/10^11 ≈ 4.498144×10⁻⁵ > 2⁻¹⁵**, conditional on OpenAI's base theorem and the retained analytic and fixed-tape interfaces. That is **9.2146906% above #48** (411862541/10^13), which it builds on. It is also 7.8378235% above the highest open claim at the time of writing, #51 (4171211781/10^14); #49 and #50 claim 4.123863984e-5 and 4.129418696e-5. The exact bit saving is 4498347/10^11.

## Change and mathematical scope

This builds on #48 (`b7194b8`), so the branch also carries the #43, #46 and #48 commits; only the last commit is new. Everything except the scalar producer is #48's `research/copied-fixed` pipeline, with constants recomputed. The new files are in `research/skip-strips/`.

**What changes.** Every vertex's leave-one-out strip sums use a **skip-prefix** layout:

`s_j = A_{j−2} + (v_{j−1} + B_{j+1})` instead of `s_j = A_{j−1} + B_{j+1}`

In the ordinary layout, the two consumers of each prefix A_i are A_{i+1} and s_{i+1}. Their envelopes are incomparable, so the second use always costs a fresh role. With the skip layout, the consumers of A_i are A_{i+1} and s_{i+2}, and cover(A_{i+1}) ⊆ cover(s_{i+2}). Likewise, the new node v_{i−1} + B_{i+1} sits inside B_{i−1}. The inherited carrier matching can join these nested pairs.

- **Layout details.** The top level runs the layout on the reversed value list. Deeper levels run it on values sorted by (support size, ±support), #48's idea. Totals follow #48's rules.
- **Matching.** It is #44's weighted optimizer, pinned in `links-{23,25}.uses` and regenerable with `optimize_matching.py`.

| | #48 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| additions (h=23 / 25) | 37,098 / 49,119 | 40,329 / 53,475 |
| carrier links (h=23 / 25) | 6,002 / 7,715 | 12,719 / 16,991 |
| roles R (h=23 / 25) | 36,432 / 48,329 | 32,946 / 43,409 |
| physical wires W | 177,530,859 | 160,799,739 |

**Hypotheses.** No hypothesis or interface changes; the bound uses the same inherited framework as #48. Two points of scope:
- This result leans more heavily on the carrier-continuation rule than #48 does. Without carrier matching, the new DAG has more roles than #48's (45,665 vs 42,434 at h=23).
- #40 and later, including #48, are outside the maintainer audit of #39 (`docs/research/community-final-audit.md`). This PR inherits that status.

## Validation

**Finite checks.** `make skip-strips-verify` checks:
- scalar exactness: every output is the exact leave-two-out sum or retained total;
- the original-envelope labels;
- pinned-link legality: every link is replayed in `profiles.cpp` and recounted independently;
- the fixed I+J profiles: 61,461 / 82,606 distinct transition matrices, 5,642 / 7,434 of them checked under several primes (CRT), with 0 disagreements;
- the full physical timeline and every dirty-scratch basis vector, in both orientations;
- all 4,073,300 data pairs, with exact rational recovery of the ten primary-prime failures;
- the exact moment, plus exact lower bounds showing that the #36 baseline and the #40–#44 and #46–#48 networks fail at the new bit saving;
- all 47 strict assembly conditions and 7 margins.

`tests/test_skip_strips.py` adds 20 tests, including leave-one-out exactness, the cover-nesting identity and negative controls.

An earlier version of the same change, applied on top of #43, was audited independently from clean copies. The audit re-ran the full producer check and recomputed every transition profile in exact rational arithmetic, with no modular step. It found no correctness issue. The stacked version here has not had that separate audit.

**Proof arguments.** As in #41, #47 and #48, which also changed the producer DAG, the new DAG enters the inherited proofs only through properties and quantities that the finite checks above recompute: disjoint additions, common points, exact outputs, admissible carrier links, the physical timeline and the transition profiles. The cover-nesting identity explains why the matching finds more links; correctness does not depend on it. The inherited written obligations are not re-proved here: the base theorem, the residual compiler and fixed-tape recursion, the physical meaning of carrier continuations and copied centers, and the analytic, routing and eventual-threshold interfaces. This is not a formal verification, and no global optimality or speedup is claimed.

prs.title: Dual suffix-skip strips: conditional κ = 4541011/10^11 > 2^-15
prs.body:
## Summary

We introduce the mathematical dual **skip-suffix** layout for leave-one-out strip sums in the 2D $(23, 25)$ data-corner geometry:

$$s_j = (A_{j-1} + v_{j+1}) + B_{j+2}$$

This improves the certified exponent bound to:

$$T(n) = O\bigl(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\bigr), \qquad \boxed{\kappa = \frac{4541011}{10^{11}} = 4.541011 \times 10^{-5} > 2^{-15}}$$

This bound **cleanly beats PR #54** ($141532521/3125000000000 = 4.529040672 \times 10^{-5}$) without checking in 250,000 lines of paid-clone tables, beats **PR #53** ($4498144/10^{11} = 4.498144 \times 10^{-5}$) by **+0.953%**, and beats **PR #48** ($411862541/10^{13}$) by **+10.255%**.

---

## Architectural Duality vs PR #53 (Skip-Prefix)

In PR #53, the leave-one-out strips were computed via the skip-prefix layout $s_j = A_{j-2} + (v_{j-1} + B_{j+1})$. While this nested prefix consumers, it introduced a structural asymmetry: pairing small-support leaves with large-support suffix sums collapsed core popcounts ($	ext{core} \to 1$). Consequently, `SharedPointCircuit` failed to merge additions across common-point groups.

By contrast, the dual **skip-suffix** layout:
- Groups additions into intermediate sums $A_{j-1} + v_{j+1}$ that maintain compact cover envelopes and core popcounts $\ge 2$.
- Enables `SharedPointCircuit` to merge **530+ additions** across groups.
- Expands carrier matching capacity by **+175 matches** on $h=23$ and **+60 matches** on $h=25$.

### Full Circuit Comparison

| Metric | PR #48 (Reordered) | PR #53 (Skip-Prefix) | PR #54 (Paid Clones) | **This PR (Dual Skip-Suffix)** | Diff vs PR #54 |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **h=23 Additions ($c$)** | 40,629 | 40,329 | 40,329 | **40,099** | **-230** |
| **h=23 Matches** | 9,533 | 12,719 | 12,987 | **12,894** | -93 |
| **h=23 Roles ($R_{23}$)** | 36,432 | 32,946 | 32,693 | **32,541** | **-152** |
| **h=25 Additions ($c$)** | 53,775 | 53,475 | 53,475 | **53,175** | **-300** |
| **h=25 Matches** | 12,625 | 16,991 | 17,243 | **17,051** | -192 |
| **h=25 Roles ($R_{25}$)** | 48,329 | 43,409 | 43,056 | **43,049** | **-7** |
| **Total Wires ($W$)** | 177,530,859 | 160,799,739 | 159,592,676 | **159,230,679** | **-361,997** |
| **Bit Saving ($a_\text{bit}$)** | $4.118833 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.498347 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.529240 \times 10^{-5}$ | **$4.541218 \times 10^{-5}$** | **+$1.198 \times 10^{-7}$** |
| **Certified $\kappa$** | $4.118625 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.498144 \times 10^{-5}$ | $4.529040 \times 10^{-5}$ | **$4.541011 \times 10^{-5}$** | **+$1.197 \times 10^{-7}$** |
| **External Clone Tables** | None | None | 251,571 lines JSON | **None (Pure Algebraic)** | **-251.5k lines** |

---

## Hardware Verification & Controls

All results are certified on hardware through the standard repository pipeline:
1. `c.verify()`: Passed cancellation-free and leave-two-out output equivalence on both axes.
2. `dense_audit(c)`: Passed exact global bitset support containment.
3. `profiles.cpp` (across 3 Mersenne primes $2^{61}-1, 2^{31}-1, 524287$):
   - $h=23$: 5,379 CRT matrices checked, **0 modular disagreements**.
   - $h=25$: 7,179 CRT matrices checked, **0 modular disagreements**.
4. `original_timeline.py`: Checked all $32,541$ roles on $h=23$ and $43,049$ roles on $h=25$ in both orientations without dirty vector discrepancies.
5. `data_corners.cpp`: Full replay of all 4,073,300 data pairs with exact rational recovery of the 10 primary-prime fallbacks (accelerated via OpenMP to under 10 seconds).

7. Assembly: All 47 strict inequalities and 7 margins verified at $\kappa = \frac{4541011}{10^{11}}$.
8. Test suite: All 20 adversarial unit tests in `tests/test_skip_suffix.py` pass.

Run the complete reproduction suite via:
```bash

It then uses bounded moment-improving carried-signal exchanges under the existing linear-independence and distinct-use constraints: **670 exchanges on h23 and 825 on h25**. These are heuristic local improvements; no weighted matroid optimum is claimed.

The cost objective comes from our exact complete-characteristic feasibility framework, rather than selecting solely by wire count or primitive XOR count. Rank-flow identities prove why subtracting linear rank preserves local price order at fixed cardinality. Universal dirty-word proofs ensure that changing the legal encoder/complement preserves arbitrary dirty scratch when the separate fresh-transfer contract is maintained.

prs.title: Searched orders on PR #49's graphs: conditional κ = 4.125007391e-5
prs.body:
## Summary

A complete single-bit-flip descent over PR #49's pinned adjacent-swap orders,
with the **role count** as the objective rather than the number of matched
carriers.

PR #49 pinned a greedy climb over the `total()` / `vector()` order bits and its
scope note explicitly disclaims global optimality. Two things differ here:

1. **The objective.** A flip can add matched carriers *and* add more additions at
   the same time, so maximising carriers is not the same as minimising
   `R = c + q - matched`. Since `W = 2N + sum_h (N // v_h) * R_h` holds the child
   list fixed, `R` is what moves the role volume and hence the exponent, so the
   descent minimises `R` directly (matched carriers and log-weight as
   tie-breaks).
2. **The search.** Every decision bit (1584 at h=23, 1900 at h=25) is flipped and
   evaluated end to end; the best strict improvement is accepted and the pass
   repeats until no single flip improves — instead of one greedy sweep.

| | PR #49 | This |
|---|---:|---:|
| h=23 roles R (matched) | 36,382 (6,077) | **36,341 (6,153)** |
| h=25 roles R (matched) | 48,255 (7,809) | **48,247 (7,825)** |
| Width W | 177,284,805 | **177,176,337** |
| bit saving | 4124034054/10^14 | **825035511/2·10^13** |
| **kappa** | 4123863984/10^14 | **4125007391/10^14** |

**+0.02773%**, still above `2^-15`. Everything else is PR #48/#49 unchanged:
RaD's point order and original-envelope labels, both fixed I+J bases, copied
centers, paid endpoint corrections, reversed data corners with exact recovery of
all ten fallbacks, the complex layer and the balanced assembly.

## Verification

Run with the repository's own machinery on this branch:

- `make ordered-descent-check` → `witness.py` derives the bit saving and kappa
  from the searched rows and certified profiles by grid search (not pinned
  constants) and checks the 47 assembly constraints, the seven margins, the
  rejection of the next bit and kappa grid points, and the exclusion of **nine**
  earlier networks at the new saving — including PR #49's own — plus six focused
  tests.
- `make ordered-descent-producer` → `producer.py` replays both dimensions with
  PR #43's independent checkers imported unchanged: scalar identity, dense
  global-bitset audit, the pinned matching read back by `profiles.cpp` with every
  edge asserted admissible, an independent recount of every matched use, and the
  complete physical timeline and dirty basis in both orientations. CRT
  disagreements are zero. The replay reproduces the stored artifacts
  byte-for-byte on a second run.
- The graphs are rebuilt from the committed bit vectors on every run, so
  `bits-{23,25}.json` plus the committed rows/profiles/matchings are the whole
  input.

Cross-checks performed while building this: the two-stage matcher used here is an
instrumented build of the pinned `scripts/partial_swap/match_positive_dag.cpp`
(the file is unchanged between this branch and PR #49), and upstream's own
`profiles.cpp` with its own Hopcroft–Karp independently reports the same
`matched` and `R` for every graph used here.

## Scope and limits — please read before merging

- This is a **single-bit local optimum** of the order space, not a global one,
  and no global optimality of the matcher is claimed beyond the pinned max-weight
  maximum matchings.
- The descent was **still finding improvements when it was stopped** (`R` had
  reached 36,336 and 48,239 in the unfinished next passes), so the reported
  numbers are a lower bound on what this search reaches.
- The search harness itself (bit-vector descent with the role-count objective) is
  not shipped; the searched bit vectors, rows, certified profiles, matchings,
  witness and certificate are.
- The inherited PR #48 dependencies and the analytic hypotheses are unchanged and
  remain conditional.

If you prefer, I can split the docs/README-headline change out, or hold the
headline at PR #49 until you have reviewed the witness.

## Files

- `research/ordered-descent/README.md` — result, method, checks, limits
- `research/ordered-descent/{bits,original,profiles,scalar,timeline}-{23,25}.json`,
  `links-{23,25}.uses` — searched inputs and replayed artifacts
- `research/ordered-descent/{witness,producer}.py`, `climbed_graph.py`,
  `optimize_matching.py`, `profiles.cpp`, `certificate.json`, `SOURCE.json`
- `tests/test_ordered_descent.py`; `Makefile` (`ordered-descent-verify` wired into
  `verify-community`); root `README.md` exponent updated

## Attribution

Base graphs, orders, matching objective and composition: **Chafik Boukhalfa**
(PR #48) and **Rohan Arun** (PR #49, with Anthropic Claude assistance), building
on RaD / hipotures (PR #41), icekylinx, James Chang, Dominik Scholz, Zhihao Chen,
Aurel Prosz / Paureel, Swapnil Jain, eumemic, Douglas Colkitt, OpenAI and
Harvey–van der Hoeven. The searched-order descent, the role-count objective and
this run were produced with AI assistance (Codebuff/Claude).

prs.title: Scheduled region orders on balanced frames: conditional κ = 5.2111890493145e-5
prs.body:
## Dependency

This branch is composed on top of the open #82 head (`3410b94`), so its diff against `main` includes that PR's content, exactly as #82 itself composes the pinned PR76/PR79 archive. The candidate added by this PR is the fourteen files under `research/envelope-scheduled/` plus `.github/workflows/envelope-scheduled.yml`.

## What this composes

The pinned envelope-balanced witness fixes one region order per axis through
`balanced_split_graph.configuration(h)['schedule']` (`cover-core` at h23,
`reverse-node` at h25). This candidate keeps every other setting — groups
`[1,1,2]`, anchors, half-plane versus row coarse sums, future-compatible
completion, 0 versus 3 carry-exchange passes, exact next-use profile costs, the
coordinate-conjugated oracle pricing at h25, the PR74 scalar-envelope
reordering, and the pinned coordinate orders `order-23.json` / `order-25.json`
— and changes only the region order: `node-asc` at h23, `width-node` at h25.

## Result

| Quantity | Pinned witness | This candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| kappa (1e-18 grid) | 5.2032798885190e-05 | **5.2111890493145e-05** |
| Bit saving | 5.2035506438388e-05 | 5.2114606283958e-05 |
| h23 / h25 auxiliary roles | 27075 / 35500 | 27032 / 35431 |
| Physical width W | 133289600 | 133068501 |

kappa = 10422378098629/200000000000000000, which is 15818321591/200000000000000000
absolute (**+0.152%**) above the pinned 5203279888519/100000000000000000, and
+0.72% above PR76's 5.1738676045141e-05. The improvement also survives on the
coarser 1e-11 grid (5.211188e-05, still above the pinned fine-grid value).

The candidate is *narrower* than the pin and has *fewer* auxiliary roles, so
this is not a width effect: the region order changes which rank-one blocks the
profiler extracts from the same physical path, and the moment inequality
`sum_t count_t (t/m)^(1-s) / W < 1` is decided by that profile shape.

## How the orders were selected

Region orders were scored by recompiling axes and evaluating the unchanged
exact arithmetic: 12 h23 orders (9 keys plus 4 hash-seeded random orders, with
`cover-core` reproducing the pinned axis-23 word byte for byte) crossed with 10
h25 orders, 120 pairs in total, at 8-20 minutes of compilation per axis. The
best pair is `node-asc` with `width-node`; at h25 the `node-asc` and
`width-node` keys happen to produce the same order.

Coordinate relabelling was searched separately as an independent lever: more
than 500 hill-climbing and random relabel draws on the pinned words never beat
the identity relabel, so the pinned `order-23.json` and `order-25.json` are
retained unchanged. Only the region order moved the number.

## What is verified

`research/envelope-scheduled/verify.py` replays both words (XOR word, dirty
basis, frame incidence), rebuilds the transition and fixed-basis profile
receipts, recomputes the profile of each axis exactly against the shipped
`profiles-23.json` / `profiles-25.json`, rebuilds the complete
child-multiplicity profile, re-derives the 1e-18 grid saving with the inherited
rational binary search, checks both moment enclosures, the independent
log-enclosure audit bound, the fixed-width bridge and the balanced assembly,
and asserts all 47 strict inequalities, the seven margins, the next-grid kappa
rejection and the independent-bound separation. `--regenerate` recompiles both
axes through this directory's `compiler.py` (role counts 27032 and 35431) and
asserts the regenerated words are byte-identical to the shipped ones; the
recorded run is `regen.log`. `test_controls.py` adds 15 controls: a duplicated
coordinate, an inconsistent mapping, unrelabelled source values or outputs, a
missing terminal synthesis, an aliased terminal, an unknown region order, a
region order that breaks the topological or carrier constraints, and a stale
bridge field are all rejected, while the recorded kappa is accepted and its
next 1e-18 grid value is rejected. CI runs both in the same three Python
versions as the pinned workflow.

## Scope and limits

The arithmetic downstream of the words is inherited unchanged: the PR48
rational logarithm enclosures, the PR65 moment/assembly/audit code, the
fixed-tape transfer, routing and recovery interfaces, prime selection and the
all-size compiler argument. Only heuristic selection among legal region orders
changed, under the same topological and carrier-candidate assertions. Nothing
in `research/envelope-balanced/` is modified; `compiler.py` and
`flag_engine.py` are copies of the pinned files in this directory, and the
copied flag engine keeps the pinned `check_flag_engine` assertion. The one
harness difference is that the oracle subprocess is awaited with a generous
timeout instead of ten seconds, because the pinned ten-second wait aborts an
already *completed* compilation at its shutdown step under parallel load,
before the word is written; it cannot change the word, which is fully
determined before that step.

This remains a conditional finite witness: no global optimality over region
orders and no measured practical speedup is claimed.

Region-order selection and verification with Codebuff (Buffy) assistance.
Inherited sources, notices and licenses remain unchanged.

prs.title: Merged auxiliary exteriors: conditional κ = 5.5354656014473e-5
prs.body:
## Conditional improvement

$$T(n)=O\big(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\big),\qquad \kappa=\frac{55354656014473}{10^{18}}=5.5354656014473\times10^{-5}.$$

That is **+6.97% over #79**, which this builds on (head 79dd6e1), and **+4.86% over #95**, the best open PR when this was opened. The bit saving is `27678860161103/500000000000000000`. All inherited all-size and analytic hypotheses remain assumptions.

## Change

Every auxiliary role pays a separate exterior edge `I − I_h⊗B` (profile `[h, m−2h]`). Auxiliary source frames are free, so each role can merge that residual into one of its endpoint edges:

- **creation edge** `I − (I_h − A_first)⊗B`: source and sink shifted by `−E`;
- **retirement edge** `I − A_last⊗B`: non-output roles only.

The choice is made per role. #79's words, gates, XORs, W and deficit are unchanged.

**Frame validity.** No gate, XOR, frame raise or schedule changes. Only auxiliary source and sink frames move; these are free in the upstream contract, and PR29's stage two already uses source `D_0`. A retirement-merged role's final segment, from its last gate frame to the sink, is charged as the single residual it already was. The inherited accounting had split that segment into a cleanup with no gate event plus the exterior.

Every gate incidence, including the center scatter after the middle mixer, therefore keeps #79's frames. #79's replay covers them: dirty basis in both orientations, and frame raises rebuilt from literal XORs. The only new matrices are the merged endpoint residuals, which are idempotent and certified exactly.

| | h23 | h25 |
|---|---:|---:|
| roles | 27,297 | 35,684 |
| merged at creation | 15,410 | 20,111 |
| merged at retirement | 4,216 | 5,149 |
| distinct merged edges certified | 8,537 | 10,601 |

**Corner-rank lemma.** For `M = I − UWᵀ` with `WᵀU = I`, the NE corner rank is:

- `(i−j+1) − r + rank U_{<j} + rank W_{>i}` for `j ≤ i+1`;
- `rank U_{≤i}W_{≥j}ᵀ` above the band.

In the PR34 fixed basis this reduces to ranks of local submatrices `X[S,T]`, so the result does not depend on the line. Each such submatrix is a 0/1 diagonal plus a rank ≤2 correction. Its rank is computed exactly over Q using 2×2 integer determinants, with no modular step.

**Bridge.** Merged edges create bit children up to **552**, above 529. The bit halving degree goes from 9 to **17**, the row coefficient becomes 1059, and the product row stock goes from `p^2000` to **`p^2200`** (gap 991/25). This affects only the row-product slack and the eventual cutoffs, not κ. The inherited `validate_bridge` recomputes all of these.

Proof and scope are in `research/merged-exterior/PROOF.md`.

## Verification

`make merged-exterior-verify` takes about 4 minutes on 4 cores. It does the following:

- Checks the controlled permutations against the pinned PR34 module.
- Recomputes all 56,303 candidate edge profiles exactly and replays the per-role selection.
- Profiles the removed transitions with the unchanged inherited profiler.
- Rebuilds the full child list on top of #79's verified profile.
- Checks the exact and independent moment enclosures, and that the next grid point is rejected.
- Checks the 47 constraints and 7 margins.

There is also a new CI group, `merged`.

The joint-dual, split-pair and balanced-split source manifests pin `Makefile`, `README.md` and the workflow file, so they are re-pinned. The only change to their certificates is the recorded manifest hash.

A full `make verify` passed on Linux (EC2) with a clean `git diff`.

As a discovery-time cross-check, all 19,138 selected edges were compared with direct NE elimination of the full 575×575 physical matrix (one line, mod 2^31−1): 0 mismatches.

## Credits

Builds on @chafreaky #79 and the stack it composes:

- @rohangar1 #59

- @DominikScholz #63, #68

- @chafreaky #60, #71

It also uses the PR34 fixed basis (jamesyc) and the PR29 two-stage endpoint note. Merged exteriors by eumemic with Anthropic Claude assistance.

This extends my merged [PR #36](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/36) at `11817ccacb564bb7f98789c20dc11d3fece207e3`, with one new commit on upstream `main` at `56b66d58297deca1d7dd130247d720e960f77a37`. The #10 → #18 → #24 → #32 → #36 proof lineage and attributed two-stage, ordinary-leaf and semantic/bulk interfaces are retained.

Under the retained multiplication framework and those analytic/tape interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{194869}{2500000000}=7.79476\times10^{-5}.
$$

## Construction

The bit network uses `(23,23)`. A common generic rational basis and opposite bank orders reduce each rank-`r` projector residual to one contiguous reversed rank-`r` child. The full involution factorization includes the complementary diagonal blocks and uses physically lower triangular adapters.

The address arithmetic acts componentwise on fixed-width atoms. Each adapter is paid as an atom loop, costing `O(V e/w)`. Stopping at `w=ceil(e^(1/1000))` uses the retained ordinary interchange at leaves and peeled remainders. A constant-size outer wrapper restores ordinary interchange; its conversion factor does not enter the recursive moment.

The complex network uses `(24,24)` with aligned pair-star orders and all 24 disjoint centers. Their total is decoded by exact division by 21. A common grid `2^(-P) * 21^(-K)`, with `K=G(D+1)`, covers the active recursion chain. Completed children preserve the incoming odd-denominator exponent; the completed outer transform restores dyadic encoding. No child return is rounded.

The coarse bit saving is `4019/50000000`, giving the ordinary bit saving `803380799/10000000000000` after stopping. The strict complex saving is `1949/25000000`. Their coarse-bit and complex moment gaps exceed `4.2909639537e-10` and `1.3338373969e-10`, respectively.

The assembly retains **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)**'s PR #23 composition of **RaD (hipotures)**'s semantic precision, routing, phase-cell inverse and bulk resampling. The rational-center charge preserves `C1=1`; the three nested row reserves are bounded by `p^4000`. The assembly bit parameter is weakened to `0.00007795982204` to leave strict room below the stopped complex leaf saving. All 47 strict constraints and seven assembly margins hold, with final absorption gap greater than `6.6129e-11`.

This PR is a cumulative refinement on the aligned-composition fixed-exterior track (#91 $\to$ #93 $\to$ #94 $\to$ #95 $\to$ #98), not a global record claim.

### Two certified stages (`research/contiguous-pair-exchange/`)

1. **Stage A — Contiguous-pair coordinate pricing with the pristine unchanged #91 engine ($\kappa = \frac{26400279929441}{500000000000000000} = 5.2800559858882\times 10^{-5}$)**:
   - In #91 (and inherited through #93–#98), the odd singleton coordinate (`22` at $h=23$, `24` at $h=25$) was placed at index `4`, splitting the chain of consecutive coordinate pairs, and coordinates `(17,18)` at $h=25$ were transposed to `(23,22)`, splitting both `(16,17)` and `(18,19)`.

prs.title: Deferred readouts on both stopped networks: conditional κ = 8.58478e-5
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

$$T(n)=O\big(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\big),\qquad \kappa=\frac{429239}{5\cdot 10^{9}}=8.58478\times10^{-5}.$$

This is **+10.1% over #104** (7.79476e-5). It builds on #104 (head 854ba7dca98651eab2050402384e1a7784534f0a, included in this branch) and keeps all of its inherited hypotheses. The next κ grid point at denominator 10^10 is rejected.

**Idea.** #104 compiles every projector residual of rank r as **one** child of width r. Under that rule, Swapnil Jain's deferred readouts pay on both networks. A slot that reads its garbage out at a start frame σ_u starts its chain at σ_u instead of 0. Its entrance child shrinks by dim σ_u, and its exterior child grows to m − h + dim σ_u. The rank moves into a child near m, where it costs less.

| | #104 | here |
|---|---|---|
| bit network | positive-label producer, R = 38,776 | Swapnil's round-seven deferred word, R = 28,866, unchanged |
| stopped bit saving | 8.034e-5 | 1.2402e-4 |
| complex network | aligned rational centres, R = 44,918 | same DAG and roles, lifted binary frames, 8,893 deferred roles |
| complex saving (binding) | 1949/25000000 = 7.796e-5 | 214657/2500000000 = 8.58628e-5 |
| κ | 7.79476e-5 | **8.58478e-5** |

**Complex construction (new).** On #104's unchanged h = 24 DAG:

- a maximum carrier matching under the inherited adjacency rules (8,966 links, R = 44,918);
- an explicit role compile;
- lifted binary frames: the F2 kernel of the functionals of every reachable root (t_S for outputs, e_i for centre A_i). The compile uses a lifted frame where it is nondegenerate and keeps the frames monotone along slot successors;
- phase one: the closure of the 24 centre completions;
- deferred frames σ_u ⊆ F0(u) ∩ ⋂ t_S^⊥ for roles that phase one does not touch and whose garbage does not reach a centre. An insertion rule nests them on every target.

The stage-one word follows Swapnil's design B. The readout coefficients come from the transpose sweep. Their only odd denominator is #104's 21.

**Bit network.** `bit_round7.py` derives the bit child list from Swapnil's two frozen round-seven data files, pinned by SHA-256. Their rank mass, 57,403,754,177, is the value that #97 reports.

## Validation

**Finite tests** (`research/deferred-stopped/complex_deferred.py`):

- The compiled word computes all 8,120 root values.
- The deferred word, replayed over Z/(2^61−1) with arbitrary scratch and data (two seeds), restores every role and adds exactly x_S to every target.
- Exact F2 checks:
  - every role chain is nested;
  - every lifted frame and every deferral frame is nondegenerate;
  - every σ_u lies in its start frame and in t_S^⊥ for each reached target;
  - the deferral frames are nested on every target in readout order.
- The one-child histogram has total rank W m − N + L = 109,450,358,336 (as in #104). Every child is below m (the largest is 574 of 576).
- `certificate.py` computes both exact moments with #104's routines, the stopped saving (1 − 1/1000)·coarse + (1/1000)·384599/10^10, the finite bridge and the 47-constraint assembly.

**Proof arguments, not machine-checked here:**

- Stage two is the complement time reversal of stage one with the same edge multiset, as in Swapnil's round seven and #104's two-stage counts. #97 replays the reflected ledger for the bit word. For the complex deferred word, this PR states stage two but does not machine-check it.
- Deferred auxiliary endpoints use the translated gauges of `notes/copied-centers-complex.tex` and `notes/endpoint-gauge-complex.tex` (PR21/PR24).
- The larger children (528 of 529 and 574 of 576) raise the product-row stock to p^33000 (PR29 used p^47000). As in #104 and #96, the stock changes only the row slack and the cutoffs, not κ.
- All of #104's inherited hypotheses. See `research/deferred-stopped/PROOF.md`.

**Reproduce:**

```sh
python3 research/deferred-stopped/complex_deferred.py
python3 research/deferred-stopped/bit_round7.py DIR   # Swapnil's round-seven files or #97's copy
python3 research/deferred-stopped/certificate.py
```

`DIR` holds `witness_23.json.gz` and `deferred_23.json.gz`: `certificates/round7/` of https://github.com/Swapnil-jain/integer-mult-kappa at commit 741e7aa078392553815df7926ee17ac5e25a8c38, or #97's copy in `research/deferred-signed/swapnil-round7/certificates/round7/`.

The `(23,23)` bit network applies the stopped whole-projector compiler from #104 to the actual deferred physical word of **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)**'s #97, based on **Swapnil Jain**'s pinned witness. ## Conditional improvement

$$T(n)=O\big(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\big),\qquad \kappa=\frac{1044939}{10^{10}}=1.044939\times10^{-4}.$$

This is **+5.87% over #116**, the best open PR when this was opened (9.8699350338e-5), and +21.72% over #110 (8.58478e-5). It is +34.06% over #104, its base. The complex side binds. All of #104's retained analytic and tape interfaces remain assumptions.

#110 independently uses the same bit-side composition: Swapnil Jain's round-seven deferred words under #104's one-child rule, with stopped bit saving 1.2402e-4. #113, #114 and #116 reuse that bit side. This PR differs from them only on the complex side.

## Change

- **Bit side: #97's deferred words under #104's one-child accounting.**
  - Every charged residual is a nested projector residual, so each counts as one child.
  - Those residuals are: slot chains, gauged exits `I−(I−σ)⊗Q`, center copies, `y_T` and `X_S` chains, data connectors and copy corrections. Garbage readouts are scalar gates.
  - Coarse saving is `620523/(5·10^9)`; ordinary saving after #104's stopping conversion is `1.2401896e-4`.
- **Complex side: a new h=24 all-disjoint rational-center producer in #104's framework.**
  - It uses 28,705 roles, against 44,918 for #104's (and #110's) producer, so `a_c = 26129/(2.5·10^8)`.
  - It ships as a 91,770-addition DAG. Supports, labels and ranks are replayed from the operands, and #104's unchanged matcher rebuilds the row exactly.
- **Bridge and assembly: #104's, at `PHASE_STOP = 10^-6`.**
  - The largest bit child is 528, so the halving degree is 367 and the row stock is `p^22000`. This only affects eventual cutoffs.
  - All 47 constraints and 7 margins hold, and the next κ grid point is rejected.

Preconditions and scope are in `research/deferred-product/PROOF.md`.

## Verification

```sh
make deferred-product-verify
```

This target does the following:

- Runs #97's literal ledger and Swapnil Jain's `check_word.py` and `check_frames.py`.
- Replays the complex DAG.
- Replays the complete signed two-stage complex word at gate level: 0 violations, continuous reflection, and a histogram equal to the row's profile. The 3,308 alternating rank-2 residuals use #104's one-child Gauss normal form.
- Recomputes the one-child list, both moments and the assembly.

A full `make verify` passed on Linux (EC2) with a clean `git diff`.

## Credits

- **Bit network:** Swapnil Jain (round seven).
- **Ledgers and integration:** @jacklightChen (#97).
- **Stopped-product accounting, framework and assembly:** @icekylinx (#104), on its retained lineage.
- **The same bit-side composition, found in parallel:** @ikeboy (#110).

This builds on #104 (`948ce1510df750f4c18b96bdaef436a86f8bf834`) and the exact #113 cyclic-strip producer (`0eee4d507092a96bde88de703f07574ba17401a8`).

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{942802139}{10^{13}}=0.0000942802139.
$$

The saving is **54.4687% above $2^{-14}$**.

## Construction

**Bit network (23,23).** Apply #104's common-basis, opposite-bank stopped compiler to every proper projector of Swapnil Jain's frozen round-seven word, pinned at `741e7aa078392553815df7926ee17ac5e25a8c38`. Every nonzero projector residual is one reversed child of its full rank. The strict coarse saving is `15513/125000000`; stopping at atom exponent `1/1000`, with ordinary leaf saving `384599/10^10`, gives ordinary bit saving `1240183559/10^13`.

**Complex network (24,24).** Keep #113's producer and legal matching: 68,188 additions, 8,120 roots, 37,802 matched links and 38,506 physical auxiliary roles. Reconstruct the invertible matched scalar word `L`, signed rational scatter `J`, and exact complete adjoint `C=JL`.

A 32,488-event closure computes the 24 retained centers first, preserving every role's full access order, including read/read dependencies. Checks cover **209,340 accesses**, retained-center boundaries and 8,096 ordinary root reads. Selected scratch is untouched by the closure and injection.

Select **9,356 nondegenerate partial subframes** (3,309 distinct frames), each contained in its first owner and every target hyperplane receiving its adjoint coefficient. Target readouts follow actual nested chains. All residuals are nondegenerate; alternating cases use the retained inverse-Gram/Gauss interface.

For dimension d inside an owner of rank b, the first child changes from b to b-d, and the exterior from m-h to m-h+d. Source and sink phases change together: in stage one use `+q_sigma` and `q_F+q_sigma`; in stage two use `-q_sigma` and `q_F-q_sigma`. The completed operator remains `q_F`. Target-front chain replacements preserve rank mass. The strict complex saving is **`5893637/62500000000 = 0.000094298192`**.

| Complete paid inventory | Bit | Complex |
|---|---:|---:|
| m / auxiliary roles | 529 / 28,866 | 576 / 38,506 |
| W | 108,516,254 | 164,065,440 |
| Recursive rank sum | 57,403,754,177 | 94,499,831,360 |
| Positive bins / maximum child | 46 / 528 | 40 / 572 |
| Rank-one copied-output children | 3,136,441 | 4,096,576 |

The complete adjoint has **11,678,073 nonzero coefficients per invocation**, with numerator magnitude at most 42 over denominator 42. Charge 16 scalar operations per term and retain the predecessor allowance:

`G = 2019773888 + 2*2024*11678073*16 = 758385205952`.

Recompute the denominator-21 exact grid, literal precision guard, completed-child height induction and `C1=1` contract. Halving factors 367, 100 and 9 give row coefficient 12,961; **p^27000** supplies degree gap `13989/25 > 0`. All copies, scalar work and wrappers are paid. With `beta=10^-6` and `eta=10^-8`, all 47 assembly constraints and seven margins are strict.

## Summary

Supersedes #104 (`research/stopped-product-rational-centers`) and #107 (`research/reversed-rational-centers`) by replacing the binary-tree prefix/suffix schedules inside the $(h, d) = (24, 24)$ rational-center complex producer and the $h = 23$ positive-label bit producer with **staggered dual-paired linear-chain schedules** (`research/staggered-rational-centers`).

Both the **complex-only** bound (holding #104's frozen `stopped-product-bit-axis.json` and `parent.AB = 803380799 / 10^13` fixed) and the **joint** bound (regenerating both the $h=23$ positive-label bit producer and the $h=24$ rational-center complex producer from source through the unmodified C++ maximum-cardinality bipartite matchers) are verified in `research/staggered-rational-centers/verify.py`:

| Metric | PR #104 (`stopped-product-rational-centers`) | PR #107 (`reversed-rational-centers`) | This PR (Complex-Only) | This PR (Joint Bit + Complex) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Complex height / degree $(h, d)$ | $(24, 24)$ | $(24, 24)$ | $(24, 24)$ | $(24, 24)$ |
| Complex addition gates $c$ | $47,796$ | $47,796$ | **$48,958$** | **$48,958$** |
| Complex non-output non-input gates $q$ | $6,958$ | $6,958$ | **$8,120$** | **$8,120$** |
| Complex matched pairs (`match_complex_general`) | $9,836$ | $9,836$ | **$18,038$** | **$18,038$** |
| Complex recursion roles $R = c + q - 2\cdot\text{matched}$ | $44,918$ | $44,918$ | **$39,040$** (**$-5,878$**) | **$39,040$** (**$-5,878$**) |
| Complex rank sum / $\ell$ | $976,842$ / $552$ | $975,786$ / $552$ | **$938,064$ / $552$** | **$938,064$ / $552$** |
| Certified complex floor $b$ | $7.798287495 \times 10^{-5}$ | $7.801725496 \times 10^{-5}$ | **$8.801801147 \times 10^{-5}$** | **$8.801801147 \times 10^{-5}$** |
| Bit $h=23$ roles $R_{\text{bit}} = c + q - 2\cdot\text{matched}$ | $38,776$ | $38,776$ | $38,776$ (inherited) | **$34,014$** (**$-4,762$**) |
| Certified bit saving $AB$ | $8.03380799 \times 10^{-5}$ | $8.03380799 \times 10^{-5}$ | $8.03380799 \times 10^{-5}$ | **$8.921551719638 \times 10^{-5}$** |
| **Headline certified saving $\kappa$** | **$7.7950234824805 \times 10^{-5}$** | **$7.7984487412405 \times 10^{-5}$** | **$8.0325171150015 \times 10^{-5}$** | **$8.8002329264725 \times 10^{-5}$** |

- **Complex-only gain**: $+2.374936 \times 10^{-6}$ ($+3.05\%$) above PR #104 and $+2.340684 \times 10^{-6}$ ($+3.00\%$) above PR #107.
- **Joint regenerated gain**: $+1.005210 \times 10^{-5}$ ($+12.90\%$) above PR #104 and $+1.001784 \times 10^{-5}$ ($+12.85\%$) above PR #107.

## Key Mechanisms

1. **Staggered Dual-Paired Prefix/Suffix Strip Schedules (`StaggeredPairedTriple`)**:
   - At even indices $i$, `prefix` advances via paired sums `add(prefix[-2], add(values[i-1], values[i]))`; at odd indices $i$, `suffix` advances via paired sums `add(suffix[-2], add(values[n-1-i], values[n-i]))`.
   - Every intermediate gate in a paired step has one fan-in at odd distance and one fan-in at even distance in the linear chain, making all paired partial sums eligible under `match_complex_general.cpp` (`non_overlap`, `valid_S`, `valid_T`) and `match_positive_dag.cpp`.
   - At the top level of `two[u,v]` (`len(values) == 11`, `len(vals) == 10`), keeping `prefix` unpaired while pairing `suffix` at odd indices $i \in \{1, 3, 5, 7\}$ preserves all 10 `suffix[i]` nodes in `lookup[s]` (so `pre[2], pre[4], \dots, pre[20]` in `complex.py` hit `lookup` with zero duplicate gates) while matching `(suffix[2m], suffix[2m-1])` via `suffix[2m+1]` and `q_m = add(vals[2m-1], vals[2m])` into `prefix[2m+1]` via `vals[2m]`.

2. **Linear-Chain Block, Coarse, and Coefficient Aggregations (`rtotal`)**:
   - Replaces balanced binary trees in `block`, `coarse`, and `coeff` with reverse linear fold `rtotal` while keeping binary-tree `total` inside `result[excluded]` so 1-, 2-, and 3-survivor inclusion-exclusion partial sums remain shared.

3. **Leave-One-Pair-Out Readout Bridge & Same-Group Pair-Star Prefix Pairing**:
   - In `complex.py` (`StaggeredComplexProducer`), when `(a ^ 1) != b` and `2 <= j < 18` and `(i // 2 < a // 2 or (j // 2) % 2 == 0)`, `missing[p][q]` is assembled via the leave-one-pair-out bridge `add(add(pre[jj], suf[jj + 2]), w[jj ^ (1 - (j & 1))])` (`jj = j & ~1`), aligning with the odd-step suffix pairs from `two[u,v]` and eliminating 680 high-rank gates.
   - For the 12 same-group pair stars `(a ^ 1) == b` (skipped by `two[u,v]`), pairing `pre` at odd `idx_w < 20` reuses `add(w[idx_w-1], w[idx_w])` from `suf` via `lookup` with zero extra gates and adds 54 matched pairs.

prs.body:
This extends my [PR #115](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/115) at `cf60442983c153a3a0f5272ea4713f99eba13c86`, with one new commit. The #10 → #18 → #24 → #32 → merged #36 → #104 → #115 proof lineage and attributed ordinary-leaf, semantic/bulk and fixed-tape interfaces are retained.

Under the retained multiplication framework and those analytic/tape interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{3146011}{10000000000}=3.146011\times10^{-4}.
$$

## Construction

The global architecture uses three invocation banks on a regular Cayley cover in dimension `3h-2`. Each local port retains its source line while the three active spaces exchange its complement with two separate blocks. The actual data frames agree at both stage boundaries. Three signed shears complete the interchange, so there are no positive-width data connectors or copied rank-one endpoint corrections. All three local words, arbitrary dirty cleanup, copied centers and auxiliary exteriors remain charged. The per-vertex rank deficit is `2v-3ell`, with `2v+3R` persistent roles.

The complex supplier adopts **eumemic**'s PR #117 h24 positive DAG, with 91,770 additions, 71,185 compatible carrier links and 28,705 auxiliary roles. A new Clifford frame theorem applies to every binary subspace, including degenerate intersections and partial gauges. Exact representatives use preimage Lagrangians; actual rank-zero adapters reconcile frames before scalar gates. The local verifier rebuilds full backward intersections and 4,599 source gauges, with readouts executed in reverse selection order.

The complex cover is `O(70,2)`. Its full order, finite routers and scalar operations remain in the semantic certificate. The per-vertex inventory has 90,163 roles, rank 6,309,018 and deficit 2,392. The strict complex saving is `786999/2500000000`, with moment gap exceeding `2.3047018455e-10`. Exact denominator-21 decoding and the completed-child `C1=1` contract are retained.

The bit supplier uses the unchanged **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)** PR #97 physical ledger based on **Swapnil Jain**'s witness. Its dimension is 67. A finite `GL_67(Z/q^w)` cover batches high matrix digits by fixed low-residue types. Unit-lower factorization leaves variable pivot units inside weighted reversed children. Nongeneric classes receive a full local-ring Gaussian fallback of at most `32m^2` proper children; its entire extra moment is charged on a fraction `10^-16` of every ideal edge. The coarse saving is `747/2000000`, with certified contaminated gap exceeding `6.3397366396e-7`; stopping gives ordinary bit saving `3731649599/10000000000000`.

The bit selector stock occupies `O(w log e)` original address digits and is restored by an explicit outer ordinary-interchange wrapper. Its uniform batching, weighted leaves, fallback, atom adapters, borrowed-row restoration and binary padding are included in the proof. The complex and conservative legacy reserves use external stock `p^160000`, with coefficient 68,505. All 47 strict constraints and seven assembly margins hold, with final absorption gap exceeding `3.4173577301e-12`.

prs.title: Paired lockstep first-stage vertices on three-stage covers: conditional κ = 3.416202e-4
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Conditional κ = 1708101/5000000000 = **3.416202e-4**: **+8.59% over #130** (3.146011e-4) and **+2.83% over #131** (3.32205398986e-4). It builds on #130 (head 6a9970a530119174507904e23592fd59ede19a5d, included in this branch) and keeps all of its interfaces. The complex side binds; the next κ grid point at denominator 10^10 is rejected.

**Idea: share and run in lockstep.** In #130's first stage the offset is 0, so a core occupies only its 24-dimensional active space kA of the 70-dimensional cover space E. Let κ be the coordinate involution exchanging e_i and e_(24+i) for i < 24. It is orthogonal, κ² = 1 and κA ⊂ B + C, so kA and (kκ)A are orthogonal for every vertex k. Pair the first-stage vertices k and kκ:

- the two cores share every auxiliary stream (each acts block-diagonally on its own directions and accepts the other's as spectators, as in #128's completed-core sharing);
- they run the same first-stage word in lockstep, so each joint frame step U₁⊕U₂ → U₁′⊕U₂′ is one nested transition, hence **one child** of width d₁ + d₂ by #130's general Clifford lemma (valid for degenerate subspaces too), instead of two children;
- the shared dirty tail has rank m − 2h + 2 dim σ instead of two tails of m − h + dim σ.

Stages two and three carry the offsets kB and k(B + C), which leave no orthogonal room, so they stay as in #130. All data streams, routers, partitions and the bit side are #130's, unchanged.

| per pair of vertices | #130 | here |
|---|---:|---:|
| persistent streams | 180,326 | 151,621 |
| complex saving | 3.147997e-4 | **3.418543e-4** |
| stopped bit saving | 3.731650e-4 | unchanged |
| κ | 3.146011e-4 | **3.416202e-4** |

The same lockstep principle applies wherever identical cores share streams on orthogonal subspaces. On #128/#129's completed-core groups (24 complex or 11 bit cores per stream) it raises κ from 1.29186e-4 to 2.05734e-4 (branch `ikeboy:research/lockstep-cores`, not opened as a PR because #130 is higher).

## Validation

**Finite checks** (`research/paired-cover/paired_cover.py`, seconds):

- #130's `three-stage-cover-complex-input.json` and `three-stage-cover-network.json` pinned by SHA-256;
- the unpaired per-vertex profile rebuilt from the input equals #130's certified children;
- κ is an orthogonal involution with κA ⊆ B + C;
- the paired profile telescopes (W·m − s = 2(2v − 3ℓ) per pair; largest child 68 < 70);
- the complex saving is the largest on the 10^-10 grid under #104's exact moment (next point rejected);
- the bit saving is #130's certified stopped saving;
- the finite bridge is #130's construction with the paired stream count (group order, local and router charges, semantic induction, row stock p^160000); all 47 strict constraints and 7 margins hold at κ, and the next κ is rejected.

**Proof arguments, not machine-checked here:** the lockstep schedule, the spectator sharing of first-stage streams and the shared tail (`research/paired-cover/PROOF.md` §3–§4), which use #130's general Clifford lemma and dirty-tail formula and #128's sharing argument. All of #130's inherited hypotheses remain.

```sh
python3 research/paired-cover/paired_cover.py
```

- **icekylinx**: the three-stage Cayley cover, general Clifford frames and weighted bit interface (#130); the stopped product-ring framework (#104).
- **an664**: completed-core sharing (#128). **eumemic**: #117's local DAG, #129, #131.
- **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)**: #97's bit ledger. **Swapnil Jain**: the round-seven bit witness.
- Everyone credited in #130's NOTICE and SOURCES.json.

Avi Eisenberg (ikeboy) prepared the pairing, the lockstep schedule and this certificate with Anthropic Claude assistance.

## Summary

Extends the [`research/cyclic-deferred`](research/cyclic-deferred/README.md) package on top of **eumemic**'s PR #117 complex DAG (`inputs/complex-dag.json.gz`, retained byte-for-byte with SHA-256 `3c034d0aae388ef567a454826f4f48b26fd8a94c71e8ffed4835271b349a783b`) and PR #114's saturated-frame / literal reflection audit package, advancing the conditional exponent saving from PR #114's $\kappa = 1.09281094468 \times 10^{-4}$ (`109281094468 / 10^15`) to:

$$\kappa = 1.11513943837 \times 10^{-4} = \frac{111513943837}{10^{15}} > 2^{-14}$$

with complex saving:

$$a_{\text{complex}} = \frac{111538935}{10^{12}} = 1.11538935 \times 10^{-4}$$

(+2,233,838 grid points on $a_{\text{complex}}$ over PR #114's `109305097 / 10^12`, and +6.72% over PR #117's $\kappa = 1.044939 \times 10^{-4}$). Supersedes PR #114, PR #117, PR #118, and PR #120 while preserving all physical ledgers, literal forward/reflected scalar-charge audits, and upstream attributions.

Also fixes a bug in PR #114's `research/cyclic-deferred/complex_deferred.py` (line 557 wrote `json.dumps(out, indent=1)` instead of `indent=2`, causing `verify.py` to fail in `test_controls.py` with `Source hash mismatch: complex-profile.json` after regeneration).

---

## Technical Contributions

All four improvements operate purely on the $\mathbb{F}_2$ frame assignment, role-compilation schedule, and deferred readout selection on the unchanged PR #117 graph ($h = 24, v = 2024, c = 91770, q = 8120, \text{links} = 71185, R = 28705, W = 124390992, \text{total\_rank} = 71647349312$):

1. **Radical-Complement Initial Frame Lifting (`U2`)**:
   - In PR #114, whenever the top-down orthogonal kernel intersection $W_x = \ker(K_x) \cap \bigcap_{t \in \text{succ}(x)} U_t$ at an addition node $x$ had a non-zero symplectic radical, `U[x]` was dropped all the way down to the elementary label envelope $E_x = \text{envelope}(x)$ (dropping 51,781 of the 91,770 addition nodes).
   - Because $E_x \subseteq W_x$ is always nondegenerate over $\mathbb{F}_2$, we decompose $W_x = E_x \oplus (W_x \cap E_x^\perp)$ and extract a maximal nondegenerate direct complement $C_x = \text{sat\_nonsingular\_part}(W_x \cap E_x^\perp)$, setting $U_x = E_x \oplus C_x$. This keeps $E_x \subseteq U_x \subseteq W_x$ nondegenerate and nested while lifting 69,450 addition nodes prior to placement and expanding initial copy-role candidate subspaces.

2. **Phase-Aware Role Compilation & Target-Reach Sacrifice Ordering**:
   - In the role compiler, a copy role $f$ created by `('copy', piv, f, x)` at node $x$ is dragged into Phase 1 (`touched`) whenever `piv` is subsequently touched by a Phase-1 operation (either via a later copy at $x$ or via `free[0]` at a descendant of $x$).
   - Partitioning `free(x)` into centre-reaching uses (`yes_c`) and non-centre-reaching uses (`non_c`), assigning `k0 = non_c[0]` (chosen as the use in `non_c` with the largest target reach $|\text{u\_reach}|$) to `piv`, emitting `yes_c` copies first, and emitting `non_c[1:]` copies last (after all Phase-1 operations on `piv` at $x$):
     - Reduces `phase_one_ops` from `18,844` to **`16,353`** (`-2,491`),
     - Reduces `phase_one_roles` (`touched`) from `13,555` to **`11,064`** (`-2,491`),
     - Expands copy-role deferral candidates from `6,385` to **`8,876`** (`+39.0%`), and
     - Cuts the mean target reach of copy-role candidates in half from `8.67` to **`4.36`**.

3. **Lazy Effective-Target Placement & Exact-Moment Local Search**:
   - Replaces static one-shot candidate ordering with a lazy priority queue weighted by $2^{\dim(X)} / (r \cdot r_{\text{eff}})$, where $r_{\text{eff}}(s, X) = |\{t \in \text{reach}(s) : X \notin \text{byT\_set}[t]\}|$ counts targets not already carrying the exact subspace $X$, re-inserting candidates whenever intersection shrinks $\dim(X)$ or $r_{\text{eff}}$.
   - Follows placement with cached steepest-ascent local search under the exact moment objective, pruning or snapping down net-negative singleton and small-cluster target-front levels (`4,464` deferred roles retained with total dimension `59,912`).

4. **Bidirectional & Plateau-Peeling Frame Sweeps (`optimize_U_for_placed`)**:
   - For any role $s$, the internal steps along `holds[s]` partition $h - \dim(\sigma_s)$ into positive increments $\Delta_i$. Since $t \mapsto t \ln(m/t)$ is strictly concave (subadditive), intermediate steps strictly between adjacent frames split one larger step into smaller steps and increase the moment.
   - Alternating bottom-up and top-down sweeps over $U_x \in [L_x, W_x]$ with directional $\Delta c = 0$ tie-breaking and connected-component plateau peeling collapses redundant intermediate role-chain steps while maintaining all $\mathbb{F}_2$ nondegeneracy and nesting invariants.

**Draft:** the focused target passes locally (Python 3.11) and the regenerated files are byte-identical. I'll mark this ready once fork CI passes.

Under #130's and #132's retained hypotheses,

**κ = 174051/500000000 = 3.481020×10⁻⁴**, **+1.897% over #132** (3.416202e-4), +4.79% over #131 and +10.65% over #130. The complex side binds; the next κ grid point at denominator 10¹⁰ is rejected.

**Idea.** #130 sets every local complex frame to its full backward intersection, the largest admissible frame. #130's own general Clifford lemma prices any nested pair U ⊆ V of binary subspaces, including degenerate ones, as one child of width dim V − dim U. So a smaller frame is also admissible if three conditions hold:
- it contains the node's label and every predecessor frame;
- it lies inside the full backward intersection;
- it is nested in every successor frame.

One forward pass replaces a frame by that minimal span whenever the local one-child cost t·log(m/t), with m = 70, decreases. Because t·log(m/t) is subadditive, merging increments a and b into a+b is cheaper. This is the shrunk-frame pass from #125, moved to #130's cover. It shrinks 15,697 frames, and #130's unrestricted selection then keeps 4,553 source gauges.

| complex local word | #130 frames | shrunk frames |
|---|---:|---:|
| unpaired (#130 cover) | 3.147998e-4 | 3.202924e-4 |
| paired lockstep (#132) | 3.418543e-4 | **3.483450e-4** (69669/2·10⁸) |
| κ | 3.416202e-4 (#132) | **3.481020e-4** |

**Checks.** Run `make shrunk-paired-cover-verify`; it is added to the `verify` workflow matrix.
- `producer.py` is #130's producer with `lift_shrunk.py`. It regenerates #117's pinned DAG, the C++ carrier matching, the physical word and the gauge selection, and requires agreement with the frozen `complex-input.json`.
- `verify_shrunk.py` is #130's complete verifier with **one assertion changed**: a frame must be *contained in* its full backward intersection rather than *equal* to it. Everything else passes unchanged:
  - exact supports and divisor 21;
  - labels contained in frames;
  - dependency and carrier nesting;
  - 236,902 replayed physical frame transitions;
  - histogram recount;
  - full incident source gauges;
  - reverse readout chains.
- **Control:** the producer also runs #130's **unmodified** verifier on the same data. It must reject the frames, and only with `Not the full backward intersection`, so every check before that assertion passes in #130's original code too.
- `certificate.py` is #132's paired certificate on the new inventory: exact moment, finite bridge, 47 strict constraints, 7 margins and next-grid rejection. It also requires the unpaired shrunk saving to exceed #130's.

**Scope.** This is a finite conditional witness. #132's lockstep and sharing arguments and #130's cover, bit interface and inherited analytic/tape interfaces remain assumptions, as stated in those PRs. That smaller frames are admissible follows from #130's lemma, which never uses frame maximality. Nothing here is a runtime or implementation claim.

**Composability.** The pass is independent of #131's scratch reuse. It may compose with #131 plus #132; that combination has not been tested.

**Credits:** icekylinx (#130 covers, Clifford frames, producer and verifier); Avi Eisenberg/ikeboy (#132 lockstep, Anthropic Claude assistance); eumemic (#117 DAG, #131); an664 (#128); Swapnil Jain and Zhihao Chen (bit word); all inherited contributors. The shrunk-frame pass and this composition were prepared by Joel Pulikkan with Anthropic Claude assistance.

This extends my [PR #130](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/130) at `6a9970a530119174507904e23592fd59ede19a5d`, with one new commit. The #10 → #18 → #24 → #32 → merged #36 → #104 → #115 → #130 proof lineage and attributed ordinary-leaf, semantic/bulk, uniform-recursion and fixed-tape interfaces are retained.

Under the retained multiplication framework and those analytic/tape interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{4609169}{10000000000}=4.609169\times10^{-4}.
$$

## Construction

The new complex local motif uses twelve coordinate pairs and 1,760 ports grouped into eight-port cubes. Its scalar identity is `I=K+H+B`: signed overlap channels supply H, coordinate-star centers supply B, and two 4-by-4 Hadamard/2 blocks per cube supply the involution K. All heavy source injections precede K. The original source registers execute K at a common rank-three frame, deliver their assigned contributions, and undo K at the full frame before scalar cleanup. This adds no K auxiliary bank.

The selected signed DAG has 24,767 additions, 7,724 root uses, 6,074 compatible carrier arcs and 26,417 auxiliary roles. Its 24 coordinate-star frames have rank 22, with copied-center loss 528. The chronological program retains 4,840 entrance gauges of rank 20. Conservative source supports include all visited directions; scalar cancellation is not used to shrink frames.

The global architecture adopts **an664**'s PR #128 completed-core sharing principle. The new cross-stage routing reuses one auxiliary bank successively in three orthogonal h-blocks. Each core includes the complete arbitrary-dirty scalar cleanup and excludes its old independent-bank exterior tail. Exact forward and inverse core actions justify one final correction of width `3 dim(sigma)` for each selected role. Both data banks also pay their rank-two complement calls. Every local operation, copied center and sharing router remains charged.

The complex shared profile has dimension 72, 29,937 roles per cover vertex, rank 2,153,528 and deficit 1,936. Its strict saving is `4856569/10000000000`, with moment gap exceeding `2.0094617553e-10`. The full `O(72,2)` group has 2,556 bits; the actual role stock has 2,571 bits and the maximum child is 60.

The bit branch retains the PR #97 / Swapnil word and original rational frames. It keeps 9,543 certified entrance gauges and omits 2,022. Omitted dirty reads move to the initial zero frame; all later ordinary operations and source frames remain inherited, and retained target chains are certified subsequences. The dimension-69 shared profile has 32,408 roles, rank 2,234,128 and deficit 2,024. The strict coarse saving is `4617656/10000000000`; the full rare-class fallback is charged with moment gap exceeding `1.4386017949e-10`. The stopped ordinary saving is `4613422943/10000000000000`.

The finite guard pays all signed mixer operations, direct dirty reads, original-source involutions and sharing permutations. A numerator-bitlength bound handles the full dirty-response matrix without a positivity assumption. Coordinate-star decoding uses divisor three on one exact grid, retaining completed-child `C1=1`. The external reserve is `p^70000`, with coefficient 20,445; q-adic selectors remain internally borrowed and restored. All 47 strict constraints and seven margins hold, with final absorption gap exceeding `9.9454090434e-11`.

prs.body:
## Summary

This PR composes and optimizes **physical gate frames and compensated birth-cut scratch reuse** (`research/cover-local-reuse`, PR #131) with **paired first-stage lockstep vertices** (PR #132) and **radical-complement frame lifting, phase-aware role compilation, donor-chain shrinking, and recipient frame snapping** (PR #133) under PR #130's three-stage Cayley cover (`m = 3h - 2 = 70`).

Both the **unpaired** three-stage cover certificate and the **paired first-stage lockstep** three-stage cover certificate are generated and verified in `research/cover-local-reuse/certificate.json`:

| Construction | Physical roles $R$ | Streams (per vertex / pair) | Complex saving | Certified $\kappa$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PR #130 (`icekylinx`, unpaired baseline) | $28,705$ | $90,163$ / vertex | $3.147997 \times 10^{-4}$ | $3.146011 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| PR #131 (`eumemic`, unpaired + local reuse) | $26,597$ | $83,839$ / vertex | $3.32426609 \times 10^{-4}$ | $3.32205398986 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| **This PR (unpaired + optimized local reuse)** | **$26,549$** | **$83,695$ / vertex** | **$3.37774769 \times 10^{-4}$** (`337774769/10^12`) | **$3.37546392004 \times 10^{-4}$** (`84386598001/250000000000000`) |
| PR #132 (`ikeboy`, paired Stage-1 lockstep) | $28,705$ | $151,621$ / pair | $3.418543 \times 10^{-4}$ | $3.416202 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| PR #134 (`GamingPuzzled`, paired + shrunk frames) | $28,705$ | $151,621$ / pair | $3.483450 \times 10^{-4}$ | $3.481020 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| **This PR (paired Stage-1 lockstep + optimized local reuse)** | **$26,549$** | **$140,841$ / pair** | **$3.68824652 \times 10^{-4}$** (`92206163/250000000000`) | **$3.68552409947 \times 10^{-4}$** (`368552409947/10^15`) |

## Key Technical Contributions

1. **Radical-complement frame lifting and phase-aware role compilation (`research/cyclic-deferred/complex_deferred.py`)**:
   - Whenever $\ker(K[x])$ is degenerate over $\mathbb{F}_2^{24}$, $U[x]$ is lifted to the maximal nondegenerate subspace $L \oplus \text{nonsingular}(W \cap L^\perp)$ containing the node envelope ($69,450$ lifted nodes).
   - At fan-out nodes ($\text{len}(\text{free}) > 1$), phase-1 uses in `Anc` are assigned to copy roles while keeping a phase-2 use on the pivot role. Because phase-1 donor eligibility (`i in Anc and a not in role_root`) is a topological invariant of the unlinked DAG nodes in the backward closure of the 24 center roots, this preserves all $2,351$ phase-1 donor roles while expanding phase-2 copy candidates and halving mean target reach.
2. **Cover-weighted local search, targeted donor-chain shrinking, and recipient frame snapping (`complex_deferred.py`, `reuse.py`)**:
   - Deferred birth gauges ($3,558$ roles) and physical mixer gate frames are optimized under the exact $m = 70$ cover moment weights.
   - Targeted minimal nondegenerate hull shrinking (`frame_smallest_hull`) along the ancestor chains of unmatched phase-1 donors increases compensated birth-cut reuses from $2,108$ to **$2,156$**, reducing physical scratch roles from $28,705$ to **$26,549$** ($744$ distinct physical source frames, $1,402$ nonzero source gauges).
   - In `select_reuse`, birth frames are prioritized by `(len(F), capacity[F], F)` and within each frame by `len(op_frames[first[b]]) - len(F)`. Split recipient birth frames ($e < f < d_1$) are then snapped toward their matched donor frame $A$ when profitable under the combined auxiliary and target moment objective, eliminating intermediate transition steps $f - e$.
3. **Per-bank literal reflection audit and Stage-1 pairing geometry checks (`reflection_audit.py`, `geometry_checks.py`, `certificate.py`, `test_controls.py`)**:
   - `framescan` in `reflection_audit.py` independently audits `source_data_histogram`, `target_data_histogram`, and `internal_role_histogram` across the source ($0 \le s < v$), target ($v \le s < 2v$), and physical auxiliary ($s \ge 2v$) port banks on both the literal chronological forward word and its complemented reflection.
   - `geometry_checks.py` verifies the Stage-1 coordinate involution $\kappa_{\text{inv}}$ ($e_i \leftrightarrow e_{24+i}$ for $i < 24$ on $E = A \perp B \perp C$, mapping $A$ into $B \oplus C \perp A$) across all $2,024$ actual $h=24$ triple ports.
   - `test_controls.py` expands the negative-control suite to 18 tests, verifying both unpaired ($2,392$) and paired ($4,784$) telescoping deficits and rejecting corrupted internal-role or target-data histograms.

## Verification

```sh
python3 -B research/cover-local-reuse/verify.py
```

Runs the full isolated temporary-directory regeneration of `complex_deferred.py`, `reflection_audit.py`, `geometry_checks.py`, `certificate.py`, and all 18 negative controls in `test_controls.py` with assertions enabled.
