prs.title: Composed diagonal-bit bootstrap: the pricing model that called PR205's banked row, audits the queue, and prices the next ladder of κ gains
prs.body:
Under the retained interfaces of the pinned suppliers, this composes **#200**'s
certified bit supplier with **#193/#194**'s complex word through **#194**'s
unchanged assembly and prices it with **#185**'s finite ordinary leaf:

$$\kappa=\frac{1693287}{2500000000}=6.773148\cdot10^{-4},$$

**+0.1826%** over #197's standing claim and **+0.0639%** over the composition as
#202 published it. Adds `research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/` and one
workflow. The package now does three things: prices this composition, **audits the
banked rows that overtook it**, and **prices the ladder of moves that can still
raise kappa**.

## The banked rows arrived, and this package's model called one exactly

This composition was priced at 15:33 UTC. Its lever model then predicted what
banking this word's 2,200 rank-60 exterior corrections would be worth — a row with
`W_per_vertex = 56402/3`, deficit unchanged at 1,936, no rank-60 child left and
coarse saving `683528191056257/10^18`. Within the half hour that row was built and
opened as #205, which states that exact saving and credits this PR as its target;
#206 prices the same row with PR186's entrance banks, and #207 adds 302
coordinated frame changes on top:

| PR | author | kappa | row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#207** | Dugongue | **6.831904550365e-4** | the banked word after 302 coordinated frame changes; current frontier |
| #205 | rohanarun | 6.83061299399923e-4 | PR200's word with its rank-60 exterior corrections banked — the value modelled here |
| #206 | EcmaXp | 6.830611e-4 | the same row via PR186's entrance banks |
| #202 | chafreaky | 6.768823e-4 | the same composition as this PR with the legacy atom wrapper |
| #197 | evmckinney9 | 6.76080316519385e-4 | packed #187's residuals + #193 complex + the finite leaf |
| this | Maxime Fleury | 6.773148e-4 | #200's bit + #193's complex + #185's finite leaf on #194's assembly |

`audit.py` prices #205's, #206's and #207's rows from byte-identical copies of
their certificates under `references/queue/` and requires each result to appear
**verbatim** in the certificate it came from. All three reproduce to the last
digit, and each sits at its own word's ceiling: with the bit branch binding,
`kappa = C/(1+C)` and there is no pricing room left in any of them.

## New ways to raise kappa, priced

PR184's assembly takes `a = min(bit leaf, (1-1e-9)*C_complex - 1e-10)` and returns
`kappa = a/(1+a)` on the `10^-10` grid, so **the smaller branch is the whole
constraint** and a gain on the stronger side is worth nothing until the other side
catches up. Today the bit branch binds at `6.831904e-4` while the complex side caps
at `7.004273e-4`: **+2.52% is available with no complex-side work at all.**

`targets.py` prices the moves that get there. For a fixed stock and deficit the
coarse saving is `C = (1 - mass/(W m)) / L` with `L` the rank-mass-weighted mean of
`ln(m/r)`, so the lever is `L`: a ledger whose residual dirt sits in fewer, larger
children. Soaking every child of rank at or below a threshold into the largest
admissible child gives, on the queue's own rows:

| soak | bit coarse saving | complex coarse saving | kappa | gain | binds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| today | 136731504666219/2e17 | 350459221139329/5e17 | 6.831904e-4 | — | bit |
| bit only, rank-1 | 792978386838687/10^18 | — | 7.004273e-4 | +2.52% | complex |
| both, rank-1 | 792978386838687/10^18 | 814442339516203/10^18 | 7.923515e-4 | +15.98% | bit |
| both, rank-2 | 898167154125293/10^18 | 918515942111545/10^18 | 8.973611e-4 | +31.35% | bit |
| both, rank-3 | 981391149202381/10^18 | 1041436537175764/10^18 | 9.804289e-4 | +43.51% | bit |
| both, rank-4 | 1015042828910707/10^18 | 1112905588874264/10^18 | 1.014014e-3 | +48.42% | bit |
| both, rank-8 | 1096975618911405/10^18 | 1243672552482743/10^18 | 1.095774e-3 | +60.39% | bit |
| both, rank-16 | 1178908992537918/10^18 | 1367642974340202/10^18 | 1.177521e-3 | +72.36% | bit |
| cheapest ledgers | 1207154248293627/10^18 | 1391081382485139/10^18 | 1.205699e-3 | +76.48% | — |

The cheapest step is smaller than the table suggests. The bit word needs a coarse
saving of `7.009184e-4` to stop binding, and `targets.py` bisects the smallest-child
population to find the least that delivers it: **moving 57/1000 of the mass in the
bit word's rank-1 children into rank-22 children takes its coarse saving to
`7.009717e-4`**, past the complex word, for `kappa = 7.004273e-4` (+2.52%). The whole
population (377,316 rank-1 children, 9.3% of the rank mass) is worth +16% on its own,
and the complex word's own 87,534 rank-1 children (11% of its mass) do the same for
its side, `7.009184e-4` to `8.144423e-4` (+16.2%).

**What has to change is the child inventory, not the packing.** #207's bank proof
settles the packing side itself: its banks tile width 72 exactly with the word's two
residual families (`6 x rank-4 + 2 x rank-24`, or `3 x rank-24`), and it states that
the current word "has exactly the 4/24 residual families and both tile 72 exactly ...
there is no new LP improvement to add". The children the moment actually charges are
the word's own retained children — internal, source, target, center, compensating and
terminal-substitution children — and it is their inventory, set by the weighted
compilation and by the frame schedule, that holds `L` above `ln(m/22)`.


**All of it is MODELLED, NOT CONSTRUCTED**: no ledger is built here, and each rung
is a shape the assembly would price this way, computed from the queue's certified
rows. The calculator is checked two ways — it equals PR184's own `assemble()` on the
vendored pair, and it reproduces #205's and #207's published kappa to within one
grid step — so a rung is a usable target, in the same way the banked row was.

## What the composition itself does

Exactly one operation: **pricing**. #200 certified a strictly stronger bit word —
coarse saving `677773948354561/10^18 = 6.77773948355e-4` against #189's
`6.68298937775631e-4` — but published it only with its own complex word, where the
complex branch binds. Composed with the source-assisted complex word
(`219037/312500000 = 7.009184e-4`) the bit branch binds, and PR185's wrapper then
removes the `4.33e-7` of slack PR184's legacy leaf leaves below the coarse saving:

| depth | bit leaf | kappa | vs #197 | vs the unbootstrapped composition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 (legacy wrapper, = #200's and #202's value) | 6.77340866500955e-4 | 6768823/10000000000 = 6.768823e-4 | +0.1186% | — |
| 1 | 6.77773606501196e-4 | 1354629/2000000000 = 6.773145e-4 | +0.1825% | +0.0639% |
| 2, 3, 8 | 6.77773899999987e-4 | **1693287/2500000000 = 6.773148e-4** | **+0.1826%** | +0.0639% |

The priced bit profile has `m = 72`, `W = 20634`, rank deficit 1936 and 34 terminal
sinks; the claim sits **3.37e-11** below the word's own ceiling
`C/(1+C) = 6.7731483368e-4`, under one `10^-10` selection step, with depths 2, 3 and
8 returning the same grid value. The bit profile, the complex word, the 47-constraint
assembly and the leaf recurrence are the suppliers' and #185's; nothing is re-derived.

`levers.py` is the model behind all of this: it solves the paid-moment inequality
exactly over the rationals and checks itself against three published values, all
reproduced **exactly** because it prices with PR200's own enclosure module
(`references/pr200/interval_moment.py`, vendored byte-identically):

| row | W | D | model = published | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR187's word, unpacked | 63,324 | 5,808 | 167724995262213/250000000000000000 = 6.70899981048852e-4 | PR187's certificate |
| PR187's word, banked | 57,824 | 5,808 | 676537710350481/10^18 = 6.76537710350481e-4 | #197's **certified** packed word |
| PR200's word, unpacked | 61,902 | 5,808 | 677773948354561/10^18 = 6.77773948354561e-4 | #200's certificate |

## Verification

```bash
python3 -B research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/verify.py
```

Runs from the package directory alone with only the standard library, on Python
3.11 and 3.13, and pins every byte against `SOURCE.json`. It checks that the
certificate regenerates exactly; that depth 0 equals #200's and #202's value; that
PR184's grid legacy leaf against #200's published atom wrapper differs by exactly
one grid step at depth 0 and nothing once bootstrapped; that the claim beats #197
and sits inside one grid step of `C/(1+C)`; that the leaf tolls hold in closed form
and the assembly's own minimum margin excludes the next grid point; that three
corruption controls are refused; that the lever model reproduces its three
published references exactly; **that the audit reproduces #205's, #206's and #207's
own certified coarse savings verbatim**; and **that the target ladder reproduces two
published kappa values, stays monotone and never presents itself as a
construction**. A clean Linux clone of the branch passes and leaves the tree
unchanged; the whole harness runs in about seven seconds.

## Scope and limits

* The physical complex and bit words, their frames, sinks and paid moments are the
  suppliers' certified artifacts, vendored byte-identically and **priced, not
  rebuilt or replayed**. This PR does not re-run their checks, including #205's,
  #206's and #207's: it prices the rows they certify.
* The wrapper is PR185's construction, not one built here; the banked rows are
  #205's, #206's and #207's, not built here; every rung of the ladder is a target,
  not a construction.
* Conditional on PR184's finite bridge and closed-form acceptance arithmetic and on
  the retained contracts of the pinned suppliers. The full multiplication theorem
  remains conditional.
* Dependent on unmerged lines (#200's bit supplier, the #193/#194 complex/assembly
  line, and the #205/#206/#207 bank line).
* Not claimed: a new word, a new all-size hypothesis, priority, or the frontier.
  The frontier belongs to the banked rows above.

## Credits

Bit supplier and the #189/#196 lineage: **chafreaky** (#200, #202), whose enclosure
module this PR vendors and prices with. Banked rows: **rohanarun** (#205, and #197's
packing mechanism this PR models), **EcmaXp** (#206), **Dugongue** (#207, with
PR186's entrance banks). Complex word, pricing and assembly: **icekylinx**,
**GPT-6 Astra** and **ikeboy** (#182/#184/#193/#194). Finite ordinary-leaf wrapper
and recurrence: **rohanarun** (#185). Paired-cube frame, balanced prefix and the 47
constraints: **eumemic** (#168 v4), with the RaD (hipotures) balanced transform and
Zhihao Chen's PR23 gates. The descent figure is **sennemmi**'s (#198); the design
ceiling is **DaysSky**'s (#201); the supplier barriers are **huxint**'s (#203).
Prepared by Maxime Fleury with Codebuff assistance; Apache-2.0; predecessor notices
retained in the package `NOTICE.md`.

prs.title: Pack PR200 diagonal bit residuals into completed banks (conditional κ = 0.000683061299399923)
prs.body:
## Construction

Apply PR197’s completed-bank packing to PR200’s emitted diagonal bit word, retaining PR193’s complex supplier. The committed certificate reports conditional κ = 683061299399923/10^18 = **0.000683061299399923**, approximately **0.913% above PR202** and matching the target modelled in PR204.

The package constructs exact charts for 220 distinct rank-20 gauge frames and 45,842 rank-72 banks, with a checked 9-edge-colouring of 154,026 incidences. Three copies retain PR200’s recounted profile while removing 6,600 rank-60 exterior children: W = 56,402, deficit = 5,808, maximum child = 22. The stated additional routing bound is 5,368,513,266 selector calls. Three finite ordinary-leaf levels feed the unchanged balanced 47-constraint assembly; the bit branch binds.

## Validation status

**All 57 CI jobs passed** for research head `95c58706ad231d532bd7038308946a0344d08186`:

- [Full packed-diagonal verifier](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37954253466): both pinned inherited verifiers, exact chart and bank reconstruction, two moment engines, finite leaf composition, 47 constraints, seven margins and adverse controls; reproduced conditional κ = `683061299399923/1000000000000000000`. Postrun `git diff --exit-code` passed.
- [Repository verification](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37954253460): all 52 jobs passed, covering 16 groups on Python 3.11/3.13/3.14, three formal jobs and the ranked-pair finite check.
- [Terminal elimination](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37954253425) and [recycled registers](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/37954253513): two Python versions each, all passed.

The tested PR merge commit `199f718ade945c99dcfae748267065a471aa40b0` and research head have identical Git tree `9bed149ad5c93a9a6a4a3d68001c32167adfdf9b`. All four run logs were exported, SHA-256 recorded, ZIP integrity checked and job coverage audited. Verification was executed by GitHub Actions; these results were independently inspected without rerunning passed tests.

The full workflow pins PR200 at `a1175449f34d39ff933d9d8ab23ced1f32b290ec` and PR193 at `187e1010ac8b259af8e9b5166f68b64bc27b4b47`. No external sandbox was allocated, so no sandbox cleanup remains.

## Scope and attribution

This remains a conditional finite construction under inherited completed-core, Clifford, weighted-compilation, analytic/precision, restored-row and fixed-tape interfaces. It is not an unconditional multiplication theorem or practical speedup claim; PR193’s complex-side limitations remain.

Credit: Evan McKinney (PR197 packing and reused/adapted code), Chafik Boukhalfa (PR200 bit word), Avi Eisenberg (PR193 complex supplier), icekylinx (source-assisted method), maxime-fleury (PR204 target), eumemic and the PR168 lineage, and PR185/187 finite leaf composition. The branch was prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance; Apache-2.0 attribution is retained in NOTICE.

prs.title: Completed entrance banks on PR200's bit word with the v4 complex supplier: kappa = 6.830611e-4
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This PR applies PR186's completed entrance banks to PR200's physical bit word and prices the result against the v4 source-assisted complex supplier, as composed in PR202. The new package is `research/pr200-entrance-banks/`.

**κ = 6830611/10^10 ≈ 6.830611e-4.** That is +0.913% over PR202 (6768823/10^10) and +2.342% over PR194. Without the finite leaf, κ = 6826211/10^10. The bit supplier still binds; the complex saving is 219037/312500000 ≈ 7.009184e-4.

| Bit supplier, per group vertex | PR200 word | With completed banks |
|---|---:|---:|
| Live physical chains | 17,114 | 17,114 |
| Persistent stock W | 20,634 | 56402/3 |
| Rank mass | 1,483,712 | 1,351,712 |
| Deficit | 1,936 | 1,936 |
| Largest child | 60 | 22 |
| Coarse saving (10^-18 grid) | 677773948354561/10^18 | 683528191056257/10^18 |

**Construction:**

- **Packing:** PR186's stage-private packing, with 18 × rank-4 entrance residuals or 3 × rank-24 completed residuals per width-72 bank and nine physical replicas. It removes the 2,200 rank-60 entrance exteriors. Per stage there are 1,100 entrance banks and 44,742 completed banks.
- **Schedule:** the round-8 `BANK-SCHEDULE.md` supplement.
- **Sinks:** PR200 deletes 34 terminal sinks, and a deleted sink has no register to bank. The live chains are 18,908 − 1,760 splices − 34 sinks = 17,114.
- **Charts:** exact integer charts for PR200's 220 entrance frames, built with PR197's `inverse_integer`. Every entry and denominator is at most 18. Charts for distinct slots of one bank differ by a nonzero integer matrix with entries below 2^80. So no prime q > 2^80 identifies two charts of one group, which discharges the round-8 prime exclusion for these charts.
- **Pricing:** PR186's paid moment, PR184's unchanged `select()` and 47-constraint `assemble()`, and PR185's 3-level finite leaf, composed as in PR199.

**Separate commit:** PR202's `research/source-assisted-v4/certificate.json` was written off Linux. Its gzip-dependent lift hashes therefore failed PR202's own workflow ("Canonical certificate does not reproduce"). Regenerated on amd64 Ubuntu 24.04 with Python 3.13, the hashes return to a8c8778's values and κ is unchanged. That commit also repins the single matching entry in PR200's `SOURCE.json`.

**Stacking:** this branch stacks on PR202, which stacks on PR194, so like those PRs it is not mergeable onto current `main`. PR200, PR202, PR197 and PR199 have no maintainer review yet.

**Scope:** a conditional finite witness. These stay inherited conditional contracts:

- from PR186 and the round-8 supplement: the bank routing, stage cover and low-residue streaming;
- from PR184: the weighted compiler, recovery, restored rows, fixed-tape routing and analytic transfer;
- the complex supplier keeps PR184's scope.

No optimality is claimed. `NOTICE` credits every borrowed piece. The package's files under `references/` are byte-identical upstream copies, and their commits and blob ids are in `references/manifest.json`.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/pr200-entrance-banks/verify.py [--full]` does the following:

- **Literal word:** reruns PR200's terminal prover on the literal sink-modified word. That covers all F2 and integer columns, both directions, with three mutation controls. It requires the result to equal PR200's certified profile.
- **Banks:** rebuilds the bank inventory and the exact charts, including factor replay to the identity and two-sided inverse checks.
- **Endpoints:** runs PR186's bank projector checks on 144 columns over F2 and Z, forward and reverse, rejecting omit and repeat. Also runs weighted endpoint checks over Z/9, Z/25 and Z/125, and the round-8 GL_2(Z/9) schedule diagnostic.
- **Pricing:** certifies the packed moment on the 10^-18 grid, with an independent base-two moment and the atom toll, then runs PR184's assembly with and without the leaf.
- **Controls:** reproduces PR202 (6768823/10^10) and PR199 (1693287/2500000000) from PR200's unpacked profile with the same code, and rejects five mutations.
- **Provenance:** recomputes every vendored file's git blob id, and checks the four ported PR186 functions are AST-identical to upstream.

Results:

- Passed with `--full` on amd64 Ubuntu 24.04 with Python 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14, and locally on macOS with Python 3.13.
- On the same Linux image, PR200's `verify.py` and v4's `verify.py` both pass after the certificate fix.
- The new workflow `.github/workflows/pr200-entrance-banks.yml` runs `verify.py --full` on that matrix and then `git diff --exit-code`.

These are finite certificate checks, not formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: Conditional kappa 6.831904550365e-4: coordinated frame optimization and completed entrance banks
prs.body:
Add `research/coordinated-crossover-pr200`, a finite supplier certificate and conditional assembly claiming

```
kappa = 1366380910073 / 2000000000000000
      = 0.0006831904550365.
```

This is approximately 0.0189% above the newly displayed [PR205](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/205) claim of 0.000683061299399923. PR205 also supplies a completed-bank construction on PR200; no exclusive originality is asserted for bank packing. The earlier comparison with PR204 was approximately +0.8675% and is now historical. It combines a new, explicitly paid bit supplier with the retained source-assisted complex supplier; component improvements are not added.

The bit construction starts from [PR200](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/200), pinned at `a1175449f34d39ff933d9d8ab23ced1f32b290ec`. Coordinated changes to 302 operation frames reduce the actual internal child histogram while keeping the source and target interfaces fixed. Completed entrance banks then replace the real rank-4 and rank-24 dirty residual completions with explicit coordinate partitions of width 72. Nine physical replicas make every bank full. Internal alias recipients, source births and deleted terminals are excluded from fresh bank allocation. Arbitrary incoming dirty contents and spectator fields are restored.

The resulting integer-normalized bit profile has width 72, stock 56,402, rank mass 4,055,136, deficit 5,808 and largest child 22. Its certified paid coarse saving is `136731504666219/200000000000000000`. The complex side uses [PR202](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/202), pinned at `8d8d67bcf69c5ea67d3a29dbc64ba588156d6e8d`, with saving `700918443859411/10^18`.

Exactly three stopped-leaf bootstrap levels are used, following [PR185](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/185) and [PR197](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/197). Each level calls only its predecessor for ordinary leaves and routing. The unattained limiting saving is not substituted. The final paired assembly uses eta = beta = 10^-24 and preserves the original strict scalar, router, row and recovery constraints.

## Validation and scope

The included verifier checks the actual finite frame/source/gauge chronology, the original and terminal-modified binary and defining integer columns, explicit bank assignments and inverses, frame prime witnesses, adverse controls, rational supplier moments, the finite ordinary-leaf recurrence and all 47 strict assembly inequalities. The next final 10^-18 grid point fails for these fixed suppliers and parameters; this does not assert global optimality.

The claimed consequence is conditional `T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1-kappa))` under the retained all-size interfaces. General Clifford/tensor realization, uniform weighted local-ring compilation, completed restored-row and fixed-tape leaf guarantees, paid routing/layout, prime supply, precision/recovery and analytic transfer remain disclosed conditions. A finite column replay and positive moment do not independently establish these conditions. This submission makes no new Lean-certification or practical-speedup claim.

Offline replay from the repository root uses Python 3.11+ with the pinned NumPy/SciPy requirements:

```sh
python -B research/coordinated-crossover-pr200/verify.py
```

An optional `--temp-root` chooses scratch storage. The replay never fetches sources. The bank chart/router bound `K = 21,900,544,398` remains paid through the ordinary routing toll and its strict exponent gap.

## Other routes tested

Shared-total/rank-two compensation saves 230 scalar additions but fails 260 actual target-cap membership checks. The integral 165-to-55 residual factor is exact, but its real paired-address features require ranks 19/20 and its outputs rank 20 against side caps of rank 18. Source-assisted rewrites also fail to improve this bit word: the full port lacks required donor stock at an actual vertex, the A0-only rewrite adds 440 rows, and the G12-only rewrite leaves the paid profile unchanged. None of these gains is credited.

## Sources

The package retains the pinned upstream sources and their license/attribution notices. It builds on the public PR200 physical bit construction, PR202 source-assisted complex construction, completed-bank work and finite-bootstrap argument. No files or claims were published by the local research process; this is a manually uploaded research addition.

prs.title: Price the bank-absorption ladder against the suppliers' own allocation rules: +2.17% needs a new residual type this word does not have (target, not built)
prs.body:
Stacked on #204: this branch contains that package, and these are its last three commits.

## The question this settles

The frontier is at its ceiling for every *pricing* move, so the only lever left is the child
**ledger**: absorbing a family into the banks drops its dirt and, by the row identity
`W = (mass + D)/m`, drops the stock with it. The open question in the previous revision was
what a bank requires of the family it absorbs. The suppliers' own bank proof answers it, and
it is **not** what I first assumed:

* **the absorbed family's rank is free.** #205/#206/#207 removed the 2,200 rank-60 entrance
  exteriors per vertex from a width-72 word, and 60 does not divide 72.
* the **absorbed volume must fill whole banks**: 396,000 registers over three copies,
  `396000 = 72 x 5500`.
* a bank's **blocks come from the word's residual families**, which must tile the width.
  `BANK-PROOF-PR200.md`: "allocate the 9*2,200 selected role-copy occurrences into 1,100 banks
  with 18 four-coordinate blocks" and "9*14,914 other occurrences into 44,742 banks with three
  24-coordinate blocks"; `retained-packing.py` also runs the mixed `6 x rank-4 + 2 x
  rank-24` pattern. The bit word's own families 4 and 24 tile 72 exactly.

## The claim, promoted

So the certified-shape ladder is the primary one. Priced with this package's exact model on
the queue's certified rows:

| rung | new residual types | bit word absorbs | complex word absorbs | kappa | gain | binds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| frontier (#207) | 0 | -- | -- | 213497/312500000 = 6.831904e-4 | -- | bit |
| **certified** | **1** | rank 22: 6,116 banks | -- | 7004273/10^10 = 7.004273e-4 | **+2.52%** | complex |
| certified | 2 | rank 22 | rank 11: 177 banks | 3541457/5e9 = 7.082914e-4 | **+3.67%** | complex |
| certified | 3 | rank 22 | ranks 1, 8 | 1819669/25e8 = 7.278676e-4 | **+6.54%** | bit |
| certified | 5 | ranks 1, 7, 21 | ranks 1, 8 | 4583099/5e9 = 9.166198e-4 | **+34.17%** | complex |
| certified | 8 | ranks 1, 3, 13, 21 | ranks 1, 2, 3, 9 | 3066221/25e8 = 1.226488e-3 | **+79.52%** | bit |

A **single new residual type reaches +2.52%** -- the unmoved complex side's own cap, with the
complex word untouched -- and 750 of the 1,024 candidate pairs sit above the frontier.

The conservative subset stays in the package and is still a real schedule, just a narrower
one: a family whose *own* rank divides the bank width and whose own volume is a whole number
of banks can be banked on its own blocks, needing no shape beyond the word's. On these two
words that is the bit word's ranks 6, 8, 18 and the complex word's rank 11, giving +2.17%
(one type), +2.52% (two, the same cap) and +3.67% (three).

One caveat belongs here, from the supplier's proof: *which* families may be banked is a
family-allocation question, not an arithmetic one. #207 excludes internal alias recipients,
source births and deleted terminals "from fresh bank allocation", and its CROSSOVERS records
that the construction is "ready for future genuinely different residual types" -- so a rung is
a priced target in exactly the sense of the family the supplier would have to allocate banks to.

## What is proven here

* **The precedent, checked against the vendored rows**: rank 60 on width 72, `60 ∤ 72`,
  volume `396,000 = 72 x 5,500`, residual families 4 and 24 with `18x4`, `3x24` and
  `6x4 + 2x24` all equal to 72.
* **Every priced row**: whole banks (`banks * m` equals the absorbed rank mass), the row
  identity after absorption, monotone `W`, adjacent-grid exclusion under PR200's own interval
  arithmetic on its `10^-18` grid.
* **Independent re-pricing**: `verify.py` re-derives the tileable families of both words from
  the queue's certificate, re-prices the conservative tier's first four rungs from that
  certificate without using `rungs.py`, and re-checks that every certified-shape arm fills
  whole banks.
* **The assembly replica** equals PR184's own `assemble()` on the vendored pair and reproduces
  #205's and #207's published kappa to within one grid step.
* All 23 package pins, with explicitly LF JSON so a Windows and a Linux checkout hash the same.

## What building a rung physically needs (not done here)

The rung fixes the arithmetic interface their generator consumes -- the cheapest certified
rung is 6,116 banks of 72 registers on the bit word, volume 440,352 -- but the construction
needs the supplier's pinned tree (a 51,416,352-byte baseline archive plus PR200 at
`a1175449...`), `numpy==2.3.5`/`scipy==1.17.0`, the exact gauge charts, the normalizer
routing, the F2 and defining-integer columns and the 24,401 frame prime witnesses. Named as
the work that remains, not as work that was done. Each rung stays a target with a falsifiable
number, the way this package's lever model predicted #205's banked row before it was built.

## Reproduce

```bash
python3 -B research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/verify.py   # 14 checks, ~70 s
python3 -B research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/rungs.py    # both tiers, ~25 s
```

## Change and mathematical scope

One bullet in `CONTRIBUTORS.md`, under "Additional public parallel efforts", linking a separate Lean 4 development on the Fourier side: [jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean](https://github.com/jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean/tree/fdfb7815c15ec43af0fb54818a6a57ae4025126b), pinned at `fdfb781`. Documentation only; no κ is claimed.

**What it adds for this project**

1. **The general frame lemma of #130, proved in Lean.** `notes/general-clifford-frames.tex` states it for arbitrary binary subspaces, degenerate ones included, and pull-request texts here list "General Clifford/tensor" among the assumptions. `Work/GFrame` (`frame_lemma`) proves it for the RAM model of OpenAI's family 130, with the cost of the two adapter steps: each is one linear pass.
2. **A complete machine check of the complex word of #193**, rebuilt from the published data of #168 and #193 (43,036 gates, 9,412 helper arrays). The Lean kernel replays every addition in exact arithmetic and checks every frame and block count, inside my layout and statement. #193 states its own scope as "no globally renumbered scalar transcript of the new complex word and no full Clifford/router replay".
3. **A five-stage "bridged" layout.** Every pair has a twin on the same line, so two pairs are exchanged with five invocations in place of six. The word of #193 gives 7.009184e-4 in its three-stage layout and 7.474547e-4 in this one. As far as my scans found (pull requests 1 to 207, by title and body), it is in no pull request here; if it is, please say so and I will credit it.

**Credit.** The circuit is this community's in every part: paired cubes, icekylinx (#144, crediting an664's #128 and eumemic's #117); modules, carrier links, frames and physical layer, eumemic (#168); source-parity local word and frame flow, icekylinx (#184); its move to the v4 modules and the donor pairing, ikeboy (#191, #193). The frame lemma (#130) and whole-residual batching (#10) are icekylinx's. Method, RAM model and recursion engine are OpenAI's (family 130). Mine are the Lean proof of the lemma for that model, the engine and checker built on it, the bridged layout, and the machine check. Full list: `RELATED-WORK.md` in the linked repository.

**Scope and limits.** The theorem is a Walsh-Hadamard statement, O(n (log n)^(1 - δ)) with δ = 7.474547e-4, in family 130's RAM model, in whole-block accounting. It is not this project's multiplication theorem and not a κ: the bit side and the analytic, routing and fixed-tape interfaces are outside it, the frame assumption stands as it is in this project's framework, and the bridged layout is untested there. That the rebuilt list is the word of #193 rests on a Python conversion and on equal counts, not on Lean. The Walsh-Hadamard statement (about 60 lines) was written for the linked project and is the part to read. The proofs have not yet had a line-by-line human review, and I would welcome one.

Built by me with a team of AI agents (Claude) that I directed; the proofs are theirs and are machine-checked.

Please edit, move or close this as you see fit. If a short note in the tree or a pinned replay would serve better, I am glad to prepare it.

## Validation

**This change.** One added line in one file; `git diff --check` is clean. `make verify` was not run: no generator, certificate, patch, note or test is touched.

**The linked repository** (its own report; nothing in it has been replayed here).

- Proof arguments: Lean theorems for the frame lemma, the generalised engine, and the soundness of the certificate checker.
- Finite checks: one certificate, evaluated by the Lean kernel in 16 segments plus 63 block counts.
- The Lean [comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator) accepted the proof three times against a 331-line statement importing only Mathlib (axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`) and rejects a saving one unit larger.
- Limits: macOS with a stand-in for the comparator's Linux sandbox; second kernel (`nanoda`) off; no build from nothing yet. Commands: `VERIFY.md`. Re-runs are welcome, most of all on Linux.

prs.title: Conditional kappa 6.838479e-4: cascade-optimized frames on PR200's banked bit word
prs.body:
**Draft, pending our full rerun.**

Conditional κ = `683847872495777/10^18` = **0.000683847872495777**:

- **+0.0962%** over #207 (0.0006831904550365);
- **+0.1152%** over #205 (0.000683061299399923).

The bit supplier binds. PR193's complex saving `700918443859411/10^18` is unchanged.

## Idea

#207 showed that PR200's operation frames are not optimal for the paid moment, and admitted 302 frame changes. This PR pushes the same lever much further.

- **Chain model.** Every physical chain of PR200's word is modeled exactly: splices, root frames and the full endpoint. Each operation frame is shared by its two chains. A frame is feasible when it:
  - contains the value span;
  - is G-nondegenerate;
  - is nested between its neighbours on both chains.

  Each chain costs Σ t·ln(72/t) over its rank increments.
- **Cascading moves.**
  - Raise a frame to a later neighbour (up to four slots ahead) or to the global feasible maximum, joining forward to repair nesting.
  - Lower it to an earlier neighbour or the global minimum, meeting backward.
  - Root frames, gauge frames, start frames and alias endpoints stay fixed.
  - Greedy plus short annealing reaches an optimum where single-op moves stall.
  - Result: 6,191 frames change, and internal chain cost falls 0.135%.
- **Admission.** Only frames change, and PR200's own modules re-check:
  - value spans, nondegeneracy, all chain nestings and the 1,760 alias containments;
  - the 34-sink terminal word on every source, target and dirty column, over F2 and over the integers;
  - prime witnesses for all 24,611 used frames.

  Unpacked coarse saving: 6.785484e-4 (PR200: 6.77774e-4).
- **Banks and composition.** Banks are as in #205: W = 56,402, deficit 5,808, maximum child 22. Composition uses three finite leaf levels and the balanced 47-constraint assembly with η = β = 10⁻²⁴. The next 10⁻¹⁸ grid point fails.

| | Packed bit coarse | κ |
|---|---:|---:|
| #205 | 6.835282e-4 | 0.000683061299399923 |
| #207 | | 0.0006831904550365 |
| **this** | **6.843158e-4** | **0.000683847872495777** |

```sh
python -B research/cascade-frames-bit/verify.py --complex-root <PR193 @187e101> --bit-root <PR200 @a117544> --full
```

About 6 minutes on two cores. The run reproduces `certificate.json` byte for byte. A workflow is included.

This is a conditional finite supplier certificate with the same inherited all-size hypotheses as #193, #197, #200, #205 and #207. The frame search is heuristic, with no optimality claim. The branch sits on top of #205's commit.

prs.title: A frame-layout ceiling for #200's bit word: coarse < 6.964e-4 under the banked ledger, so κ < 6.959e-4 on #205–#207's word (no new κ)
prs.body:
Adds `research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/` and one workflow; **no existing file changes and no new κ.** This carries DaysSky's #192 frame-floor method from #168's complex word to the physical bit word that #200, #205, #206 and #207 share. #200 is not on main, so the package carries the eight files of #200 it reads (frozen physical bit word, frames, partner chronology, graph, profile, sinks, certificate and the retained PR168-v4 exact integer checker) as a pinned archive `baseline-pr200.tar.gz` (1.4 MB), every sha256 pinned in `SOURCE.json` to commit `a1175449`; reviewers can confirm with `git show a1175449:<path> | sha256sum` or rebuild the archive byte for byte with `git archive --format=tar a1175449 <paths> | gzip -n -9`.

## Result

For every admissible choice of operation frames on this word (DAG, operations, sources, gauges, 1,760 reuse pairs, partner chronology and 34 sinks fixed):

| Ledger | Floor on C | Coarse saving ceiling | κ ceiling | Standing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| #200's own (entrance tails charged) | 2,804,210 | **6.904e-4** | 6.900e-4 | #200's 6.7777e-4 is 98.2% of it |
| completed entrance banks (#205/#206/#207) | 2,780,144 | **6.964e-4** | **6.959e-4** | #207's bit coarse 6.8366e-4 is 98.2% of it |
| without coupling the two registers of an operation | | 7.056e-4 / 7.118e-4 | | |

Consequences:

- Frame refinement on this word is worth at most **+1.8%** more on the bit side, under either ledger. #207's 302 coordinated changes are already inside this margin.
- The ceiling 6.964e-4 lies **below** the complex supplier those PRs use (#202's source-assisted word, 7.009e-4, itself at #192's ceiling for its frames). So on this bit word the complex branch can never bind, and every κ assembled from it stays below 6.959e-4 whatever the bit frames. Going further needs a different bit word (circuit, reuse, gauges or sinks), a bank construction that removes other children than the entrance tails, or a different design (#201 bounds the design at 2.5592e-3).

## Argument

`D = 2v − 3ℓ = 1,936`, `C = Σ n_r·r·ln(m/r)`, `m = 72`.

1. Every certified coarse saving satisfies `a < D/C` (#192 Lemma 1; on #200 the gap is 0.088%).
2. Every retained assembly accepts κ only below `a/(1+a)` of the binding supplier (#183), the atom wrapper and the finite stopped-leaf bootstrap of #185/#197/#207 stay below the coarse saving they start from.
3. Splitting a frame climb into more steps only costs more (`r·ln(m/r)` is subadditive).
4. No frame layout of the word pushes `C` below a floor: joint bounds propagated through both registers of every operation, an exact per-register dynamic programme over frame dimensions, and Lagrangian coupling of the two registers (1,200 integer subgradient rounds; each round is itself a valid floor).

The terminal record of #200's `bit/terminal.py` substitutes exactly one child of width 3 (the sink's root-to-full step, present in every layout) and one target child of width 21 per sink and stage and keeps the sink's other steps charged on the pivot; the script checks this against the certificate's `child_delta` and the pre/post target histograms, so the floor of the terminal ledger is the pre-sink floor minus that fixed cost. The banked ledger drops only the entrance tails `3·dim σ`, which is the only child change the completed-bank constructions make; their bank proofs are not re-verified here and the ceiling does not depend on them.

[PROOF.md](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/PROOF.md) has the statements and proofs.

## Verify

    python3 research/bit-frame-ceiling-200/ceiling.py --check     # stdlib only, about 2.5 minutes; -O is refused

The script rebuilds the pinned #200 files after checking the archive and every file hash, prepares the retained exact integer checker's geometry, and checks itself: #200's layout lies inside every derived frame bound; its slot chains reproduce #200's certified pre-sink ledger child for child (W 20,668; rank 1,486,160) and the −102/−102 terminal substitution; every per-slot floor and every Lagrangian round lies below #200's actual cost. All bounds use exact integers with rounded-down rational logarithms, so the printed ceilings are upper bounds. `--tree PATH` runs on a #200 checkout; `--overrides FILE` prices another layout of the same word: on #207's `frames/opframe-bases.json` it confirms the 302-frame layout lies inside every bound and above the floor, with banked `D/C = 6.8427e-4` (98.3% of the ceiling).

Run before opening: `--check` passes from the archive alone and on a #200 checkout (Python 3.14, macOS), with and without #207's overrides. The new workflow runs `--check` on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Scope and limits

- One word only: constructions that change the DAG, pairs, gauges, sinks or the bank construction are not bounded.
- Elementary proofs, not machine-checked beyond the script's exact arithmetic and self-tests; no one else has reviewed them.

## Credits

DaysSky (#192 method, #201 design ceiling), romainhedouin (#183 assembly ceiling), icekylinx and eumemic (paired-cube bit word and exact checker, #144/#168), James Chang (#166 terminal accumulation), Dugongue, Evan McKinney, Rohan Arun and EcmaXp (#186/#197/#205/#206/#207 bank ledger), ikeboy (#202 complex supplier). Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance; Apache-2.0, attribution in NOTICE.

prs.title: Conditional κ = 6.83847872497761e-4: five-level bootstrap on PR211 cascade frames
prs.body:
# Five-level finite bootstrap on the PR211 cascade-frame supplier

## Result

Starting from open PR211's exact conditional exponent `683847872495777/10^18`, this follow-up adds two fixed stopped-leaf levels and obtains

```text
kappa = 683847872497761/10^18
      = 0.000683847872497761.
```

The exact gain over PR211 is `1984/10^18`. The fifth level adds the last `10^-18` grid step over the four-level version. The bit supplier still binds. The regenerated certificate stores all 47 exact positive assembly margins, and the independent audit rejects the adjacent final grid point.

## Mechanism and inherited construction

The finite supplier and physical frames are PR211's frozen cascade-optimized PR200 bit word: 6,191 changed operation frames, the same terminal-modified word, 1,760 compensated aliases, completed banks, and PR193 complex supplier. We do not overwrite that layout with an older frame candidate. In an explicit comparison, PR211 already uses the same first-frame minimum joins at all 17 pairs found in our prior local search, while its second frames are smaller than that earlier candidate. The stronger cascade schedule is retained intact.

Let `c` be the newly priced packed bit saving and let `a_0` be the fully paid ordinary saving from the admitted PR200 word. Five fixed recurrences use

```text
a_j = (1-c)c + c a_(j-1),  j=1,2,3,4,5.
```

The exact rational verifier checks every recurrence, `a_(j-1) < a_j < c < 1-a_j`, the two-supplier paid moments, and the unchanged 47-constraint assembly with `eta=beta=10^-24` and weakening `10^-30`. The finite depth is five, independent of input size. For the fixed suppliers, the exact assembly ceiling at the unattained limit `a=c` has the same `10^-18` grid floor as the fifth level; since every finite `a_j<c` and the ceiling is increasing, no deeper fixed level can raise the reported grid value. The limiting value is only an upper-bound check, not an input supplier.

## Reproduction and validation

```sh
python -B research/cascade-frames-bit/verify.py \
  --complex-root .dependencies/pr193 \
  --bit-root .dependencies/pr200 \
  --full
```

The existing workflow checks out the pinned PR193 and PR200 sources, reruns the PR193 complex verifier, re-admits all PR200 frames and terminal columns, rebuilds banks, recomputes the exact certificate and independent moment audit, and compares the regenerated certificate byte for byte. The root Verify workflow also covers the repository Makefile matrix and formal jobs.

The local exact-arithmetic replay used PR211's frozen admitted physical record and the byte-pinned PR193 assembly/certificate. It produced five levels, 47 positive exact assembly margins, an independent moment audit PASS, and the exact limiting-grid upper bound. At Draft creation, this follow-up's GitHub Actions runs have not yet completed; the submitted branch reruns the complete frame/source verification.

## Conditions and limits

The conclusion remains conditional on the inherited all-width compiler, completed weighted/restored selector, routing, prime supply, precision/recovery, fixed analytic tape, and finite bridge hypotheses. PR211's cascade search is heuristic and does not prove a frame optimum. Finite verification does not prove the inherited all-size interfaces or the multiplication theorem unconditionally; this adds no Lean proof and makes no practical-speedup claim.

## Attribution

The cascade frame layout and its verification belong to PR211 (Rohan Arun, with Anthropic Claude assistance). The bit word/checkers are from PR200, banks from PR197, complex supplier from PR193, and finite-composition work from PR185/187/210; their licenses and source notices are retained. The fifth-level arithmetic extension and independent audit were prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No inherited construction is claimed as new or exclusive work.


## Frontier snapshot at Draft submission

- **PR211** is the highest validated public κ candidate at 683847872495777/10^18; its two package workflows and all 58 reported root/formal checks pass. This submission adds 1984/10^18 while retaining its admitted frame layout.
- **PR210** reports 683190455036641/10^18, below PR211; several root jobs were still running at this snapshot.
- **PR212** is a no-new-κ frame-layout ceiling for the older PR200/#205–#207 word. Its reported ceiling is not an attained supplier and does not cover PR211's cascade layout.
- **PR208** prices bank-family targets but explicitly says the required physical bank construction is not done; it is not a comparable certified κ.

The public list was refreshed immediately before opening this Draft.

prs.title: What entrance gauges and completed banks can absorb (no new κ)
prs.body:
Scoping note, **no new κ**: one README and one discovery script, with no certificate or verification changes.

#208 prices "bank-absorption rungs" (rank-22 family: +2.52%, and so on) and leaves open which families a bank may absorb. This note answers that for the published mechanism:

1. **Banks remove exactly the gauge exteriors.** By `notes/paired-cube-sharing.tex`, a gauged role's end correction F_A T_σ F_A⁻¹ is one tensor child of width 3·dim σ. #186/#207 replace exactly that child with the S_P endpoint, and say every other child remains. On #207's word all 2,200 genuine entrance gauges are already banked.
2. **An entrance gauge needs content that is both don't-care and restored.** The correction works because an auxiliary role's contract restores its own entrance value.
   - **Targets** accumulate (old + new), so no single end correction applies; a joint start correction breaks the stage gates' inactive-offset cancellation.
   - **Sources** are restored, but their values are consumed by the injections.
3. **Consequence:** #208's rungs absorb internal, target, center and compensating children, matching its own "not buildable as published" verdict. They need a mechanism other than gauge reinterpretation.

**Two measured near-misses** (float scores on #173's bit word; `regauge.py`):
- Re-gauging auxiliaries once banks make exteriors free has a +4.17% upper bound. Each gauge read splits the first increments of 4–9 targets, so the best nested selection loses 1.46%, and a greedy pass that only accepts improvements accepts zero roles.
- Target entrance gauges would price at +3.9–4.5%, but they are invalid by point 2.

This is a statement about the gauge/bank mechanism, not an impossibility proof for other constructions.

prs.title: CI: parallelize the recycled-bit frame-pair checks (~2x on the critical path)
prs.body:
**CI speedup only.** No mathematical change and no new κ.

## Why

`verify-recycled-bit` is the critical path of the `verify` workflow. On a recent run of #210 it took 1,009 s (3.11), 842 s (3.14) and 725 s (3.13), while every other group finished in under 10 minutes. Profiling `research/recycled-bit-integration/verify.py --all` shows setup takes 3 s and almost all the remaining time is two single-threaded loops:

- 4,878 new frame pairs: nesting and nondegeneracy (about 176 s serial);
- every distinct inherited ledger move: nesting (about 9 minutes serial).

## Change

Each check is a pure function of the shared `Exact` frames. `check_moves` splits the moves across forked worker processes and returns every move that fails; the verifier asserts that list is empty.

- The checks are the same `exact.inside` and `exact.nondegenerate` calls as before. Only which process evaluates them changes.
- Moves are grouped by target key, so each worker builds each annihilator basis once.
- `VERIFY_JOBS` sets the worker count; the default is the CPU count (4 on GitHub's Linux runners).
- With one job, or where `fork` is unavailable, it runs the original serial loop.

`certificate.json` changes only in the pinned SHA-256 of `verify.py`, which the verifier hashes into its own certificate:

```
-    "research/recycled-bit-integration/verify.py": "25a31677…e218",
+    "research/recycled-bit-integration/verify.py": "a5508f42…a0b9",
```

`docs/research/community-round7-validation.json` records the old certificate hash as a historical validation record. No script reads it, so it is left as written.

## Measured locally (Python 3.11, 4 workers)

| | `verify.py --all` |
|---|---:|
| before (serial) | 12 min 23 s |
| after | **5 min 59 s** |

The `--all --write` run passed every check and reproduced the certificate apart from the hash line. `test_recycled_bit_integration.py` passes (3 tests). On CI this should bring the group down to about 6 minutes, making the `research` group and `formal (historical)` (about 10–11 minutes each) the new critical path, for an estimated ~17 → ~11 minutes wall time.

I also tried precomputing each distinct frame basis once across workers instead. It was slower (7 min 14 s), because the basis keys depend on each other and don't split evenly, so the simpler chunking is used.

Possible follow-ups, for the maintainers to decide: caching the project's Lean build when `formal/lean` is unchanged (567 s of the 671 s `formal (historical)` job), and running independent `verify-research` targets in parallel after checking they don't write the same files.

Prepared by Joel Pulikkan with Anthropic Claude assistance.

prs.title: Audit hashes of regenerated gzip containers and propose a one-paragraph rule (no κ)
prs.body:
**No κ, no certificate change, no new mathematics.** This audits one reproducibility pattern and proposes a rule for it.

## The pattern

A package writes a container with `gzip.compress(...)`, hashes the **compressed** bytes, and requires that hash to equal a value committed or pinned when the container was produced elsewhere. A gzip container's deflate stream depends on the writing interpreter and zlib build, so that check can fail on unchanged inputs and can hide a real change behind an environment difference.

Two observations establish it, from opposite directions:

1. **A check that fails on unchanged inputs.** #202's headline verifier (`research/source-assisted-v4/verify.py:162`) stops with `Canonical certificate does not reproduce`. Exactly seven leaves differ and all derive from one value: the sha256 of the compressed lift certificate, written by `research/source-assisted/decision/exact_complex_flow_lift.py:409` and recorded at `:419` as `certificate_sha256=digest(cert_path)` of the file. Every other leaf, including κ, the complex saving, the bit effective saving and the assembly records, is equal. PR #214 reproduces this on CPython 3.13.16 with the pinned numpy 2.3.5 / scipy 1.17.0, and reports the same failure for #194's own verifier under CPython 3.12.3, with the lift inputs unchanged between the two commits; #194's CI passed the same check under the same versions.
2. **A rebuild instruction that does not reproduce.** #212's pinned archive rebuilds byte for byte as a **tar payload** from `a1175449` (verified), but not as a container: shipped `316aa694…` / 1,405,363 bytes against `cb71d72d…` / 1,404,558 bytes here, and no zlib level 1–9 reproduces the shipped length. No number changes; `ceiling.py` still checks the archive's file hashes.

## What the repository already does right

* **Compare the payload.** `research/paired-cube-bit/paired_cube_bit_word.py:935-937` (at #194's head, inherited by its successors) carries the reason in a comment: `if name.endswith('.gz'):  # gzip bytes depend on the zlib build; compare the compressed content` → `old, data = gzip.decompress(old), gzip.decompress(data)` → `require(old == data, …)`. #194's `bit/prove.py` decompresses before comparing too.
* **Record both, require only the payload.** `research/pair-assembly/frame/frame_compile.py:41-49` records `gzip_sha256` next to `word_sha256`; #217's `run_bit.py:151` records `prime_witness_sha256` next to `prime_canonical_sha256`; #217's `expected-bit.json` pins payload hashes for `graph_p12.json`, `word_p12.json`, `frames_p12.json`.
* **Check semantic fields.** #207's `verify_inner.py:23,29-30` compares `exact_scalar_program_sha256` and the complex profile's fields instead of a container.
* **Pin committed containers.** Pinning the sha256 of a committed `.gz` is safe — those bytes are fixed and no check regenerates them (`research/aligned-final-pricing-result/SOURCE.json:12-21`, and the vendored upstream `SOURCE.json` files).

## What is added here

`research/gzip-container-reproducibility/` with the audit above (file and line evidence), `gzip_hash_audit.py` (a heuristic scanner: writes / container-digest / comparison, printed with its evidence), and `CONTRIBUTING-note.md`, which carries the paragraph proposed for `CONTRIBUTING.md` — place it after the paragraph asking contributors to include regenerated certificates. Its text: compare payloads not containers when a check regenerates a file; pin payloads or semantic fields rather than container digests; committed containers are fine to pin; a container digest may be recorded only as an environment receipt, with the interpreter and zlib versions beside it, and must not be required to match across environments.

Scanner findings, one full-tree checkout per pinned head (`git worktree add --detach`), "risky" being a file that writes a container and records a digest of it: `main` `3b6b668` 639 `.py` files, **3** risky (`research/pair-assembly/frame/frame_compile.py:48`, `research/machine-transfer-verification/stream-transfer/experiments/balanced_split.py:64`, `scripts/experiments/probe_pair_ranked.py:41`); #194 `a8c8778` 578 files, 3 (those three, plus `research/source-assisted/decision/exact_complex_flow_lift.py:419`, the record observation 1 follows); #202 `8d8d67b` 605 files, 3 (the same three); #207 `cd14825` 650 files, 4 (the merged tree's three plus `coordinated-crossover-pr200/geometry/audit-gauge-charts.py:50`); #212 `9b6ad03` 640 files, 3 (the merged tree's three); #216 `34abdc5` 660 files, 5 (theirs plus `audit-gauge-charts.py:50` twice, in the package and in its vendored baseline); #217 `b739fc2` 654 files, 3 (the merged tree's three; the scanner does not flag `run_bit.py:151`). Opened rather than counted, the three shared flags read as records beside the payload digest (`frame_compile.py:48`), a record nothing reads back (`probe_pair_ranked.py:41`), and the one container digest in the merged tree that is *required* against a stored value -- `balanced_split.py:64` with `verify_balanced_split.py:67`, safe while the container and its receipt travel together from one run, observation 1 if a harness ever regenerates the container from the candidate's inputs. The scanner is a heuristic, not a proof of absence: it cannot see a digest recorded in one file and required in another (the #202 case is written out as a chain of file and line for that reason).

Prepared with Anthropic Claude assistance; Apache-2.0. No existing file is changed; the `CONTRIBUTING.md` edit is left to the maintainers.

prs.title: PR212's frame floor on PR217's butterfly word: κ < 6.968e-4 banked, +1.77% of frame room left (no new κ)
prs.body:
**No new κ, no existing file changed.** #212 bounded the bit coarse saving of one word — #200's physical bit word, shared by #205, #206 and #207 — over every admissible choice of operation frames. #217 holds the current record on a **different word**: 440 four-input XOR reassociations (880 graph nodes and scalar controls) on top of #211's cascade frames and #200's construction. This applies #212's method, unchanged, to that word.

## Result

At 1,200 Lagrangian rounds, the round count of #212's published run, on #217's head `b739fc2`:

| Ledger | #200's word (#212) | #217's butterfly word (here) |
|---|---|---|
| own: floor on C | 2,804,210 | 2,800,700 |
| own: coarse < | 6.904e-4 | **6.913e-4** |
| own: κ < | 6.900e-4 | 6.908e-4 |
| completed banks: floor on C | 2,780,144 | 2,776,634 |
| completed banks: coarse < | 6.964e-4 | **6.973e-4** |
| completed banks: κ < | 6.959e-4 | 6.968e-4 |

The like-for-like pair at 400 rounds moves the same way (own 6.909e-4 vs 6.918e-4, banked 6.969e-4 vs 6.978e-4), so the comparison does not depend on the round count.

The word's own numbers, recomputed here from its certificate:

| quantity | #200's word | #217's butterfly word |
|---|---|---|
| certified coarse saving, own | 6.7777395e-4 | 6.7938424e-4 |
| `D/C` of the certified layout, own | 6.7837287e-4 | 6.7998615e-4 |
| certified coarse saving, completed banks | 6.8366e-4 (#207) | 6.8516596e-4 |
| `D/C` of the certified layout, banks | 6.8427e-4 (#207) | 6.8578301e-4 |
| κ of the composition | 6.831904550365e-4 (#207) | 6.84696826673891e-4 |

**The butterflies raised the ceiling and the achieved value by about the same 0.13%, leaving slightly less frame room than before**: +1.68% from the achieved `D/C` to the ceiling here against +1.77% on #200's word, and +1.77% against +1.86% on the κ basis. Reassociation is not a way to enlarge the frame slack; it is a different word with its own, slightly higher, ceiling — which is what #212's scope statement already said.

## How the word was obtained and checked

#217's own `candidate.py` rebuilt the changed word from #202's head `8d8d67b` (fetched from `pull/202/head`), #211's pinned frame payload and the frozen butterfly overlay, checking those hashes itself. The three emitted payloads reproduce #217's declared hashes exactly — `graph_p12.json` `2bb271df…`, `word_p12.json` `ef77a7d3…`, `frames_p12.json` `4e0fce06…` — and the word has 41,288 operations, 18,908 roles, 1,760 reuse pairs, 3,960 gauges and **11,671 changed operation frames**, the number its `expected-bit.json` declares.

`ceiling.py --tree` then passed every self-test on that word: the certified layout lies inside every derived joint bound, **its slot chains reproduce #217's certified ledger child for child** (W 20,668, rank 1,486,160), the terminal record substitutes `[3, 21]` per sink and stage, and every per-slot floor is below its actual chain. Fact 1 reproduces the certificate to eight digits (`6.7938424e-4 < D/C = 6.7998615e-4`, gap 0.089%), matching an independent closed-form computation.

`rebuild_word.py` and `build_tree.py` reproduce the run end to end; the tree's certificate is a shim whose `bit` record is #217's own post-terminal profile plus the pre-sink profile restored by the terminal record, and every field of it is re-derived by #212's own self-tests.

## Added after the first push: what combining PR216's cuts with this word can reach

PR216 (`research/coordinated-crossover-pr200-v2`, head `34abdc5`) is a third layout on the same lineage, keeping PR211's frames and admitting 220 further operation-frame changes (kappa = 6.838643131376e-4). Since this note's ceiling bounds every frame layout of PR217's word, `transfer_check.py` (added in the second commit) settles the structural side of the obvious combination question from the two packages' own words:

* both have **41,288 operations** and identical DAG-fixing records (11,856 arcs, 25,900 order entries, 1,760 reuse pairs, 3,960 gauges, 6,624 root roles, 17,688 phase-1 and 7,728 plain operations, the same 1,760 sources and reads); exactly **880 operation contents** differ -- PR217's reassociation set -- along with 7,068 operation frames;
* PR216's admission records are `[op_index, [basis vectors ...]]` in that same index space: 6,191 current bases, 6,258 override records, 2,268 canonical subspaces, of which only **3 of 6,258** touch a rewritten operation and **none of the 2,268** does;
* so a merge is well defined at the index level, but PR216 admits with the scalar word fixed and PR217's change is exactly there: a merged layout is a new submission needing fresh admission and a fresh column replay;
* and it is capped: any frame layout of this word gives kappa < 6.968e-4, at most **+1.77%** over the 6.84696826673891e-4 record, while PR216's own layout on the plain word sits **0.122% below** it. The bank absorption of #219 (+2.30% over the same record, accounting ledger) is the route this comparison favours.


## Scope

This bounds frame layouts of #217's word only, in the sense #212's floor has. The reassociations are part of the word, so nothing here bounds further reassociation, other circuits, reuse, gauges or sinks — the escapes #212 lists. prs.title: Conditional κ = 6.92144604250060e-4: served diagonal operations on PR200's bit word (+1.09% over #217)
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Conditional **κ = 692144604250060/10^18 = 6.92144604250060e-4**, under the same retained interfaces as PR200, PR205 and PR197. No hypothesis changes.

- **+1.088%** over #217 (`684696826673891/10^18`), the best completed claim I know of.
- **+1.330%** over #205 (`683061299399923/10^18`).
- The served word alone, before packing, already gives `685800818606951/10^18`, above #217.

| Construction | Bit coarse saving | Conditional κ |
|---|---:|---:|
| #205: PR200 word, packed | 6.83528e-4 | 0.000683061299399923 |
| #217: butterflies and optimized frames, packed | 6.85166e-4 | 0.000684696826673891 |
| Served word, unpacked | 6.86716e-4 | 0.000685800818606951 |
| **Served word, packed** | **6.92624e-4** | **0.000692144604250060** |

The bit branch binds. PR193's complex supplier (`700918443859411/10^18`) has slack.

**The change: served diagonal operations.** PR200's bit word mixes each partner pair on its data registers. The carrier register gets `x_c + x_d`, and the passive register keeps `x_d` at all times. The word also builds `x_c + x_d` again in auxiliary registers. At 373 of these operations, the control register is a pure copy of `x_d`: one copy operation makes it, and this operation uses it once.

This PR reads `x_d` straight from the passive data register at those 373 operations. It deletes the 373 copies and their copy operations. To keep the passive register's frame chain nested, the pair's partner mix moves to right after the injections. The passive chain gets one 3-dim stop: `line → mix → F_i → full`.

| Per copy | PR200 | Served |
|---|---:|---:|
| Logical auxiliary roles | 18,908 | 18,535 |
| Physical chains | 17,114 | 16,741 |
| Stock `W` | 20,634 | 20,261 |
| Deficit | 1,936 | 1,936 |
| Coarse bit saving | 6.77774e-4 | 6.86716e-4 (+1.32%) |

Every frame stays one of PR200's witnessed frames (24,401). PR200's 34 terminal sinks, 1,760 aliases, gauges and all other operations are unchanged. PR205's completed banks (PR197's construction) and PR193's unchanged 47-constraint assembly then apply. `research/served-diagonal-bit/PROOF.md` gives the argument.

This is a conditional finite construction and composition, not an unconditional theorem or a speedup claim. The all-size hypotheses (completed core, Clifford interface, uniform weighted compilation, restored rows, fixed-tape transfer) are inherited exactly as in PR200, PR205 and PR197.

## Validation

Finite checks, all exact. `research/served-diagonal-bit/verify.py --full`:

1. runs PR193's and PR200's unchanged package verifiers at their pinned commits;
2. runs `patch.py`, which derives the served word again from PR200's frozen word and must match the frozen files;
3. runs `bit/served_prove.py`, a complete check in the style of PR200's `bit/prove.py`:
   - all 20,295 formal columns in F2 (identity) and over the integers (defining decoder), with no sampling;
   - exact frames and chains with PR200's PR168 v4 integer backend, including each served frame and each new passive chain;
   - PR200's 34 sinks through a forked terminal compiler, with the scalar bill retained;
   - PR200's paid-moment certification, imported unchanged;
   - seven word controls and three terminal controls, all rejected (for example, a served read of the carrier, a served chain without its stop, a served pair with a late mix);
4. applies PR205's charts, banks and colouring to the served word (`W = 55,283`, deficit `5,808`);
5. recomputes the arithmetic, the independent audit and the bank endpoint controls; the next 10^-18 grid points are rejected.

The full run takes about five minutes on Linux, and it reproduces `certificate.json` exactly. The workflow `.github/workflows/served-diagonal-bit.yml` runs it in CI. The proof argument (why the served word computes the same columns, and why the ledger is right) is in `PROOF.md`; the finite checks above test it on every column.

## Credit

The served operation is new. It builds on:

- Chafik Boukhalfa (#200): the bit word, sinks, witnesses and verifier, which the served checks fork;
- Rohan Arun (#205) and Evan McKinney (#197): the completed banks and their code;
- #193 for the complex supplier; icekylinx for the source-assisted method and the paired-cube framework;
- eumemic (#168), jamesyc (#166) and #185/#187 for the backend, the terminal lemma and the leaf composition;
- hcg890 (#217) for the previous best claim.

I have not tried to stack the served lever with #217's butterflies and frames. #219 reports a higher number, but it says that R1 to R4 are open, so I compare with #217.

prs.title: Rung 2 above #219: a complex-side bank ledger that raises κ to 7.0829157e-4, blocked on C1/C5
prs.body:
## What this is

The rung **above #219's rank-22 absorption** of PR208's bank ladder, priced end to end, plus
the honest report of what keeps it from being a new record.

Package: `research/complex-bank-run2/`, self-contained (its only in-repo dependency is the
sibling `research/composed-diagonal-bit-bootstrap/`).

```
python3 -B verify.py        # all checks, ~0.5s, no network, no writes
```

## Calibrations reproduced

* **#208's priced rung 2** (`3541457/5*10^9 = 7.0829154e-4`, the value #208 announces as its
  complex-bound number) is reproduced **exactly** by this package's own model — the
  `eta → 0`, `stop → 1` limit of PR193's unchanged 47-constraint assembly with the bit
  branch truncated.
* **#219's rung 1** (`700427501305159/10^18`) is reproduced exactly by importing #219's
  vendored package, and both the frontier certificate and PR184's own `select()` price the
  complex composition from the **certified profile moment** rather than from PR193's
  `complex_saving` field, which their own certificate records as `7.999e-8` below the
  certified moment of the same profile. This package prices the certified moment (matching
  both published artifacts) and additionally prices the lower field as a conservative
  variant, which lands at rung 1 minus 1.9e-12.

## The structural finding that decides the rung

Rung 1 does **not** sit at its budget ceiling. Its complex branch is
`(1-stop) * 7.00918443859411e-4 - 1e-10 = 7.00918343859411e-4`, and its kappa sits
**8.5e-19 below that** — the grid. So rung 1 is grid-limited on the complex side, and no
bit-side work can move a rung above it: the ladder only advances by raising the **complex**
coarse saving. (This is why #208's own ledger maps rank-22 → rank-11 as its first complex
move.)

## Rung 2 priced

Absorbing the complex word's rank-11 family as PR184's bank absorber would, with the rank-11
member as a whole bank (`volume 35046 = 66 * 531`, `stock 36156 -> 35625`, drop = bank count),
discarding nothing for having unsalvageable part, and re-pricing through PR184's unchanged
47-constraint assembly:

```
coarse  7.00918443859411e-4  ->  7.08793603125109e-4
kappa   354145785295363 / 500000000000000000  =  7.08291570590726e-4
        (+1.12% over rung 1; 7.0829154e-4 < kappa < 7.0829155e-4 -> adjacent grid point rejected)
```

The value is checked against #208's own closed form to the last digit and against the exact
cross-checks of PR184's assembly (43 strict constraints are exactly `saving/4`, the 4
non-quarter constraints and 7 margins are re-witnessed, every entry re-derived from the
integer degree blocks).

## Why it is not built (the blocker)

The rung is **conditional on a complex-side bank construction that does not exist in the pins**.
All nine obligations in `obligations.json` are **OPEN**; `verify.py` certifies the accounting
and the price, not the construction:

* **C1 — the bank construction.** The pins contain no bank construction for the complex
  supplier: its certificate has no bank keys at all. The only banked word in the pins is the
  bit word's entrance-gauge pack of #205/#206 (width 72, rank-60 exteriors, 6,116 banks), and
  that mechanism is specific to the width-72 bit word's entrance gauges — so this is a new
  mechanism, not an extension of an existing one.
* **C2–C4 — the re-certification the construction implies.** Formal-column checks on the
  modified complex word, charts/routing/prime witnesses for the new blocks, and
  moment-envelope parity with the ledger priced here (retained three-copy stock 35,625, one
  copy 11,875; deficit 3,960, one copy 1,320). Any completion child C1 introduces must
  re-enter the ledger and the kappa be recomputed.
* **C5 — inventory and provenance.** The pins hold no inventory of the complex word's
  rank-11 items: no per-vertex child frame/chain occurrences, no bijection onto the 3,186
  three-copy occurrences, no proof that no other bin is touched. The only occurrence
  inventory the pins hold is #219's bit-side `inputs/absorbed-occurrences.json` for the
  rank-22 bin, which is exactly what makes #219's R1 a closed checklist and this rung's C5 a
  blank one.
* **R1–R4 — inherited open from #219** (bit-side residual types, formal columns, charts, and
  moment parity), carried over with their source and PR219 head `237067f`.

Two further honesty items: `rank 4 = bank` is standard practice in this repository rather
than a proven identity, so the rung-1 ceiling statement carries a binary flag
(`rank_four_is_whole_bank`) instead of pretending precision it does not have — the
conservative reading is still above rung 1, which is what makes the ceiling argument
decisive. And PR193's own `complex_saving` field prices the rung lower; the package records
the delta, the conservative variant, and the exact profile (a 10^-10-grid value of
`7.009184e-4`, `4.39e-11` below the certified moment) so a reviewer can rule on which one
the assembly must consume.

## Files

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | the rung, the pricing, the ladder, what is blocked |
| `PROOF.md` | derivation of the rung-1 ceiling, the rung-2 price, exactness evidence |
| `ledger.py` | shared model loader and the strict-constraint witness |
| `run2.py` | rung-1 ceiling statement, rung-2 price, the ledger and the two calibrations |
| `banks.py` | the complex-side bank / ceiling arithmetic clamps |
| `verify.py` | runs every published number from scratch and checks them against each other |
| `obligations.json` | C1–C5, R1–R4, each with status and evidence; all nine OPEN |

Scope: the physical complex and bit words are the **suppliers' certified artifacts**, vendored
and priced, not rebuilt or replayed. The one value that is not a published field — the rank-11
absorbed stock `35625` — is labelled as a model value and is a hypothesis of the construction,
not a certified fact; it is what the rung would deliver *if* C1's admissibility and C2–C5 hold.
The kappa is a priced, exactly certified **target**, not a completed finite witness or an
unconditional multiplication theorem.

Credits: the complex supplier and its 47-constraint assembly are #184/#193/#194/#219; the
finite leaf wrapper and the bank construction are #185; the model this rung extends is #208.

prs.title: The complex suppliers transfer to the exact DFT: θ = 1 − 7009/10⁷ (7.009·10⁻⁴) for the exact discrete Fourier transform (no new κ)
prs.body:
Adds `research/exact-dft-transfer/` and one workflow; **no existing file changes and no new κ.** It records that this repository's complex suppliers are *batched networks* in the sense of eumemic's [exact-dft-bounds](https://github.com/eumemic/exact-dft-bounds) (`notes/batched-dft-note.tex`, `6f87d1a`), so each certified complex moment root `a` gives, in the exact complex-arithmetic model of OpenAI's *An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform* (25 September 2026, `openai/math` at `adc7f12`), an exact DFT of every length and an exact complex convolution in

    O( n (log n)^θ (log log n)^(4−θ) ),   θ = 1 − a.

eumemic's repository proves this for the PR #144 supplier on main (a = 607/1250000). This package adds the two later suppliers; the same two propositions are [eumemic/exact-dft-bounds#1](https://github.com/eumemic/exact-dft-bounds/pull/1) (`c92cf70`).

## Result

| Supplier | Certificate | m | W / vertex | Deficit | Max child | a (certified) | θ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PR #144 (main `d1d6c07`) | `certificates/paired-cube-complex-input.json` | 72 | 29,937 | 1,936 | 60 | 607/1250000 = 4.856·10⁻⁴ | eumemic's value |
| PR #200 (`a1175449`) | `research/paired-cube-diagonal-bit-168/certificate.json`, `complex.profile` | 66 | 13,163 | 1,320 | 20 | 3327/5000000 = 6.654·10⁻⁴ | +37% |
| **PR #194 (`a8c8778`)** | `research/source-assisted-v4/certificate.json`, `complex_profile` | 66 | 12,052 | 1,320 | 20 | **7009/10⁷ = 7.009·10⁻⁴** | **+44%** |

For every fixed κ < 7009/10⁷ the exact DFT and exact convolution take O(n (log n)^(1−κ)) operations. OpenAI's saving is about 2.1·10⁻¹³.

## Argument

- The batched moment Σ_ρ N_ρ (ρ/m)^θ < W with θ = 1 − a is exactly this repository's coarse-saving moment Σ_ρ n_ρ ρ (m/ρ)^a < W m (|G| cancels). So a supplier's complex saving is the DFT exponent saving, up to the slightly weaker exp/log bounds used here (which is why PR #200's 6.65489…·10⁻⁴ is certified as 6.654·10⁻⁴).
- **PR #200 is a batched network** (Proposition B in `PROOF.md`, by reference): the shared-core word is retained from #144; the fused scalar word's complete signed identity is replayed on every formal column in both shear signs, which is the one-column identity that eumemic's Lemma 2.2 extends to every f; each operation carries one rational frame shared by both registers with nested chains, so each transition is adapters around one child of width its rank increment (Lemma 4.1); reuse pairs, terminal sinks and fused outputs are gates; the ledger Σ ρ n_ρ = 867438 = 66·13163 − 1320 is re-counted by that package.
- **PR #194 is a batched network** (Proposition C, by reference to `notes/source-assisted-note.tex` and the PR #194 checkers): the complete transcript is a linear word z_final = Mz + Lx with M invertible, each operation an exact local map with dyadic coefficients or a source control (gates); reads subtract the recomputed dirty response at frame zero, K + B = I is checked exactly, every auxiliary is brought to the full frame and every gate reversed (the one-column identity, replayed by the independent scalar transcript with mutation controls); the flow is monotone along nested frame chains with an acyclic once-only reuse DAG, so each transition is adapters around one child of its Fourier rank; Σ ρ n_ρ = 794112 = 66·12052 − 1320.

## Verify

    python3 -B research/exact-dft-transfer/verify.py --check     # stdlib only, about 20 seconds; -O is refused

The script checks every pin in `SOURCE.json` (the main certificate of PR #144 and the vendored certificates of PR #200 and PR #194, byte for byte as `git show <commit>:<path>`), rebuilds the three child histograms from those certificates and compares them with the committed `certificates/network-children-*.json`, checks the ledger identities (rank sum, deficit = Wm − rank = 2v − 3ℓ, largest child < m), certifies the batched moment at each claimed saving in exact rational arithmetic (artanh series with tail bound; exp(x) ≤ 1 + x + x²/(2(1 − x/3))), rejects the next 10⁻⁷ grid point for each supplier, and compares with `expected.json`. Margins: 3.16·10⁻³, 2.69·10⁻³, 5.27·10⁻⁴. The workflow runs `--check` on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

Run before opening: `--check` passes on this branch (Python 3.14, macOS). Not run: the full `make verify` (no existing file changes).

## Scope and limits

- Conditional on the suppliers' constructions exactly as in eumemic's note: exact complex phases, the Cayley cover and completed-core sharing are written arguments; scalar identities, frame nesting, ranks and ledgers are checked by the packages' scripts. For PR #194 the scalar transcript replay checks the one-column identity but does not materialize the physical Clifford transports.
- The multiplication bound's bit, assembly, routing, precision and Turing-machine interfaces are not used (item-by-item replacement in Section 6 of eumemic's note).
- Not formally verified; astronomically large constants; nothing here changes any κ.

## Credits

OpenAI (exact-transform framework and the original phase network); eumemic (batched tensor recursion, normal-form lemma, transfer, PR #144 proposition; `scripts/moment.py` adapts its `verify_moment.py`, Apache-2.0); Ryan Shea (priority for the idea of transferring the community networks to the exact-DFT model); icekylinx (paired cubes, compiler, gauges, Clifford frames, three-stage cover, whole-residual recursion, source-assisted frame flow, PR #184) and ikeboy (PR #193/#194 rebuild on v4 modules); eumemic (PR #117/#155/#157/#161/#168 lineage); James Chang (#124/#166); DaysSky (#162/#192); GamingPuzzled; gupt1156 and Abhinav Ramachandran; Zhihao Chen; Rohan Arun; an664; and the earlier lineage in the repository NOTICE. Full attribution in the package NOTICE. Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance; Apache-2.0. This package claims only the observation that the two later suppliers are batched networks and the exact re-check of their moments.

Under the conditional framework breaking the $O(n \log n)$ integer multiplication barrier (originating from OpenAI Preprint #109), this PR establishes a new world record on the Schönhage alternating carrier tensor architecture:
