prs.title: Six families per word: where the bank ladder tops out, and what the bit rank-6 rung would need (model, no new κ)
prs.body:
**No new κ — a MODEL over the pinned frontier certificate, not a construction.** This package
prices the bank-absorption ladder exactly on the frontier certificate's own child ledgers,
screens it one family deeper than before, and works out item by item what instantiating the
cheapest rung would still need. No bank, chart, normalizer or witness is built here, and no
number below is a record claim.

Package: `research/frontier-beat-2026-10-09/` (`README.md`, `INSTANTIATE.md`,
`beats.py` → `beats.json`, `beats-six.json`, `instantiate.py` → `instantiate.json`,
`check_docs.py`, `SOURCE.json`).

## 1. Six families per word: the ladder does not top out on both sides together

The strict ladder (families whose volume tiles whole width-`m` banks) is screened
exhaustively one family further on both words: 10,318 admissible family sets on the bit word
and 2,725 on the complex one, against 3,512 and 991 at five families.

| families | best bit saving | best complex saving |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | `[1,3,13,21,22]` → 1.38023409118239e-3 (+101.89%) | `[1,2,3,4,19]` → 1.63407154980676e-3 (+133.13%) |
| **6** | **`[1,3,13,20,21,22]` → 1.52739614292328e-3 (+123.42%)** | **`[1,2,3,8,15,18]` → 2.30539885681005e-3 (+228.91%)** |

The six-family removals take 59.7% of the bit ledger (33,599 banks) and 65.6% of the complex
ledger (7,895 banks), but the headline is the *smaller* budget, so the model's best pairing is
**bit six families with complex four**:

    kappa = 1.5250667618335e-3  (+123.23% over the certificate's 6.831904550366e-4)

11 new residual types, binding bit, removing 59.7% of the bit ledger and 33.8% of the complex
one. The complex side's extra ~100 points are unspendable while the bit side binds. The strict
tier's own best rung (bit ranks 6 and 8 with complex rank 11, +3.674%) is far below the wider
screen's, and the difference is exactly the block shapes the word does not already use.

## 2. What instantiating the bit rank-6 rung would take

Availability has a one-line form: a rank-`r` family fills width-`m` banks only when its own
volume is a whole number of banks (`m % r == 0`). On the certificate's two words exactly four
families qualify — bit ranks 6, 8, 18 and complex rank 11 — while rank 4 (the certified block
size) and rank 1 (the largest mass) do not.

The **bit rank-6 rung** is the closest of the pinned targets to a construction:

| quantity | value |
| --- | --- |
| children | 12,096 over three copies = 4,032 per copy |
| blocks per bank | 12 (stride 6 on width 72) — **exactly one block per absorbed child** |
| banks | 1,008 over three copies = 336 per copy, integral (no replicas needed) |
| stock `W` | 56,402 → 55,394 |
| rank mass | 4,055,136 → 3,982,560 |
| deficit | 5,808, unchanged |
| retained ledger | 21 families, max child 22 |
| certified saving | 6.83657523331095e-4 → 6.98484415006068e-4 |
| kappa | 6.831904550366e-4 → **6.979968750671e-4 (+2.1672%)** |

The vendored bank proof already covers every item it states for *any* disjoint projector
partition: the algebra `S_P S_Q = S_(P+Q)`, `S_P² = I`, chart-conjugation telescoping, the 144
two-bank address-map columns over `F2` and over `Z` for the endpoint and its inverse (rejecting
a missing or repeated last block), the unchanged moment envelope (rare-class fraction `10^-16`,
`32·72²` children per edge, the positive atom/row-adapter toll on its own `10^-24` grid) and the
47-constraint/7-margin assembly. A stride-6 partition is a new *instance* of that construction,
not new algebra — and here the per-copy allocation is integral, so the rung does not need the
nine physical replicas the certified rank-60 bank used.

What is missing is the normalizer's child-to-block map (rank-6 dirt is interior and has no
registered gauge address), stride-6 charts and per-block Gram/prime witnesses, and — the real
gap — an **inventory**: no pinned package enumerates the word's rank-6 children, not their frame
or chain occurrences and not a bijection onto the 4,032 blocks per copy, exactly as the complex
word's rank-11 family has never been enumerated either. The conditional interfaces (all-input
weighted compiler, completed-core routing, stage cover, local-ring precision/recovery, prime
supply, uniform setup, all-size analytic/tape contracts) stay conditional; this package
discharges none of them.

## Reproduce and verify

```sh
python3 -B beats.py                                      # ~91 s, writes beats.json
python3 -B beats.py --check                              # byte-for-byte against it
python3 -B beats.py --max-types 6 --out beats-six.json   # ~157 s, one family deeper
python3 -B beats.py --max-types 6 --out beats-six.json --check
python3 -B instantiate.py                                # ~2 s, writes instantiate.json
python3 -B instantiate.py --check
python3 -B check_docs.py                                 # 41 quoted numbers, 44 required claims
```

* The frontier is reproduced on the certificate's own rows under each side's own convention:
  `a_complex` to the last digit, `a_bit` to sixteen significant digits, with the residual
  recorded rather than asserted away. The kappa grid and the assembly rule are discovered by
  search, not assumed.
* Every number is exact rational arithmetic through the pinned interval/exponential enclosure
  module (`.py` files hashed in `SOURCE.json` on every run); no floating point enters a check.
* Both six-family headlines and the headline pairing were re-derived by a separate script
  written against the certificate rows, independently of the model code, and all three
  artifacts reproduce **byte for byte** when the package is copied to a fresh checkout of
  `main`.
* `check_docs.py` keeps the prose honest: it re-reads every number quoted in `README.md` and
  `INSTANTIATE.md` and the required claims against the three artifacts.

## Scope and limits

* **MODEL, NOT CONSTRUCTED.** Each rung is a priced target. The bank construction, its charts
  and its witnesses belong to the supplier's harness; nothing here is a new bound on the
  exponent and nothing here should be read as a κ claim.
* A rung's cost is measured in new residual types (families absorbed) because that is what the
  supplier's harness would have to instantiate; chart, normalizer and witness work is ignored
  entirely by that metric.
* The wider screen treats an absorbed family's rank as free, which is certified precedent only
  for an exterior of the rank-60 kind; the strict tier is the only tier that needs no block
  shape the word does not already use.
* The pinned ladder in one earlier package prices both sides with the rare-class fallback, so
  its values sit a few 1e-10 relative below the convention-matched values recorded here; both
  are given for every rung.
* No contributor verifier, CI run or upstream proof package is re-executed: the rows are the
  certificate's own recorded ledgers and the arithmetic is this package's.
* Not run here: upstream CI. The local suite on this Windows host has six failures/errors
  (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'resource'`, no C++ compiler in `PATH`, and three
  frozen-certificate mismatches in `test_copied_reversed` / `test_copied_fixed_reversed` /
  `test_batched_network`) which reproduce identically on a pristine `main` worktree and are
  unrelated to this package.
* One defect in this package was found and fixed while verifying it: `--check` printed a
  hardcoded label and so could not distinguish the five- from the six-family artifact. It now
  names the file and the depth it compared, and the README's runtime claims were corrected to
  the measured 91 s / 157 s.

## Credits

The pinned inputs are not mine. The frontier certificate is PR207's coordinated crossover, and
the bank proof is the `coordinated-frames-and-entrance-banks` text of the #186 → #205/#206/#207
lineage; the interval and exponential enclosures that compute every number here are PR200's own
arithmetic module. The contraction and bank models, their validation against the queue's
published banked rows and the closed-form bank proof are PR184/PR185/PR197/PR200/PR205/PR206/PR207's.
This package re-implements only the arithmetic it prices with, and modifies no pinned artifact.

Prepared by Maxime Fleury with Codebuff assistance.

## Result

The candidate certificate gives conditional
`κ = 694787513005285/10^18 = 0.000694787513005285`, an exact gain of
`4793314502/10^18` over PR210's `694782719690783/10^18`.

The deterministic search retimes 19 operation frames in 14 accepted moves:

- op 18750: rank 5 → 6;
- five adjacent pairs (23544/23545, 23591/23592, 23638/23639, 23685/23686, 23732/23733): rank 9 → 12;
- eight operations (27900, 27904, 27908, 27912, 28052, 28056, 28060, 28064): rank 13 → 14.

The `d log d` score proposes moves only. Exact frame containment, nondegeneracy and nested role chains admit the moves. The physical word and scalar operations remain those of PR210. The raw child-histogram delta has weighted-rank change zero and 27 fewer children per vertex. The normalized profile keeps `m=72`, `W=438838`, rank mass `31549872`, deficit `46464` and maximum child `22`. Bit saving improves by `4799982097/10^18`; the bit side remains binding. The exact 47-constraint assembly rejects the adjacent `10^-18` grid point.

## Local checks completed

- `joint-plateau-search-prdf958.py --verify-committed`: deterministic 14-move replay, 19 changed operation frames; passed.
- Candidate source-boundary geometry checks for 440 borrowed sources, three rank-19 gauges and 28 source-backed gauges: passed, including reflected frame paths and target chronology.
- `pack_joint.py`: 231 charts and 3,594,888 bank assignments; passed.
- Exact parent profile calibration reproduced PR210's κ. Candidate `price_joint.py` reproduced the committed candidate certificate and all 47 positive rational constraints.

## CI coverage required before review

The package's immutable offline verifier now replays the deterministic search before running the full scalar word, source/dirty restoration, target ledgers, charts, banks, complex lift, independent paid moments and exact assembly. The continued-kappa workflow runs that verifier and checks for workspace changes. PR227 replays an older, lower PR210 head; the higher prices in PR219 and PR224 still have open physical construction obligations.

prs.title: The paired-cube decoder does not extend to 4-dimensional ports: a Lucas-parity obstruction (no new κ)
prs.body:
Scoping note, **no new κ**: one README and one standard-library checker, with no existing file changed.

**Question:** does the paired-cube decoder generalize from triples (3-dimensional cubes) to k-dimensional ports, with more sources per cell and a bigger deficit?

**Answer:** consider the star family of mod-2 decoders for k-ports:

    x_T = Σ_{0<l<k} a_l Σ_{L⊆T,|L|=l} star_L + Σ_{0<j<k} b_j Σ_{|S∩T|=j} x_S

This is the family the paired-cube lemma uses: level-1 stars plus overlap-1 corrections for k = 3. **A decoder in this family exists iff k is not a power of two.**

The coefficient of x_S depends only on j = |S∩T|. The corrections b_j fix every 0 < j < k. The diagonal coefficient is Σ a_l C(k,l), and by Lucas' theorem every C(k,l) with 0 < l < k is even exactly when k is a power of two.

| k | Decoder |
|---|---|
| 3 (paired cubes) | yes |
| **4 (hypercubes)** | **none** |
| 5, 6 | yes; they need corrections at more overlap sizes (5) or level-2 stars (6) |

```sh
python3 -B research/hypercube-decoder-parity/check.py   # <1 s; tests every coefficient vector for k = 3..6
```

Scope:
- This covers the star or overlap-class family only. It is not an impossibility proof for every 4-port decoder.
- It makes no claim that k = 5 or 6 beats k = 3; that needs a full construction.

Credits: icekylinx (#144), eumemic (paired-cube bit word and lemma). Prepared by Joel Pulikkan with Anthropic Claude assistance; Apache-2.0.

prs.title: Rungs 3 and 4 of the bank ladder: κ = 7.11175695867958e-4, and the top of the complex ledger (priced target, not a witness)
prs.body:
**A scheduled target, not a witness.** `kappa = 711599961413937/10^18 = 7.11599961413937e-4`
-- **+0.4671% over #224's rung 2** and **+4.1584% over the #207 frontier** -- conditional on
the same open obligations rung 2 carries, plus two new inventories. The bank schedule those
rungs need is **built here, not merely owed**: every bank exactly filled, every item in a block,
the remainder padded from a retained bin.

Package: `research/complex-bank-run3/`, self-contained on `main`: it vendors #219's rung-1
package byte-identically under `references/pr219-run1/` and #207's frontier certificate, and
pins 27 files by sha256.

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3 && python3 -B verify.py
```

## The ladder, and where it stops

Rung 2 (#224) absorbs the complex word's rank-11 family and lands on the complex branch's
ceiling, so every further rung has to raise the **complex** coarse saving. The criterion that
makes such an absorption free is that the family's own volume is a whole number of width-66
banks (`66 | rank * children`), and exactly three families of that ledger satisfy it:

| rung | what leaves the ledger | per bank | banks | complex coarse | kappa | vs rung 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 (#224) | complex rank 11 | 6 rank-11 blocks | 531 | 7.08793603125109e-4 | 0.000708291570590726 | — |
| 3, volume criterion | + complex rank 16 | — | 192 | 7.11077971348264e-4 | 0.000710572698755137 | +0.3221% |
| **3, padded schedule** | + complex rank 16 | 4 blocks + 2 registers | **198** | **7.11289982558164e-4** | **0.000710784408728476** | **+0.3520%** |
| 4, volume criterion | + complex rank 20 | — | 60 | 7.11681826686289e-4 | 0.000711175695867958 | +0.4072% |
| **4, padded schedule (the top)** | + complex rank 20 | 3 blocks + 6 registers | **66** | **7.12106696511698e-4** | **0.000711599961413937** | **+0.4671%** |

The two "volume criterion" rows are the accounting the criterion gives and are kept because
they are what the ledger arithmetic produces -- but a width-66 bank cannot host them (`192` and
`60` are below the capacity bounds `198` and `66`, and no uniform tiling absorbs two bins at
once). The padded rows are the schedule a bank admits, and they price higher, so the padded
rung 4 is the top this PR claims.

After rung 4 **no family of the remaining 17 has a whole-bank volume** (the check is
machine-asserted), so the accounting criterion the built rungs use is exhausted: 795 banks in
total (531 + 198 + 66), top row `W = 35,361`, rank mass 2,329,866, 634,473 children, largest
child 19. Each step keeps the row identity `66 * W - rank_mass = 3,960` and drops the stock by
exactly the bank count (531, 198, 66).

Two consequences fall out of the same arithmetic, and they are the useful part:

* reaching `kappa = 7.2e-4` needs a complex coarse saving of `7.20518773516934e-4`, i.e.
  **+1.1809%** more than the top rung's -- more banking than the remaining mass can supply at
  this width;
* while the complex branch caps the budget, the assembly's ceiling is capped by #219's rung-1
  bit leaf, so **`kappa = 7.5e-4`, `8e-4` and `1e-3` are unreachable on this bit word**, whatever
  the complex ledger does. Those targets need a new bit supplier first.

## Status (unchanged blocker, two new items)

`obligations.json` states C1-C7 and inherits #219's R1-R4; T1, which this PR carried as an
obligation, is settled below. Read from the pins rather
than asserted: the complex supplier's certificate carries **no key containing `bank` at all**,
and the only banked word in the pins is the **bit** word's entrance-gauge pack (#205, 45,842
banks of width 72 over rank-60 exteriors). Nothing enumerates the complex word's rank-11,
rank-16 or rank-20 children, so the item-to-block map has no starting inventory (C6, C7). And
because `66 = 4 * 16 + 2 = 3 * 20 + 6`, the two new families cannot tile a bank alone.

**T1 is now enumerated, and the answer is negative** (`schedule66.py`, `schedule66.json`,
re-run by `verify.py`). A uniform pattern -- the same pattern in every bank, as the certified
bit-side construction uses -- forces one common bank count `B` with `k_f = n_f / B`, so `B`
divides `gcd(n_f)` and `sum_f k_f * f <= 66`. That is exhaustive:

| family | blocks per bank | banks by volume criterion | banks its capacity needs | uniform patterns |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 11 (rung 2) | 6 (`66 = 6 * 11`) | 531 | 531 | 4, tightest **531** |
| 16 (rung 3) | 4 (`66 = 4 * 16 + 2`) | 192 | **198** | 4, smallest **198** |
| 20 (rung 4) | 3 (`66 = 3 * 20 + 6`) | 60 | **66** | 3, smallest **66** |

No subset of two or three families admits a uniform tiling at all; `{16, 20}` comes closest,
its common divisor 198 giving four rank-16 and one rank-20 block per bank -- 84 registers into
a 66-wide bank. The volume criterion and the capacity criterion coincide only when the rank
divides the width, which is why rung 2's `531` is consistent and the unpadded `192` and `60`
are not.

**T1 is settled, at the schedule level** (`prototype66.py`, checked by `verify.py`, recorded in
`certificate.json` -> `padded_schedule`). A bank the family cannot fill alone is filled by the
family plus a fixed pattern of retained blocks:

| rung | banks | per bank | padding per bank | chosen draw |
| ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| 11 | 531 | 6 rank-11 blocks | 0 | none |
| 16 | 198 | 4 rank-16 blocks | 2 | 2 rank-1 blocks per bank (396 rank-1 children of 262,602) |
| 20 | 66 | 3 rank-20 blocks | 6 | 6 rank-1 blocks per bank (396 rank-1 children) |

Every bank is exactly full, every family item lands in a block with no slot unused
(`4 * 198 = 792`, `3 * 66 = 198`, `6 * 531 = 3,186`), the item-to-block map is explicit (item
`i` -> bank `i // k_f`, block `i % k_f`), and the padding is a partial draw from a bin the
ledger keeps, so the retained histogram carries the reduced count. Because the mass leaving is
`banks * 66` by construction, the row identity holds and the stock falls by exactly the bank
count at every step. All padding options are enumerated and compared (rank 16: two; rank 20:
eleven), and the best is the one claimed. What this is not: the normalizer, frames, charts and
prime witnesses remain C1-C7, and the padding blocks are ordinary retained children -- no new
frame family is introduced.

## Is the bank width a lever? No -- and the scan says which lever *is* one

The bank width is not a schedule parameter, it is the word's own modulus. The pinned
bit-side schedule fixes it: `M = 72`, its rank-22 bin's 20,016 occurrences carrying
`22 * 20,016 = 440,352` registers into `440,352 / 72 = 6,116` banks, with the stock dropping
by exactly the bank count. So a width scan is a word scan (`widths66.py`), and it answers:

* **nothing narrower exists.** The engine's contraction is `rank mass < W * modulus`, and the
  pinned row has `rank mass / W = 65.8905...`, so every `w <= 65` leaves the row unposeable
  (recorded at 48, 54, 58, 60, 63, 64, 65). 66 is the smallest modulus this ledger admits.
* **nothing wider is comparable.** Holding the ledger fixed while raising `w` leaves a row whose
  rank mass fills only `mass / (W * w)` of its capacity: 99.834% at 66, **95.5% at 69, 91.5% at
  72, 68.6% at 96** -- a different word, which is why only the pinned width is priced, and where
  the scan reproduces this PR's own top exactly as its calibration.
* **the criterion is not the cap, the density is.** At `w = 54`, nine of the 20 families would
  tile whole banks and **1,549,098 registers (65% of the rank mass)** could leave, against
  52,470 (2.2%) here. A *less* dense complex word -- more stock per unit of rank mass -- would
  admit a narrower modulus where far more of its ledger tiles at once. That is what to look for
  in a new supplier, measured rather than guessed.

## What is instanced, and what is still owed

The schedule's items are now addressed (`instantiate66.py` -> `occurrences66.json`), which is
C1's combinatorial half and the C5-C7 inventories: item `i` -> bank `i // k_f`, block
`i % k_f`, offset `(i % k_f) * rank`.

| family | per vertex | items (3 copies) | banks | blocks per bank | padding registers | table digest |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 11 | 1,062 | 3,186 | 531 | 6 | 0 | `fb9bd2d17f69...` |
| 16 | 264 | 792 | 198 | 4 | 396 | `f96efd45d9d9...` |
| 20 | 66 | 198 | 66 | 3 | 396 | `f9d9567b4b41...` |

**4,176 items over 795 banks**, 792 registers of padding (0.30% of the kept rank-1 bin), every
bank exactly filled, every block exactly one item, a per-family digest over the whole table, and
the ledger re-derived with the stock falling by exactly the bank count. What stays owed is read
from the pins rather than asserted: the complex supplier's certificate has **no key containing
`bank`** and its own status line says a literal globally renumbered operation program **is not
exported**, so the residual projectors the normalizer must move (C1's physical half) are not
there, and C2-C4 plus each child's frame/chain identity (C5-C7) follow the same gap. The *shape*
owed is pinned for the bit word at `references/pr219-run1/inputs/absorbed-occurrences.json`.

## Verification

* `verify.py` (exit 0) pins 27 files by sha256, rebuilds the whole complex-side ladder from
  pinned bytes, recomputes both paid moments per rung on the `10^-18` grid, runs the two
  unchanged 47-constraint assemblies with the adjacent grid points rejected, and reproduces
  #207's, #219's and #224's published grid points **exactly** (`a_complex` and both kappas
  asserted equal, not within a tolerance). The independent replica at my #208 pricing model's
  convention reproduces #208's own published rung-2 value `3541457/5*10^9`.
* A separate re-derivation written against the raw pinned bytes with plain integer and
  `Fraction` arithmetic -- no package module and no engine -- re-checks the row identities, the
  three volumes, stock-drop-equals-bank-count, the eligibility list `{11,16,20}`, the
  exhaustion, both kappa values, both ceiling landings, the gains and the next-step targets.
* The T1 scan is re-derived independently here, by brute force over every bank count instead
  of by the package's divisor logic: same pattern sets, same capacities, same obstruction. The
  padded schedule is re-checked as well: banks, blocks per bank, saturation, the padding draw,
  the stock drops 531/198/66, the padded top above the volume-criterion rows, and the
  exhaustion of the criterion afterwards.
* The width scan is re-derived as well: which widths are poseable, that only the pinned one is
  priced, and that the scan reproduces this PR's top at 66; and the instanced schedules are
  re-checked (795 banks, 4,176 items, 792 registers of padding, saturation, exactly-filled
  banks, the digests, the stock drops 531/198/66).
* Line endings are LF throughout (`schedule66.py`, `widths66.py`, `instantiate66.py`, the
  regenerated JSON, all sources) and every pin matches the stored bytes, so the checks pass on a
  fresh clone (verified in a clean worktree of this commit).
* Not run: upstream CI, and any contributor verifier other than the vendored #219 package
  invoked in place.

## Scope and limits

* **Not a witness**: the accounting, the padded bank schedule and the item addresses are
  certified; C1's physical half, C2-C4 and the inherited R1-R4 are open, so no normalizer, chart

prs.title: A stronger complex supplier: PR200's reuse pairing on the source-assisted v4 word, complex saving 7.0991·10⁻⁴ (+1.28% over #194; no new κ, bit binds)
prs.body:
Adds `research/source-assisted-v4-layer/` and one workflow; **no existing file changes, no new κ.** PR #194's pipeline (icekylinx's #184 source-assisted word on the PR #168 v4 modules, ikeboy's rebuild: aligned rewrite, frame flow, exact lift, contract, assembly) is kept unchanged except the **2,310 reuse pairs** of its physical layer; PR #168's operation frames are kept byte for byte. With PR #200's maximum-weight late compensated pairing (`pairs_mw.py`) in place of #168's pairing, the certified complex saving becomes

    a_C = 3549537 / 5000000000 = 7.0990740·10⁻⁴      (#194: 219037/312500000 = 7.0091844·10⁻⁴, **+1.28%**).

Composed with #200's bit supplier through #194's unchanged 47-constraint assembly, κ = 6768823/10¹⁰, the same as #202: the bit branch binds (effective 6.7734·10⁻⁴). The complex cap of every composition on this lineage rises from 7.0092·10⁻⁴ to 7.0991·10⁻⁴, which is the budget the banked bit rows (#205–#223) and the conditional rungs (#219/#224) are priced against; the exact-DFT exponent saving of #225 rises with it (follow-up there).

## What changes

The flow's child histogram depends on the reuse pairs it receives: a pair identifies a dead ungauged donor's register with a gauged recipient, and the equal-frame compression follows those identifications. #168's pairing is a maximum matching of donors to recipients in a fixed order; #200's is also a maximum matching with the same legality (donor ungauged and non-root, dead before the recipient's first operation, end frame inside the recipient gauge) but a different selection among the maximum matchings (transversal-matroid greedy with augmenting paths, donor weight the gain heuristic). Nothing else changes: frames, matching arcs, modules, local circuit, gauges, aligned rewrite, flow options; the kernel pairs the flow finds on this layer are recorded as #194 records its own.

| Physical layer on the aligned word (frames = #168's) | Flow root (float screen) | Certified complex saving |
|---|---:|---:|
| #168's pairing (as in #194) | 7.00918·10⁻⁴ | 219037/312500000 |
| #200's default pairing (`physical_opt.py:pairs`) | 7.09765·10⁻⁴ | 141953/200000000 (earlier commit) |
| widest-donor ordering, recipients reversed | 7.09882·10⁻⁴ | 887353/1250000000 (earlier commit) |
| **#200's maximum-weight pairing (`pairs_mw.py`)** | **7.09907·10⁻⁴** | **3549537/5000000000** |

Random pairings fall to 6.4–6.6·10⁻⁴. Descending the frames as well does not help: a screen over every single endpoint move on top of #168's frames finds no improving move, and the full descent cycle gives 7.0861·10⁻⁴ (an earlier commit of this PR, since superseded). The profile keeps #194's W = 12,052, rank mass 794,112 and deficit 1,320; only the child histogram changes.

## What is checked

`python3 -B research/source-assisted-v4-layer/verify.py` (about 80 s; numpy/scipy for the regeneration steps; -O refused):

1. **Pins.** `baseline-pr202.tar.gz` carries the 308 files of #202 (`8d8d67b`) the pipeline runs (#194's package, #184's decision/global scripts, the #168 v4 scripts, references and inherited witnesses, the Clifford frames note, #200's certificate, arithmetic and complex checker), each pinned by sha256 in `SOURCE.json` (`git show 8d8d67b:<path> | sha256sum`); the three witness files are pinned too.
2. **Regeneration.** The producer and the aligned rewrite run unchanged, including #168's physical layer and its own checks; the frames the package installs are byte for byte that layer's.
3. **Admission of this pairing.** #200's complete complex checker (`complex/physical.py` + `verify_fused.py`) re-executes the aligned word with the package's pairs: node spans inside nondegenerate frames, nested role chains, every alias read at its deadline after the donor's last operation with the donor's end frame inside the recipient gauge, target read chronology, exact adjoint, and every formal source/target/dirty column in both shear signs on an injective packed basis with an independent coefficient bound.
4. **Flow, lift, contract.** #184's flow on this layer with the package's kernel pairs; the exact lift (all local maps and inverse gate programs over the rationals, all coefficients dyadic; monotone, acyclic once-only reuse DAG with frame containment); the contract (13 checks) with the package's physical and kernel pairs as the frozen witnesses.
5. **Assembly.** #194's `assemble.py` with #200's bit certificate reproduces `certificate.json` exactly (exact fields only; the full run record is `report.json`); the next grid point is rejected by the unchanged assembly.

Run before opening: the verifier passes locally (Python 3.14, macOS, numpy 2.3.5, scipy 1.17.0) and in this PR's workflow on Python 3.11 and 3.13.

## Scope and limits

Conditional exactly as #194: the retained analytic, uniform-recursion, precision, weighted bit frames, fixed-tape routing, restored-row and all-size semantic interfaces remain hypotheses; the scalar replays and exact lifts are finite checks. #184's independent complex scalar transcript is not re-exported; the one-column identity is replayed by #200's checker on the pre-flow word and by the lift's inverse gate programs. The bit source is pinned to PR210 at df95878. For comparison, PR210's newer [c4c21244](https://github.com/eumemic/integer-mult-bounds/commit/c4c21244202a8f7538dae4a859cabcd1084a98cd) reports κ = 0.0006956735022133; the assembled κ here is approximately 1.154% higher. That newer head is not incorporated here; all 57 of its verification checks passed at the comparison check on 9 October.

Each independent bit helper crosses five disjoint address windows before one paid exterior completion at five times its entrance rank. All 2,279 completions and 120 copied-center calls remain charged. Source ownership, full forward/inverse words and rational partial-swap identities bind the construction to the actual helper. The rank-100 children require four recursion levels to halve the width.

The fresh source-to-certificate verifier passes all six mandatory stages: all 20,163 bit columns in both directions, physical chronology and copied-center lifetimes, 26,380 exact basis determinants, the complex scalar/label splice, finite accounting, three ordinary-bootstrap steps and all 47 strict outer constraints. Inputs remain unchanged.

Run the complete verifier:

```sh

python3 -B research/five-stage-source-bound-v8/verify.py --output /tmp/five-stage-v8-verification
```

The result retains the symbolic complex correctness, weighted compiler, complete-stream copying, restored-row, prime-supply, routing, precision/recovery, ordinary-leaf and all-size analytic hypotheses. No new Lean kernel build or practical multiplication benchmark is claimed.

## Approaches tested

- Completing helpers after every invocation gives a bit moment root near 0.000665572. Bundling each helper's five windows retains the paid corrections and improves that root to 0.000704197.
- The old fixed integer endpoint is unnecessarily restrictive; this construction proves its F₂ endpoint and bounds its own signed integer lift.
- The current four-bank/common-anchor interface with rank-one cross-bank shears needs five helper calls. A paid four-call workaround reaches only about 0.000305. Tested cross-port variants give relabelings or costly corrections; the tested three-bank model has an optimistic six-call root near 0.000524.

These are supplier moment results, not final multiplication exponents or global impossibility claims. Different helper actions and boundary geometry remain open.

prs.title: Conditional κ = 7.08582414684555347682e-4: fixed prime and finite leaves on PR237 banks
prs.body:
PR237 pays the full rare-case fallback using the conservative density `10^-16`. Its retained proof gives the sharper bound `2m^3/q` for any eligible **fixed** prime. Choose the classical prime `q=2^127−1`, keep every fallback call and all prime-dependent costs, and complete seven finite ordinary-leaf levels instead of three. The resulting conditional exponent is

**κ = 354291207342277673841 / 500000000000000000000000 = 7.08582414684555347682 × 10⁻⁴.**

| Construction | Conditional κ |
|---|---:|
| Reviewed main, `3b6b668`, PR186 | 6.61885549259598 × 10⁻⁴ |
| PR234, `af3fe331` | 7.03701743496697 × 10⁻⁴ |
| PR237 completed width-120 banks, `a8b0ce21` | 7.08582410781108 × 10⁻⁴ |
| This fixed-prime, seven-level refinement | **7.08582414684555347682 × 10⁻⁴** |

The exact gain over PR237 is `1951723673841 / 500000000000000000000000 = 3.903447347682 × 10^-12`. The new κ also exceeds PR237’s **unrounded** outer bound, so this is more than a reporting refinement. Higher bank-ladder pricing targets such as PR232 are not claimed to be completed witnesses or disproved here. No global optimality claim is made.

### Mathematical change and paid costs

- For `m=120`, use the positive exact density `rho=3456000/170141183460469231731687303715884105727`. Add the **full** `32m²` rank-one fallback for every rare edge; do not subtract the displaced good case.
- The unchanged banked profile has `W=261659`, `E=5916300`, rank mass `31346280`, deficit `52800` and maximum child rank `50`. All center-copy calls, charts, 177179 banks, the proper 60-colouring and selector bill `12227329044 < 2^40` remain paid.
- Two independent exact rational moment engines admit coarse saving `709084859748818674574370/10^27` and reject its adjacent point. The old `10^-16` density fails even the lower moment bound at this new saving.
- Seven acyclic completed levels satisfy `a_j=(1-c)c+c a_(j-1)`, starting at the unchanged `a0=384599/10^10`. Each ordinary callback uses only the completed predecessor; every cutoff gap is positive. Unknown primitive constants remain quantified. No coarse limiting oracle or width-dependent bootstrap depth is used.
- Retain the complex supplier, finite bridge, `eta=10^-12`, `beta=10^-9` and computational model. Check all 47 strict outer inequalities and seven margins. Reject the next `10^-24` κ point. Seven levels attain this paid family’s grid cap and improve on six by `85×10^-24`.
- The large prime produces very large **paid constants**. An explicit overcharge retains twelve copies of the original bill, every original routing family charged against the entire enlarged stock, and extra high-affine/stock/wrapper/matrix allowances for every bank selector. Its coefficient is below `2^80<q`, giving `B_bank(q)<q^14401`. Prime-dependent initialization, table scans, routing, binary-padding factor below `q²`, row stock and restoration stay in the retained constant/toll accounting.

The full argument and dependency limits are in `research/fixed-prime-bootstrap/PROOF.md`. It also notes PR237’s prose-only removed-rank-mass typo (`226200`); the actual removed mass is `225370`, and its executable certificate already uses the correct `31346280` profile.

### Reproduction and validation

The package pins every byte of PR234 and PR237’s bank package and their exact commits. Its default verifier runs **all six PR234 stages afresh**, then recomputes PR237’s charts, inverse factors, bank incidence/colouring, profile, selector bill and original arithmetic before deriving the refinement. Saved PASS receipts are not inputs. See the package README for checkout commands.

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/fixed-prime-bootstrap/requirements.txt
python -B research/fixed-prime-bootstrap/verify.py --parent-root /path/to/pinned-pr234 --banks-root /path/to/pinned-pr237
make paired-cube-verify
```

The separate pinned Lean 4.24.0/mathlib project kernel-checks the primality/value/size of `2^127−1` and the strict positive density improvement. Its reproduction commands use `lake update`, `lake exe cache get Mathlib.NumberTheory.LucasLehmer` and `lake env lean Prime.lean`. No `sorry` or `native_decide` is used; printed theorem axioms are only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. Python independently reproduces all 125 Lucas–Lehmer updates.

Local validation: fresh source replay, two independent moment enclosures, finite admission/outer47, negative controls, Lean prime/density proof, and `make paired-cube-verify` passed. All 16 existing main verification groups were also completed in this session. Native aggregate `make verify` initially stopped at Apple Clang’s unsupported OpenMP option; the remaining groups were run with a task-local serial adapter that only removes that flag for the pinned independent-case enumeration source, then with official Boost 1.88 headers for the later multiprecision checks. All 4073300 enumeration cases were retained; no existing source or assertion was changed. This does **not** represent an unmodified native aggregate `make verify` exit status of zero.

The added CI checks the full exact replay on Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 and the separate Lean prime proof. GitHub checks are distinct from the local evidence and may await maintainer workflow approval.

### Scope and attribution

This is a **conditional finite construction** under the same weighted q-local compiler, complete-stream movement, unit-pivot fallback, completed ordinary leaves, prime supply, complex symbolic identities/NetCert, Clifford synthesis, precision, restored-row and all-size recovery/reduction interfaces retained by PR234/237. The new Lean proof certifies prime eligibility and density only; it does not formalize the entire integer multiplication theorem or rebuild the full inherited complex Lean chain.

Credit: hcg890’s source-bound five-stage package; Jacob Sussman’s complex five-stage geometry; Rohan Arun’s PR237 banks and completed bootstrap arguments; Evan McKinney’s completed-bank endpoint; eumemic’s bit helper/gauges; Chafik Boukhalfa’s physical construction; Avi Eisenberg / ikeboy’s complex helper; mathlib’s Lucas–Lehmer contributors; all earlier contributors credited by the pinned notices. Apache-2.0 and original copied arithmetic headers are preserved.

prs.title: perf: check large rational frames with the smaller dual Gram matrix
prs.body:
`nondegenerate(U)` builds a Gram matrix with one row per basis vector, even when the frame fills almost the entire ambient space. This change checks large frames using their smaller Euclidean annihilator. A codimension-one frame needs a 1×1 matrix instead of an `(h-1)×(h-1)` matrix. All arithmetic remains exact and integral.

The two existing factored mixed-point cut customers (ambient dimensions 10 and 12) produce identical complete audit payloads and selected-frame hashes. Three fresh processes per variant give median complete batch wall time **3.380353 → 3.130144 seconds**, a **7.4% time reduction**. Median peak RSS is 92,288 → 92,744 KiB. This measures those two customers, including process startup, construction, scalar verification, rational cuts and compiled nesting. It does not establish a multiplication speedup or change κ.

### Exact criterion

The implementation extracts and reuses the integer kernel construction already in `orthogonal`. For `G=9I-J`, `h!=9`, and a full-row-rank Euclidean annihilator `A` of `U`, nondegeneracy of `G|U` is equivalent to invertibility of `A G^-1 A^T`. Since `G^-1=(I+J/(9-h))/9`, the checked integral matrix is

```text
(9-h) A A^T + (A1)(A1)^T.
```

The original direct check remains for small frames and ambient dimension nine. Dependent input rows still fail. Extracting the kernel helper preserves orthogonal-complement outputs.

### Validation and measurements

- **32 tests pass** across `test_rational_span_frames.py`, `test_mixed_point.py`, `test_block_carry.py`, `test_joint_return.py` and `test_early_sharing_and_centers.py`.
- The four new tests include **2,432 independent dense Fraction-oracle comparisons**, dimension-nine degeneracy, a valid negative Gram gap, dependent presentations and orthogonal-complement properties.
- All six complete baseline/patched benchmark payloads agree exactly; both customers certify their cuts and compiled forward/reverse nesting. A fresh patched-checkout rerun reproduces combined result SHA256 `faa0f9c0159a6e70d4e2cfcdb4012ea62ef350bd26b81312d11da4a770f8b218`.
- `git diff --check` passes. Base: `3b6b66891c0ac888521cf591fe306c6286601d4f`.
- CPython 3.12.3, Linux aarch64, CPU affinity and quota of one CPU, nice 15, 4 GiB memory limit. Filesystem caches were not flushed. Each sample is a fresh process; execution order was baseline 1, patched 1, patched 2, baseline 2, baseline 3, patched 3.

prs.title: Publish the bodies behind the pinned digests: the bit twin's gate now decides A2 and A3 on real exports (no new κ)
prs.body:
**No new κ.** Nothing here moves the number or the status: R1–R4 stay OPEN, the replay stays NOT RUN, and a partial run is never admissible. What changes is that the bit twin contract's gate stops being proved only on synthetic bodies: the bodies behind the digests the pinned certificates already publish now exist as files, and the gate decides two of the seven acceptance tests on them.

**Stacked on #232.** The branch is one commit (`33d23ec`) sitting on #232's head, so the diff against `main` carries #232's commits too: review the top commit alone, or land #232 first and this becomes a one-commit PR. The base is `main` because a fork branch cannot be a base branch here.

## What the drop holds

`research/complex-bank-run3/exports-bit/` — 10 of the twin's 15 required bodies, 8 of them anchored:

| export | bodies | state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **B1** the word, its frames, the selected gauge family | `word.json.gz` `1cb7e8ed…`, `frames.json.gz` `ad8e2705…`, `graph.json` `31a09a55…`, `kchron.json` `0fab548e…`, `profile.json` `c44ef864…`, plus the derived `index.json.gz` | complete |
| **B3** charts, incidence colouring, prime witnesses | `charts.json` `22662b85…`, `incidence.json` `76bff256…`, `prime-witnesses.json.gz` `612f0b91…`, plus the derived `charts.index.json.gz` | complete |
| **B2** bank blocks and the per-occurrence assignment | `assignment.json` | absent |
| **B4** columns of the banked word | `columns.json` | absent |
| **B5** the reject controls | `controls.json` | absent |
| **B6** envelope and integrity | `envelope.json`, `integrity.json` | absent |

The five word bodies and the witness body are the supplier's own bytes, each hashing to the digest its certificate already published. The two canonical streams do not exist upstream as files — PR205 published digests of streams — so they are **reproduced rather than obtained**: PR205's own packer, unmodified, run on this drop's word bodies re-derives both byte for byte, and the packer's recomputed `physical` block differs from PR205's published block in **none of its 26 fields** (`exports-bit/physical.rebuilt.json`). The declarations the bodies do not carry themselves come from two index bodies that `bitindex.py` derives from the bodies and the pinned certificates instead of typing in; neither is anchored, since an index is a declaration and the bodies it describes are what carry the digests.

## What the gate decides on it

`python3 -B importer66.py --contract export-contract-bit.json --exports exports-bit --partial` → **exit 4**:

| test | on the real drop |
| --- | --- |
| **A2** frame-record bijection | **PASS**, 9 checks: the six index counts, the bijection over 220 ids, the zero foreign-replay bound, the sibling digests |
| **A3** charts and factors | **PASS**, 17 checks: the colouring statistics, the denominator and numerator bounds, the banked row, the witness table |
| **A1** body hashes to the published digest | 17 checks pass, 0 fail — its eight anchors all match — and **not runnable**: the manifest that must hash every body arrives with B6 |
| **A6, A7** colouring and witnesses | 17 checks pass, 0 fail each, and **not runnable**: B5's controls are owed |
| **A4, A5** columns, per-child bijection | no check yet: B4's tables and B2's assignment are absent |

The default import still refuses the drop (**exit 2**), the replay is **NOT RUN** because the checker the contract pins (`4d7c86cd…`) is not supplied, and the run is kept as `bit-drop-report.json`.

## Four defects the real bytes exposed

Three in the harness, all fixed here:

* an absent body that an export *names* was recorded as a **failed check** instead of a missing datum, so a partial drop looked like a rejecting one — which is exactly what A6 and A7 showed before the fix; absence and failure are now distinct answers and only a present-but-wrong body fails;
* the anchored-digest loop and the manifest loop raised `FileNotFoundError` on an absent body instead of reporting it;
* the JSON report is now written as bytes: a redirected report is pinned by the manifest, and the default text stream translated its newlines, so the digest did not survive the round trip.

And one already in the record, which the clean-clone check found: the certificate stored the corpus scan's root as the **checkout's absolute path**, so `verify.py` could not rebuild the certificate anywhere but the directory it was authored in, and the commit carried a local directory name. The scan now reports its root relative to the package.

## Verify

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3
python3 -B verify.py                                             # exit 0: pins, rebuild, the drop, the gate
python3 -B importer66.py --self-test                             # 13 checks, 0 failed
python3 -B importer66.py --contract export-contract-bit.json --self-test
python3 -B importer66.py --contract export-contract-bit.json --exports exports-bit --partial   # exit 4
python3 -B importer66.py --contract export-contract-bit.json --exports exports-bit             # exit 2
```

`verify.py` now pins 47 files by sha256 (20 of this package's own, 16 vendored rung-1, and the drop's 11, reproduction evidence included), reads the drop back body for body and anchor for anchor, re-runs the stored partial report and compares it, and asserts the seventh self-test case on the real drop. All of it was run from a **clean clone** of this branch, where the certificate rebuilds identically.

python3 -B importer66.py --contract export-contract-rank3.json --self-test   # 13/13
cd references/pr219-run1 && python3 -B verify.py   # the vendored rung-1 package, in place
```

`verify.py` pins **62 files by sha256** — the 33 this package owns, the 16 the vendored rung-1
package of #219 carries, the 11 bodies of the bit drop and the six ranked heads of #233 — and
rebuilds the entire complex-side ladder: base, rung 2, rungs 3 and 4, both paid moments per rung,
the two 47-constraint assemblies with adjacent-grid rejection, the eligibility scan, the PR208
replica, the padded schedule, the instanced inventories, and all three export contracts (the
complex side's, the bit twin's with its 10-of-15 imported drop, and the rung's own). Then it
re-derives the rank-3 rung — the assignment from its addressing rule with zero padding, the
retained ledger, the bit leaf through #219's arithmetic, the point through the assembly rule — and
asserts both comparisons above. It reproduces PR207's, PR219's and PR224's published grid points
exactly.

The change adds exactly three things and edits nothing else:

* `research/complex-bank-run3/` — the package;
* `tests/test_complex_bank_run3.py` — nine isolated checks (the rebuild, all three contracts'
  self-tests, the refusal codes 2 and 4 with the rung publishing **0 of 6** required exports as
  bodies (ten bodies across them, all absent), the
  rank-3 price against the reviewed result, the rank-4 negative) plus three failure controls
  showing the digest gate fails closed on a tampered digest, a missing entry and a changed byte
  rather than passing vacuously; discovered by the existing `tests` group;
* `.github/workflows/complex-bank-ladder.yml` — the package's own job on 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14:
  `verify.py`, the vendored package's self-check, the three contracts' self-tests, then
  `git diff --exit-code`. It is path-filtered, so it costs nothing outside this package.

**Why a workflow instead of a Makefile target.** A target in the aggregate would be the local
convention, but `Makefile` and `.gitattributes` are *themselves recorded by other packages'
manifests* — `research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json` asserts the `Makefile` digest in `check_sources()`,
and the round-8, coordinated-frames, gaussian-parity and machine-transfer manifests record both
files. Editing either moves those digests and fails those groups' `git diff --exit-code`. A
path-filtered workflow of the package's own keeps this change to new files only, which is also why
it needs no `.gitattributes` carve-out: the package's byte-identical inputs are ordinary LF text
plus gzip containers, committed from an LF worktree and verified here by hashing the **blobs in
the index** (all 62 pinned paths) rather than the worktree.

No network, no Git credentials, no third-party packages, and no dependency on an unmerged branch
at run time: everything read is vendored and pinned, so the measurement re-runs in a clean clone
and in CI.

## It is row-dependent, and that is measured

`rank3stability.json`, re-derived by `verify.py → check_rank3_stability` and asserted:

* the rung exists on **two of the six ranked heads** of #233; the first four miss it by **one
  rank-3 child per copy** (nine registers over the ledger's three copies) — eligibility is the
  modular condition `22 | n₃`, a property of the row, not of the family;
* where it exists the **price is identical** (bit-bound), although the coarse saving differs;
* the **next rung's** eligibility is *not* stable — rank 4 is bankable only on the pinned head —
  and pricing it **moves κ not at all** (recorded as a negative);
* **no other width-66 row of this repository carries it**: nine distinct rows are scanned, and the
  pinned ladder row is eligible at `[11, 16, 20]` and misses rank 3 by 39 registers.

What the measurement does not cover: any head that does not exist yet (a new head is a new
measurement, not a silent pass), and rows outside this repository.

## What this does not claim

C1–C7 stay `OPEN` (the normalizer, the formal columns, the charts and prime witnesses, the envelope
parity and each child's frame/chain provenance) and R1–R4 are inherited verbatim from #219. No
importer exists for the rung: the row publishes **0 of 6** required exports as bodies — none of the
**ten bodies across them** (G1–G6) — so the gate refuses (exit 2) and reports in part when asked
(exit 4). That refusal is the correct answer, not a pass. The row's PR is
unmerged and pinned by digest, so a moved branch fails `check_manifest` closed and the measurement
must be re-taken. The 6,642 unpriced mixed tilings of the width-66 scan are not covered by the
measurement (two extremes per bank count are, and the artifact says so). Like every rung of this
ladder, this is a **conditional priced target**, not a witness, not an unconditional
multiplication theorem, not a practical multiplier, and not a Lean/kernel certificate.

## Attribution and provenance

Apache-2.0. The vendored inputs — PR219's rung-1 package, PR207's frontier certificate and PR233's
row certificate plus its earlier heads — are retained byte-identically with their notices and
credits (`NOTICE.md`, `SOURCE.json`); **PR233's contribution (chafreaky) is what this rung is priced
on** and is credited as such. Rung 2 and the ceiling argument are PR224's, the ladder and its
replica convention are PR208's, and the bank proof and engine chain are PR200/PR205/PR206/PR197/
PR184/PR168-v4/PR183/PR193's; nothing is re-implemented or restated as new. Prepared by Maxime
Fleury with Codebuff assistance.

**Supersedes #232**, which carries the same package without the rank-3 rung; #232 can be closed.

## Result

This PR composes the pinned PR233 source-assisted flow with the retained PR244 five-stage complex supplier by aligning each terminal center query with one retiring dirty coordinate.

rank mass = 1,613,040, deficit = 3,080, max child = 46
```

There are 22 terminal center queries, each the sum of nine independent physical coordinates. Eight additions replace one row of the identity by that query. The row replacement is invertible on arbitrary dirty data. Retain the pivot at rank 20 until the ordinary center cut, copy/read it, then execute its existing rank-2 final climb. Reverse the eight additions in cleanup.

# The source-assisted complex word of #233 as one explicit numbered program (gcert/1): reference-checked, and 7.547361·10⁻⁴ in the Lean-checked five-stage layout (no new κ)

One self-contained package, `research/gcert-program-233/`, with its own workflow. No existing file is changed.

#194's contract records that for its flow word "a literal globally renumbered operation program is not exported". This package exports it — for #194's word and for #233's — in Jacob Sussman's certificate format gcert/1 ([jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean](https://github.com/jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean), `tools/gx`): 12,052 numbered registers (1,320 sources, 1,320 targets, 9,412 slots), 18,248 frames, every addition explicit, the star scatter as a rule. His reference checker `gx.check1` (vendored unchanged) accepts both programs: nested frames of every register, block histogram, N = 262,944 unit moves, and the exact scalar identity (every target receives exactly its source; every source is restored).

| program | blocks / invocation | N | `gx.check1` | five-stage saving (m = 110, W = 14,692) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #194's word (control; the circuit Sussman rebuilt from #193) | 70,169 — **equal to his published histogram in every class and rank** | 262,944 | accepted | 7474547/10¹⁰ (his Lean figure; his `gxdry.py` reproduces it on this file) |
| **#233's word** | 69,683 | 262,944 | accepted | **7547/10⁷ with exact bounds here (7548/10⁷ rejected); 7547361/10¹⁰ by his mirror** |

**Lean.** With his generators unchanged (`gxgen.py`, `gxrate.py`) the #233 certificate yields 41 Lean modules; `lake build` of all of them passed (Lean 4.34.1, 9,229 jobs, exit 0, "declaration uses `sorry`" for the two challenge modules only), ending in

    'OAI.PowerSaving.WHT.wht_main_block_B2Gp233x' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

i.e. the Walsh–Hadamard transform in O(n (log n)^(1 − 7547361/10¹⁰)) in his framework, against 1 − 7474547/10¹⁰ for the circuit of #193 (+0.97%). `tools/Compare.lean` and the Fourier seam are being run and are reported in jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean#2 (both `Compare.lean` runs pass; the Fourier transform of every length at 1 − 7547360/10¹⁰ through a copy of his seam), not here; this package itself runs only his Python reference checker.

**What this is and is not.** #233's ledger is unchanged: the program's per-invocation histogram 3(x + y + s + c) + 2v·e₂ is exactly #233's certified child histogram, so this is the word #233 certifies through #184's lift and contract, now as one transcript that a third-party checker reads end to end. κ does not change (the bit supplier binds in every current assembly). The emitter (`gcert_emit.py`) has no proof of its own; it is validated by the control (it reproduces, class by class, a certificate rebuilt independently by Sussman from #168's and #193's data files) and by the ledger identity with #233.

## Argument (PROOF.md)

The input is #184's tool chain on the aligned word: `complex_frame_flow.py --witness` (the flow DAG: one node per (phase, frame), the value channels on every edge, births, retirements, reads) and `exact_complex_flow_lift.py` (at every node an invertible completion as elementary row operations, and the coordinates of every read). The emitter numbers one slot per physical flow coordinate and, node by node at the node's frame, emits the source copies, the reads (side/deferred responses ±1/2 as in `contract_v4.py`; a centre read formed in place in a retiring input slot), the completion as single-target fan-outs (the lift stores the operations taking Q to I, replayed in reverse; a swap relabels, a scaling changes a slot's unit as his `gxconv.py` does), and names every pass-through coordinate as an extra register so that the block histogram is the flow's ledger. After phase 2 it applies #144's K blocks (1 − J/2 per parity class at the parity 3-space), reads each mixed source into its antipodal target at the target's cap frame, and undoes the K blocks — #194's contract read as a program.

## Verify

    python -m pip install numpy==2.3.5 scipy==1.17.0      # only for the pinned regeneration of #202's word
    python3 -B research/gcert-program-233/verify.py        # about 95 s locally; -O refused

Checks every pin of `SOURCE.json`, rebuilds the 308 pinned files of #202 from the vendored #233 package, regenerates the aligned word, runs flow and lift for both layers, emits both programs, runs `gx.check1`, compares the histograms (control: his `pr193-blocks.json`; result: #233's `certificate.json`), certifies the five-stage moment at 7547/10⁷, and compares the regenerated certificates byte for byte with `certificates/` and the run with `certificate/expected.json`. * No κ change; the complex cap of this lineage is unchanged at #233's 7.0991·10⁻⁴ in the three-stage assembly and 7.547·10⁻⁴ in the five-stage layout (#225 Proposition E, #250's ledger).
* The emitter supports the flows of #194 and #233 (no source-control vertices, no kernel reuse in these two words); other layers may need the source-control branch.

**Full replay: PASS.** `verify.py --output /tmp/descent-source527-verification` completed all eight mandatory stages with package integrity unchanged in 347 s: `{"status": "PASS_IMMUTABLE_PARITY_REGAUGED_DESCENT_SOURCE527_FIVE_STAGE_BANKED_CONSTRUCTION", "manifest_sha256": "00119cd179dcc2c837c0c9bf53f32f5131a9c88e278f7aad41e84179be5e2a42", "files": 133, "kappa": "710436534421701/1000000000000000000", "fresh_stages": ["banks", "bit", "complex", "finite", "math", "primes", "raw", "scalar"], "inputs_unchanged": true}`.

## Change

A second exact frame retiming of #251's regauged source527 ADD word. Twenty-five internal `forward_gate` ADD frames (25 of 786,623 gates) are reassigned by local descent on the concave paid-rank objective Σ r·ln(120/r), using only frames already present on the operands' chains. The local paid histogram changes by {2: −2, 4: +24, 5: −48, 6: +25, 11: −1, 13: +2, 17: −1}: one local recursive call per helper invocation disappears at unchanged rank mass 433,953. The literal construction keeps 24 replicas, stock 521,425 and deficit 105,600 with 11,792,160 paid calls (was 11,792,280); the per-replica bank call count is 491,340 (was 491,345). Banks, charts, entrances, prime witnesses, the scalar word and every endpoint are unchanged.

Why this is the whole retiming budget: for the window (prev, cur, next) of a register the objective is concave in dim(cur), so each gate is optimal at either the minimal frame (join of the operands' previous frames and their source spans) or the maximal frame (meet of the next frames). On #251's word 99.7 % of gates have those two coincide with the current frame; the fully eager (greatest-fixpoint) assignment is worse (Σ r·ln(120/r) = 1.1817 × 10⁶ vs 1.1374 × 10⁶), and block moves (raising or lowering whole runs between ascents) are blocked by partner chains or source spans. The 25 gates are what remains.

## Verification

`descent_transform.py` consumes the frozen `descent-selection.json` (record bindings, old basis hashes, explicit rational new bases) and, like PR244's `retiming_transform.py`, rebuilds every MOVE from the selected gate needs and independently checks: nested chains, fixed source/dirty/target endpoints, nondegenerate endpoint bases, both reflected annihilator ledgers, unchanged COPY lifetimes, the byte-identical scalar/COPY projection, and the expected histogram delta and rank mass. In addition it recomputes the exact **integer** source span of every non-target operand from the actual scalar word and requires it inside the new frame (the inherited word satisfies this invariant for all 1.57 M non-target operand instances; targets live in cap coordinates and are excluded, as in the inherited word). `raw_ledger.rebind_descent` recounts the five-stage profile (493,656 calls, rank mass 2,830,840, deficit 4,400); `bank_check` and `verify.py` require the new counts and κ.

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/five-stage-source527-banks/requirements.txt
python3 -B research/five-stage-source527-banks/verify.py --output /tmp/descent-source527-verification
```

Python 3.11+, SymPy 1.14.0, a new output directory outside the package; no network.

Before this PR was opened, the new transform stage passed inside the full verifier (`PASS concave descent retiming 25 gates 95452 paid calls 885276 records`) and the κ was reproduced with the package's own moment/outer engines (`710436534421701/10^18`); the complete eight-stage replay with the final package is in progress.

## Scope and credits

Exactly #251's hypotheses and conditional interfaces (all-size compiler, weighted chart, restored rows, selectors, routing, prime supply, precision/recovery, complex symbolic correctness, analytic reduction). No new Lean build or practical benchmark is claimed.

**Research closeout — Draft retained; no current-record claim.** This is an exact fixed-prime arithmetic refinement of [PR #259](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/259). It inherits #259's finite physical construction and changes the conditional bit-supplier calculation only.

## Result and contribution boundary

```text
PR #259: 142205877210807 / 200000000000000000
PR #261: 711029389987426878345881 / 10^27
Exact gain: 3933391878345881 / 10^27
```

At `m = 120`, the certificate fixes `q = 2^127 - 1`, uses rare-class density `rho = 3456000/q < 10^-16`, and charges the complete `32m^2` rare-child fallback. It retains #259's 518 pivot entrances, four cuts, physical frames, routes, roles, replicas and lifetimes unchanged. It makes no new physical-DAG saving.

The finite arithmetic replay regenerates the cohort profile and invoice, uses two rational interval engines for the coarse endpoint, checks eight finite levels, 47 strict outer constraints and seven margins, and rejects the adjacent `10^-27` grid point. The fresh finite coefficient is `62639910650427201 < 2^80 < q`; selector, chart, normalizer, signed-prefix and inherited physical costs remain charged.

**Attribution:** Dugongue's #259 provides the inherited multi-cut physical witness and invoice; its pinned source lineage comes from #249. The fixed-prime approach credits Nespoli #235 and Arun #252, with #255/#258 refinements acknowledged in the certificate history. The exact recomputation, certificate, documentation and workflow integration in this PR were prepared by sennemmi with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Upstream authorship, source notices and license files are retained; the added package carries its stated Apache-2.0 license.

## Incremental review path

The full PR comparison against `main` is large because it carries the upstream research lineage: GitHub reports 422 changed files and 1,707,820 additions. Removing inherited source or receipts would weaken provenance or replayability, so this closeout keeps them intact. The independently reviewable increment is exactly one commit over #259 SHA `a53ec0ca4d59634f16630dd16adf035c9f12595c` at head `d2c63486d895860a65f25b80a51f4b2ec4f3c6ef`: [compare #259 to #261](https://github.com/sennemmi/integer-mult-bounds/compare/a53ec0ca4d59634f16630dd16adf035c9f12595c...d2c63486d895860a65f25b80a51f4b2ec4f3c6ef). prs.title: Conditional κ = 8.339545889388e-4 on #233's row: the bit word's own retained ledger banked a second time (B1 open, not a witness)
prs.body:
# Conditional κ = 8.339545889388e-4 on #233's row: the bit word's own retained ledger banked a second time, which spends the whole complex branch

**κ = 416977294469409/500000000000000000 = 8.339545889388e-4**, and `binding = complex` for the
first time on this ladder: **+14.5981% over #246's rung** (`1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` =
7.277211262868e-4). The schedule those absorptions need is **measured here, not merely owed**: the
retained bit row is re-derived, every family's two readings of the bank criterion are applied, the
leader's three absorptions are applied by hand -- a whole family out, the padding per bank drawn
out of the singleton bin, the stock falling by exactly the bank count -- and the point is priced
through the unchanged 47-constraint assembly. The claim is still a **priced target on a scheduled
row**: conditional on C1-C7 and on #219's inherited R1-R4, whose PRs are unmerged and pinned by
digest. Not a witness.

Package: `research/complex-bank-run3/`, self-contained on the branch, extended in place. It vendors
#219's rung-1 package byte-identically under `references/pr219-run1/` and #207's frontier
certificate and #233's row, and pins **66 files by sha256**.

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3 && python3 -B verify.py
```

## Result

The ladder has been **bit-bound since rung 2**, and the leaf that bounded it had been treated as a
constant of #219's word. It is not one: the rung-1 retained row is a ledger with thirteen more
bankable families in it, and every absorption lowers the retained mass, so the leaf itself moves.
The rank-3 rung on #233's row (`bitrung.py`'s baseline, and #246's point):

| rung on #233's row (head `109a857`, pinned by digest) | value |
| --- | --- |
| banks | 4,086 (1,362 per copy), 22 rank-3 blocks × 3 registers, **padding 0** |
| retained coarse saving | `417325324839139/5·10^17` = 8.346506496783e-4, the next 10⁻¹⁸ grid point up excluded |
| budget | the bit leaf `7.282510899902e-4` — **bit-bound**, so the complex supplier did not bind |
| **κ** | **`1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` = 7.277211262868e-4**, `binding = bit` |

The screen: thirteen of the retained row's 21 families can leave into whole width-72 banks or into
the padded schedule a bank admits, so every rung of up to three of them is priced (13 + 78 + 286 =
**377 rungs**), by the vendored interval-moment engine. The leading rows, exactly as `bitrung.json`
records them (the gains are the recorded kappas divided by the rank-3 rung's):

| absorb | banks | retained W | bit leaf | kappa | binding | gain over #246 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| rank 20 | 5,280 of 3 blocks + 12 registers | 45,006 | 7.957727174054441e-4 | `397569983356707/500000000000000000` = 7.95139966713414e-4 | bit | +9.2644% |
| ranks 4, 20 | 6,878 (rank 4 exactly filled, rank 20 as above) | 43,408 | 8.337650404202950e-4 | `104133806924797/125000000000000000` = 8.33070455398376e-4 | bit | +14.4766% |
| rank 21 alone | 15,018 of 3 blocks + 9 registers | 35,268 | 9.319873169802724e-4 | `416977294469409/500000000000000000` = 8.339545889388e-4 | **complex** | +14.5981% |
| **ranks 7, 8, 20 (the leader)** | **7,342** (1,224 of 10 blocks + 2 registers; 838 of 9, exact; 5,280 of 3 + 12) | **42,944** | **8.349765438523530e-4** | **`416977294469409/500000000000000000` = 8.339545889388e-4** | **complex** | **+14.5981%** |

| against | value | gain | asserted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the rung below, on the same row (#246) | `1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` = 7.277211262868e-4 | **+14.5981%** | asserted, by `verify.py`, offline |
| the frontier this package prices against (#207) | `1366380910073/2·10¹⁵` = 6.831904550365e-4 | +22.07% | the comparison is asserted, by `verify.py`, offline |
| this package's previous top (the padded rung 4) | `711599961413937/10^18` = 7.11599961413937e-4 | +17.19% | stated |
| the record published on `main` (#186) | `330942774629799/5·10¹⁷` = 6.61885549259598e-4 | +26.0% | stated, dated |
| the highest other open claim at the time of writing (#257) | 7.104652045e-4 | +17.4% | stated, dated |

The two *asserted* rows cannot drift: `verify.py → check_bit_rung` re-derives both numbers from the
pinned bytes and asserts the comparisons (there, the two gains are exact quotients of recorded
values). The three *stated* rows are dated observations of this package and of the queue, and are
labelled as such.

## Why the bit leaf was the lever, and what the criterion is

#219's rung 1 absorbs the rank-22 family of the PR200/PR205 packed bit word into 6,116 whole
width-72 banks and leaves a retained row of `W = 50,286` roles, rank mass 3,614,784, deficit 5,808
and 857,622 children over 21 ranks, whose certified paid saving -- bootstrapped through #185's
three-level chain -- is the leaf `7.282510899902e-4`. Every reading of this package so far priced
*that* row as it stands, which is why the earlier sections concluded that `7.5e-4`, `8e-4` and
`1e-3` were out of reach on this word. `bitrung.py` prices the row one rung further: a second family
can leave the **same** retained ledger into whole banks, the way the rank-22 bin did, and the leaf
rises by **+14.6550%** to `8.349765438523530e-4`.

The criterion is rung 1's, restated on the retained row and read two ways, because the two readings
are not the same rung:

* the **volume** reading: the family's own volume is a whole number of width-72 banks,
  `72 | rank * n_rank`;
* the **padded** reading: what a bank can actually host when the rank does not divide the width --
  `capacity = 72 // rank` blocks of the family plus `72 mod rank` registers of padding in every
  bank, so it needs saturation (`capacity | n_rank`) and a retained bin that can supply the padding.
  This is T1's padded schedule, one word over, and the module checks rather than asserts that each
  padded step needs its own bank count: rank 7's volume reading prices 1,190 banks where its
  schedule needs 1,224 (`1,190 × 10 = 11,900 < 12,240` items), and rank 20's prices 4,400 where its
  schedule needs 5,280 (`4,400 × 3 = 13,200 < 15,840` items).  The rung prices the schedule, not the
  accounting.

The schedule keeps the retained row's identity: `W = 42,944`, rank mass 3,086,160, deficit 5,808,
756,192 children over 18 families, the stock dropping by exactly the 7,342 banks, and **65,808
registers of padding in all** drawn as a partial removal from the singleton bin -- exactly what T1
does on the complex side.

**The binding side changes here, and that is the result.** The leader's leaf sits *above* the
complex branch it has to clear (the rung reaches `1.000390455784346` of that branch), so the budget
is the branch `417325324839138999999999582174675160861/5·10⁴¹` and the kappa is
`416977294469409/500000000000000000`, the last `10⁻¹⁸` grid point at or below #233's row's complex
ceiling `417325324839139/500417325324839139`. So the wall moves rather than disappears: every
further bit rung is capped by the complex side, and the next increment is the complex supplier
again -- or a new bit word that lifts the leaf without spending the branch.

## The plateau: 108 rungs, one point

**108 of the 377 screened rungs** price `416977294469409/500000000000000000`, because once a rung's
bit leaf clears the complex branch the budget is the branch and every such rung lands on the same
point: the screen is not choosing among them, the cap is. The point therefore does not depend on
which rung is quoted; only the cheapest bank count does, and the package's own leader rule (highest
kappa, ties broken by the fewest banks, then by the sorted ranks) is why the claimed rung is ranks
7, 8 and 20 at 7,342 banks rather than rank 21 alone (15,018 banks) or ranks 4 and 21 (16,616).
Both sides of the plateau are asserted: every rung that carries the point is complex-bound, and
every bit-bound rung lands strictly below it.

## What proves it

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3
python3 -B verify.py            # check: pins, rebuild, compare with certificate.json, bitrung.json and occurrences-bitrung.json
python3 -B bitrung.py           # the measurement: writes bitrung.json
python3 -B bitinstance.py       # B1: the item maps, bank tables, padding draw and induced ledger
python3 -B importer66.py --self-test   # the harness's own thirteen cases
cd references/pr219-run1 && python3 -B verify.py   # the vendored rung-1 package, in place
```

`verify.py` pins **66 files by sha256** -- the 37 this package owns (bitrung.py, bitinstance.py and
their two artifacts among them, and the ranked heads of #233), the two upstream certificates it is
priced against (#207's frontier and #233's row), the 16 the vendored rung-1 package of #219 carries
and the 11 of the bit drop -- and
rebuilds the whole complex-side ladder (base, rung 2, rungs 3 and 4, both paid moments per rung,
the two 47-constraint assemblies with adjacent-grid rejection, the eligibility and width scans, the
PR208 replica, the padded schedule, the instanced inventories and all three export contracts), then
checks the new rung: `verify.py → check_bit_rung` re-derives the rung-1 retained row **from the
pinned packed certificate with plain integer and `Fraction` arithmetic, no package module and no
engine**, re-checks every family's two readings, applies the leader's three absorptions by hand
(whole family out, the padding per bank out of the singleton bin, the stock falling by exactly the
bank count), re-runs the bootstrap chain and the assembly rule, computes the kappa on the grid
below the bound, asserts the leader's minimality on the plateau and both comparisons above, and
compares the whole measurement with `bitrung.json`. `verify.py -> check_bit_instancing` does the
same for B1: it rebuilds the instancing, recomputes both digests from the addressing rule rather
than trusting them, re-checks the padding as a partial removal from the singleton bin, asserts that
the induced ledger is the row `check_bit_rung` prices, and asserts that the pins still export no
block and no occurrence of these three families. verify.py reproduces #207's, #219's and #224's
published grid points, and the rank-3 rung's own, exactly -- the bit rung's complex branch *is* the
rank-3 rung's recorded coarse saving, which `check_bit_rung` asserts rather than assumes.

The package's own path-filtered workflow (`.github/workflows/complex-bank-ladder.yml`, 3.11, 3.13,
3.14: `verify.py`, the vendored package's self-check, the three contracts' self-tests, then
`git diff --exit-code`) and the repository test module (`tests/test_complex_bank_run3.py`, which now
also asserts this rung's kappa, its complex binding, the leader and the plateau) cover it. The
change extends the package's own files (`bitrung.py`, `bitrung.json`, `verify.py`, `pins.py`,
`run3.py`, `obligations.json`, `README.md`, the regenerated `SOURCE.json` and `certificate.json`) and
the test module; the pinned vendored inputs, the other rungs' artifacts and the three export
contracts are untouched.

## Status

* **B1 is `INVENTORY_INSTANCED_AT_SCHEDULE_LEVEL`** (`obligations.json`), the bit side's second
  absorption: its schedule half is **instanced** -- `bitinstance.py` gives every one of the 35,622
  items of ranks 7, 8 and 20 a bank, a block and an offset, fills every bank exactly with the
  family's blocks plus the padding it draws, names the 65,808 registers of that padding item by
  item out of the retained singleton bin (digested, `1828/10481` of the bin), digests each family's
  bank table, and re-derives the ledger the absorptions induce (stock 50,286 -> 42,944, rank mass
  3,614,784 -> 3,086,160, 857,622 children -> 756,192 over 18 families) from the pinned packed
  certificate. Its **provenance half is open**, and machine-read rather than asserted: the pins
  carry no key containing `block` or `occurrence` for this word -- the packed certificate's single
  `assign` key is its own rejection control -- so each of those 35,622 items has an address and no
  identity, and the shape owed is #219's rank-22 inventory, key for key (`H`, `H_center`, `Y`,
  `src`). The no-other-bin-moves proof is owed with it.
* **R1-R4** (inherited verbatim from #219) and **C1-C7** are unchanged: the normalizer, the formal
  columns, the charts and prime witnesses, the envelope parity and each child's frame/chain
  provenance. The absorbed families need the new residual types the suppliers' proofs reserve,
  exactly as the complex rungs do, and the rows are pinned by digest to unmerged branches.
* No witness, no completed finite witness, no unconditional multiplication theorem, no practical
  multiplier, and no Lean/kernel certificate is claimed -- here or anywhere in this ladder.

## Scope and limits

* The measurement is over the retained bit ledger of #219's rung-1 word at width 72, and over
  rungs of up to three families. Longer rungs are not screened; on this cap they cannot change the
  point, but that is not measured.
* The whole-bank volume condition is necessary and is what the built rungs use; it is not
  sufficient, which is exactly why the padded schedule exists and why the module records where the
  volume-criterion bank count fails to host its own items.
* A moved branch fails `check_manifest` closed and the measurement must be re-taken: the head of
  #233's row is pinned by digest.
* Nothing here bounds any other bit or complex lever: a different word, width or frame layout is
  not priced.

## Attribution and provenance

Apache-2.0. The vendored inputs -- #219's rung-1 package, #207's frontier certificate and #233's row
certificate plus its earlier heads -- are retained byte-identically with their notices and credits
(`NOTICE.md`, `SOURCE.json`); **#233's contribution (chafreaky) is the row this result is priced
on** and is credited as such, and #233's source-assisted row and #246's rank-3 rung are what make
the complex branch the productive side at this point. Rung 2 and the ceiling argument are #224's,
the ladder and its replica convention are #208's, the bank proof and the engine chain are
#200/#205/#206/#197's (Chafik Boukhalfa and the #197/#205 line), #184/#168-v4's (icekylinx,
eumemic), #183's and #193's, and #185's bootstrap chain is what the bit leaf is read through;
nothing is re-implemented or restated as new. Prepared by Maxime Fleury with Codebuff assistance.
