prs.title: Deep retiming
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

got a strict improvement over the current record, but it is small.

New result: κ = 144727257636539/(2·10¹⁷) ≈ 7.236362881826950×10⁻⁴, up from PR #279’s 7.235715900074640×10⁻⁴. That is +0.0089%, about a tenth of what #279 itself gained

## Validation
clone repo
cd ~/Desktop/integer-mult-bounds
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r research/five-stage-gen4-deep-retiming/requirements.txt   # installs sympy==1.14.0
make deep-retiming-verify

## further explanation

# Register-level retiming of the gen4 five-stage word

**κ = 144727257636539/(2·10¹⁷) = 7.23636288182695 × 10⁻⁴**, conditional, bit supplier binding.
This is **+6.47 × 10⁻⁸ (+0.0089 %)** over PR279 (7.23571590007464 × 10⁻⁴). It is a small, strict
improvement of the exponent saving, not a runtime claim.

## What changed

Only `descent-selection.json` and the counts pinned to it. The package is otherwise PR279's
`five-stage-gen4-banks`: the same bit word, scalar program, banks, entrances, charts, complex supplier,
moment engines and outer assembly. `descent_transform.py` is byte-identical and applies the new frozen
selection under exactly the contract it already enforced for PR279:

- every retimed ADD gate gets a nondegenerate frame (G = 9I − J Gram test);
- the gate frame contains the exact integer source span of every non-target operand after the gate;
- every register's frame chain stays nested from its unchanged initial frame to its unchanged final frame;
- COPY lifetimes, copied-centre scatters and every gate inside a copy window are untouched;
- the scalar/COPY projection is byte-identical, and both reflected annihilator ledgers are rebuilt.

The selection retimes **1,093** ADD gates (PR279: 880), removing **922** local recursive calls (PR279: 880)
at unchanged rank mass 425,742. The five-stage profile has 482,936 calls (PR279: 483,146) and rank mass
2,809,600. Local paid-histogram delta against the parity-fused word:

```
{1: −1784, 2: +855, 3: −5, 4: +29, 5: −65, 6: +2, 7: +70, 8: −33, 9: −35, 10: +59,
 11: +5, 12: +7, 13: −24, 14: −3, 20: −880, 21: +1760, 22: −880}
```

The 880 source-pair retimings of PR279 are all retained; the further changes are on dirty-register chains.
Bit coarse saving 362080158564507/(5·10¹⁷) ≈ 7.24160317129014 × 10⁻⁴ (PR279: 7.24095525220252 × 10⁻⁴);
the adjacent 10⁻¹⁸ grid point is rejected as before.

## How the selection was found

The cost model is exact: along a nested chain a step is paid iff its dimension strictly increases, with
first-order weight r·ln(120/r); total mass per register is fixed by its endpoints, so only the number and
split of steps can change. Three searches were run on the parity-fused word (scripts in `search/`):

1. **Single-gate neighbour moves** (re-use an operand's adjacent frame). Run globally, this reproduces
   PR279's 880 gates exactly and finds nothing else: PR279 is a local optimum for that neighbourhood.
2. **Register block moves.** For one register at a time, a DP over its whole gate sequence chooses
   frames from the partner's adjacent frames, the register's own frames and their joins. The partner's
   cost change is charged inside the DP, and every accepted move is re-checked by exact recount of all
   affected chains.
3. **Raise/lower cascades.** Raise one gate to a later frame and close forward by joins (or lower and
   close backward by meets), accepting only an exact decrease.

All searches converge to the same optimum from independent random orders.

## Scoped negative results

These are reported so others need not repeat them.

**Frame retiming is nearly exhausted for this word.** Forward-minimal frames (joins of operand states
and spans) and backward-maximal frames (meets of future constraints) coincide at most gates, because
dirty registers accumulate binary-tree sums whose spans pin frames from below while shared side roots
and partner carriers pin them from above. A decoupled per-register DP bound suggests +3.35 %, but that
ignores partner coupling; with coupling, three different neighbourhoods all stop at +0.009 %.

**Target and source chains are structurally fixed.** Targets step 0→21→22→23 (or 0→20→21→22→23)
because shared side roots deliver to several targets whose 23-dimensional caps meet in a 22-dimensional
space. Delivering the last share at a target's own cap would need a different delivery order, which
would change the byte-identical scalar program.

**More compensated reuse pairs are impossible in this word.** Removing one dirty register is worth about
60 frame merges (≈ 6–8 × 10⁻⁵ relative each), so this was the most valuable lever examined. All 1,760
rank-21 gauges are eligible recipients, but the maximum matching is 1,494 even **ignoring timing**: the
binding constraint is donor-frame containment. Only 2,420 of 8,829 dead registers end inside any rank-21
gauge frame, and the 20 components of the compatibility graph have Hall deficits summing to exactly 266.
No rank-20 gauge has a single frame-compatible donor. A larger matching therefore needs a different word
(more donors with small final frames), not a different matching or schedule.

## Scope

Unchanged from PR279: conditional on the retained all-size compiler, common weighted chart, restored
rows, selectors, tape routing, prime supply, precision/recovery, complex symbolic correctness and the
analytic reduction. The finite replay is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

Prepared with Anthropic Claude assistance (Claude Opus 5.5); Apache-2.0. Builds on PR279 (Rohan Arun),
PR276 (DreamingOfClouds) and every source credited in `NOTICE.md`.

prs.body:
## e8-clean-padding: bank padding fused into clean-sink helper climbs on #390's E8 complex program; conditional κ = 1.000385913854264e-3

**κ = 125048239231783/1.25·10¹⁷ ≈ 1.000385913854264 × 10⁻³**, which is +1.65691·10⁻⁷ (+0.0166 %) over #390 (1.000220222889528e-3). It is complex-bound:

- b = 40055507598519/4·10¹⁶ ≈ 1.001387690e-3, up from #390's 1.001221667e-3.
- The bit side is our #382 word (c ≈ 1.006907e-3 > b). #390's larger c gives the same κ.

### What is new
#377's banks pay a separate rank-1 C child on coordinate 72 to complete each width-73 bank; #390 keeps 3,123 per stage.

We fuse that padding into the final climb of a helper in the same bank: (M₁·C_[d]·M₂) ⊗ C₇₂ = (M₁⊗I)(C_[d]⊗C₇₂)(M₂⊗I), so rank d + rank 1 becomes one rank d+1 child. This is legal only if nothing touches the helper afterwards.

- **#352's cleanup bracket rules it out for every helper.** In #378's word all 775 lifting helpers receive x → helper gates, and those can only be undone at FULL, after the final climb.
- **#390's dirty-preconditioned bracket permits it for zero-row sinks.** That bracket is target precancellation y −= B·A⁻¹·h, helper prewhitening h ← A⁻¹h, and FULL repair of N_r·x only. A helper with N_r = 0 is never touched after its final climb.

We search #390's word for **free** sinks: an exact combination of helpers already at the helper's exact frame, applied after its last influence on y. The search finds exactly three: 301, 324 and 387, each with final lift rank 2. For 301 the gates are `h276 += h1021/2; h301 −= h276/2; h276 −= h1021/2` (frame 731), with analogous gates for the other two (frames 744 and 759). They need no climbs and leave the paid local histogram unchanged.

Each invocation then has three rank-2 + rank-1 pairs become rank-3. The 96 fused occurrences per stage sit in 96 distinct ordinary banks of #390's own assignment (routes fix coordinate 72). Profile delta: {1: −864, 2: −864, 3: +864}. Live (58,899), deficit (9,984), max child (48) and halving degree (2) are unchanged.

The 16 additional candidates that need paid donor advances (the same count #390 reports) all lower b, so none is used.

### Checks (`bash research/e8-clean-padding/verify.sh /fresh/dir`; Python 3.11+, stdlib only)
- **Pins:** git-blob pins on #390's `prefix18`, `sink-audit` and `prewhite`, #378's word, Sussman's gx, and #382's word.
- **Words:** Sussman's `gx.check1` (E0–E7, exact scalar) and the gxcore mirror on #390's prefix18 word, on #390's main word (+355/403) and on ours. The x/y operator rows and retained totals of ours equal #378's, and the five sink rows are exactly zero.
- **Regeneration:** the free-sink search over all 773 lifting helpers regenerates exactly our gates.
- **Bracket:** our reimplementation of #390's bracket reproduces #390's `prewhite.json` gate for gate.
- **Local program:** the fused program, in both orientations, is replayed on all 1,023 live columns. The replay checks private work erased, common exact labels, and no event on a fused sink after its padded climb. Five mutation controls are rejected.
- **Price:** #390's b and κ are reproduced from its own emitted program. Ours is priced with both PR #315 engines (adjacent grid point excluded) and PR #315's outer assembly (47 strict constraints).

### Conditions
- **Re-opened, with the replacement argument in PROOF.md:**
  - #352's emitter/validator chronology (#390 had already replaced it);
  - #377's padding as a separate end-of-schedule cover sweep, for 96 banks per stage. This uses the retained arbitrary-dirt invocation property, and the compiler admitting a C child spanning local coordinates plus window coordinate 72.
- **Not re-run:**
  - #390's rank-8 endpoint adapters, Clifford edge audits and finite invoice. We add 9 scalar gates per invocation, the bracket sizes change from 1,550/7,800 to 1,556/7,776, and no new local edge is used;
  - all of #377/#352's retained interfaces;
  - #382's bit admissions.

This is a conditional finite construction, not a formal verification.

### Credits
- **Dugongue (#390):**
  - the prefix rewrites;
  - the dirty-preconditioned bracket, which is what makes cleanup-free sinks possible;
  - sinks 355/403;
  - the heterogeneous banks.
- **jacklightChen (#377):** the nine-stage component, banks and padding.
- **#352:** the local invocation, compiler and emitter.
- **Jacob Sussman:** the E8 unit and gx/gxcore.

- **PR #315:** the engines and outer assembly.
- **Ours:** #378, #382, and here the fusion, the free-sink search and the checks.

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa (chafreaky) with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance.

Commit `be2a06b`; it builds on our #384 (`8148cd0`) and #382 branches.



**Repository CI.** This branch includes PR #318's unchanged three-file joint-dual source-pin repair (certificates/joint-dual-kappa.json, certificates/joint-dual-validation.json, research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json), as #366 and #368 do, so the repository-wide `verify (joint)` job passes. prs.body:
This adds `research/e8-signed-prefix`, an offline, source-bound finite construction with

**kappa = 125311832453733 / 125000000000000000 = 0.001002494659629864.**

Against the frozen PR392 head `ac55c57035c197f744390fe4bc9cf49df1b61816` (0.001000220224856110), this is an increase of **0.22739%**. The snapshot includes PRs through 393. No claim is made against later work.

This is a **conditional finite construction**, not an unconditional integer-multiplication theorem or a Lean certificate. The inherited all-size supplier, dirty-bank, compiler, ordinary-call/borrowed-row restoration, precision and analytic interfaces remain conditional and are stated in the proof.

## New contribution

We extend the positive target-prefix mechanism of PR390 to signed donor coefficients and apply it to PR376's latest R781 complex word, reconstructed from PR378. The selected witness has **25 disjoint pairs: 16 with q=+1 and 9 with q=-1**. It does not claim a shared-donor/fanout gain or an unrelated new algorithm.

At a common initial zero frame, subtract q times the donor target; synthesize the exact difference of the two prefixes using source/write-version/frame tokens; then restore q times the donor at their common recovery frame. The initial donor value and its accumulated prefix cancel identically for arbitrary dirty inputs. All original helper/source frame visits remain, including visits whose scalar delivery cancels. Setup, recovery, endpoint adapters, work registers and phases are charged.

The local paid histogram delta is

```
rank:   1   2   3   4    6   7
calls: -8  -8  -7  -8  -14 +23
```

This preserves rank mass and strictly improves the moment for every exponent between zero and one. It removes 22 child calls per invocation, or 1,584 across the 72-invocation complex assembly. The actual dirty scalar operator, retained totals and helper cleanup are unchanged, so the original literal response K remains valid.

## Composition and direct credits

- **PR376**: exact helper substitutions/frame repairs producing R781, and bit helper reuse.
- **PR378**, with **PR365/374** ancestry: far-retimed complex source.
- **PR377**: compressed nine-stage complex assembly, phase/owner framework and finite invoice.

- **PR392**: applies that refinement to the preceding prefix supplier and is the frozen comparison point.

We compose these ingredients through the actual paid profile and 47 strict outer constraints; we do not add reported kappa gains. The complex supplier binds. The bit coarse saving remains 255384852701747/250000000000000000.

## Reproduction and validation

From the uploaded directory, with Python dependencies in `requirements.txt`, C++17 and Boost headers:

python -B verify.py /absolute/path/to/a-new-output-directory

Set `CXX` and `BOOST_INCLUDE` only if needed. The verification is offline and source dependencies are included. It checks this changed composition rather than running unchanged public PR pipelines.

The replay covers reconstruction/negative controls, all 1,021 independent dirty columns in both local orientations, private restoration, 950 exact Clifford frames and 3,140 directed edges, Gaussian endpoint phases, the full nine-stage global template, 56,232 bank assignments, all 14,709 live-family cover corrections, independent template decoding, the changed finite invoice, both exact rational moment engines, the bit component and all 47 outer inequalities. Result and frozen comparison

This adds `research/e8-response-subspaces`, a self-contained finite conditional construction with

**kappa = 101331088745971 / 100000000000000000 = 0.001013310887459710.**

The comparison is #399 at `b974e481efd2f771cda2dcdd71c91f133793558f`, claiming 0.001002661106042177. The relative improvement is **1.0621516436%**. The source sweep is frozen through #399; this does not claim priority over later submissions. No separately reported gains are added.

## What changes

The starting word is #398's R781 signed-prefix construction. Instead of restricting entrance gauges to existing frames or odd rank-one vectors, we synthesize **26 new response subspaces** of dimensions 1, 2, 4 and 5. The fixed witness has **119 pivot helpers, 143 donors and 240 literal entrance shears**, with unit numerators and denominators 1 or 2.

For each pivot, the exact target-response columns satisfy `K_p + sum c_pd K_d = 0`. Disjoint group role sets make the entrance transformation explicitly invertible. The constructor checks the complete identity `M_new = M_old diag(I,I,S)` in all 1,021 raw columns and checks every nested frame transition; clean-input agreement is not the acceptance criterion.

The additional mechanism is **two-sided residual normalization for even or degenerate entrance spaces**. For the actual phase-sensitive chart `T_E`, exact Clifford decomposition gives `F T_E^-1 = L C_(9-dim E) R`, with explicit rank-zero monomial unitaries. Applying `R^-1` before the complete old-response phase and `L^-1` after complete cleanup leaves the data unchanged and exposes the standard coordinate residual. This uses a separately checked block-diagonal dirty endpoint, not just a zero response column, and does not commute adapters through internal gates. Both orientations and all Gaussian phases are checked. All **17,136 boundary adapters** are emitted and charged.

The mixed residual inventory per stage is `{4:120, 5:208, 7:64, 8:560, 9:5296}`. Explicit coordinate routes place it into **748 width-73 banks** with padding `482 x rank1 + 1 x rank10`. The literal inverse owner matrices, actual owner injectivity, inherited interleaved data/idle schedule, cover corrections and private namespaces are independently decoded.

## Exact accounting

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| Local replicas / stages | 8 / 9 |
| Complete local invocations | 72 |
| Banks per stage | 748 |
| Live / physical stock | 14,412 / 15,203 |
| Paid child count | 316,107 |
| Rank mass | 1,049,580 |
| Deficit | 2,496 |
| Maximum child rank | 48 |
| Complex coarse lower bound | 507169363968149971159 / 500000000000000000000000 |
| Unchanged bit coarse lower bound | 255384852701747 / 250000000000000000 |

The finite reserve bridge is recomputed from the changed emitted source and independent decoder. The required row coefficient is 15,445, below the retained 20,161 allowance. Two exact rational moment engines and six fixed ordinary bootstrap levels yield the stated rational kappa through all **47 strict outer inequalities**. The complex supplier still binds.

## Reproduction and evidence

From the added directory:

```sh
python -B verify.py /absolute/path/to/a-new-output-directory
```

The default replay uses Python 3.11+ and GCC/Clang C++17 (`CXX` may be set). It is offline, source-hash checked, and does not rerun public PR pipelines or discovery searches. It freshly checks the changed scalar programs, both entrance orientations, 532 new/reflected local Clifford edges, all **13,312 residual address columns**, emitted banks and invoice, eight adverse structural controls, the new exact reserve bridge, moments and outer assembly. The unchanged bit component and old local phase edges are reused only through pinned prior receipts and exact source/witness bindings. `--replay-bit` optionally reruns the bundled bit component with its documented dependencies.

`VALIDATION.json` records executed source hashes and the final result; `MANIFEST.json` covers the upload bytes. No compiled binaries or discovery outputs are required. Research notes retain sufficient identities, bounded search results and unpriced routes for future workers.

## Direct sources and related mechanisms

- **#398** supplies the exact signed-prefix R781 input and prior phase evidence.
- **#396** directly inspires the entrance response-kernel route. This package extends it to synthesized larger/even/degenerate spaces using explicit two-sided normalization; it does not relabel entrance kernels as an unrelated invention.

Further compiler/supplier ancestry includes #352, #363, #373, #370, #375, #266 and #234. All bundled upstream headers and notices are retained.

## Scope and future work

This is a **finite conditional construction**, not a Lean certificate or an unconditional integer-multiplication theorem. The inherited all-size compressed-window lift, arbitrary-correlated dirty-bank semantics, recursive compiler, ordinary-call/fixed-tape/restored-row, precision and analytic interfaces remain assumptions. Result

Adds `research/e8-shared-donor-chains` with

**kappa = 1016422320428301 / 10^18 = 0.001016422320428301**, approximately **0.3070561% above #401** at `7844f72c6051a4408284c3092490687061675c1a`.

The snapshot is frozen through #401, including the downloaded #376 head `7aa9d9f0247bb60c0519704bbca18990011e2a37`. This is a comparison against that snapshot, not against later submissions. The changed finite supplier, reserve bridge, exact moments and outer assembly are rebuilt together; independent gains are never added.

## New mechanism: nested shared-donor gauges

#401 required complete role disjointness between response-gauge groups. That restriction is stronger than the algebra needs. If pivots are excluded from every donor set, the entrance matrix still has the form `S = I + N` with `N^2 = 0`, even when donor helpers appear in several groups. Consequently the literal shears commute and the inverse is explicit.

The physical restriction is handled constructively: each reused donor's assigned entrance spaces form a nested chain. The entrance gates are scheduled in increasing dimension, so the actual donor register visits that chain once, with every rank difference and later climb charged. No free joins, frame resets or hidden copies are assumed.

This expands the fixed witness from **119 to 194 pivot helpers**, using **204 donors in 42 groups**, with **36 donors shared by two groups** and **37 distinct entrance spaces**. All **484 literal entrance gates** have unit numerators and denominators 1 or 2. Exact reconstruction checks all 1,021 raw columns, all gate-omission response leaks, and the actual nested paths.

## Additional chronological target recovery

A new recovery uses donor target124 and destination125. If their prefix increments are `u` and `u+v`, respectively, the literal transformation is:

```text
125 -= 124
124 receives u; 125 receives v
125 += 124
```

For arbitrary initial dirty values, the destination ends at `a-b+v+(b+u)=a+u+v`. This pair overlaps an inherited dependency from125 to172. Its setup must occur after the existing zero-frame setups; moving it across that dependency fails a negative control.

The old disjoint-role/sum heuristic is replaced by an exact **chronological 120-column target-matrix identity**, alongside the complete 1,021-column raw equality, both independent symbolic endpoint checks, common-frame checks, private erasure and phase admission. All 52 target shears have identity endpoint in forward and chronological inverse-adjoint orientations. The helper/source cleanup subword is unchanged.

Its paid delta is `{1:+1,3:-1,4:-1,6:+1}`, with unchanged rank mass and one extra scalar gate. The broader native prefix screen found this pair where a prior three-target basis screen required an unavailable compatible third target.

## Incorporated public improvement

From **#376 at7aa9d9f0247bb60c0519704bbca18990011e2a37**, this also takes the single frame change for `target201 += helper491/2`: frame203 of rank8 becomes frame942 of rank7. Structural matching locates it at B1592 in the new word; raw equality and nesting are freshly checked. This contributes `{1:-2,2:+1}` and is credited public work, not our new mechanism.

The complete combined local delta versus #401 is `{1:+150,2:-12,3:-46,4:+1,5:-7,6:-6}`, with rank mass reduced by79. All 4,162 final frame transitions are nested.

## Complete finite accounting

The phase-correct two-sided residual normalization from #401 is retained and freshly applied to all37 entrances. Both boundary monomials surround the complete old-response/main/cleanup invocation; they are not commuted through its scalar gates. Both orientations must restore every independent helper token and erase private work before that wrapper theorem applies.

Eight replicas per stage give residual inventory `{4:120,5:216,7:72,8:1144,9:4696}`. The explicit integer packing uses **738 width73 banks per stage**, down from748, with **394 rank-one pads**. All27,936 boundary adapters, inverse owner permutations, cover corrections and private workspace are charged.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| Complete local invocations | 72 |
| Banks per stage | 738 |
| Live / physical stock | 14,322 / 15,113 |
| Paid child calls | 321,066 |
| Rank mass / deficit | 1,043,010 / 2,496 |
| Maximum child rank | 48 |
| Real scalar primitives across invocations | 5,707,776 |
| Required / retained row coefficient | 15,445 / 20,161 |
| Complex coarse lower bound | 254364121477661453089 / 250000000000000000000000 |
| Unchanged bit coarse lower bound | 255384852701747 / 250000000000000000 |

The complex side binds. The new source-counted reserve bridge, two exact rational moment engines and six fixed ordinary bootstrap levels satisfy all **47 strict outer inequalities** at the displayed rational kappa.

## Reproduction and validation

```sh
python -B research/e8-shared-donor-chains/verify.py /absolute/new/output
```

Default requirements are Python3.11+ and GCC/Clang C++17; `CXX` can be set. The replay is offline and needs no discovery solver or Lean. It reconstructs each transformation, checks dirty columns and both symbolic orientations, verifies **810 new/reflected local Gaussian phase edges** and **18,944 residual address columns**, then independently decodes all6,248 inverse routes, the bank schedule, profile and full invoice. Eight adverse structural mutations must fail, including omitted adapters, wrong inverses, aliased owners and underpriced padding.

Unchanged bit and old local-phase evidence is explicitly reused through exact source/witness bindings. `--replay-bit` optionally repeats the bundled bit component using its documented dependencies. No unchanged public PR pipeline is run by default. `VALIDATION.json` binds executed bytes; `MANIFEST.json` covers the complete upload. Discovery scores and finite solver optimality are not accepted as mathematical certificates.

## Sources and retained research

- **#401**: exact119-gauge baseline, arbitrary entrance-space two-sided normalization, mixed-bank architecture, source-bound receipts and portable framework.
- **#376**: the newly incorporated frame edit, plus earlier helper/lifetime ancestry; the new head and older input lineage are distinguished in NOTICE.md.
- **#398, #390**: signed and positive target-prefix recovery.
- **#396**: entrance response kernels and the odd rank-one route generalized in #401.
- **#378, #365, #374**: retiming/frame ancestry; **#377**: nine-stage complex geometry, Clifford representatives, owner routing and finite invoice.
- **#381** and earlier **#376**: unchanged bit composition.
- **#387, #392, #185**: ordinary bootstrap/slack; **#384, #315, #144, #23**: exact engine lineage.
- **#400, #394, #395, #399**: reviewed heterogeneous-bank/prewhitening/padding-fusion routes. Their distinct cleanup bracket is not added; the attempted compatibility construction and its unpriced tradeoff are recorded.

Further source ancestry and original author/license notices remain intact. Research notes include native search counts, the sufficient shared-donor and chronological-recovery arguments, structural DAG matches, failed bounded screens and unpriced alternatives. The fresh DAG retrieval is bounded and mostly source-only, not a new Lean certification or an exhaustive theorem-library audit.

## Scope

This remains a **finite conditional construction**, not an unconditional integer-multiplication theorem or Lean certificate. Inherited all-size compressed-window lift, arbitrary-correlated dirty-bank semantics, recursive compiler, ordinary-call/fixed-tape/restored-row, precision and analytic interfaces remain assumptions. We do not claim to invent linear transvections, establish literature-wide novelty or prove global optimality. General acyclic pivot/donor dependencies and an entrance-preserving prewhitening/fusion combination are possible next routes; neither is assumed in this result.

prs.title: Conditional κ = 1.016526770666368·10⁻³: response-gauge re-pivoting (checker-clean) and padding fusion on #404's shared-donor R781 E8 complex program (+5.71·10⁻⁸ over #406)
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds `research/e8-repivot-fusion`, a conditional finite construction with

**κ = 7941615395831/7812500000000000 = 1016526770666368/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.016526770666368 × 10⁻³** (complex-bound).

That is **+1.044502·10⁻⁷ over Dugongue's #404** (1.016422320428301e-3) and +5.71·10⁻⁸ over rohanarun's #406 (1.016469657190768e-3).

| | b (complex coarse) | κ |
|---|---:|---:|
| #404 (control, reproduced from our emission of its word) | 254364121477661453089/2.5·10²³ | 1016422320428301/10¹⁸ |
| ours | 508780574407464422817/5·10²³ ≈ 1.017561149e-3 | 1016526770666368/10¹⁸ |

The bit side is #404's pinned coarse bound, c = 255384852701747/2.5·10¹⁷ ≈ 1.021539e-3 > b, so the complex side binds.

Profile delta vs #404 is {1:−216, 3:+72, 4:+72, 5:−144, 6:+72}. Live is 14,322, m = 73, the deficit is 2,496, and there are 738 banks per stage.

**Base.** We re-implement #404's word from its data: its 194 shared-donor entrance gauges on #398's signed781 word, its 124/125 recovery and #376's frame edit. Both of #404's frozen hashes are reproduced (`65b0f9dd…`, `d18ccdc5…`). Our emission of that word under #390's dirty-preconditioned bracket reproduces #404's 24-digit b and κ exactly. None of #404's scripts were run.

**New: gauge re-pivoting.** A response-gauge plan is a span of relations e_p + Σ c_{p,d} e_d. Choosing a different pivot column for the same span zeroes the same response space, so M = M₃₉₈ · diag(I, I, S′) still holds with all 194 pivot columns zero. The rank is checked exactly, and the operator is checked on all 1,021 columns. Pivot dimensions, the residual inventory and #404's bank patterns are unchanged.

The pivot choice is what fixes denominators and which register carries which gauged dirt. We swap four pivots:
- **555 → 748 (plan 28).** #404's word fails gxcore's sixths rule (E5) at register 947, because 555 has five half-coefficient donors. After the swap every coefficient is an integer.
- **1019 → 958 and 1020 → 1001 (plans 0 and 5).** 1019 and 1020 become donors with coefficients −2, −2.
- **585 → 636 (plan 27).** The inverse column of sink 387 stops meeting a gauged coordinate.

We do not use #404's 124/125 recovery, because it fails gx E4 at target 125. That costs −5.69·10⁻⁸, and it is included in the totals above.

**Padding fusion (our #394/#399), now composable on the response-gauge line.**
- The only same-frame zero-row sinks are 301, 324 and 387. Each needs exactly −1/4 of one helper (1019, 1018 and 1020), and the coefficient is unique: there is no solution without that helper.
- On #401's and #404's gauges, 1019 and 1020 are pivots, so the quarter breaks sixths. That was the blocker we recorded in #402.
- After re-pivoting, a quarter of their even-coefficient dirt stays in sixths, so 301 and 387 are fused.
- 324 is not fused. Its 1018 is the only donor of pivot 941, which leaves nothing to re-pivot. Ungauging 941 needs a 739th bank, and an advanced-donor uncompute prices at −3.1·10⁻⁷.
- We also check the premise of #404's research note on sink isolation: for both fused sinks, a_G = b_G = 0 on all 194 gauges.

**Target re-synthesis (our #402).** y₁₇₇ and y₂₂₀ climb (6, 2) instead of (3, 5). The full raw operator is identical.

**Banks.** The 16 fused occurrences own slot 0 of 16 distinct rank-1-padded banks, with the padding on coordinate 72.

**Retained hypotheses.**
- Inherited from #404/#401, not re-run: two-sided normalisation and entrance-chart phases (same 37 entrance spaces), bank routes and owner injections, the finite invoice, and the bit component via receipts.
- Re-opened:
  - phases of the four re-pivoted entrance tokens;
  - owner placement of the 16 fused slots and the fused final climbs;
  - the 177/220 target edges;
  - the scalar invoice.
- Inherited from #398/#376/#392/#377/#352 as in our earlier packages.

**This is a conditional finite construction, not a theorem or formal verification.**

**Attribution.**
- **Dugongue:** #404 (shared-donor gauges, the base), #401, #398, #390.
- **rohanarun:** #406, #405, #400, #396, #395, #387/#392.
- **applecrusher:** #376 (helper substitutions, frame edit 203 → 942).
- **jacklightChen:** #377.
- **#352:** the local invocation and emitter.
- **Jacob Sussman:** E8 unit, gx/gxcore.
- **DaysSky** (#363, #373, #375, #381) and **utcorvusvolat-dotcom** (#370): the bit lineage.
- **DreamingOfClouds:** #315 engines.
- **Ours:** #378, #394/#399, #402, and here the re-pivoting.

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa (chafreaky) with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance.

The branch also carries PR #318's unchanged three-file joint-dual source-pin repair (certificates/joint-dual-kappa.json, certificates/joint-dual-validation.json, research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json) for repository CI. No mathematics changes.

## Validation

Commit `2eca2715826bb899a17d013552d5cf35d42567d1` is on top of our #402 branch (`ac91a9c`).

From a fresh clone:

    bash research/e8-repivot-fusion/verify.sh --quick /tmp/e8p-q   # EXIT 0
    bash research/e8-repivot-fusion/verify.sh /tmp/e8p-full        # EXIT 0 (all regenerations)

This needs Python 3.11+ and the standard library only. The verify covers:
- the manifest, which matches `git ls-files`, and the git-blob pins, including #404's `selection194.json`, `bank-patterns.json` and `RESULT.json`;
- our #399 and #402 pipelines as controls;
- #404's hashes, b and κ as controls;
- the recorded gx/gxcore rejections of #404's word;
- re-pivot span and operator identities;
- gx.check1 + gxcore on the base, the sinked word and ours;
- the 324 negative control;
- regeneration: the free-sink scan finds exactly 301/324/387, the isolation screen holds, and re-synthesis discovery finds exactly 177/220;
- both-orientation replay on all 1,021 live columns with mutation controls;
- bank placement and price;
- Sussman's checkers with the flipped-sign and source-span controls on ours.

The CI workflow is `.github/workflows/e8-repivot-fusion.yml` (Python 3.12 and 3.14).

## Correctness: #406, #408, #409 and #410 fail Sussman's checkers; this word passes

We re-implemented each word from its published data and checked it against the frozen hashes: #406 `3f67e51a…`, #408 `7a5d0d09…`, #409 `e775f810…`, #410 `5243b69b…`. We also reproduced #408's, #409's and #410's exact b and κ from our own emission, using their own replica counts and bank patterns.

Jacob Sussman's `gx.check1` **and** `gxcore` reject all four words with **E4: a pivot is the target of a gate reading y**. This comes from #404's 124/125 recovery, which all four inherit.

With that recovery removed, `gxcore` still rejects two of them:
- **#409, E5 at register 275** (and at 204 for its group [51] alone). Its own sequential groups [51] and [195] pivot on half-coefficient relations (1010, 910). Their half-unit gauged dirt then meets a /2 gate.
- **#410, E5 at register 947.** This is #404's pivot 555.

We fix both by exact re-pivoting, with the same relation span checked by rank: 1010 → 739 and 910 → 531 in #409's groups, and 555 → 748 as in our #407. The submitted word passes `gx.check1` (E0–E7), `gxcore`, a flipped-sign control and the source-span rule.

## Change and mathematical scope

The word is built on our #407 base: #404's 194 gauges with our four re-pivotings, #376's frame edit and no 124/125 recovery. On top of it:
1. **#410's eight entrance enlargements (eumemic), re-implemented.** Our `enlarge()` regenerates #410's `enlarged205.json` byte-for-byte from #408's selection. The 1020 enlargement is carried by our re-pivoted row of 1001, which has the same relation and roles.
2. **#409's four sequential groups (rohanarun), re-implemented, with groups [51] and [195] re-pivoted.** These give ten promoted pivots and 55 prepended unit shears, and every sequential source is read before any entrance write to it.
3. **Padding fusion of sinks 301/387 (ours).** 1019 and 1020 are even-coefficient donors after re-pivoting, so the −¼ uncomputes stay in sixths.
4. **Our #402 target 177/220 re-synthesis**, relocated as #406 does.

Exact checks:
- The full raw operator and the retained totals equal #398's operator times the literal 555-gate entrance prefix on all 1,021 columns.
- All 204 gauged response columns are zero.
- Both local orientations validate, and five mutation controls are rejected.

Banks use 32 replicas, 2,943 width-73 banks per stage and 1,495 rank-1 paddings less 64 fused. Live stock is 57,207, m = 73, and the deficit is 9,984. On the replica count:
- 64 replicas give exactly the 32-replica value, and 16 give less.
- #408's 205-pivot selection re-optimises the same rank-1 entrances that #409 promotes into, so it is not orthogonal; we keep #409's groups.
- Further rank-1 groups on this word all add rank-1 climbs and lose (−5·10⁻⁷ or worse), which is consistent with #409's negative screen.

- **Re-opened:** phases of the six re-pivoted tokens, the 64 fused slots and climbs, and the 177/220 edges.

prs.title: Split centres and source-basis reuse for conditional κ = 0.001120864952258278
prs.body:
This combines a new split-centre complex construction with source-centre reuse on the bit side, in one commit based on main at `12a4934d15006e8c10f9b2264f13f8f341be802b`.

Under the retained compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{560432476129139}{500000000000000000}
=0.001120864952258278.
$$

The combined saving is approximately **6.9522% above [#425](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/425)**. The bit supplier binds the new assembly.

## Construction

On the complex side, cancel the coordinate-source contributions that appear with opposite signs in the centre and side decoders before lifting them to address operators. The 112 code-line targets then use eight rank-eight centres; the eight coordinate targets use rank-one identity copies. Their total copied rank remains 72. Removing 112 coordinate-source helpers and eight dedicated full-centre helpers reduces R from 680 to 560. The dirty response is recomputed from the new word, and both orientations include literal source/helper cleanup and exact heterogeneous-centre phases.

On the bit side, start from #426's R767 word. Form its nine retained sums with an invertible basis change on the source rows, copy them sequentially, and apply the literal inverse before continuing. This removes nine helpers. Compose the resulting R758 word with the compressed dimension-64 geometry from #386, replaying the actual reflected copy chronology and all new bank owners. The changed prefix needs 223 bits and is charged at 256 bits; the old 192-bit allowance is not reused.

| Selected supplier | Complex | Bit |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ambient dimension | 73 | 64 |
| Auxiliary rows | 560 | 758 |
| Live recursion stock | 12,720 | 14,502 |
| Physical stock | 13,298 | 14,511 |
| Rank deficit | 2,496 | 2,496 |
| Certified coarse saving | 0.001183986549206329 | 0.001122122700265139220566 |

Both exact moments include the retained bad-branch allowance. Six fixed bootstrap levels and all 47 strict outer inequalities give the displayed κ; the next grid point and invalid-parameter controls are rejected. The result is calculated from the two emitted programs, not by adding independently reported gains.

One self-contained package, `research/e8-bit-elimination-reuse/`, with its own workflow, plus one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

### Mechanism

1. **#370's producer with new parameters** (67 of 520 entries changed) gives R = 863.
2. **Elimination reuse of dead helper slots** gives R 863 → 740.
   - A dead helper still holds a leftover x-content, an F₂ sum of source lines.
   - Before a later helper is born at frame F, take an F₂ relation among the leftovers of dead slots inside F. One gate at the join of their frames empties one slot, and the new helper takes it over.
   - The 9 retained totals also take dead slots; their leftover lines are read at the full frame.
   - 114 slots are reused by helpers and 9 by totals.
3. **Single-gate frame retiming**, #389's idea: 37 gate moves.

**Overlap.**
- #426 (ai-nanachi) published the same slot-reuse mechanism first: 55 "clean resets" on #376's R822 word, giving R767. We developed this pass independently. On a different base word it finds 114 reuses plus the 9 totals.
- #433's nine-sum source-basis change frees no register here, because the totals already sit on dead slots.

`bash research/e8-bit-elimination-reuse/verify.sh [--quick] DIR`: about 40 s quick, 67 s full.

- **Provenance.** Manifest; 52 vendored files pinned by git blob id. Every cited complex b and κ must equal that PR's own receipt.
- **Rebuild.** The word is rebuilt from pinned inputs and must equal the shipped word. #370's producer regenerates #370's word as a control.
- **#370's independent checker:** exact F₂ on all 980 columns with dirty helpers, and Gram determinants > 0 on every frame (only prime 2). 6 word-level and 6 reuse-specific mutants are rejected.
- **Official checkers.** PR #266's legality at NCOPY = 9; NCOPY = 8 is rejected. Five-stage and B₄ formal columns, with 18 omitted-bridge controls rejected.
- **#386 layout.** Geometry, source-bound template, audit and price.
- **#433's engine, invoice and tail.** These reproduce #433's own c and κ exactly, and #386's, #425's and #431's κ. The tail uses 47 strict inequalities; the next grid point, zero η, zero β and unit β are rejected.
- **B₄.** #381's geometry, banks (T = 9), finite bill and price.

- #386's compressed-layout arguments, including two-level halving (max child 42/64).

prs.title: Format obstructions (no new κ): exact bounds on window width, copy cost and label dimension
prs.body:
**Format obstructions (no new κ): exact bounds on window width, copy cost and label dimension, checked on `gx.check1` programs and on #425's mutable-basis word.** This is a research package of statements, proofs and
exact checks. It claims no new κ. It fixes what three formats can and cannot do and shows where the remaining
freedom is.

| | statement | checked on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | a contribution that reaches a register by a drop-free path forces its frame to contain the source label, so lossless x_T → y_S needs orthogonal labels | every gate of the p = 3, p = 10 (#327) and p = 11 (#193) programs: 0 violations in 3.1 M gate checks |
| **B** | k_a + Σ_j rk C_j ≤ m; with corrector rank h − 1, m ≥ 1 + s(h − 1) | rank h − 1 on all families (replayed correctors for the complex programs and #425; in-cap neighbourhoods for the bit and E8 rows); **#425's word has m = 73 = 1 + 9·8, so the bound is attained** |
| **C** | the drops that carry a total to its readers cost at least rk(U(P) × U(Q)) | equality: 360 (p = 10), 440 (p = 11), 72 (#425 centres, 57 gathered sources each); for the E8 bit dual the package computes the bound 72, which equals the copy loss #370 reports (not replayed) |
| clique bound | Σ_K k_T ≤ r on a clique of drop-free pairs | ω = p (bit), 8, 8, 12, 12 (complex, p = 4..7); 20 ports pairwise lossless in the p = 10 program; ω = 8 on E8 |
| E8 labels | the h = 9 labelling of the E8 in-cap graph is unique; no k = 2 labelling in dimension ≤ 17 | exact SAT, with calibrations and a positive control |
| **P** | for fixed-role B₂ windows over F₂ (one helper set, same slots, slot-carried pairs spanning) the stage windows are orthogonal, m ≥ s·h, under (P1)–(P2) | computed on the complex #327 and #193 programs only (399/400, 483/484). **Compressed windows circumvent it**: #425 (m = 73 < 81) and, for the bit word, #386 (m = 64; Theorem P is not claimed for ℚ forms). Not a general obstruction |
| **S** | a mutable-basis word with b_x modified sources and b_y read targets is simulated in the immutable-source / no-target-read format with R + b_x + b_y helpers | exact on #425's word: 904 = 680 + 112 + 112 |

**What this means for the swarm.** A–C and the clique bound bound m and the copy rank, the label dimension for a given
in-cap graph, and (through the five-stage ledger D ≤ N_data·k, read from upstream) D. They do **not** bound the
helper count R, nor the idle and stock costs, which is where #425, #433 and #442 gained. A further κ gain in these
formats has to come from R or the stock, or from a new port family whose corrector rank is below h − 1 with a cheap
decoder.

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/format-obstructions/requirements.txt    # python-sat 1.9.dev15, networkx 3.7, mpmath 1.3.0, numpy 2.3.5
python3 -B research/format-obstructions/verify.py --output /tmp/format-obstructions-out   # about 90 s on 12 cores (15 CPU-minutes), no network
```

## What changed

One new self-contained package, `research/format-obstructions/`, plus its path-filtered workflow. No existing file
changes. Vendored byte for byte (sha256 in `SOURCE.json`): Jacob Sussman's `gx.py`, the p = 11 certificate of #193, the
p = 10 program of #327, #425's `FULL-WORD.json.gz` (regenerated with its own scripts; the sha equals its
`EXPECTED.json`), the cost model of #346 (from #310) and the p = 10 bit histogram of #325. The one local input is the
p = 3 toy program.

## What `verify.py` checks

It verifies the pins, then runs 91 tasks in a process pool and compares every number with `expected.json`:
- `gx.check1` with the exact scalar identity on the three programs, the taint replay of Theorem A at every gate, the
  corrector ranks of Theorem B and the copy bounds of Theorem C;
- the p = 3 toy: split scatter, cst 18 → 16, exhaustive optimum over all cut chains;
- Theorem P (rank of the cross-Gram constraints), the forced-copy count (10 per overlap, exact over all odd a, b) and
  the contamination scan (1,160 candidate directions);
- #425's word: frame and taint replay, exact scalar replay over ℚ, the Theorem S conversion and its replay;
- the pinned pricer on the p = 10 bit histogram (pinned root reproduced; context only);
- the E8 SAT checks: uniqueness at h = 9, k = 2 at r = 16 (255 patterns) and r = 17 (256), all UNSAT.

Negative controls: shifted labels and a corrupted port; a toy cut outside the radical; the immutable/no-target-read
detector flags 1,640 source modifications and 112 target reads on #425's word and 0 on the converted word; omitted K
and omitted compensation rejected; k = 1 at r = 8 UNSAT and r = 9 SAT, h = 8 UNSAT, the k = 2 encoder at r = 18 accepts
the direct sum.

## Verification

- **Replays:** two fresh-copy runs in other working directories (macOS, Python 3.12.14, python-sat 1.9.dev15,
  networkx 3.7, mpmath 1.3.0, numpy 2.3.5) pass every check; CI has not been run yet.
- **Independent audit:** Independent read-only audit (separate Claude agent): two blockers found and fixed; re-verified.

## Status, honestly

- **κ:** no new κ.
- **Scope:** Theorems A–C and the clique bound are proved for the frame model of PROOF.md §1, which contains the rules E0–E3
  of `gx.check1` and #425's common-label rule; the correspondence is by reading, with no mechanical proof and no Lean.
- **Layout hypotheses:** (B1)–(B2) of Theorem B and (P1)–(P2) of Theorem P were read against Sussman's
  `Work/Bridge/Net.lean`, `Work/BridgeGeom/Stage.lean` and `Work/BridgeGeom/Net.lean` (f010392c); they are consistent
  with the statements there, but this was read, not formally verified. Two points are open: whether the backward stages
  1 and 3 count as "the same program", and whether the stage-j target frames lie in ι_j(q_S)^⊥. Theorem P holds for
  fixed-role B₂ windows over F₂ only; #425's nine-stage windows (m = 73) are outside it.
- **Bit side:** no bit word is replayed. Theorem P (stated for F₂ windows) and the overlap measurements were computed on
  complex programs, and nothing is claimed about Theorem P for ℚ forms such as #386's; the pricing context uses the
  p = 10 bit histogram (the file copied from the `math.json` that #325's verification writes) and is a pricer-model
  output.
- **Theorem S:** a bound on helper count, not on price (the simulation prices 13 % below #425's word under the coarse
  formula). Replayed by the package's detector on #425's word, not by `gx.check1`.
- **E8 labels:** the SAT results are for the full E8 in-cap graph only.

## Attribution

- **Jacob Sussman:** gcert/1, `gx.check1`, the frame lemma, the five-stage layout and the E8 complex unit.
- **jacklightChen (Zhihao Chen):** #425's word and its conjugation semantics; #386.
- **Dylan Crow (utcorvusvolat-dotcom):** #370 (E8 bit word, root coordinates) and the #310 cost model.
- **Louis Harrison:** #346 (the vendored pricer).
- **Avi Eisenberg (ikeboy):** #193. **icekylinx:** #144, #184 and #433. **chafreaky:** #200, #233, #256.
- **eumemic:** #168. **DaysSky:** #162, #352 and #442. **hcg890** and **SovereignSteak:** #234 and the five-stage ledger.

The statements, proofs, checks and packaging were prepared by DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via
Claude Code. Every upstream notice is retained; see `NOTICE`.

prs.title: Under review (split-residual interface): cross-copy idle-axis hosting, one residual on two copies of one idle child; computed κ = 0.001330733966732373 not established
prs.body:
Conditional **κ = 1330733966732373/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.330733966732373·10⁻³**, bit-bound, **+5.13 % over #447** (1.265848755025709·10⁻³, complex-bound), +7.53 % over #442 and +17.44 % over #434. Neither local word changes: complex #433 (R = 560, m = 73), bit #434 (R = 747, m = 64). The idle windows are #442's.

## Change

In #442's idle-axis hosting a whole helper residual sits inside the pending coordinates of one data family. Bit residuals have width 8 − e (637 of width 8, 104 of width 7, 6 of width 4) and complex residuals width 9, while the idle children have ranks 7/14/28/42 (bit) and 8/16/32/48 (complex). A rank-7 child cannot hold a width-8 residual, a rank-14 child holds one and wastes six coordinates, and so on: 6,944 of the 45,360 pending bit coordinates per replica and 5,760 of 51,840 complex ones stay idle and are paid as remainder children.

A child acts on every copy (side, port) of its pair, and all copies share the child's window. This package lets a residual lie across the pending sets of **two copies of the same idle child**. With P = P₁ + P₂ the identity D_{P₁}·D_{P₂} = D_P (the parents' D_{P'}·D_{P−P'} = D_P) writes the dirty invocation's factor on the residual as a product of a factor on each family; each is moved to the child exactly as in #442 §2, since the window is a property of the pair; and each child's remainder is exact by #442's fact (b). Every child's capacity, copies × rank, is then a multiple of the residual width, so the remainders almost vanish. A residual never spans two children or two pairs. The route is still an elementary coordinate permutation of the address space; the finite invoice charges one further route factor per helper selector.

The selection is an integer programme over counts n(child, stage, width) on the concatenated tape of each child's copies (maximise Σ ln(m/r) × hosted coordinates, subject to availability and, on the bit side, exact width-64 tiling of the leftover). `SELECTION.json` freezes it; `--discover` recomputes it with scipy.

## Result

| supplier | #442 saving | this saving | live stock | hosted residuals (split) | max child |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bit, m = 64, R = 747 | 1.239085·10⁻³ | **1.332507·10⁻³** | 9,457 → 8,592 | 46,160 of 53,784 (12,496) | 24 |
| complex, m = 73, R = 560 | 1.267453·10⁻³ | **1.437532·10⁻³** | 8,400 → 7,680 | 40,320 of 40,320 (13,720) | 48 |

Both rank deficits stay 2496. The bit max child 24 is one partial copy of a rank-28 child; the complex max child 48 is the 133 copies per replica of the rank-48 final children that the complex supply cannot fill (5,040 residuals against 5,760 width-9 slots per replica). Since #447 is complex-bound at 1.267453·10⁻³, the complex component here should also lift #445/#447's eleven-stage bit words; that composition is not claimed.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/cross-copy-hosting/verify.py /absolute/new/output` (Python 3.11+, standard library only; the output directory must not exist). It

1. runs #434's complete verifier from scratch;
2. regenerates both hosted templates from #434's fresh outputs and the frozen selection;
3. runs an independent audit that shares no code with the generators: windows re-derived from each schedule; for every replica and invocation exactly one owner record per helper; every hosted residual has one or two pieces on copies of the child it names, widths summing to the residual width, inside the pending set, pairwise disjoint per (child, copy), inside the window and off the active pair; exact remainder children and bank tilings; profile, live stock and deficit 2496 recomputed; twelve mutation controls rejected (including a split across two children and a split whose widths do not sum to the residual width);
4. prices both suppliers with the two inherited rational moment engines and fresh finite invoices (prefix 226 bits charged 256, two-level coefficient 488 bits charged 512, row coefficient 18,355 < 20,161; complex row coefficient 15,443);
5. runs #434's strict outer assembly: six bootstrap levels and all 47 inequalities, with the next grid point and the zero-η, zero-β and unit-β controls rejected.

Local transcript: `PASS_FULL_CROSS_COPY_HOSTING_COMPOSITION` on macOS (Apple silicon), Python 3.14.3, 5 min 48 s including the full #434 replay; every value equals `EXPECTED.json` and both template hashes match. CI is not claimed before it runs.

## Scope

This is a written finite extension of #442's hosting interface: a helper residual's physical slot may lie in two data families of one idle child. That is the principal new review point; [PROOF.md](research/cross-copy-hosting/PROOF.md) gives the argument from the parents' two facts. #442's own extension (helper residuals on data streams during idle windows) and all inherited interfaces remain assumptions: the all-size compiler, correlated dirty-bank and compressed-window interfaces, restored work, tape/common grid, precision and analytic transfer. The global operator identity is argued and checked combinatorially, not replayed numerically on the address spaces. No Lean proof and no unconditional integer-multiplication theorem is claimed.

This branch is #442's branch plus one new directory, `research/cross-copy-hosting/`; no inherited file is changed. The cross-copy selection, generators, audit, assembly and proof note were prepared by higherbeing with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance.

> **Caveat (added after #451).** #451 shows that #448's cross-family residual split is not an exact factorization: D_(a+b)⊕I has trace 90, against 54 for D_a⊕D_b. This package's word splits 1,807 of its 8,140 hosted residuals across two different data families, and #451's trace argument reproduces exactly on our (4,4) splits. **The κ claimed below therefore rests on #448's routing derivation as disputed in #451, and should be treated as not established** until a fully charged compiler or a regrouping theorem covers these splits.

> - The target-mixing lemma and the eleven-stage construction are independent of the dispute.

Conditional **κ = 269548909542967/(2·10¹⁷) = 1.347744547714835·10⁻³**, **1.2783% above #448** (1.330733966732373·10⁻³). The bit supplier binds, at **c = 1.349563·10⁻³** (+1.28% over #448's 1.332507·10⁻³). #448's complex supplier is unchanged (b = 1.437532·10⁻³, nine stages) and has 6.5% of room.

| bit word | stages | hosting | max child | bit c (·10⁻³) | κ (·10⁻³) | over #448 |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| #448 (R747 word) | 9 | cross-copy | 24 | 1.332507 | 1.330734 | 0 |
| unmixed (`stacked_unmixed`) | 11 | cross-copy | 56 | 1.340476 | 1.338682 | +0.597% |
| **target-mixed (default)** | **11** | cross-copy | 56 | **1.349563** | **1.347745** | **+1.278%** |

## Change and mathematical scope

Three independent levers stack on #443/#444's R740 rank-138 bit word, each behind the checks that already exist for it:
- **#448's cross-copy hosting**, used unchanged: a helper residual may lie across the pending sets of two copies of one idle child (the tape rule).
- **Eleven compressed stages** (m = 78, five data pairs, 24 bridge shears, 11 local invocations), as in #445 and #447. The idle pairs then offer 73,920 pending coordinates per replica against 63,602 residual coordinates (45,360 against 52,038 at nine), so **all 8,140** helper residuals are hosted (1,807 across two copies), no bank remains and the live stock is the data alone: 1,200 families.
- **Target mixing** (F2 analogue of #425's target packets). For two targets whose delivered prefixes inside a frame G coincide, the receiver takes the donor's register with one addition at G, plus a frame-0 preconditioner and a scatter fix. 46 receivers; the target climb falls by 0.72% per invocation; R = 740 and every helper width are unchanged.

chafreaky's #445 independently reached eleven stages. While building, our eleven-stage single-copy variants matched #445's κ and bit c to every digit; that single-copy check is not part of this package.

## Validation

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/e8-r740-replica32/parent436/requirements.txt
python -B research/e8-eleven-stage-cross-copy/verify.py /abs/new/output      # CXX, BOOST_INCLUDE as for #443; --quick, --no-anchor, --discover-check
```

`verify.py` checks the pins, runs #443's and #448's verifiers unchanged, then:
- **Anchors (nine stages):** the generalised geometry equals #386's; the parent template equals #443's byte for byte; the generalised tape emitter reproduces **#448's bit template byte for byte**, and the generalised assembler reproduces #448's `EXPECTED.json` (κ, both lower endpoints, both template hashes).
- **Eleven stages:** geometry (1,320 route checks, 77 factors, no new prime); the template's scalar replay on 9,340 columns with all 24 omitted-shear controls rejected; the C++ formal-column checker at `-DKPAIRS=5` (1,940 columns, 24 controls); independent audit of the template (944 projectors, 15 mutation controls) and of the hosting (windows, pieces, owners, remainders; 20 mutation controls, incl. split pieces on non-adjacent copies and widths that do not sum); the exact two-moment price, three-level halving, six bootstrap levels, all 47 strict inequalities, next-grid and parameter controls.
- **Mixed word:** regenerated from #443's word; C++ cohort legality, five-stage and K = 5 formal columns, `mutate_records` (6 of 6), the Gram check of all 944 frames; `e8core.replay` on 980 columns, a strict check of the 92 target operands, four mutants rejected (no preconditioner, no scatter fix, mixing at the full frame, mixing omitted).

Local transcript: full wrapper PASS twice from fresh copies (macOS, Python 3.14.7, g++-16 = Homebrew GCC 16.2.0, Boost 1.92); each run replays #443 and #448 in full before the eleven-stage steps (seconds). CI covers Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Scope and open obligations

Conditional, like its parents. The principal review points are:
1. **Lemma (bit labels)** (`BIT-LABEL-LEMMA.md`, `PROOF.md` §6): the bit-label conjugation for target-to-target adds at a common frame. It extends #425's lemma, which #425 flags in the same way. The checks fix the F2 identity, the frames and the spans; they do not prove that the physical bit label acts identically on a target used as an operand. The unmixed variant does not depend on it.
2. **#448's cross-copy hosting lemma**, now applied to every residual of an eleven-stage word, and #442's hosting lemma it builds on.
3. **Compressed windows at eleven stages**: m = 1 + s(h − 1) at s = 11 is checked finitely (every projector, route, schedule and owner), not proved.
4. **Finite constants**: three-level halving (max child 56: 2·56³ = 351,232 < 78³ = 474,552; coefficient 504 bits unmixed, 511 mixed, charged 512), and a bit row 3·(m² + 1) + 10,161 = 28,416 above the inherited 20,161 (the outer assembly needs only 10⁶ − (51/25)A > 0). #445's elementary orthogonal-cover count is an alternative that keeps 20,161; not used here.
5. **One replica**: with no bank to tile, T = 1 (#443/#448 use 8 or 32 replicas only to fill width-64 banks); the price is independent of T.

prs.body:
## Result and comparison

This adds `research/e8-whole-pool-portfolio`, a reproducible conditional construction with

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{253308389885063}{200000000000000000}=0.001266541949425315.$$

That is **+0.04820338% over #451** (`0.001265931727546219`). The complex supplier binds.
This is a conditional finite artifact, not an unconditional multiplication theorem or Lean certificate.
It does **not** claim to beat #453's higher posted number: #451 supplies a trace obstruction to the
cross-family splitting derivation used there. This construction keeps every residual in one whole family.

## Two construction mechanisms

1. **Whole-residual pooling across replicas.** Allocate the eight replicas jointly rather than solve
   identical per-replica integer packing problems. Every helper stays on one physical array family,
   with a complete slot isometry, a disjoint orthogonal block, and its checked idle window. Both actual
   family and absolute coordinate identities are audited. Complex delta relative to the selected #451
   idle inventory is `{1:-2,7:+8,16:-8,55:+6,64:-4}`. Rank mass stays unchanged; the moment improves.
2. **Invocation-specific complete-program portfolio.** Five reverse calls at stage 5, replicas 0..4,
   use a fully checked rank147 provider; the other 83 use rank149. Each variant adds two residual
   coordinates and changes its local profile by `{1:-2,4:-4,5:+4}`. Whole-owner pooling pays those ten
   additional coordinates by changing a remaining rank52 child to rank42. The full difference from
   uniform pooled rank149 is `{1:-10,4:-20,5:+20,52:-1,42:+1}`. This improves bit-side reserve; it gives
   no further final-kappa increase while the complex supplier binds.

These use whole-slot reindexing/orthogonal-idempotent composition and equal complete-map substitution,
respectively. Structural sources include Mathlib's block-diagonal multiplication and the project's
MUB projection-factor identities. They are sources of mathematical analogies, not Lean certificates
for this artifact. #450 target mixing and two historical partial-prefix recoveries are also used,
but are explicitly credited as prior techniques rather than presented as additional new mechanisms.

## Exact invoice

| Supplier | Window | Live | Physical | Rank mass | Deficit | Maximum child |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bit | 78 | 9600 | 9609 | 745536 | 3264 | 56 |
| Complex | 89 | 9600 | 10178 | 851136 | 3264 | 64 |

Complex profile: `{1:170358,2:68992,3:18624,4:19712,5:38336,7:3840,8:9792,55:6,64:1732}`.
Both actual profiles are priced together. Independent proposed gains are never added.

The coefficient bound charges all 88 chronological calls and all bridges, even with foreign-replica
hosting. Route-extra3 and 100,000 finite dispatch operations are charged. The bit row cover is19,431;
the retained complex fractional-depth row reserve is20,161 with its explicit cutoff condition.
Both exact moment engines, six bootstrap levels, and all47 strict outer inequalities are used.

## Reproduction and validation

```sh
python -B research/e8-whole-pool-portfolio/verify.py /absolute/path/to/new-output-directory
```

Requires Python3.11+, SymPy, a C++17 compiler and Boost headers; set `CXX`/`BOOST_INCLUDE` if needed.
No network, optimizer, SciPy, prebuilt binaries, or Lean installation is required. Assertions must be enabled.

Fresh validation reconstructs both complete local providers, all980 dirty columns each, eleven-stage
orientation checks, exact Gram/prime witnesses, and all74,720 columns of the heterogeneous unbanked
controller. It checks65,120 whole bit helpers and49,280 whole complex helpers, physical-axis collisions,
phase recipes, emitted instruction digests,19 bit routing mutants and10 complex routing mutants.
The exact final profiles/templates match the frozen expected invoice. See `VALIDATION.json` and
`REPLAY-MANIFEST.json` for the source-bound replay; `MANIFEST.json` covers final upload contents.
Unchanged public verification chains were not redundantly rerun: inherited complex Clifford evidence
is explicitly retained with its source bindings.

All-size compiler, arbitrary-correlated dirty hosting, target-label, compressed-window, restored-work,
common-grid/tape, precision, and analytic contracts remain inherited assumptions. Finite controls do
not prove these contracts. No global packing optimality or literature-wide priority claim is made.

## Sources, rejected routes, and future work

Direct sources and inspirations include #451 (rank149 whole-host baseline, row bound and trace review),
#450 (target mixing only), #445/#447 (eleven-stage schedules), #443/#439/#417 (response kernels and
residual isometries), #442 (whole idle-family hosting), #433 (complex split-centre/source-basis work),
#425/#386/#370 (mutable basis, geometry and producer), #401/#404 (shared donors/prefix recovery),
and #315's rational outer-assembly lineage. #453 supplied a useful source collection/local comparison;
its split-based price and #448's disputed splitting step are not used. #452 was reviewed but not used.
Exact head pins and licenses are in `PROVENANCE.md`, source headers, and `notices/`.

`RESEARCH.md` preserves the actual discoveries, bounded searches, library analogies, rejected coordinate
splitting attempt, and future routes. Early placement checks on the split attempt did not establish an
operator identity; those larger prices are expressly withdrawn. Product-coordinate factorization must
not be confused with a direct sum of independent array families. The next useful search variables are
larger whole-owner pools and independently correct complex-program portfolios, always with actual
operator semantics and a complete shared invoice.

Developed with OpenAI assistance. No claim of an independent all-size theorem or exclusive priority.

**What is new: the bit word R = 715** (#436's R740 → 715).
1. **A carrier lower bound, and a word that meets it.** In this format a copy of source x_s that first acts above its line frame
   serves only targets in a hyperplane section of s^⊥ (frames contain everything they touched). The 63 lines of E7 = s^⊥ are a
   spherical 4-design, Σ_r ⟨r,u⟩²⟨r,v⟩² = 16(|u|²|v|² + 2⟨u,v⟩²) > 0, so no two hyperplanes contain them: every source needs ≥ 3
   registers, i.e. **≥ 240 carriers**; likewise every target needs ≥ 2 helpers reaching its hyperplane (240, met since #370).
   #370-lineage words spend 272 carriers because each frame line 2e_m enters the D4 sums of seven blocks. **Frame-pair D4 sums**
   (D4(c) = Bcw[c] + FP + FP', FP = 2e_a + 2e_b over the 12 pairs of one AG(3,2) direction plane) meet the bound: R 740 → 724.
2. **Eleven cancelling re-expressions** (a rule rewritten as x ⊕ y of existing symbols; overlap cancels inside its frame): R 724 → 715.
3. #443's replica kernel rebuilt for the new word (deterministic search, coordinate entrances), and #450's target mixing
   **generalised to chained receivers** (a donor that is itself a receiver); it reproduces #450's mixed word byte for byte.

wrapper and the R715 package's full wrapper from scratch, then the exact composition (two moment engines per side, six bootstrap
levels, all 47 strict outer inequalities, next-grid and parameter controls). The bit package regenerates the word from its frozen

checker on the kernel and mixed words, #443's C++ cohort legality and formal columns at five and eleven stages, mixing mutants, Gram,
eleven-stage template and hosting audits, and its own assembly. Two fresh-copy runs agree apart from timing fields (results, both
supplier RESULTs and the complex AUDIT byte-equal). The R715 word was also checked by an independent validator.

**Review points**
- **Carrier bound** (proof above): the 4-design identity for E7 and the frame-containment argument give ≥ 240 carriers; it is a
  scoped bound for this format, not used by the certificate.
- **Rekid legality**: each of the 11 re-expressed rules uses existing symbols whose frames lie inside the rule's frame, the
  hierarchy stays acyclic (the compiler's recursion requires it), every consumer frame contains the rule's frame, and content equals
  the F2 sum of its kids (checked by `hier_word.py` before compiling).

prs.title: Conditional kappa = 0.001274548075945587: full-nine-axis kernel normalization and same-owner spectator borrowing
prs.body:
This adds `research/e8-tensor-normalization/`, a self-contained replay package for the changed construction.

The composed conditional exponent is:

**kappa = 1274548075945587 / 10^18 = 0.001274548075945587**

This is **+0.6303146486% over #456**. The source snapshot is frozen through #457; this comparison makes no claim about later PRs.

## Mechanisms

### 1. Normalize the complete dirty-helper invocation

For each one-dimensional complex entrance E, the exact helper endpoint is:

    Phi = T_full T_E^-1

We factor this as:

    Phi = L (C8 tensor I1) R

Here L and R are explicit Gaussian monomial maps. Wrapping the complete local call with their inverses admits the desired operation while preserving all nine physical dimensions, global phases, and arbitrary dirty contents.

The scalar-backward program retains its original frame chronology and uses the same endpoint wrappers.

### 2. Borrow the inactive ninth axis from the same owner array

The eight active axes lie inside the pending idle child. The spectator lies in its orthogonal complement within the same ambient array.

The complete invocation acts as identity on that borrowed coordinate. Consequently, only the eight active axes are removed from the child's paid remainder. Every simultaneous invocation has a disjoint full physical footprint and an explicit orthogonal route.

This construction does not split a helper across owner families or fit a nine-dimensional function register into eight dimensions.

Together these mechanisms admit **#449's existing 79-pivot response kernel**. The separate gauge-80 modification is not used. The witness applies the complete kernel in all 77 calls of the seven-replica, eleven-stage construction and explicitly records all 6,083 spectator borrows.

## Composition

| Supplier | Construction | Lower saving |
|---|---|---:|
| Bit | #457 rank151 + #450 target mixing + reused #455 two-prefix recovery | 0.001276174621854442560268 |
| Complex | #449 kernel79 + the admission mechanisms above, using #456's seven-replica layout | 0.001305231506267591 |

The bit supplier binds.

The complex moment's finer lower endpoint is 0.001305231506267591990847. Assembly conservatively rounds this downward to 18 decimal places. Gains are composed through the supplier profiles and outer assembly, never added.

The complex profile is:

    {1:153851, 2:71764, 3:4807, 4:17248, 5:33266,
     6:2, 7:2254, 8:6356, 40:1, 64:2046}

Its ambient dimension is 89, live stock is 8,400, physical stock is 8,978, rank mass is 744,744, and deficit is 2,856.

Monomial wrappers are charged per ambient array entry, including every exterior slice. The invoice conservatively charges sixteen real primitives for every helper per complete call and includes the existing routing/compiler reserves. No clean full-array temporary is assumed.

## Reproduction

```sh
python -B research/e8-tensor-normalization/verify.py /fresh/output/directory
```

Requires Python 3.11+, SymPy, a C++17 compiler, and Boost headers. Set `CXX` and `BOOST_INCLUDE` where necessary. Replay requires no network, optimizer, or Lean installation.

Checks include:

- Changed bit native compilation, legality, formal columns, stage composition, Gram frames, and whole-owner routing.
- Both 800-column complex scalar orientations, 2,932 exact phase edges, and 240 data endpoint adapters.
- Fourteen canonical entrance wrappers, each checked on 512 Gaussian-dyadic columns, with 70 negative controls.
- Independent ownership and active/complement replay, full nine-axis orthogonal routes, and complete-program dispatch.
- Rational moments, conservative finite invoices, six bootstrap levels, all 47 strict assembly inequalities, and adjacent-grid and parameter controls.

## Sources and attribution

Direct reuse: **#449, #456, #457, #455, #450, #451, and #454**.

The hosting/compiler/word lineage additionally includes **#442, #433, #425, #417, #386, #377, and #370**. The outer formula follows **#434/#315**.

Exact pinned sources and retained notices are recorded in `PROVENANCE.md` and the manifests. We do not claim the public response kernels, target-mixing identity, whole-pool framework, or reused prefix recoveries as new discoveries.

Earlier tensor-isomorphism work suggested two structural adaptations:

- Paired primal/dual coordinate changes suggested the endpoint normalization.
- Active/complement projectors and orthogonal-block constructions suggested the restored spectator borrowing.

The multiplication identities are established separately in `PROOF.md`; these connections are mathematical inspiration, not imported Lean certification.

## Research record and future directions

`RESEARCH.md` preserves the unsuccessful screens and their scope, including Steinberg/transvection rewrites, terminal-observable substitutions, common-frame centralizers, cleanup compression, and full-footprint-only allocations.

The conservative E510 admission produced only a small gain. Permitting an explicitly restored spectator in the same owner array changed the allocation constraint and admitted all 79 pivots.

A smaller 112-pair ablation establishes strict moment improvement using:

    16^alpha < 2 * 8^alpha, for 0 < alpha < 1.

The next useful target is the binding bit supplier, including a rigorously justified bit analogue of spectator borrowing. Further complex-only saving does not currently improve the composed exponent.

## Scope

The inherited all-size supplier, hosting, compiler, and outer-assembly interfaces remain conditional.

This is not an unconditional sub-n-log-n multiplication theorem or a fresh Lean certificate. It supplies concrete local and storage arguments, finite witnesses tied to pinned sources, and a replay of the changed construction.

prs.title: Remove compact FFT reservation and top-bit costs with complementary reservoirs
prs.body:
The compact FFT currently transforms its reserved axes individually, imposing `c > q`, and processes extra top bits at cost `O(Vd)`. This supplies a conditional construction removing both costs while retaining the original all-input dirty-core, routing, precision and analytic interfaces.

Complete every Fourier round of one half of the axes while the other half supplies restored dirty fields, then exchange roles. Route each exceptional top-bit round into virtual chunks filled with existing unselected coordinates. At most five global coordinate routes serve an entire FFT; no Fourier axis is enlarged. Ordinary complete-zero-row padding is retained.

The resulting FFT cost is `O(V [p^tau polylog(p) + ell d^lambda_prime])`. The proof accounts for complete front/back fields and row indices, actual pass chronology, arbitrary dirty contents, pointwise frequency alignment, inverse normalization, the constant number of paid routes, and p+2 precision. It also provides explicit compressed eventual-capacity bounds.

**No new kappa is claimed.** Gaussian arithmetic and scalar work still limit the current composition. This removes two FFT implementation costs that would otherwise remain even after those separate algorithms improve; kappa = 1 remains unproved.

The stream maintains each quadratic term and its forward difference, subtracts the old term on a mixed-radix carry, and makes fewer than 2T adjacent axis-record visits over T entries. The proof includes a constant-tape schedule, O(p) persistent control state, short arithmetic widths and the original lexicographic output order. No per-output scan of all axes or table of T phases is required.

The same exact residue, denominator and precision feed the retained exponential routine. Numerical errors, disk format, endpoint products and frequency convention are unchanged. Polynomial-ring products remain a separate cost.
