prs.title: Gauge44 factory and whole-family assignment for conditional κ = 0.001649483702558979
prs.body:
This extends the pinned [#635](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/635) construction with a changed arbitrary-helper-input factory and 44 rank-four cold endpoints. It is one new commit based on main at `17ce0c79b7b51c2634b439ea5a2b754f09909693`.

Under the retained all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, normalized wrappers, whole-call hosting, precision/tape, exact-recovery, analytic-transfer and bit H1–H5 interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1649483702558979}{10^{18}}=0.001649483702558979.
$$

The saving is **0.80931% above #635**. This compares exponent savings, not practical runtime. The conservative complex model separately certifies κ `0.001649483699681650`.

## Construction

Within each eight-source factory, exchange four source registers with equal clean copies at their common rank-one frame. This changes how arbitrary initial helper values propagate while preserving the clean operands. Complete the four coordinate totals to an invertible retired-row basis using frozen low-frame forms, and place available totals on source carriers.

The resulting protected-column and inverse-support calculation exposes 44 rank-four cold directions. Exact dyadic input premixes, low-frame tails and a recomputed FULL inverse realize them. Both row and column isolation are checked before removing an ended helper from cleanup. All scalar gates and dirty-input compensations are included in the finite invoice.

| Quantity per invocation | Complete #635 JP8 | Gauge44 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Source / target ports | 112 / 112 | 112 / 112 |
| Helper registers | 492 | 492 |
| Rank-four cold endpoints | 22 | 44 |
| Total helper residual width | 3,894 | 3,794 |
| Local paid rank mass | 5,750 | 5,650 |

All 72 invocations use the new supplier. An explicit assignment covers 35,424 helper roles, retaining 7,168 live and 7,670 physical families. The whole-family matcher concentrates idle remainders using a capacity exchange argument; 288 integer majorization receipts justify its updates. All 72 final callwise remainder histograms are optimal with the other calls fixed. No joint global optimality is claimed.

Every idle remainder is charged. The final global rank mass remains 520,704, with deficit 2,560 and largest child rank 48. The improved rank distribution certifies complex saving `0.001652208994368411824947`.

The unchanged [#543](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/543) bit supplier gives `0.001653826988146798944268`; **the complex side binds**. No bit improvement is claimed.

## Contribution sources and prior PRs

| Source | Contributor | Retained contribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#635](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/635), `a6895a69f8ad98ab45777b03e9e6f48888c39f6f` | jeremykothe2, DreamingOfClouds and credited upstream contributors | K-triangle/Port480 construction, R492 allocation, transported stages, HPE machinery and global admission baseline. |
| #604 and the #591/#592/#593/#599/#601 lineage | DreamingOfClouds, jeremykothe2 and credited contributors | Cold endpoints, exact premixes, low-frame tails and native endpoint interfaces. |
| Joint-prefix and frame/identity lineage | Dominik Scholz, chafreaky and credited contributors | Joint-prefix construction, frame coalescing, artifact identities and retained controls. |
| [#543](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/543) | eumemic and credited predecessors | Unchanged bit supplier and its conditional interfaces. |
| Retained framework and exact engines | Credited upstream contributors | Whole-call hosting, precision/tape bounds, rational moments and analytic assembly. |

My [#535](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/535) contributed post-center rank-four response kernels; [#531](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/531) supplied the SAME504 factory and global package; [#523](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/523) supplied the 112-port restriction; and [#433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433) supplied split centers and source-basis reuse. Earlier #10, #18, #24, #32, #36, #104, #115, #130 and #144 concern batched boundaries, partial swaps, gauges, certified assembly and frame/cover constructions. These are provenance, not additive numerical gains. Original source-specific notices, including asynchronous-scheduling credits, remain in the ancestry.

The new source-branch gauge, retired-row completion, source-carried totals, exact 44-end construction and whole-family matching are contributed by **icekylinx**, with **GPT-6 Astra** assistance. Local review and packaging used **OpenAI Codex**. Original licenses, notices and assistance disclosures are retained.

## Proof and validation

The incremental package is `research/gauge44-global/`.

- `CONSTRUCTION.md`: exact local construction, protected directions and full cleanup.
- `hosting/PROOF.md`: capacity, exchange and integer majorization proof.

prs.title: Research: paid-copy E8 exact-RAM realization with an attributed DFT corollary
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds a self-contained alternative paid-copy E8 realization under `research/e8-paid-copy-ram-20261013/`, with the Pro provider proof preserved verbatim, an independently reconstructed exact checker, complete source attribution, and an attributed cyclic-Fourier corollary. No existing witness, upstream source, workflow or selected-result pointer changes.

At fixed architecture depth one, the positive Gaussian kernel uses h=9, v=120, real rank 8, R=6968 paid helpers, W=7208 and m=27. The full rank histogram has deficit 24, and its exact moment at 1/15000 has more than one rank-mass unit of slack. The charged all-matrix padding/private-memory proof gives C tensor k in O(2^k(k+1)^(14999/15000)) exact complex RAM work. The existing OpenAI exact-width compiler/sector/CRT/chirp machinery then gives the positive cyclic DFT at every length in O(N(log N)^(14999/15000)(loglog N)^(45001/15000)), eventually O(N(log N)^(29999/30000)).

The cyclic result requires one supplied exact canonical root of explicitly selected order below 1024N^3. Extracting other roots, nonzero scalar-preparation divisions, scheduling, packing and the fixed chirp operand's transform are paid. Indexed access and logarithmic integer-word arithmetic have unit cost; complex cells have unrestricted exact values. Architecture depth is fixed independently of N. Root acquisition from rational arithmetic, finite-alphabet sequential tapes, bit multiplication, numerical stability, practical crossover and new Lean certification are outside the claim.

This is not a record supplier or a new Fourier-transfer mechanism. PR225 already documents community transfer and stronger rates; PR256/274 and Sussman's earlier E8 unit also report stronger rates and a much smaller R=783 core. The proposed value is the explicit independent paid-copy construction, dirty/private ownership proof and reproducible depth-one corollary. PR631's bit-side star-reader puncture result has a different decoder/model and is not refuted. Exact pins and the current overlap check are in NOVELTY.md and SOURCE.json.

OpenAI's imported compiler/transfer attribution and Apache license are retained. The contribution discloses substantial OpenAI Pro/Codex assistance, credits Pro for the retained provider construction, and distinguishes the separate fresh Codex adversarial referee. Earlier E8, frame/cover, dirty-response and community transfer contributors retain credit in NOTICE.md.

## Validation

A fresh independent adversarial referee accepted the mathematical theorem in this specified-root exact-complex-RAM model. The packaged checker reproduces all ten of that referee's mathematical result groups exactly; only authentication, CLI/output and the optimized-Python refusal were adapted.

The complete deterministic `--check` passes. Checks include all 7208 live symbolic columns in both orientations, 3601 phase projectors, 240 owner routes, the rational strict moment/padding parameters, dirty DAG compensation, primitive-root Newton/Toeplitz identities, ragged sector operators, 4273 working/root lengths, 62284 CRT phase pairs and eleven exact three-transform chirps. Negative mathematical controls and separate corrupt-import/optimized-output controls pass. Package hashes, whitespace and exact fourteen-file scope were checked independently before publication.

```
python3 -B research/e8-paid-copy-ram-20261013/verify.py --check
```

Python 3.9+, standard library only. Finite checks corroborate the reviewed universal proofs; they are not a giant transform implementation or a formal theorem proof. No contributor generator, full repository suite or Lean build was executed, and no such pass is claimed. This is a draft research contribution for review, with no new multiplication kappa or priority claim.

prs.title: Conditional κ = 0.001652528731617094: PR589 bit supplier and dissolved owner map on PR645's gauge44 construction
prs.body:
## Summary

Conditional κ = **0.001652528731617094** (conservative 0.001652528728737236). This is +1.43×10⁻⁶ over PR648 and +3.05×10⁻⁶ over PR645.

**Two changes on PR645's gauge44 construction:**

1. **Bit supplier: PR589 instead of PR543.** PR648 showed that with a well-packed owner map, the gauge44 complex side certifies more than PR543's bit supplier allows (0.0016538), so the bit side was binding. This package cites the merged PR589 tuned bit supplier (c = 0.001733427039589844, reproduced by main's own replay). Its `EXPECTED.json` is pinned by git blob `e293ddc5`, byte-identical to main's `research/e8-bit-p111-tuned/tune/EXPECTED.json`. The bit deficit is now **derived** from the bit word's parameters, 32·(888−567) = 10272, instead of PR543's hard-coded 9984, with an equality guard. With PR589 the complex side binds again.
2. **Owner map: dissolve.** Starting from gap-merge packing, a new "dissolve" move empties a bin by spreading its roles into defect gaps under the same window, capacity and one-per-time constraints. This leaves idle mostly in rank-48 bins.

**Verifier changes** (reviewed): `code/assemble.py` (load and derive the bit supplier), new `code/bit_supplier_controls.py`, and a new `bit-supplier-controls` stage in `verify_global.py` asserting 12 rejected controls, including a revert to the hard-coded 9984. Reverting the call site to 9984 makes the full chain fail at `check_moment`. The other 20 Python files are byte-identical to PR645. `independent/price_profile.py` is ported to PR589.

**Review:** an independent reviewer judged the composition SOUND (packaging fixes applied). It checked the pinned blob against main, recomputed the deficit, confirmed that no bit constant is left at PR543 values, and re-traced all 12 controls to their intended assertions. It also recomputed κ: 0.001651096360425895 under PR543 (bit binds; equal to PR648) and 0.001651929911890057 under PR589 for the previous map.

**Scope:** main's ledger records PR589 as supplier-only headroom; composing it into a complex assembly is new here and should be reviewed as such. prs.title: Research: the complex delivery layer is rigid — target hosting and raw-face sharing closed exactly
prs.body:
**Research note; no κ claim.** Adds only `research/complex-delivery-rigidity/` (README, scripts, results, manifest). No supplier, certificate, verifier or existing file changes. Based on `main` at `17ce0c7`.

## Two exact negative results on the K-triangle word (#622 lineage)

Slot copies and the in-place mixing of the 8-sums are about 15 % of the complex local rank mass. Two proposed ways to remove them, "group delivery" (my #520 §3) and target-hosted / output-borrowed registers (#571's open list), are closed on this word family:

1. **No target can host a face or 8-sum for other targets.** Checked on all 14 blocks from the pinned constructor, executed unchanged with a role dump: a target's cap contains an 8-sum's span iff it consumes it (112/112); two consumers have consistent coefficient ratios only in opposite tetrads (ratio `σ_x[p0]σ_z[p0]`, constant on their 3 shared keys), while same-tetrad pairs share 2 keys with opposite ratios; a target's own-row frame lies only in same-tetrad caps; and the own read cannot be deferred (own registers are never written after their last target read, but the module's next read lifts the frame out of the cap in all 112 cases). Hence every cross-tetrad target-to-target read is frame-illegal and same-tetrad sharing is the existing butterfly, once per target. A CP-SAT read-ordering model with exact atom flow confirms the 8-sum-level floor: pure registers need 20 copies per block (bound 12) against the 8 the word uses with 2×2 mixes.

2. **No read order of face registers removes the slot copies.** In the raw word no register is read by two targets of the same block; all 120 multi-reader registers are #531's cross-block raw reads. The pollution-tolerance census over all 168 (key, consumer-block) incidences shows a target's frame after the butterfly, or after its own row plus the selected faces, is inside the caps of no consumer group (0/1344 each); only the bare own-row frame is tolerated: 160/448 foreign cases for selected incidences (56 are used by #531), 64/896 for non-selected ones, and 96 of the 112 non-selected incidences have no tolerated foreign target at any stage.

So under the hub's rules (monotone frames, target frames inside `u_t^⊥`, helpers never reading targets, own row first) the delivery layer is at its floor; #646's measured loss from more skeleton atoms and #645's gain in the factory layer point the same way. The README states what a rule-level change would have to touch.

## Reproduction

```sh
sh research/complex-delivery-rigidity/reproduce.sh /tmp/delivery-rigidity
```

Standard library only; `order_model.py` needs `ortools` and is skipped otherwise (its recorded runs are in `results/`). The constructor from `research/complex-571-cold14-k492` and the inputs from `research/direct-delivery504-global` are read in place and not modified.

prs.title: No new κ: the square-root wall — every current assembly has κ < 1/2 (checked)
prs.body:
**No new κ.** This adds a structural ceiling that applies to the manuscript and to every assembly in the repository.

**Theorem.** An algorithm built on the shared framework runs in time Ω(n·√(log n)), so κ ≤ 1/2. Each assembly's own accounting makes this strict: κ < (1 − δ)/2 < 1/2.

## Change and mathematical scope

The package is `research/sqrt-log-wall/`: `README.md` (statement and proof), `wall_check.py` (standard library only), `NOTICE.md` and `LICENSE`, plus one path-filtered workflow. No existing file changes.

Every assembly keeps the manuscript's reduction (`upstream/build/sections/08-assembly.tex`):

- **The box.** A d-axis cyclic transform with `Tp = Θ(n)` stored bits and axis lengths `t_i ≤ r = 2^ℓ`, so `dℓ ≥ log₂ T`.
- **One pass per butterfly level.** ℓ simultaneous rounds.
- **One pass per axis.** d Gaussian line passes, applied axis by axis.
- **Two cost rows.** The dimension row with margin ε (packed products) and the scalar-work row with margin 1 − ε − δ (chirps, twists and scalar products).

**Proof.**
- Each pass reads every stored bit, so the time is at least (d + ℓ)V ≥ 2√(dℓ)·V ≥ 2√(log₂ T)·V = Ω(n√log n). Hence κ ≤ 1/2.
- The rows require κ < ε and κ < 1 − ε − δ. Since max_ε min(ε, 1 − ε − δ) = (1 − δ)/2 and every assembly has δ > 0, the bound is strict.
- **Network side.** The butterfly row's margin is εq with q = 1 − λ′ < 1 − τ = a, so κ < min(εa, 1 − ε) ≤ a/(1 + a) < 1/2.

**Escaping the wall** needs a different skeleton: several butterfly levels per pass, fewer than d axis sweeps, or a reduction other than the d-axis box. Better networks, frames, recurrences, constants or parameters cannot cross it.

## Where things stand

| assembly | κ | below 1/2 by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| selected record (`certificates/selected-result.json`, research outer engine) | 1.635527·10⁻³ | 306× |
| best tex assembly (`notes/paired-cube-assembly.tex`) | 4.609169·10⁻⁴ | 1085× |
| manuscript (`08-assembly.tex`; its εC₁ < 1 with C₁ = 20 caps it at 1/20) | 2⁻¹⁸² | — |

- **Selected record.** The certificate's margin gaps give ε = 0.998364 and δ = 1.25·10⁻²⁵. The binding rows are εq and 1 − ε − δ ≈ q, so κ ≈ a, the bit-network saving.
- **Inside the wall.** The real limit is the network saving a, and no all-network bound on a is known.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/sqrt-log-wall/wall_check.py` prints `PASS_SQUARE_ROOT_WALL_REDUCTION` (about 9 s). It passed locally on Python 3.12 and 3.14 against main at `17ce0c79`. It checks, from source text and the certificate:

1. 11 verbatim facts of the manuscript's reduction, rows and parameters;
2. both margins and the boxed κ in each of the nine assembly notes;
3. `dimension=eps`, `scalar_work=1-eps-delta` and the margin-above-κ slacks in all 122 research outer engines that define margins;
4. ε, δ and q for the selected record, recovered exactly from its certificate's outer table, with κ < min(ε, 1 − ε − δ) ≤ (1 − δ)/2 and κ < εq < q/(1 + q) < 1/2 in rational arithmetic;
5. d + ⌈log₂T/d⌉ ≥ 2√(log₂ T) for every log₂ T ≤ 4096 and every d.

As a negative control, changing the manuscript's `g_7=\epsilon` makes the check fail with exit status 1. CI runs the check on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

## Scope

- This is a statement about the framework's schedule and accounting, not a lower bound for integer multiplication in general.
- The pass bound assumes each level round and axis pass reads the whole box, as every current assembly does.
- No Lean proof is claimed.

## Credits and AI disclosure

prs.title: Composite cyclic inverses: exact certificates and modular lifting
prs.body:
Ali Romman's #621 proves uniform cyclic-kernel conditioning for prime-power radices and leaves other composites outside its claim. This package adds an **integral seed-certificate lifting mechanism for specified composite families**, together with six stronger fixed-radix certificates. **No new κ is claimed.**

If `A f_s+B f_s*=d` is an integral Bézout identity and p is prime with p not dividing s*d, the written proof establishes nonvanishing for `r=s*p^a` for **every a>=1 and every primitive root choice**. Reduction modulo p sends the two integral kernels to `z^(r-s) f_s` and `f_s*`; modular coprimality then lifts back to characteristic zero. Independently checked seeds give:

| Family | Condition on prime p |
|---|---|
| `r=2*p^a` | p not in {2,3} |
| `r=3*p^a` | p not in {3,43} |
| `r=4*p^a` | p not in {2,37} |

The proof handles reciprocal degree loss explicitly. #621's inherited norm/cofactor and Fourier arguments supply quantitative circle and inverse-norm bounds uniform in cyclic length, integer stride and unit scalar gauge. Excluded primes limit this modular route; they are not characteristic-zero counterexamples. This is not a theorem for all composite radices.

Separate exact certificates at **6, 10, 12, 14, 15 and 18** cover all 30 primitive embeddings symbolically and give sharper explicit rational bounds. The standard-library checker reconstructs cyclotomic polynomials and tail-product kernels without importing the SymPy generator or either predecessor checker. The lifting diagnostics reuse that independent integer engine and work over potentially reducible modular coefficient rings.

python3 -B -I -O research/composite-cyclic-bezout/verify_lifting.py --check research/composite-cyclic-bezout/LIFTING-EXPECTED.json

prs.title: Research: prove higher-target star-code hierarchies and decoder geometry
prs.body:
Research contribution with uniform proofs and exact finite certificates; **no new κ or physical supplier**.

This determines how much simultaneous information global proper-star observations can expose after puncturing. It extends the original asymmetric decoder obstruction into sharp one-/two-target geometry, a complete graph-case hierarchy, and uniform higher-target theorems. The new exception is concrete: at `q=p-k=2,k>=4`, a localized affine cube decodes three selectable targets using eleven deletions, beating every three-minimum-star span. Four and five selectable targets also need exactly eleven deletions.

### Completed results

- **Every available rank at k=2:** complete generalized-weight hierarchies with and without the empty star, including their higher-rank differences and the p=2 exception. Graph witnesses lift to rigorous upper bounds for higher k.
- **Every k>=2,q>=3:** the first two nonzero word weights are `2q+2` and `4q+2`. There are no intermediate weights. The third generalized weight is `6q+3`; every optimum is a triangle of minimum stars, with exactly `2^(k+1) binom(p,k-2) binom(q+2,3)` such subcodes.
- **Prescribed triples, q>=3:** exactly `6q` deletions suffice iff the three target columns are independent on some optimal triangle. Larger budgets for triples failing that criterion are not classified.
- **The complete q=2 third-weight boundary:** `d3=15` for k=2,3; for every k>=4, the first five generalized weights are `(6,11,14,15,16)`.
- **Earlier results retained:** uniform minimum-word rigidity, complete optimal two-dimensional-subcode classification, and the exact prescribed-pair budget (`4q+1` when signed intersection is at least k−2; otherwise `4q+2`), plus the original unpunctured and target-local results.

A generalized weight `d_r` gives the exact `d_r-r` deletion budget for **some selectable r-target set**. It does not assign that budget to every prescribed set. Code statements cover both proper-star spaces; the original uniform overlap corrections are absorbed only at power-of-two k. Exact nonlinear postprocessing of these same observations does not improve the information thresholds.

### Review and reproduction

Only `research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/` changes. Start with its README, then `HIGHER-GRAPH.md` and `HIGHER-WEIGHTS.md`. The latest extension is separated into graph/checker commit `76f007ab` and uniform-theorem/cube commit `7d526020`.

```sh
for check in higher cube boundary; do
  python3 -I -O -B "research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/${check}_verify.py" --self-test || exit

```

The new checks include four complete graph partition DPs, 8,224 literal edge restrictions, 449,606 complete small-code subspaces, **7,135,750 rank-three subspaces**, and weight distributions of 523,776 graph-code words. They verify 68 optimal graph decoders with 1,511 full-code restoration controls; fifteen cube decoders on full port families with 165 displayed-subcode restoration controls; and all five shortening spaces in the exceptional k=3 boundary. The cube receipts contain literal proper-star expansions, targets, deletions, coefficients, and scalar cost counts.

Python 3.11.13 and 3.14.5 produce byte-identical new receipts under isolated optimized execution. Relocation, receipt corruption rejection, output preservation, inherited checker replays, and immutable source hashes pass. Proofs and code received separate AI-assisted reviews; no independent human or proof-assistant verification is claimed. Finite enumeration supports the written uniform proofs rather than replacing them. Unrelated repository-wide regeneration, selected supplier cold replay, and hosted CI are not claimed.

Original base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`; higher-target continuation base: `8bcbaafe8590d30eff9c0ae5fd9e49479c84038c`. prs.title: Research: dirty echo, verifier repair, and priced bit-sharing boundaries
prs.body:
PR628's binary dirty commutator has quadratic factor-call growth and an executable phase-alias admission defect. This contribution adds a subquadratic multiway echo, a one-line alias guard, an exact full-transform/bit integration experiment, and bit-sharing cost gates that include physical owner restoration. The integration works functionally, but its complete recursive bill rejects this direct adapter as a route to larger κ. This is a construction refinement, executable repair and scoped negative research result.

### Local construction and verifier repair

The multiway echo composes noncommuting factor shears while restoring arbitrary borrowed data. Fixed fanout 8 reduces the leaf-call exponent from 2 to approximately 1.602452 with O(log n) borrowed arrays. At 512 factors the exact count falls from 262,144 to 21,952, using 21 arrays instead of 9. The flat variant takes 4n−4 calls and n−1 arrays. The complete inherited error recurrence is included; this is a classical local primitive, not an admitted multiplication supplier.

At pinned PR628, `phases is x` passes admission even though phases must remain read-only. For `x=phases=[1,1]`, outer b=1/4 and eight fractional bits, execution returns x=[1,15/16]. The submitted patch rejects source/target/scratch phase aliases before mutation. Replay applies the actual patch to the pinned Git source. More precision does not repair this exact counterexample.

### Full-transform and bit integration

`research/dirty-echo-integration/` implements:

- An all-role complex adapter and Boolean address-chunk interchange, including outputs on every role borrowed during execution.
- Complete normalized synthetic Fourier transforms over C[y]/(y^r+1), stored bit-reversed frequency order, signed monomial twiddles, opposite transforms and correctly normalized convolution.
- Independent exact references, instruction/interface corruption controls, source pins and deterministic evidence.

Three shears per pair complete the all-role adapter. Even granting one recursive child per additive leaf and making routing, phases, storage, preparation and precision free, its moment is `3 N(n)/(2 n^(1-b))`. Since `N(n) >= 4n-4`, its moment at saving zero is at least `6-6/n >= 3`. This rejects **this adapter's** bill for every nonnegative saving; it is not a lower bound for other integrations or suppliers.

Two exact counterexamples prevent silently substituting different operators: replacing the triangular Newton factor by its cyclic counterpart fails at radix 4, with a rank-r−1 boundary correction; the radix-3 cyclic kernel is singular on a length-5 cycle over GF(4). The latter rules out the unrestricted finite-field analogue, not restricted lengths or Boolean address permutations.

At κ=0.01, both retained supplier savings must exceed 1/99. With unchanged widths and volumes, uniform reductions of all paid terms would need to exceed approximately 2.70% for pinned #589 and 2.47% for pinned #659. These are exact-moment diagnostic targets, not feasible fractional deletions or replacement suppliers. No κ gain is attributed to the echo integration.

### Bit sharing priced before construction

`research/bit-role-sharing-budget/` extracts the actual PR589 local paid profile and all 661 Boolean columns, retains the complete frozen hosting remainder and fallback, and compares role-sharing budgets at the necessary bit saving 1/99 for κ=0.01.

- Equal-call pooling saves dispatches but not volume-weighted recursive work. A fixed-address-permutation rank argument also excludes fewer queried role volumes under arbitrary invertible XOR row charts and restored private dirt. Different address-dependent charts and native primitives are outside this model.
- Even ideal rank-8 consolidation of every local rank unit fails the target. Making all retained-total copies free still fails. The corresponding bit-only outer ceilings are below 0.002644610326897 and 0.007315906873875; neither is an achieved supplier.
- With the original rank mass and boundary remainder, cap 55 fails and cap 56 is the first passing relaxation. A hypothetical integer rank-57 invoice allows 431 extra rank-1 repair calls globally and needs over 98.48% of local rank mass fused. The eight-stage interpretation applies only to one port's active spaces; cross-port sharing has a larger span.
- A different arithmetic target is ideal rank-8 consolidation plus 100 **net paid rank units** removed per invocation after hosting: 99 fails, 100 passes. This is not achieved by simply deleting helpers or XORs.

No replacement supplier was built: the simple sharing classes fail even under favorable complete-cost bounds, and the passing high-rank/mass-reduction targets still lack an operator and hosting plan. No new κ is claimed. The independent positive-atanh engine reproduces the current bit root and agrees with the inherited Mercator engine on 133 complete invoices. Normal/optimized evidence is byte-identical; 108 small coded-query programs, 384 positive-control basis columns, source/scatter/expected-evidence mutations and a relocated minimal replay are checked.

Standalone command: `sh research/bit-role-sharing-budget/replay.sh /tmp/bit-role-sharing-budget`. Expected final line: `PASS_BIT_ROLE_SHARING_REPLAY`. The combined command below now includes this screen. Final overlap review through #716 distinguishes #705/#708/#714/#715; no new pinned coordination issue was found.

### Concrete bit-sharing candidate and physical hosting gate

`research/bit-sharing-hosting-gate/` follows the 100-net-unit arithmetic target with an exact scalar candidate and a source-bound reconstruction of all **126,432** frozen helper reservations. Neither candidate is admitted as a supplier.

- The nine-stage source-bank masks have one exact dependence: the last source is the XOR of the preceding eight. Nine running accumulators per replica can therefore share the source part of the retained decoder totals at the scalar level. The actual snapshots have rank-nine dirty contamination. The proposed owned-storage plan adds 288 persistent rows and nine temporary rows; source extraction, copy, clear and XOR costs are listed. ADDRESS-chart alignment is still unproved. Even gifting it, the maximum COPY credit is only **7 rank units per invocation**, with target moment 1.026605906228685.
- A hypothetical free producer eliminating 13 helper paths removes **104 local rank units**, but the explicit idle owners must complete all 104 vacated directions: **zero net credit**. The new complete profile is priced after coalescing those directions at the owners' original boundaries. Every one of the 439 single-helper eliminations has the same mass conservation. These favorable screens do not assert a replacement producer exists.
- The previous 100-unit screen granted rank-8 consolidation everywhere. Keeping the 222 rank-7 data climbs makes 100 and 101 fail; **102 first passes that narrower relaxation**. More fundamentally, under the current data/cover boundary identity, even zero COPY cost saves only 63 per invocation. Reaching 100 requires a changed boundary term.
- A scope control changes the hosting remainder: free elimination of all helper work plus perfect data consolidation still fails with COPY retained, but passes if COPY is also granted free. Thus 100 is not a universal necessary condition for other suppliers; the complete moment remains decisive.

The package verifies all 888 source-bank columns, retained source/dirty ranks and reflected copy forms, reconstructs chronological windows and disjoint owners independently of the parent allocator, and compares **449 complete invoices with two exact rational engines**. Normal, optimized and relocated minimal replays agree; six ownership/admission controls plus source/receipt corruption controls are rejected. prs.title: Consolidate six circuit PRs: 31.72% fewer bit ADDs and 22–25% fewer complex primitives

This batch retains six complete research packages and supplies one **source-pinned, executable integration** with actual-word native and whole-owner replay. It also composes the raw factory changes in this PR with the cheaper complex lowering.

prs.title: Research audit: tensor E8 rate and finite-depth center-copy correction
prs.body:
Research note / mathematical audit; **no new multiplication κ**.

PR647's retained provider proof states a tensor-depth moment limit, while its packaged verifier focuses on depth one. ```
9^n k_n = 28/(2739 log 3) * (1 - (3/2)(3/5)^n) + O(n/9^n),
```

## Result and scope

**Independent verification / research note; no new kappa.** This adds an independent finite-geometric-sum oracle for `(W-rho I)^(-1)`, where `(Wx)_i=tau_i*x_(i-s mod L)`, and checks the bilinear inverse transpose. It compares exact results with the neighboring rounded single-factor primitive from Chafik Boukhalfa / chafreaky's PR628, after cycle-local gathering and scattering.

For a stride cycle C of length m and phase product h_C, the written identity is

`(W_C-rho I)^(-1) = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} rho^(m-1-j) W_C^j / (h_C-rho^m)`.

The oracle uses exact rational complex arithmetic, not the predecessor's affine two-pass scan or Gaussian elimination. It checks both inverse products on every matrix entry. The dual independently reverses the stride and shifts phases by s, **without conjugation**, then checks the result against the actual inverse transpose.

A concrete length-6 / stride-2 witness rejects using one global phase product or the global length in place of each cycle's own closure. These are counterexamples to deliberately incorrect extensions, **not a defect in PR628's stated neighboring scope**. No such defect was found in the tested domain.

**Predecessor credit:** PR628 already provides constant-gauge arbitrary-stride sorting and the direct-sum infinity-norm argument. Neither is claimed new. The additional evidence covers independently varying phase products on multiple cycles and the bilinear dual through a different exact algorithm. Gather/scatter routing, phase reads, storage and restoration are not declared free or newly improved.

## Pins and package

- Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`.

Eight fixed four-block Clifford words at m=3, W=3, s=8 remained unresolved by bounded support and polynomial searches. A determinant argument now excludes every invertible complex scalar realization of those words: when paths with the same interior group product have the same accumulated unary rank, the total unary rank must be at least W*m.

The written theorem allows arbitrary width and any number of scalar mixing blocks, subject to that explicit path-homogeneity hypothesis. The finite checker specializes to three-qubit, three-register formal projective Clifford words. This does not settle the full register problem or claim a new primitive or kappa.

- Eight newly closed four-block follow-ups.
- Twenty-three further exclusions among 32 evolved words; nine fail the hypothesis and remain unclassified by this criterion.
- All 33 PR #680 words as regressions, recovered without support/torus solving.

The search consequence is concrete: repeated products alone are insufficient. A successful word below the W*m cost needs coincident interior products with different accumulated ranks.

prs.title: Scoped negative result: minimal E8 mixed-port extension is saturated
prs.body:
## Result

Scoped negative result; no new kappa. Every compatible non-root port added after at most 14 E8 root-line deletions, with the inherited nine-dimensional labels, forces the same D7 equality case up to Weyl symmetry. Exactly one non-root port type fits. Adding it makes every nonzero reader span all eight physical dimensions, so no further nonzero port can be added within this model.

The exact star copy cost rises from 64 on 106 root ports to **72 on 107 mixed ports**. This rules out improving the copied-information ratio by the minimum-puncture mixed-port mechanism before implementing helper or restoration work.

This extends Chi Zhao's #631 sharp threshold with equality classification and saturation. GamingPuzzled's #620 already computed the coordinate-axis example's approximate ratio; that example is credited, not claimed as new. #669's paired-hypercube result and #703's quaternionic result have different scopes.

Changes are confined to four files in `research/e8-minimal-mixed-port/`: proof, independent standard-library checker, exact receipt, and source pins. The checker uses a Gram-row basis instead of the predecessor's orthonormal factorization. The written Weyl-chamber reduction separates exhaustive coverage from finite replay.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-minimal-mixed-port/verify.py
```

Expected: PASS for 8 maximal flats, all 511 nonzero readers before and after augmentation, one non-root candidate, and 5 negative-control categories; star costs 64 and 72. Every run compares the complete regenerated receipt with the checked-in JSON.

Validation passed on Python 3.14.8 and Python 3.11.15 with optimized mode. Controls reject duplicate non-root ports, even labels, each of the 14 forbidden root restorations, a full-rank normal request, and a malformed simple system. A separate AI-assisted implementation generated the signed roots in a different order, chose another binary basis, and checked ranks over GF(3), with exact annihilators for deficient spans. It independently confirmed costs 64 and 72. Selected-record integrity, source hashes, and staged whitespace checks pass.

The expensive repository-wide and selected supplier cold replays were not repeated. No existing supplier, generator, assembly, `upstream/` file, or selected-frontier pointer changes.

prs.title: Format limits part 2 (no κ claim): erratum to #595, exact invoice prices, frontier-word censuses, decoder floors, spec requirements, centre and fragmentation walls
prs.body:
**No κ claim.** This continues the merged #595. It records what we have proved and measured about the limits of the construction format and of the shipped #656 word, including an erratum to #595. Every result states its scope. Each is marked *CHECKED* (recomputed by `verify.sh`; *CHECKED (log)* = a shipped, sha256-pinned log is compared), *ARGUED* (proof or file:line argument in the README) or *RECORDED* (an earlier run that is not repeated; notes are shipped where the row names them).

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/format-limits-2/requirements.txt          # sections 5-9 only
bash research/format-limits-2/verify.sh /fresh/output/dir                    # 233 PASS lines, ~22 s; step 0 fails hard on any MANIFEST/provenance mismatch
E1_FULL=1 bash research/format-limits-2/verify.sh /fresh/output/dir          # also re-runs #595's a5 unchanged: 228 PASS lines, ~62 s
```

### Results
| id | result | status |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | **ERRATUM to #595.** The ×1.15–2.15 "schedule/ρ family" multipliers (#595 census item 8, open problem 3) come from dropping idle-frame rules, not from a ρ family: idle changes free ×2.15, one-child batching ×1.55, no split pre-stretch ×1.18 at s = 9 (×1.15 best, s = 5), both sides. | numbers CHECKED; reading ARGUED |
| E2 | ρ is not a verifier input (it is the hard-coded final bank swap). Over all pair-preserving ρ at P ≤ 3 (reachable set exactly Sp(4,2) = 720 and Sp(6,2) = 1,451,520) none beats B_K: multiplier 1.000. | (b) CHECKED (log, re-run and compared); (a) ARGUED |
| P1 | Complex invoice calculus on #626 (reproduced to 16+ digits): centre −1 = +22.6% b; one cst unit +2.81%; one port +2.15%; one w9 helper +0.068% (+0.137% if its width merges). | CHECKED |
| P2 | Bit invoice calculus on #555: c reproduced to 24 digits; cst unit ±2.80% c, port 2.15%. Word-level helper knobs (0.06–0.11% c) not re-run. | root, mass, cst rows CHECKED; rest RECORDED |
| P3 | Helper exchange rate by width on #649: w9 0.070% (no merge) / 0.140% (merged), down to w4 0.026 / 0.072; explains the old 0.027–0.143 spread. | CHECKED |
| P4 | Stage count s = 9 → 7 is worse at every R: hosting overflows 8.7%, b₇ only +0.21% over b₉ at equal R. | CHECKED (model) |
| P5 | The climb mass is a forced cover (mass = mW − deficit): mass padding is illegal, frame annealing on the #626 ck/jp8 words gains 0.0% b (fixed op order; jump-merging frame raises as in #741 were not in the move set), "fewer helpers" is not a gain. | identity CHECKED; SA outcome RECORDED |
| C1 | Provenance census of #656: 492 helpers born at 4 allocation sites: S1 scratch 224, S3 packet copy 156, S4 slot copy 112; κ identity exact. | CHECKED (tags from a recorded rebuild) |
| C2 | The shipped word is a dirty-borrow program, not a clean SLP: 2056 distinct read rows (minimum chain cover 2056), 268 of 422 B-phase helpers are pure dirt, equal to the S3 + S4 sites. | CHECKED |
| C3 | The 112 ports form a cap in F₂⁹ (no three XOR to 0, every hyperplane misses ≥ 48); 8-port blocks sit at dimension ≤ 5. | cap CHECKED; corollary ARGUED |
| G1 | Gauge-free cold-end bound N_cold ≤ Σ_b(\|Q_b\| − rank C[Q_b]); #645 attains 44. | CHECKED on #645; 504 / K480 values RECORDED |
| G2 | Gauge44 is gauge-optimal at 44 for its frame schedule; read-order ceiling 48 (+0.13–0.16% b), home-first legal ceiling 46. | 44 = bound CHECKED; ceilings RECORDED |
| G3 | **Theorem.** A helper can end at a hyperplane U only if the supports of its row of M⁻¹ and its column of M lie in Q_U; covers every reordering and relay strategy. | ARGUED (Lean on #593's package RECORDED) |
| D1 | Complex decoder floor on P112: exactly 8 costly terms give cst ≥ 64 (9 label spans over 440,880 supports); all costly terms β ≥ 8 and n ≥ 9 give cst ≥ 72; n = 8 is infinitesimally rigid up to gauge. Open: mixed β ≤ 7 terms with n ≥ 9. | counts, spans, rigidity CHECKED; step (b), (c) ARGUED; flip-walk logs CHECKED (log) |
| D2 | Any n = 8 exact P112 decoder is D = XA, T = XA⁻ᵀ; absorbing one frame line costs exactly +1 cst, a pair +2 (≈ 272k and 951k sampled cases). | ARGUED; census CHECKED (log) |
| D3 | Non-star complex decoders exist: exact cst 63 on all six single-line P111 punctures, cst 56 on P104. Their buildability price is negative (net −0.1 to −10% b). | hits CHECKED (exact); walks CHECKED (log); price RECORDED |

| F3 | S1 block scratch cannot be shared or shortened inside the format: 16 distinct sparse forms per block, 0 of 16 equal twins retireable. | RECORDED |
| F4 | Twin substitution for the 73 frame-insulator helpers fails on #656: all 111 twin reads are value-exact, 0 of 111 are legal one at a time (each raises 2–6 final caps), 0 of 73 helpers deletable. | RECORDED (exact oracle, not shipped) |
| F5 | Re-ordering reads of read-only S3 faces fails on #656: for 27 of the 32 structurally clean faces every B slot from the last write to the copy slot (window ≈ 740–860 ops), in given and reversed reader order, gives 0 legal reads. | RECORDED (exact oracle, not shipped) |
| F6 | The opening miner on the rebuilt #664 word finds 2534 disjoint-lifetime helper pairs; all 2534 need frame growth and none is frame-nested, so 0 register-reuse openings: the same rigidity as #656. | CHECKED (log) |
| O1 | Cross-block totals ("X4" faces): 2688 reach-10 quads all span 4 blocks; ledger 12.21% b (hypothetical design) does not close. | faces CHECKED; ledger RECORDED |
| O2 | #617 → #622 K-triangle ledger on the moment engine: ideal gross +0.52% b for 12 helpers, net +0.0146% after 6 lost cold ends and rewired climbs. | RECORDED |
| App. | **Appendix: conditional candidates** (5 items, each with one blocking condition; none is a result). | unverified |

31 rows by primary status: 21 CHECKED, 6 ARGUED, 4 RECORDED.

### Open problems
- **Mixed-beta decoders with n >= 9** (D1): a cst below 64 on P112 would have to mix terms with beta <= 7.
- **An order-free fragmentation ceiling** (F1, F2): the loose order-free bound (2478 psi/call) is uncalibrated.
- **Non-projection rational labels** (S2) and **a frame schedule with |I| > 8 per block** (G1, G2).
- **Value-exact re-threading beyond the fixed order and DAG** (F2).

README, "Conditional candidates (unverified: could work IF...)": 5 items, each with one measured fact and one blocking condition (S1 scratch never read, single-packet S4, order-free frame slack, radix-4 first climb, partner-merge of pure-dirt helpers). None is a result. Two earlier candidates were tested and failed (F4, F5).

*Update after submission:* single-packet S4 (item 2) is answered negatively: 18 of the 28 deferred S4 adds are illegal even when deferred alone, checked on cycles 0–1. The never-read S1 drop (item 1) is mostly answered negatively: given the shipped end-of-A frames, each of the 11 eight-line S1 blocks needs all 16 registers (forced-matching argument). Blocks (0,1,*) and the true-cap case remain open. See the README appendix.

prs.title: Research theorem: nine-call bound for arbitrary invertible three-register targets
prs.body:
PR468 proves that three invertible lower-triangular rational 3×3 targets need nine rank-one calls in the abelian three-register bit model. This research theorem removes the target-triangularity assumption: the minimum remains nine for **arbitrary invertible rational targets**.

The new connection is to extract a dimension-independent disjoint-subset lemma from PR468's low-corank argument. With at most two frame relations, every target is a sum of a disjoint subset of paid frames. This gives a six-call bound for arbitrary invertible 2×2 target triples and closes the formerly flagged block case in address span four. The other reductions and the complete span-five search remain unchanged. The note expands the proof, including the associated-graded common-J argument, rather than extrapolating from a bounded word test.

The extension covers strictly more targets: the package exhibits I, C, C² with characteristic polynomial of C equal to x³−2. These cannot be made jointly lower triangular by any common rational left/right coordinate changes. Their nine-call construction is checked as an exact formal group-algebra identity.

prs.title: Research note: sharp off-target proper-star puncture threshold
prs.body:
PR669 proves the sharp puncture threshold for target-local stars and explicitly leaves punctured decoders using arbitrary off-target stars open. This **research note / scoped negative result** closes that larger scalar class: for every power-of-two k >= 2 and p >= k, decoding one retained target requires exactly **2(p-k)+1** deleted ports. **No new kappa or paid supplier is claimed.**

The written elementary proof establishes the stronger identity d(C_{p,k}) = 2(p-k+1) for the global degree-<k star evaluation code, including the empty star, for every k >= 2. It uses generalized-cube parity, an even-face lemma and restriction induction. At a power-of-two k, permitted target overlap-class corrections add no functions to that code. The attaining witness uses one nonempty (k-1)-star.

A ten-star p=5,k=4 example reaches the same threshold while all 16 target intersection cells survive. Thus PR669's **minimum threshold** extends globally, while its **local cell feasibility criterion** does not. Exact elimination checks local infeasibility for this example.

Changes are limited to research/global-star-puncture/ and one scoped workflow. The accepted conditional kappa remains 51110230636731/31250000000000000; selected-result, existing suppliers, generators and upstream/ are unchanged.

```sh
python3 -B research/global-star-puncture/verify.py

All 28,680 pair syndromes in the second domain are distinct. Coverage also includes all 38,344 codewords in seven small domains, exhaustive even-face support checks in dimensions 1–4, valid generalized-face cubes, and a non-power-of-two positive escape control. ## Result

**Research note and scoped negative result. No new kappa or physical supplier.**

PR620 leaves the copy cost of asymmetric Gaussian E8 decoders open. This contribution proves a lower bound of **40 Gaussian rank units / 80 rational rank units**, for any finite number of scalar binary totals and the pairing-rank charge of #446. Under the separate #595/#620 deficit accounting, `D/T <= 120(s-1) - 80s = 40s-120`. prs.title: Research consolidation: uniform proof of the archived 2P+1 stage bound
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The archived campaign report M claims that exchanging P bank pairs requires at least 2P + 1 stages. Its discussion mixes a four-call rank argument with finite searches for P <= 3. This research consolidation supplies a self-contained uniform argument and confirms the same bound; it does not claim a new kappa or controller.

For two blocks of dimension P*v, consider calls that add a rank-at-most-v linear function of one block to the other, with arbitrary invertible block-diagonal bridges. The potential rank(A) + rank(D) starts at 2P*v and ends at zero. The first call cannot lower it, and every later call lowers it by at most v. Thus at least 2P + 1 calls are needed, over every field. The existing Sussman borrowing chain attains the count. The endpoint is measured before the designated terminal exchange; physical frames, helper contracts, restoration and all-size/analytic interfaces remain separate obligations.

prs.title: Scoped negative result: PR626 jp8 and ck A/B frames admit no next complex tick at fixed order (exact duals, no new κ)
prs.body:
# Fixed-order A/B frame exclusion for the selected PR626 complex providers

**Scoped negative result; no new κ.** Base `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Sprint track: complex supplier (OS seed 23).

## Claim

Take the emitted programs of the two selected #626 complex providers: **jp8**, used in 64 of the 72 calls, and **ck**, used in 8. Use both orientations. The macro list, order and operands stay fixed, as do every start frame, final frame and target level, each centre chain, and the frame of every macro outside phases A and B. Any frame in F_2^9 may then be assigned to any A or B scalar macro, simultaneously. No assignment that is legal under `hpe_audit_local.py`'s frame rules yields a native complex moment below one at

    b_next = 102387919519255428911/62500000000000000000000

This is the next 10^-24 grid point above #626's accepted endpoint. With owners, widths, the bit supplier and the outer assembly unchanged, frame-only reassignment therefore cannot raise the binding complex endpoint, and so cannot raise the selected κ.

## Proof (finite, exact)

1. **Domains.** Forward joins from the fixed starts and pins give `lo_i`, and backward meets from the finals and pins give `hi_i`. Every legal frame satisfies `lo_i <= G_i <= hi_i`. In these words `dim(hi/lo) <= 3`. The verifier enumerates every subspace in each interval and checks completeness: 2, 5 or 16 choices per macro (`model.py`).
2. **LP.** For each component of free macros, the local-polytope LP uses variables x(i,G), plus nested pair variables y on consecutive macros of a register (counted with multiplicity). Every legal assignment is a 0/1 point of this LP. Each register's total climb is fixed, so the paid local moment equals sum n_k c_k plus a constant, where c_k = k^(1-b) - k. The common positive factor m^b/(mW) is dropped.
3. **Duals.** Each component has a rational dual whose entries are linear forms in c_2..c_9. The verifier checks two things. First, every reduced cost is >= 0 at b_next, using two rational engines: its own atanh/alternating-series engine, and the pinned repository `moment.py`. Second, the dual objective equals the literal #626 baseline as an exact coefficient-vector identity. By weak duality, every legal assignment costs at least as much as the baseline.
4. **Global step.** Using the pinned #626 `ASSEMBLY.json` profile, both engines put the baseline global moment minus one at about +6.49e-25 at b_next. Every child term increases with b. So for each call, each reassignment has a local moment at least the baseline's at b_next, and the reassigned supplier is rejected at b_next and above.

Small components (63 for jp8 and 96 for ck, per orientation) are also brute-forced over all legal assignments as an independent cross-check.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-k492-frame-bound/verify.py            # committed inputs, ~30 s, stdlib only
python3 -B research/complex-k492-frame-bound/verify.py --controls # six controls must be rejected
```

Expected: `PASS_FIXED_ORDER_AB_FRAME_EXCLUSION_PR626` and `PASS_CONTROLS 6 of 6 rejected`. `--work DIR` checks fresh outputs of `research/complex-k492-owner-repair/verify.sh DIR` instead.

The inputs are the jp8/ck `CANONICAL-WORD` and `LOCAL-PROGRAMS` files. Their gzip SHA-256 equals the hashes recorded in `research/community-k492-audit/pr626/replay/mixed-global/base/providers/*/INDEPENDENT-LOCAL-REPLAY.json`, and the decompressed payload hashes are pinned in `SOURCES.json`.

This was validated in two ways: the full #626 provider replay was run fresh on macOS with Python 3.12, and its outputs matched; and the verifier was run on Python 3.11 and 3.15. Running with `-O` is refused.

The six controls are:
- a dropped component
- an inflated dual
- an incomplete domain
- the accepted (rather than next) endpoint
- a legal but worse baseline, which the duals must not certify
- the wrong word

`gen_duals.py` (needs highspy/scipy) nominates the duals; it is deterministic, reproducing the pinned payload hash. `explore/exact.py` (needs ortools) solves the same exact model with CP-SAT and reports the baseline objective as optimal for both words. It is a solver cross-check, not part of the proof.

## Exploratory findings (not shipped as checks)

- A per-register rank-path relaxation, which drops shared geometry, leaves gaps on 410 jp8 registers.
- A coupled dimension-only relaxation claims a large spurious gain, which shrinks after pair-span cuts but does not vanish.
- Greedy and annealed block moves and a flag-structured frame family all found no improvement.

So the geometric subspace constraints are what close the gap, which is why the full subspace LP is needed.

## Scope

Not covered:
- scalar rewrites, reordering, or changed cuts or centres
- frames of zero-frame precondition, cleanup-tail and full-frame-cleanup macros
- changed starts or finals (and so widths), owners, hosting or the invoice
- the bit supplier, other words (for example the open #645/#659/#685 lineages), or other outer theorems

The result holds at the fixed exponent b_next, not for all exponents. All inherited all-size, compiler, realization, hosting, precision, tape and analytic assumptions remain. This is a finite certificate, not a Lean proof.

## Credit

The method follows chafreaky's #557 (`research/frame-domain-ceiling`, PR551 word): complete F_2 domains, an LP relaxation and symbolic exact duals. This package is a new implementation against the emitted #626 programs. Concurrent #698 (thakrarsagar) proves ck B-phase optimality at fixed end-of-B frames for all exponents; this result independently corroborates it at b_next and adds jp8, joint A/B freedom and the global next-tick exclusion. #661 (yuj1r0) is the bit analogue.

The suppliers and their lineage are Jeremy Kothe (#622), Chafik Boukhalfa (#626), DreamingOfClouds, icekylinx and the selected-record contributors. Prepared with substantial AI assistance (Anthropic Claude). Apache-2.0.

- Its paid profile is `32 H1 + 17 H2 + 11 H3`. The specified direct circuit with the same helper left idle has `48 H1 + 12 H2 + 6 H3 + H9`. Both have rank mass 99.

## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research note with a finite circuit construction and exact verification. No new κ.** The selected certificate, its κ (`51110230636731/31250000000000000`) and `upstream/` are unchanged. All files are new, under `research/r420-block9-factorization/`.

This PR replaces it with 24 XORs. Regenerating the literal reverse cleanup saves 14 more, at the rank-eight full frame. D, A, the scatter, the retained totals and every other B gate are unchanged.

| Quantity | Original | Replacement |
|---|---:|---:|
| Block 9 XORs | 38 | 24 |
| Literal cleanup gate records | 2,661 | 2,647 |
| Complete native scalar ADDs | 26,916 | 26,888 |
| Local reverse positive prefix bound | 2,270,064 | 2,234,964 |
| Local forward positive prefix bound | 144,651 | 144,651 |
| Paid rank mass | 5,112 | 5,112 |

- **Exact block identity.** Write `T_ab = I + e_a e_b^T`. The old and new chronological gate lists have the same positive integer transfer matrix, so block 9 computes the same linear map over every commutative ring, F2 included, on arbitrary register contents. The signed inverse is also identical, and the ordered physical output assignment is kept. The complete dirty-restored word is certified over F2; its defining endpoint is not claimed over the integers.
- **Positive bounds do not grow.** The positive reverse transfer is entrywise no larger, with 22 strict entries. Block followed by positive reverse improves 102 entries, and its unit-input maximum falls from 973 to 137. The unchanged exterior operations are monotone on nonnegative bounds, so the domination carries through the whole word and no prefix bound increases. The five-stage payload stays at 100 bits and the nine-stage charge at 192 bits.
- **No hidden cost.** The change adds no helper, source access, copy, frame change or recursive child. Every register keeps its frame path, and the paid histogram `{1:1320, 2:1440, 4:60, 5:120, 8:9}` is unchanged. The interface is #543's original H1–H5, including literal cleanup reversal (H4).
- **Search.** A seeded walk factors the block's 12-by-12 transfer matrix from both ends: subtracting a dominated row removes a final gate, subtracting a column removes a first gate, and entries stay nonnegative. With OS seed 19 it ran a fixed 2,000 trials. 372 reached the identity, 236 of those had a dominated positive reverse, and the best has 24 gates. 24 is not claimed minimal.

**Predecessor work.** Details and pins are in the README and SOURCES.json.
- eumemic's #543, reviewed at `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535`, supplies the R420 word, source plan, integer norm objective, interleaved interface and exact checker, building on #493.
- The exporter, checker and pricing lineage is credited in the README: Dylan Crow (#370 word and exporter), DaysSky (bridged cohort checker), DreamingOfClouds (#503/#510 and #463 nine-stage pricing), Zhihao Chen (#425 interface), Chafik Boukhalfa (common-label and hosting/emitter work), and the cumulative authors in the selected maintainer review.

**Open obligations.**
- Build the globally hosted owner program, physical invoice and outer assembly for the changed word, and update the supplier bindings. In the nine-stage invoice's scalar term, `9 * 32 * local_additions + bridge_additions`, the local saving would remove 8,064 ADDs; nothing hosted is regenerated here.
- Settle whether 24 gates is minimal for this block.
- Discharge the inherited all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-basis realization, pooled hosting, normalized residual, precision/tape/exact-recovery and analytic-transfer assumptions.

No κ change follows from the local count: the recursive profile and rounded prefix budgets are unchanged, and the selected assembly is complex-bound.

[Research note and proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/README.md), [frozen circuit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/CANDIDATE.json), [certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/CERTIFICATE.json), [source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/SOURCES.json), [validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/VALIDATION.json), [verifier](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/verify.py) and [search](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/08b4a039ba4938dd4f4c89a69759f49ed21923ef/research/r420-block9-factorization/search.py).

**Overlap.** The pre-submission refresh at 05:31 UTC on 13 October searched the titles and bodies of the 320 most recent PRs (#462–#782, all states) and read every R420 circuit PR among them; none changes block 9's gates. `main` is still at base `66849e1`, so no merged change touches the word. #670 (yongjae321) and #674 (x0hu) resynthesize blocks 3 and 5, by local F2 rewrites and explicit sum sharing. #688 (Ali Romman) composes those two, and #681 (alluri-ritual) consolidates #688 with phase-A, D, decoder and complex-supplier work; none of the four touches block 9, and no composition with them is certified here. Two of its 101 windows, `[120,124)` and `[126,130)` of the expanded original cleanup (one XOR each), lie inside block 9's reversed segment `[120,158)`, which this PR replaces wholesale, so the two savings are not additive. #710's conjugation lies outside that segment, and #691 (mtpsl) applies the same forward-equality and reverse-domination test to phase-A quad 13. #686, #694, #713, #716, #733, #742, #759 and #774 change the frame-zero compensation D, and #708, #748 and #753 change the phase-A decoder totals; each saves more than 28 ADDs. prs.title: Research construction: R420 target-basis compensation saves 7,879 XORs within the existing 192-bit nine-stage prefix charge (no new κ)
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Status: research construction with exact verification. No new κ.** The selected certificate, its κ (`51110230636731/31250000000000000`) and `upstream/` are unchanged. All files are new, under `research/r420-target-compensation/`.

eumemic's #543 R420 bit word implements its frame-zero dirty-helper compensation D, `y <- y + K s` for a fixed binary 120-by-420 matrix `K`, with 19,922 XORs. This PR factors `K` through a reversible target basis. D first applies 205 target transvections `y[a] ^= y[b]`, whose product is `E`. It then adds helpers along the 11,633 nonzero entries of `R = E K`, and finally repeats the 205 transvections in reverse order. Over F2 the result is `E^-1 (E y + R s) = y + K s` for arbitrary incoming targets and helpers. D never writes a helper or a source and needs no workspace.

| Quantity | #543 | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| D XORs (entrance + helper injections + exit) | 19,922 | 12,043 (205 + 11,633 + 205) |
| Complete native word, XORs | 26,916 | 19,037 |
| Hosted instructions, 288 local calls | 8,603,712 | 6,334,560 |
| Forward / reverse positive bounds F / B | 144,651 / 2,270,064 | 144,651 / 4,409,580 |
| Local payload `64 F^3 B^2`, bits (cap 104) | 100 | 102 |
| Nine-stage prefix `2^18 F^5 B^4` / charge, bits | 189 / 192 | 192 / 192 |
| Two-level coefficient / charge, bits | 416 / 512 | 424 / 512 |

- **Unchanged.** Only D changes. The 420 helpers, the nine COPY/ERASE pairs, every register's frame path, the paid profile `{1:1320, 2:1440, 4:60, 5:120, 8:9}` with rank mass 5,112, and the recursive children stay as they are. The bit lower bound and the selected κ reproduce exactly.
- **Prefix.** The reverse bound grows. The search admitted a row step only if F stayed at most 144,651 and B at most 4,409,638, the largest B with `2^18 F^5 B^4 < 2^192`, so the existing 192-bit nine-stage and 512-bit two-level charges still hold. The unrounded invoice coefficient increases. The claim is fewer instructions under unchanged charges, not a measured speedup.
- **Changed hypothesis.** The new D breaks #543's gate-local H2, under which D gates read only helpers, and #543's direct `K_equals_D` extraction no longer applies. The verifier records both predicates as false and keeps every other H1–H5 check. In their place, README.md proves a semantic D-boundary lemma: D runs at frame zero and implements exactly `(x, y, s) -> (x, y + K s, s)`, so the unchanged remainder of the word sees identical values and frames. The verifier checks that boundary on all 660 symbolic columns.
- **Search.** OS seed 18 chose this object (`18 mod 3 = 0` among three candidates). At each step a greedy pass scored every ordered pair of target rows, kept only steps that passed an exact incremental prefix check, and broke ties with the seed. It stopped after 205 steps and 2,941,680 pair evaluations, when no admissible positive-gain pair remained; the cap was 1,000 steps. An unrestricted control with the same seed reached 10,384 D XORs but needed 201 nine-stage bits and broke the 104-bit payload cap, so it is kept only as a rejected control. 12,043 is not claimed optimal.

**Predecessor work.** Details and pins for 39 source files are in README.md and SOURCES.json.
- eumemic's #543, reviewed at `2065fe4f72a914d907f1046603f5a36f17018535` and building on #493, supplies the word, the compensation matrix, the interleaved interface and the checker this package reuses.
- Credit carried from #543's lineage: Dylan Crow (E8 word, record and checker lineage), DreamingOfClouds (#503/#510, generalized nine-stage accounting), DaysSky (bridged columns, whole-call hosting), Zhihao Chen (mutable-source/common-label and compressed geometry) and Chafik Boukhalfa (physical routes, templates and audits). Chafik Boukhalfa's selected #626 supplies the complex lower bound that the hosted replay cites.
- Dugongue's #476 and #478 used the reversible donor-receiver target identity on R715 phase B. Each transvection pair here is that identity, applied to the compensation.
- Mikhail R. Gadelha's concurrent #686 published the semantic D-boundary substitution first. This PR claims no priority for it or for basis factoring.

**Open obligations.**
- A maintainer must accept the semantic D-boundary lemma in place of the gate-local H2 and update the supplier's source bindings.
- B sits 58 below the nine-stage cutoff, so combining this D with any change that raises F or B needs a fresh prefix recount.
- The all-size compiler, common-label/mutable-basis realization, pooled hosting, normalized residual, precision/tape recovery and analytic-transfer assumptions remain inherited.

[Research note and proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/README.md), [frozen recipe](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/candidate.json), [certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/CERTIFICATE.json), [hosted certificate](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/HOSTED-CERTIFICATE.json), [source pins](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/SOURCES.json), [validation record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/VALIDATION.json), [seed, search and overlap record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/RESEARCH.json), [verifier](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/verify.py) and [search](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6be7364e0245c5a1c931cb1c43b3da991b755850/research/r420-target-compensation/search.py).

**Overlap.** No coordination issue exists; the only open issue, #650, asks about Discussions. The circuit was nominated and frozen locally before any concurrent D PR was read (RESEARCH.json records the freeze at 04:19 UTC on 13 October), and nothing from those PRs is imported. The package README records the overlap as of 04:25 UTC, when only #686 and #694 had appeared. A refresh between 05:28 and 05:37 UTC searched PR titles and bodies through #788 and read every PR among them that changes D. `main` is still `66849e1`, so nothing on D has merged. Many open PRs now change this D, and two reach lower counts:

| PR | Basis and recipe class | D XORs | Native XORs | Nine-stage bits |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| This PR | target; 205 successive steps | 12,043 | 19,037 | 192 |
| #686 | helper; one pair | 19,814 | 26,808 | 189 |
| #694 | helper; 201 disjoint pairs | 12,988 | 19,982 | 192 |
| #713 | target; 57 disjoint pairs | 16,772 | 23,766 | 191 |
| #716 | target; 60 disjoint pairs, optimal among disjoint pairs | 16,672 | 23,666 | 191 |
| #742 | target; shared donors | 16,634 | 23,628 | 192 |
| #759 | target; rooted forest | 15,138 | 22,132 | 197 |
| #774 | target; forest with optimized cuts | 15,025 | 22,019 | 197 |
| #733 | #694's helper basis, then 57 target pairs | 11,554 | 18,548 | 195 |
| #681 | #694's helper basis, then 56 target pairs, in a six-PR consolidation | 11,562 | 18,378 | 196 |

The last column applies this package's nine-stage formula to each PR's reported F and B. The other D PRs check the local payload against 2^104 and leave the hosted prefix to integration; #681 reports 196 bits itself, and the formula reproduces it. #681's native count includes its phase-A, phase-B and decoder changes.

- **Lower counts.** Scott Woolsey Biggart's #733 and the D stage of Alluri's #681 use 489 and 481 fewer D XORs than this PR. Both exceed the 192-bit nine-stage charge: #681 raises its allocation to 256 bits and replays the hosted invoice at that charge, and #733 leaves global invoices open. This PR does not settle whether their extra savings are worth the larger allocation.
- **What this adds.** Of the D constructions that keep the existing 192-bit charge, this one saves the most, 945 XORs more than Greer Guthrie's #694. Apart from #681's consolidation, it is the only D package that replays the complete nine-stage hosted invoice. Its D of 12,043 lies below the 14,921-XOR floor that Oscar Fennell's #759 certifies for rooted target forests, a floor Anthony's #774 corroborates, so this circuit lies outside that class, as it lies outside the disjoint pairs of Sagar Thakrar's #716. Scott Woolsey Biggart's #713 published the first target-side circuit, at 04:40 UTC, followed by #716 and ellipsi2's #742.
- **Composition and conflict.** These PRs replace the same D subword, so they are alternatives; no file paths collide. #733 shows that a helper basis and a target basis compose. At #694's F = 202,699, however, the 192-bit charge allows B only up to 2,892,279, against #694's own 2,446,788, so this PR attempts no such composition. cxnmai's #748 changes K itself through a decoder-total representation, which would require recomputing this recipe on the new matrix. #731 (Joshua Snider) and #762 (Sagar Thakrar) verify the baseline K and complement this work. #749 (Sricharan Vagvala) takes target pairs to the JP8 complex supplier. The phase-A, phase-B and cleanup PRs (#670, #674, #688, #691, #708, #710, #753, #754) change other subwords; combining any of them with this D needs the prefix recount above.

## Validation

From the repository root (Python 3.11+, standard library only):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r420-target-compensation/verify.py
```

Output, re-run on base `66849e1` with this package before submission (Linux, Python 3.12.3, about 3 seconds):

```text
PASS_R420_TARGET_COMPENSATION D=19922->12043 total=26916->19037 columns=660 rank_mass=5112 nine_bits=192 controls=13
```

`python3 -I -B research/r420-target-compensation/search.py` reruns both seed-18 trials and compares the full result with the frozen recipe. It printed `PASS_REPRODUCIBLE_SEARCH guarded_steps=205 D_adds=12043 trials=2 seed=18` in the same pre-submission run.

The optional complete hosted replay needs a C++17 compiler, Boost headers, and `requirements.txt` (SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.3.0) in a virtual environment. It writes a fresh directory under `build/`:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/r420-target-compensation/replay_hosted.py
```

Expected final status:

```text
PASS_R420_TARGET_COMPENSATION_HOSTED local_adds=19037 hosted_events=6334560 prefix_charge=192 coefficient_charge=512 kappa=unchanged
```

- **Finite checks.**
  - `verify.py` runs #543's exact lattice, frame and symbolic-row engine, plus a separate Boolean walk of all 660 columns in each direction. It checks the frozen recipe without trusting or rerunning the search, and rejects all 13 negative controls. One control omits the whole entrance basis: it passes when targets start at zero but fails the arbitrary-target boundary.
  - The hosted replay freshly compiles the predecessor C++ engines. It checks 900 five-stage and 1,380 nine-stage formal columns with 6 and 18 omitted-bridge controls, and 4,740 unbanked parent columns; the parent and hosted audits reject 17 and 16 mutations. Four record controls omit a basis ADD, a helper ADD or a COPY, or understate a MOVE rank. All 47 outer assembly inequalities reproduce the selected κ from #626's pinned complex lower bound. The recorded run, on Linux with Python 3.12.3, SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.3.0 and GCC 13.3.0, produced a full report equal to HOSTED-CERTIFICATE.json. It was not re-run for this submission.
- **Proof arguments.** README.md proves the D-boundary lemma, its substitution into the unchanged word, and the exact incremental formula the search uses to admit steps. None of these is inferred from the finite replay. The identity holds over F2; the positive integer bounds are recomputed from the literal instructions in both orientations.
- **Repository checks.** `make selected-record-check` passes: `PASS selected record, exact kappa, original source inventory and proof supplement: 51110230636731/31250000000000000`. `git diff --check` is clean, and no existing file or `upstream/` byte changes. The verifier above was re-run on the submitted commit.
- **Not claimed.** This is not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem or a cold replay of the complex supplier; #626's complex bound is pinned and cited. It claims no circuit optimality, no measured speedup and no composition with any other D, phase-A, phase-B or cleanup change. No repository-wide suite, eleven-stage physical replay, remote CI or Lean pass was run.

Sprint: bit-supplier track, OS seed 18. The claim and its result update are recorded locally. |---|---:|---:|
| h=23 | 72.876 s | 30.901 s |

prs.title: Research: certified format ceilings for Eisenstein/Gaussian/Hurwitz E8 copy floors (no κ claim)
prs.body:
**Research note and tooling. No κ claim and no word.** Contributed by Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani), with substantial AI assistance.

Builds on the extension-ring E8 floors already proved: #620 (screen), #703 (Hurwitz cost exactly 10), #738/#770/#767 (Gaussian floor 40), #798 (Eisenstein cost ≥22, open in [22,40]) and #765. It does not re-prove them. It turns them into **certified B_K format ceilings** using the unchanged `research/format-limits-corrected` engine.

## Findings
- **The outer assembly is saturated.** The selected κ equals a/(1+a) for the binding complex supplier to a relative 1.4e-16. So ring, transform length, resampling and Fürer/SS/HvdH-type outer changes can gain at most a factor 1+a ≈ 1.0016.
- **Eisenstein bit side.** A decoder of cost ≤24 would give a ceiling above 1/99 (cost 24: X ≤ 1.150e-2; cost 25: X ≤ 1.0053e-2). Cost ≤28 still beats the realised E8 bit unit (6.000e-3). Coordinate-total decoders cost at least 28 (new exact clique bound), so only non-coordinate decoders inside #798's open interval could matter.
- **Gaussian floor 40** gives X ≤ 7.688e-3. **Hurwitz** gives no positive saving for s ≤ 13.
- **Complex side (argued).** An Eisenstein complex unit has an F₄ window of at least ω = 7, which gives X ≤ 8.07e-3 even at cost 22. The current complex unit caps at 5.19e-3. So the label-field route cannot give κ > 0.01 in the B_K format, though it could still give a several-fold ceiling rise if a cost ≤24 bit decoder exists.

## Reproduce
`python3 -B research/label-field-census/census.py --json out.json` runs in about 4 minutes with numpy only and reproduces `RESULT.json`. Not covered: s ≥ 15, non-coordinate decoders in the clique table, realisability of Q(ω) frames, and helper/hosting/analytic obligations.
