prs.title: Research: degree-controlled cyclic inverse bound by root reflection (no new kappa)
prs.body:
PR621 proves a uniform circle gap for the prime-power cyclic kernels, but its Fourier-to-operator step pays an additional inverse-gap power. This contribution applies classical root reflection, the Dolzhenko-Spijker arc-length inequality, and Hardy coefficient control to obtain a degree-only multiplier.

For a degree-`n` polynomial `P` with `|P(z)| >= delta > 0` on the unit circle, the note proves

```text
||1/P||_W <= (1+4n)^2 / delta
||P(tau Z_L^w)^-1||_infinity <= (1+4n)^2 / delta.
```

The bound permits interior, exterior, repeated, and zero roots and is uniform in cyclic length, integer stride, and unit phase. A degree-one family shows that the inverse-gap exponent one is necessary; the quadratic degree factor is not claimed optimal. The proof includes elementary derivations with explicit constants and distinguishes the analytic argument from finite tests.

For PR621's notation, the constant changes from `A(1+4X^2)` to `A(1+4n)^2`, where `A=delta^-1` and `X=n H^(nD/2)`. The dominant logarithmic term is halved asymptotically. At radix 71, the exact ceiling of `log2` of the sufficient norm bound changes from 695,757 to 347,859. These are norm overestimates, not working-precision or runtime measurements. The previous unpublished local weighted-Fourier audit gave 521,801; its proof and notice are retained for comparison.

### Reproduce

Python 3.10+ and the standard library:

```sh
python -B research/rational-circle-bound/verify.py
python -B research/rational-circle-bound/test_package.py
```

Expected markers: `PASS_RATIONAL_CIRCLE_BOUND` and `PASS_PACKAGE_CONTROLS`.

Executed on Windows 11 / Python 3.12.2, including a relocated offline copy under isolated optimized Python:

- 126 exact reflection families and 756 boundary identities.
- 546 dense-versus-finite-geometric cyclic inverse comparisons, covering 9,516 inverse entries and including zero/noncoprime strides.
- 6,565 finite Hilbert-matrix inequalities and 128 exact near-circle parameter instances.
- 14 exact prime-power budget comparisons, 21 mathematical/admission controls, and eight package fault tests.
- A clean patch application with byte comparisons and an optimized replay of the applied artifact. Package attributes preserve source bytes across Windows checkouts.

The finite cyclic tests use supplied rational root families, not newly computed cyclotomic kernel inverses. No proof assistant, independent human review, full repository replay, second-platform replay, or remote CI result is claimed. The unchanged PR621 foundation replay was not repeated.

### Scope and attribution

Only `research/rational-circle-bound/` is added. Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. The source package was prepared in a partial pinned-input worktree; the published commit uses the complete upstream tree and that upstream commit as its parent. The selected frontier and upstream implementations are unchanged.

Credit Ali Romman for PR621's kernel setting, nonvanishing theorem and circle certificate; Dolzhenko, Spijker, Hardy and the classical Blaschke theory for the analytic tools; and Baranov-Zarouf for the inspected normalized arc-length statement and historical attribution. Source notices and six immutable source/context files are preserved. The standard finite-geometric oracle also appears in Joshua Snider's PR692; it is not claimed as a new solver here. PR628 and PR764 address distinct rounded-scan questions.

This is an application relative to the inspected repository work, not a literature-priority claim. Preparation, rounding/error propagation, scratch restoration, routing, tape/compiler/hosting and full multiplication transfer remain open. The new norm bound has not been integrated into PR628/PR764 precision recurrences. **No new kappa, complex saving, or BIT saving is claimed.**

The pre-publication overlap check inspected PRs through #799. Concurrent #796 (Hao Yan / FanPUYen, head `22902155c7875139e43e4fdf15723142d6709bdd`) gives nonarchimedean root valuations and explicitly distinguishes them from complex root moduli and conditioning; it is a separate audit. The local claim records the continuation of the earlier OS-seed-71 mathematical audit and the absence of a pinned coordination issue.

prs.title: Tooling: pack cyclic routing states with identical exhaustive receipts
prs.body:
The historical cyclic routing checker stores more than half a million nested scalar/routing states. This replaces those state keys with an injective, order-preserving integer encoding, reducing verification time and Python allocation peaks while retaining every original exhaustive-search receipt. **Tooling improvement; no new κ or negative result.**

## Contributor

**4RchYMing** ([GitHub](https://github.com/4RchYMing), authenticated account ID 275918740). Git author: `4RchYMing <275918740+4RchYMing@users.noreply.github.com>`, explicitly specified by the contributor. The predecessor's authorship and notices remain intact.

## AI Assistance

Prepared with **substantial OpenAI Codex assistance** for implementation, mathematical reasoning, independent test implementation, experiments, documentation, and delivery. No independent human peer review is claimed.

## Base Commit

`66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60` is the original implementation and benchmark baseline. Upstream subsequently advanced to `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`; all 19 relevant original checker/certificate, pinned dependency, test-runner and CI input files there are byte-identical. The compatibility receipt is retained in `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json`. OS-cryptographic assignment seed **87**, verification-engineering track. Three candidates, measurements, the local claim, and overlap review are recorded in `research/cyclic-routing-performance/SELECTION.json`. There is no pinned coordination issue.

## Research Scope

Only `audit_cyclic_topology.routing_state_search`: two-port XOR words on 2, 3, or 4 arbitrary-input roles, with the existing depth cap of seven. Preserve scalar/routing joint-state distinctions, full-routing saturation pruning, stopping rules, terminal tests, every frontier digest, and all eight cyclic seed controls. Selected-frontier records, `upstream/`, and the contributor list are unchanged. The #741 frontier selected by newer upstream commits is outside this contribution.

## Method

Place each scalar row in a separate fixed-width integer lane and the complete routing bit set in the low bits. The encoding is injective and preserves the original tuple ordering. XOR updates affect only the target lane; the routing extension remains unchanged. Decode sorted keys to preserve the exact original hash input. The README proves these invariants and explains why the permutation lookup agrees with the old predicate on reachable invertible matrices.

Only the historical certificate's changed checker-source binding is regenerated. Benchmark processes load the original implementation from its pinned Git object and compare the **entire** certificate after restoring that one binding. Source dependencies and the original certificate are hash-pinned.

## Results

- **529,066 four-role states**, all frontier digests, terminal counts, saturation counts, and complete historical certificate fields are preserved.
- Final seven alternating fresh-process pairs on Windows 10 / CPython 3.12.14: complete-process median **3.788324 s → 2.680431 s**, **1.413× faster / 29.24% less elapsed time**. The earlier seven-pair run is retained too: **1.368×**. All 80 receipts across five benchmark series, including the separate memory runs, agree.
- Separately traced Python allocation peak: **131,099,209 → 80,510,849 bytes**, **38.59% lower**. This is not RSS; tracing is disabled in timing runs.
- **Full independent coverage:** the dense-F2/literal-permutation-set oracle checks every cap 0–7 for all three widths, including all 529,066 four-role states. Every receipt field agrees. A scalar-only merge control loses coverage despite retaining the same negative Boolean and is detected.
- **14 tests pass on each of CPython 3.11.16, 3.13.15 and 3.14.7**, plus all 14 under 3.14.7 `-O` (56 successful test executions). `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json` retains command output and source hashes.
- Minimal offline replays in a path with spaces pass. Modified dependencies, reused output paths, and invalid parameters are rejected. Selected-record/source-inventory and staged whitespace checks pass. `VALIDATION.txt` retains command output.

Additional same-host, same-input pairs on the CI interpreter versions show that the speedup varies by interpreter:

| CPython | Original process median | Packed process median | Speedup | Python allocation peak reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3.11.16 | 3.436026 s | 2.553110 s | 1.346x | 38.59% |
| 3.13.15 | 3.628811 s | 2.902232 s | 1.250x | 38.61% |
| 3.14.7 | 3.842965 s | 3.198651 s | 1.201x | 42.42% |

Each row uses seven alternating fresh-process pairs and separate memory runs. All samples, including the more variable 3.14 timings, are retained. These are within-version comparisons; **1.413x is not a universal guarantee**.

## Reproduction

Python 3.11+ standard library and Git; use a full clone containing the base commit and a fresh output path:

```sh
python3 -B research/cyclic-routing-performance/benchmark.py --pairs 7 --out routing-benchmark.json
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_cyclic_routing_packed.py -v
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_finite_bit_contract.py -v
```

Expected: `PASS_IDENTICAL_COMPLETE_ROUTING_RECEIPTS`; five and nine tests pass. `SOURCE.json`, `RESULT.json`, `INITIAL-RESULT.json`, `RESULT-python311.json`, `RESULT-python313.json`, `RESULT-python314.json`, `VALIDATION-MATRIX.json`, and `EXPLORATION.json` retain pins, exact dependency versions, all measurements, and exploratory evidence. Repeat the commands under each Python interpreter with fresh benchmark output paths; add `-O` before `-m` to reproduce the optimized-mode tests. The README gives the argument and review map.

## Limitations

This measures one historical verifier, not selected-supplier replay or multiplication runtime. OS caches were not flushed; absolute timings vary. There is one separately traced memory run per mode in each benchmark series. The four-role frontier remains unclosed; no claim extends beyond depth seven. The independent implementation shares the documented joint-state reduction and saturation rule; it does not independently prove those reductions. This is not a Lean formalization or a new multiplication theorem, and all inherited transfer/physical/compiler/precision/tape/analytic assumptions remain.

## Change and mathematical scope

- The ordered positive integer forward matrix of the block is identical in all 144 entries, so every arbitrary block input gives the same exit values.
- The positive reverse matrix is entrywise no larger: 32 entries are strictly smaller, the entry sum falls 321 → 103 and the largest row sum falls 134 → 26.

**Search record.** Seeded two-sided nonnegative elementary-factor reduction on the fixed 12×12 forward matrix. The OS-random assignment seed 18 (bit-supplier track) selects block 18 mod 10 = 8. The search seed 801018 was fixed before the first trial. 10,000 trials, each stopped at the current best length: 144 reached the identity, 10 of these also had a dominated reverse matrix, and improvements came at trial 21 (33 gates) and trial 318 (30 gates). A separate seed-18 run was interrupted, found no improvement and was not used. No minimality or exhaustive-coverage claim is made.

prs.title: Research: exact frame search certifies #741 and #626 providers frame-optimal (rediscovers #741; negative result)
prs.body:
**Update: current selected word (#741).** Rebased on main after #741 merged. I gave CP-SAT PR699's SW4 word (`d232183f…`), using the admissible model with the audit's hpe cone caps and fixed tail frames. In 27 s it returned `OPTIMAL` with exactly #741's profile `{1:2556,2:334,3:430,4:194,5:56,8:8}`, so the solver rediscovers #741's gain without guidance. `check_sw4.py` applies #741's recipe and reproduces its pinned output hash `e7804702…`. The LP optimum over all frame assignments then equals #741's weight: 18155.950422 linear and 18219.665540 exact-root at #741's complex root, with gaps under 1e-9. So **no frame-only change of the selected word can raise κ**; PR699's frame slack (6.90 units) is exactly what #741 recovered. Six commuting-reorder restarts on #741, each re-solved by the LP, gave no gain. The receipt is `RESULT-SW4.json`. This work does not touch the R420/R439 bit or E8 lines (#789/#790/#792, #765/#767/#770).

**Negative result, scoped. No κ change.** By Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani), with substantial AI assistance (an AI coding agent wrote the search code and ran the experiments).

The complex side binds the selected κ. In the 64 jp8 calls, unit climbs make up 160,768 of the 181,659 rank-1 children. Paid children are exactly the frame climbs that `hpe_audit_and_transport.py::climb` counts, and the scalar program never reads frames. So I treated every A/B/tail gate frame of the selected provider words as a variable and searched all of them exactly.

**Result.** For #626's `jp8` and `ck` words (content hashes pinned in `complex-k492-owner-repair/data/SPEC.json`, rebuilt fresh by the package's `verify.py`), the paid profile is optimal over every frame assignment of the fixed gate sequence:

| word | gates | input weight | LP optimum (HiGHS) | CP-SAT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| jp8 | 4471 | 18475.029780700 | 18475.029780701 | OPTIMAL, same value |
| ck | 4507 | 18568.580702034 | 18568.580702035 | OPTIMAL, same value |

The weight is the linearised moment, Σ d·ln(48/d). Each word's rank mass is fixed by its widths, so at the selected root a* the exact criterion is Σ d·(73/d)^a*. That weight is also LP-optimal at the input (gap below 1e-9). The model relaxes the audit: it omits the hpe cone caps and cold_end conditions and leaves tail frames free. So no frame regroup, coalescence or promotion recipe of any size can raise κ on these words. Lifting every frame to its greatest feasible value costs +3.8%. Annealing over commuting reorders (the `build_gate_moves.py` rule), followed by an exact frame re-solve, gave no gain in 11 restarts (`ORDER-SEARCH.json`). That is a sample, not a proof for all orders.

**Context for κ > 0.01.** Jensen's inequality gives a ≤ −ln p / E_mass[ln(73/r)]. At the current deficit (2560 / 523264), a ≥ 0.01 needs a mass-weighted geometric-mean child rank of at least 44.7; today it is 3.66. At today's child ranks it would instead need a deficit of at least 15,425 (6.0×). Reaching it needs new scalar structure, not frame bookkeeping. About 1,700 of jp8's 2,512 rank-1 climbs are helper unit climbs.

**Files.** `research/frame-lift-search/` contains the model, the LP/CP-SAT solvers, the order search, `RESULT.json` and `ORDER-SEARCH.json`. `tests/test_frame_lift_search.py` checks the lattice model on the in-repo #571 prefix word. There is also a one-line experiment-log link.

**Verification.** `check.py` ran on a fresh `complex-k492-owner-repair/verify.py` rebuild (Linux, Python 3.13) and reports `PASS_FRAME_ONLY_LP_OPTIMAL_FOR_SELECTED_PROVIDERS`. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_frame_lift_search` passes. I did not run `make verify`: no generator, certificate or selected-record file changed.

**Limits.** HiGHS is a floating-point LP, not an exact rational dual certificate, and CP-SAT's `OPTIMAL` comes without a proof log. The scalar program, helper count, dispatch, hosting and bit supplier are out of scope.

prs.title: Tooling: 1.13x faster exact stage-pair audit with identical receipts
prs.body:
The historical stage-pair audit spends most of its runtime in exact rational arithmetic. This replaces two wasteful patterns with identical operations, preserving every receipt and rejection check. **Tooling improvement; no new kappa.**

## Changes

1. `scripts/audit_fused_block.py` — `rational_rank` skips redundant `Q(x)` construction when an entry is already a `Fraction`. `Q(Q)` returns the same value after needless normalization.
2. `scripts/audit_stage_pair.py` — `modular_rank` converts denominators through a cached `_mod_inv(d, prime)` helper (same `pow(d, -1, prime)` call) instead of one fresh `pow()` per matrix entry. `lru_cache` does not cache exceptions, so a non-invertible denominator raises the same `ValueError`.

No matrix, pivot order, stopping rule, candidate list, or rejection predicate was touched.

## Measurements

Fresh-process timings of `certificate()` (compute only), CPython 3.12.14 / Windows, stdlib only. OS caches not flushed; host not isolated. Timing is descriptive, not a pass threshold.

| run | original (s) | optimized (s) |
|-----|---:|---:|
| 1 | 16.63 | 14.31 |
| 2 | 15.79 | 13.96 |
| 3 | 15.57 | 13.64 |
| median | 15.79 | 13.96 |

Median 15.79 s to 13.96 s: 1.13x faster, 11.6% less wall time. Microbenchmarks: `rational_rank` 3.05x on 50 sampled frames; modular conversion 1.42x on 20 sampled matrices.

prs.title: Research: signed rank transport excludes unitary register mixers (no new kappa)
prs.body:
A forward/inverse coefficient potential gives a general search constraint: **unitary scalar register mixing cannot save paid rank**, regardless of word length, mixing locations or noncommuting frames. The same obstruction holds for scalar multiples of unitaries and for mixers jointly made unitary by the supplied positive diagonal metrics. In particular, the three-stream rank-three endpoint needs nine calls throughout this subclass.

For arbitrary nonunitary mixers, the argument becomes a quantitative necessary condition. Define

`p_ij(g) = Re(S_ij[g] (S^-1)_ji[g^-1])` and `Phi(S) = sum rank(g) p_ij(g)`.

Scalar mixing preserves Phi exactly. A paid call of cost c on row i changes it by at most `c(1+2*N_i)`, where N_i is the negative mass of that row's pairing immediately before the call. A full-rank three-stream endpoint has Phi=9. Thus **an eight-call solution requires accumulated paid-row negative mass at least 1/2**. A Cauchy–Schwarz version requires a local coefficient-row/inverse-column norm product of at least 9/8 at some paid prefix.

`PROOF.md` proves the identities for any symmetric subadditive group metric and derives the positive-diagonal-gauge corollary. A matrix-sparsity metric extends the scalar-unitary obstruction to formal words with arbitrary invertible matrix frames, free monomial maps and two-sparse butterflies, including non-Clifford frames. The finite implementation specializes to the pinned three-qubit Clifford model.

**No new kappa or positive eight-call primitive.** The general nonunitary problem remains open. Potential and negativity are necessary diagnostics, not endpoint certificates. The theorem is in a formal complex group algebra; it does not infer formal linear independence from a concrete matrix representation, import an FFT lower bound into the multiplication model, or cover clean ancillas without an independent-stream argument.

Validation:

- Exact standard-library Q(omega) arithmetic, with omega²+omega+1=0. All 71 named prefixes and their actual inverses agree with independent dense Gaussian Clifford multiplication; both formal inverse identities are checked.
- Seven named controls include valid nine-call endpoints, eight-call deletions, complex positive diagonal gauges, and an exact two-call example attaining the local excess bound: one call gains 5/3 using negative mass 1/3.
- Two explicit false-positive controls matter for search: a five-call word has Phi=9 but fails the endpoint; an eight-call amplification trap has 200/201 correct coefficient mass in its deficient column while Phi stays 8.
- 126 paid/free inverse controls, exact squared norm inequalities and invalid-metric mutations pass. Relocation, source corruption, false endpoint receipts, wrong phase inverses, corrupted pairings and optimized-mode rejection are replayed by `validate.py`.
- The isolated replay takes about 3.1 seconds locally. `make selected-record-check` passes on base `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`, selecting #799 at `1661634653669567/10^18`. No full `make verify` or selected supplier cold replay is claimed for this standalone addition.


Only `research/signed-rank-transport/` is added. Credits: Nir Ailon's [2014 quasi-probability/conditioning work](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.1307v5) and [paraunitary follow-up](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03278v6) supply the mathematical inspiration; eumemic's PR288 and its retained Swapnil Jain/upstream lineage supply the register framework; littleBro's PR680/705 supply two unchanged model/dense modules, byte-pinned in ORIGINS.json. prs.title: Scoped negative result: one added P112 total cannot reduce fixed-reader copy cost
prs.body:
## Scoped negative result — no new kappa

PR717 leaves open whether mixed pairing-rank totals can improve the P112 complex decoder. This package rules out one exact family: **adding one total while retaining the eight coordinate reader columns cannot lower copy-rank cost below 64**, even with arbitrary real coefficients and an arbitrary 112-component source correction outside the coordinate column space.

For `X X^T = 2G`, the family is

```text
X X^T = sum_j x_j (x_j-a_j z)^T + (Xa) z^T,
a in R^8, z in R^112.
```

It includes every exact nine-term factorization retaining those reader columns, up to nonzero column scaling, and the transposed class. It does **not** cover arbitrary changes of the reader columns, masked completions with extra free terms, multiple additional totals, other geometries, or arbitrary physical delivery programs.

The proof uses annihilator dimensions. Exact premises cover 511 binary functionals and all 3,272 sign classes. At full eight-coordinate support, the linear system has rank 63 rather than 64: each of its 128 nonzero kernels forces contradictory correction values at 56 ports. That extra compatibility check is included explicitly. This is a written theorem with exact finite certificates, not an inference from failed searches or a proof-assistant multiplication theorem.

## Reproduce and validation

```sh
python -B research/p112-single-lift/verify.py
python -B research/p112-single-lift/independent_check.py
```

Expected: `PASS_P112_SINGLE_LIFT` and `PASS_P112_SINGLE_LIFT_INDEPENDENT`.

- Standard library only; Windows/Python 3.12.0 normal and optimized checks pass.
- A relocated Git archive passes on Python 3.11.9 with `-O -S -B`; regenerated certificate is byte-identical.
- The independent implementation imports neither the main verifier nor its geometry module. It checks 511 integer minors with Bareiss elimination and repeats all binary ranks using set elimination.
- Nine mathematical negative controls, four independent arithmetic controls, and four additional source/certificate corruption controls pass.
- Original-base selected-record integrity and staged whitespace pass. `upstream/`, existing generators, and the selected frontier are unchanged.
- Repository-wide `make verify`, selected-supplier cold replay, and proof-assistant verification were not run. The new package has not run in hosted CI: the GitHub token lacks `workflow` permission, so the proposed scoped workflow was removed after a rejected push. Account permissions were not changed. Existing repository CI is separate from these local results.

At submitted head `125ce25bdae421627b56077adc14940c2d0aa52f`, all five existing upstream workflows report `action_required`; [Verify research artifacts](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38362262287) has no passing result. No hosted CI pass is claimed. GitHub reports the PR mergeable. The exported patch also passed application checking against an isolated index at the exact base, and the final portable ZIP passed its verifier after fresh extraction.

## Provenance, overlap and accounting

Exact base: `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`. Seed **40**, structural decoder research, drawn once from OS randomness. The local claim, full coverage, source pins and validation receipt are in the package. Only this isolated research package is added.

prs.title: Research: pay for preparation, execution, restoration and tape for #621's cyclic inverse at every stride (no κ claim)
prs.body:
The [K492 review](docs/research/community-k492-review.md) leaves one obligation open for #621 (Ali Romman). That PR's `L`-uniform inverse bound still needs paid costs for efficient preparation, rounded execution, restoration and tape. #628 (Chafik Boukhalfa) pays for preparation and neighbouring-stride execution. #764 (Charles Bethin) sharpens the scan rounding. For any stride other than ±1, #628 routes cycles through two merge sorts costing `O(L(B+log L) log L)`. Those sorts bring back the `log L` factor that the inverse bound removed.

This PR adds `research/cyclic-inverse-stride-bridge/` and one CI workflow. **No existing file changes. No new integer κ, complex b, or BIT c.**

## Result

- **Theorem 1.** A Euclidean chain/closure recursion solves `y_i = x_i + b_i y_(i-w)` for any stride. A lag-`w` FIFO built from two stacks gives every pass its predecessor in natural order. Each level at least halves the length. A single stable factor then costs:
  - at most `40L` sequential record moves (largest observed: 29.68 per entry through `L=131072`);
  - `O(L)` rounded operations;
  - an error of at most `min(K,1/β)(u/β)(5+4B/β)+u`.

  The error bound holds for every `L`. The proof reuses #764's shared-suffix identity `1-Q ≥ βG`. A concavity argument shows that coefficient margins never fall below `β` at any recursion depth.
- **Theorem 2.** Composing the solver with #628's certified factorization gives `P(τZ_L^w)^{-1}` at precision `p+(n+2)g+O(log r) = p+O(r^4)`, with no `L` term. One admission condition, `p ≥ log2(log2 L+2)`, depends on `L`.
- **Verdict.** For one kernel inverse on fixed sequential tapes, the cost with all four obligations paid is `soft-O(r^3(p+r^4)) + O(rL)·M(p+r^4) + O(rL(p+r^4))`. That cost per entry does not depend on `L`, so **#621's gain survives payment at the single-kernel level**. Restoration in this model is cheap: the input tape is never written, and scratch tapes are erased at linear cost.

## Validation

`python3 -B -I -O research/cyclic-inverse-stride-bridge/verify.py --check` prints `PASS_CYCLIC_INVERSE_STRIDE_BRIDGE generic=2052 kernel_cases=300 controls=4 max_records_per_entry=29.671875`. It passed under system Python and the repository venv (Python 3.13, Linux). It needs only the standard library and takes about 100 seconds.

- **Generic cases (2052).** `L=1..18`, every stride in `[-L,L)`, three margins and two grids. Each case is compared exactly with an independent per-cycle geometric-closure oracle. The margin invariant is checked at every recursion level.
- **Kernel cases (300).** These use all ten #628 certified kernels (radix 3 through 16), two gauges, `L ∈ {1,2,3,5,8}` and all strides for `L≤5`. Each case checks Theorem 2's exact budget together with #628's perturbation bound and the expanded residual. 81 cases are also compared with a dense Gauss–Jordan solve.
- **Controls.** The replay rejects a rotated closure reseed, too little precision, a unit coefficient and a wrong inner-shift direction.
- **Vendored sources.** The #628 files are byte-identical to head `0768f97d` and are hash-pinned; the verifier refuses drift.
- **Repository checks (Linux, base `66849e1`).** I did not complete a full `make verify`.
  - `make verify` passed seven targets with no failures: `verify-community`, `verify-producers`, `verify-partial-gauge`, `verify-three-stage-cover`, `verify-paired-cube`, `verify-recycled-bit` and `verify-entrance-banks`. My one-hour local limit then stopped the run during `gen4-bank-verify`.
  - `make selected-record-check` and `make verify-tests` passed separately: 549 tests, 0 failures, exit 0.
  - I did not run `frontier626-verify` or the later targets. This PR changes no existing file and does not affect the selected construction.
  - `git diff --cached --check` passed.

## Still open

- A borrowed-array (dirty) form of the stride solver for the exact-width model. #628's dirty route still covers that model, at `O(p+log(D+1)+r^5)` precision.
- Composition across the complete transform, phase collection and normalization.
- The multiplication reduction.
- The `O(r^4)` guard is a proof bound. Numerical probes put the true `min|P|` near `2^-10` for `r≤32`; those probe values are not certified here.

This is not a formal verification. The written proof carries the all-`L` claims, and the finite cases support the reference implementation.

## Credits

- **#621, Ali Romman (@aliromman).** Kernel and the `L`-uniform bounds.
- **#628, Chafik Boukhalfa (@chafreaky).** Factorization, preparation, phase and dirty-shear budgets, and the vendored certificates.
- **#764, Charles Bethin (@cbethin).** The shared-suffix identity and the inverse-square scan bound.

New work by **Rohan Guliani (@Rohansguliani)**, prepared with substantial AI assistance. Apache-2.0. No literature-priority claim is made.

prs.title: Research audit: sharp linear inverse bounds for balanced weighted cycles (no new kappa)
prs.body:
This research audit gives the exact worst-case infinity norm of a linear inverse on a balanced weighted cycle with bounded local weight magnitudes. It supplies rational attaining weights and a scoped negative result: exact unit cycle products, unit-circle spectrum, and arbitrarily small local weight deviations do not preserve a length-independent unit-weight inverse estimate.

**Status: research note / scoped negative result with independent exact verification.**

For `P(z)=z-33/32`, cycle length 256 and every weight within 1/16 of one, the simple two-block witness has inverse norm strictly between 1936 and 1937. The exact maximum over the admitted class lies between 2164 and 2165. The inherited unit-weight estimates would be 800, or 160 using the interior-root count. **This does not contradict PR803:** those matrices violate its explicit all-integer-power norm-one assumption. No new kappa or rounded implementation is claimed.

The written proof gives the exact cycle-local power factor K, transfer with one factor K, a sharp extremal inverse formula, the constant/linear/exponential local-error regimes for a linear polynomial, and a sufficient strict perturbation guard. The universal arguments are separate from the finite checks. The analytic Wiener bound from Rafael Guevara's PR803 is an explicit inherited premise; the cycle criterion and counterexample/extremal formulas have their own elementary proofs.

Reproduce offline with Python 3.10+ and its standard library:

```sh
python -B research/weighted-cycle-power-audit/verify.py
python -B -m unittest discover -s research/weighted-cycle-power-audit -p test_package.py -v
```

Expected: `PASS: exact weighted-cycle power audit` and 11 tests passing. Evidence covers:

- 1,377 generated weighted-permutation cases and 9,990 exact signed-power samples, plus 18 admission/failure controls.
- 72 dense inverses checked against 504 independent affine basis solves; 96 sharp-inverse attainments; 108 complex-phase inverses; three exact length-256 extremal solves; ten near-unit threshold certificates.
- 48 sharp power-cap witnesses / 2,600 direct path products and 240 polynomial perturbation cases (155 admitted, 85 inconclusive).

Normal and optimized replays from a clean export of staged Git blobs passed, as did the source/tamper/mutation checks and the selected-record check at the starting base. Full `make verify` and supplier cold replays were not run: only the new `research/weighted-cycle-power-audit/` package is added, with no existing generator, selected certificate, schedule or `upstream/` changes. This is not proof-assistant formalization or a full multiplication-theorem audit.

Exact base: `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261`. PR803 pin: `d213ac12d4a1ab8f717d942e844df318ceb395fb`. Ryan Pinto's PR692 geometric-resolvent pin: `c5b53a5e80372a1fae9830d8dcf21aaabce3f729`. prs.title: Tooling: 1.54-1.71x faster #741 complex replay by running independent pinned stages concurrently
prs.body:
**Status: tooling improvement.** No κ, construction, predicate, pinned file or selected record changes. `make frontier741-verify` is unchanged and remains the reference replay.

Base: `7ee02b7c96d85f22b38d28bd7ed49bb8c1aeb261` (main). Track: verification engineering (sprint seed 85).

## What changed

The complex half of `make frontier741-verify` (874 s of 1158 s in the c290b7b receipt) runs the 22 stages of `research/complex-sw4-frame8/verify.py` one after another. Many are independent. For example, the fresh PR558 ancestor replay shares nothing with the gauge44 → p6n → SW4 → frames chain, and three control stages read only the final word.

`scripts/verify_complex741_parallel.py` (opt-in `make complex741-parallel-verify`) executes the pinned `verify.py` itself, statement by statement, after checking its SHA-256 (`7706065e…`, the value in the package `MANIFEST.json`):

- The prelude runs unchanged: manifest check, vendored source pins, environment.
- Each `run(...)` call goes to `verify.py`'s own `run` function on a worker thread once its prerequisites in `STAGE_DEPS` have passed. Command line, environment, `run_portable.py`, logs and failure handling are the original code.
- Statements that read stage output (ancestral linkage loop, all count assertions, `RESULT.json`, `RECEIPT.json`) run unchanged, in their original order, after all stages pass.
- It refuses a changed `verify.py` or a stage list that differs from the table.

## Evidence

**Schedule against a recorded trace.** `research/complex741-parallel-replay/record_access.py --record DIR` runs the unchanged sequential `verify.py` under a Python audit hook loaded through a `.pth` file, so it also covers the `-I` children. The hook logs every open, listing, rename, delete and mkdir per stage. `ACCESS.json` covers 83 processes. No stage writes outside the work directory except into fresh `tempfile` directories. No pair of stages left unordered by `STAGE_DEPS` has a write/read, write/write, write/list or mkdir/list conflict, and deferring the ancestral linkage loop conflicts with no later stage. Two independent recordings gave identical access sets. The table keeps argument-derived edges, which are stricter than the trace requires, because audit hooks do not see `stat`.

**Equivalence.** Three full replays on one machine, each in the same absolute work directory:

| Replay | Result | Total |
|---|---|---:|
| sequential `verify.py` | PASS κ = 1661202643272239/10^18 | 594.7 s |
| driver `--jobs 8` (default) | PASS, same κ | 386.4 s (1.54×) |
| driver `--jobs 3` | PASS, same κ | 347.7 s (1.71×) |

`compare_replays.py` checked all 304 files of each tree pair. Sequential vs `--jobs 8`: 233 byte-identical, 50 JSON files differ only under `seconds`/`elapsed_seconds` or in SHA-256 digests of the same file where that file is itself accepted (checked to a fixed point), and 21 logs differ only in decimal elapsed times or such digests. Nothing else differs, and the other two pairs give the same result. Every generated word is byte-identical. Masking floats in logs is a relaxation; the JSON outputs are compared without masking. Negative control: changing the last digit of κ in `global-replay/ASSEMBLY.json` and one integer in a log produces exactly those two rejections.

The parallel time equals the dependency chain gauge44 → … → `all-native-phase-edges` → global admission, so more workers cannot shorten it. Applying that chain to the Linux stage times in c290b7b gives 457 of 874 s. That is an estimate, not a measurement.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_complex741_parallel.py   # 15 tests
make complex741-parallel-verify                                         # PASS 0.001661202643272239
python3 research/complex741-parallel-replay/compare_replays.py SEQ_DIR PAR_DIR   # exit 0, "0 other differences"
```

(`SEQ_DIR` and `PAR_DIR` must be replays made at the same path, one after the other.)

## Scope and limits

- Measured on Windows 11 (16 logical CPUs, CPython 3.12.14), one run each, host not isolated. **Linux was not run for this change.** The sequential package replay also passed on this Windows machine.
- Covers the complex supplier only. The bit replay (`tune/verify.sh`, needs C++17 and Boost) could not be run here and is unchanged. Running it beside this driver would hide most of its 284 s; I leave that for someone who can test it.
- The trace and comparison are evidence for this pinned `verify.py`; the SHA-256 pin forces re-derivation after any package change.
- Finite replay does not prove the multiplication theorem; inherited assumptions are unchanged.

## Credit and overlap

Replays chafreaky's #741 package and the contributors credited in its `PROVENANCE.md`. eumemic's #154 proposed concurrent execution of the `make verify` groups; this applies the idea inside the selected complex replay, with a recorded trace. It does not overlap #824 (stage-pair audit), #818 (R420 RREF) or #838 (binding audit).

Prepared by navinor (Aaron Wang) with substantial AI assistance (Claude) in design, code, measurement and prose.

prs.title: Tooling: exact modular rank fast path for historical joint-frame verification
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This contribution adds an opt-in verification package under
`research/joint-frame-modular-screen/` for the historical
`scripts/audit_joint_frames.py` certificate.

The adapter uses exact elimination modulo 101 to certify full rational
rank. If the modular reduction is rank-deficient, or a denominator is
divisible by 101, it falls back to the unchanged original rational
elimination routine. No approximate rank decision is used.

The supplied benchmark records a reduction in median complete-certificate
wall time from 1.952577 s to 1.701918 s (12.8% lower) across seven
alternating fresh-process A/B pairs. All fourteen timed certificates
are byte-identical. One individual pair was slower; the timing result
is specific to the recorded environment, not a universal speedup claim.

This is a tooling improvement, not a new construction or conditional
bound. No improved kappa or practical integer-multiplication speedup
is claimed.

## Provenance and scope

- Exact investigation base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`
- Assignment track: verification engineering
- OS-random assignment seed: 85
- `SOURCE.json` records SHA-256 and Git-blob pins for 36 predecessor inputs.
- `CLAIM.json` records task selection, the local claim, and overlap checks.
- `NOTICE.md` credits predecessor and related concurrent work.

The supplied patch adds only this research package and leaves existing
scripts, default verification commands, the selected frontier, and
`upstream/` unchanged.

## Validation

The supplied verification record reports:

- All 2,644 actual uncached rank calls agree individually with the
  original rational routine: 752 modular full-rank certificates and
  1,892 exact fallbacks.
- 12 focused test groups, including an independent determinant/minor
  oracle over 530 binary matrices and 240 seed-85 rational matrices.
- Four deliberately incorrect kernels detected by counterexamples.
- All eight unchanged historical tests pass with both engines.
- All fourteen timed complete certificates match exactly.
- Source-drift controls and rejection of disabled assertions.
- Successful `make selected-record-check` and staged whitespace checks.

Reproduce from the repository root using Python 3.11+ on Linux or macOS,
with a fresh output path:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/joint-frame-modular-screen/verify.py --pairs 7 --output /tmp/joint-frame-rank-result.json
```

Expected final marker:

```text

```

Expected historical certificate SHA-256:

```text

```

`PROOF.md` supplies the algebraic equivalence argument for the fast path.
The finite test campaign and certificate replays are not a formal proof
of the full multiplication theorem.

## Limitations and checks not performed

This package targets the historical joint-frame audit, not the selected
supplier reconstruction. It does not reopen the closed fixed-boundary
search or resolve the inherited obligations of the selected theorem.

Full repository `make verify`, selected cold reconstruction, Lean builds,

prs.title: Research audit: sharp physical counter costs with direction reversals (no new kappa)
prs.body:
The existing physical ripple-counter theorem correctly bounds calls in one fixed direction. This **research note / adversarial mathematical audit** supplies an exact signed-potential identity for arbitrary directions and a sharp run-based invoice: for width `w >= 1`, `N` calls in `K` maximal constant-direction runs cost at most `4N + 2(w-1)K` literal transitions. If `H` runs contain wraps, the sharper bound is `4N + 2(w-2)K + 2H`.

Alternating wraparound calls attain the uniform bound; alternating nonwrapping calls across the middle edge attain the no-wrap bound. At width 4 and seven calls, these cost 70 and 56 transitions respectively, whereas an invalid extension of the old fixed-direction bound gives 36. This establishes that excluding wraps alone does not justify arbitrary-direction `O(N+w)` for this primitive. It identifies **no error in the existing fixed-direction theorem or selected multiplication construction**, and claims **no new kappa**.

Eight isolated files under `research/counter-reversal-audit/` contain the handwritten uniform proof, an independent single-cell tape interpreter, exact deterministic receipt, source pins, fault-injection tests, scope/attribution, validation and local sprint claim. The primitive invoice excludes controller dispatch, preparation, payload, reset/restoration and recursive scheduling; those remain explicit obligations. Finite replay is not a formal proof of the universal statement or full multiplication theorem.

Reproduce with Python 3.10+ (standard library):

```sh
python3 -I -B -O research/counter-reversal-audit/verify.py
# PASS_COUNTER_REVERSAL_AUDIT schedules=130305 literal_executions=16376 controls=10
```

prs.title: Research: cubic precision and exact coarse-grid recovery for cyclic inverses (no κ)
prs.body:
Reduces the growing-radix precision guard for PR628's neighboring cyclic inverse from **O(r^4) to O(r^3)**. Every partial inverse is bounded by the full inverse and its complementary polynomial, using the standard Mahler-measure inequality. Bounding all rounded prefixes together avoids multiplying the worst reciprocal margin once per factor. PR621's circle bound is unchanged.

The written proof gives `W <= max(p,w)+12r^3+m` fractional bits for a source of norm at most `2^m`, including exact coarse-grid source recovery, and a factor-preparation budget `b <= p+6r^3+m`. Integer magnitude bits have the same cubic order. With the inherited preparation algorithms, neighboring-layout execution and setup cost `soft-O((Lr+r^3)(max(p,w)+r^3+m))`, plus charged phase access and longer phase descriptions.

The new in-place schedule evaluates the inverse, adds its result to a target, applies the forward factors, and rounds the source back to its original grid exactly. This requires **owned widened words with reserved low zero bits**, whose capacity is explicitly charged. Rounding the target increment to the original grid also gives signed shears that compose and cancel exactly with one fixed precision budget for a planned word.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.11+:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/cubic-cyclic-inverse/run.py --out /absolute/fresh/output
```

Validation:

- 5,220 exact integer budget cases across all 116 prime-power radices from 3 through 512.
- 120 actual kernel executions; 60 compare every prefix with independent dense solves. All check expanded polynomial residuals, recovery bounds, exact source restoration and total kernel error at most `2^-128`.
- 20 interacting shear-word cases, including 12 dense comparisons and exact whole-word cancellation; ten rejection controls across both suites.
- Complete fresh runs passed on macOS/Python 3.11 and 3.14 and Linux aarch64/Python 3.14, in approximately 66–72 seconds. All three generated mathematical artifacts are byte-identical. Receipts, logs, source manifests and artifact hashes are included. Scoped Python 3.11/3.14 CI is added.

**No new κ, complex b, BIT c or measured multiplication speedup.** The asymptotic claim comes from the written argument; finite tests do not implement Pan's worst-case factorizer. Arbitrary dirty-bit restoration, common-label/Clifford compilation, arbitrary-stride restored-source scheduling, complete-transform accounting and the multiplication reduction remain open. The full repository suite and selected supplier were not rerun for this isolated package.

Credit Ali Romman for #621, Chafik Boukhalfa for #628, and the standard Mahler-measure, periodic-filtering and approximate-factorization methods. prs.body:
**Scoped negative result. No new κ.** Only `research/complex-x4-frame-bound/` is added. The selected record, `upstream/` and every supplier file are unchanged.

## Claim

Take the selected complex word, PR799's X4 word (content `1e1d99ba…`, all 72 complex calls), and fix its scalar program, start and end frames (so all widths), cut, centres, target levels, precondition, FULL cleanup and early-cleanup membership. No such assignment admits b_next = 0.001664400278850482327914, the next 10⁻²⁴ tick above the selected complex endpoint. The pinned `outer.py` gives κ < b/(1+b) (`compact_phase_layer` with `complex_above_bit`), and b_next/(1+b_next) lies below the next κ tick. Frame reassignment alone cannot raise the selected κ.

## Method and evidence

- Forward joins and backward meets give complete frame intervals: 5,163 gates are forced and 1,201 have 2, 5 or 16 choices. The verifier enumerates every interval and checks each size against the Gaussian-binomial count.
- 140 components, with a local-polytope LP of 9,483 rows and 12,019 columns in total. Dual entries are integer linear forms in C₂…C₉ (C_d = M_d − d·M₁). Of the reduced costs, 8,582 are identically zero and 3,437 are strictly positive under outward bounds from both pinned engines (`moment.py` and `base_two_moment.py`). Each component's dual objective equals the selected cost as an exact coefficient identity.
- Global step: 72 × local + {1:1, 3:1, 44:1, 48:2396} equals the pinned global profile. Both engines put the moment above 1 at b_next and below 1 at the selected endpoint.
- The start-of-B centre equality is relaxed to a charged climb, and native-chain conditions beyond `audit_local.py` are not imposed. Both only enlarge the feasible set.
- Cross-check without duality: 12 random legal reassignments (40 frame changes each) pass the pinned `audit_local.py` unchanged, with exactly the profile the model predicts, and each is strictly costlier at b_next. The auditor refuses a frame below the forward join and a mismatched profile.
- Six rejection controls: a dropped component, an inflated dual, an omitted frame choice, the accepted endpoint in place of b_next, a legal but costlier baseline, and a changed word.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/complex-x4-frame-bound/verify.py --controls
```

Expected final line: `PASS_X4_FRAME_ASSIGNMENT_EXCLUSION controls=6/6`. This takes about 5 s, uses the standard library only and refuses `-O`. Optional: `crosscheck.py` (about 1 min), and `verify.py --word <fresh X4 FULL-WORD.json.gz>` for a rebuilt word. `gen_duals.py` (HiGHS) only nominates the duals and reproduces `data/DUALS.json.gz` byte for byte.

- A minimal closure of 21 committed files, extracted with `git archive` into an empty directory, passes the verifier and the cross-check.

Per call, 1,745 of the 2,548 rank-1 children, all 56 rank-5 children and the eight centre descents lie on edges between forced frames. A κ gain from this supplier needs a scalar change (read sets, order, tail membership), new start or end frames, or an owner and hosting change.

## Scope

Not covered: scalar rewrites, reordering, read-set exchanges, early-cleanup membership, entrance promotions or other width changes, owners, hosting and the invoice, the bit supplier, and other outer theorems. The exclusion holds at b_next for this fixed word. Inherited all-size, realization, hosting, precision, tape and analytic hypotheses remain. This is a finite certificate, not a Lean proof.

The method is chafreaky's #557 (PR551 word). ntedvs's #776 applies it to #626's jp8 and ck words without tail frames. Rohansguliani's #815 solves PR699's SW4 and #626's words with floating-point LP and CP-SAT, with tail frames fixed. prs.title: Research audit: CK Horner reversal raises scalar-grid guard from 3 to 5 bits (no new kappa)
prs.body:
The bidirectional Horner circuits in #837 preserve their exact endpoint maps and gate savings, but can need a finer intermediate fixed-point grid. This **mathematical audit** establishes the exact fractional guard requirements of all six pinned scalar programs and supplies a complete-word rounding counterexample. **No new κ.**

For inputs on `2^-p Z^N`, with an unbounded integer part and working grid `2^-(p+g) Z`, exact representability of every intermediate for every input is equivalent to `g` being at least the largest reduced binary denominator exponent of any prefix-map coefficient. The package gives the proof, complete prefix replays, and sharpness witnesses.

| Scalar projection | Forward binary/NAF baseline | #837 bidirectional |
|---|---:|---:|
| CK forward | 3 | **5** |
| CK backward | 8 | 8 |
| JP8 forward | 4 | 4 |
| JP8 backward | 27 | 27 |
| SW4 forward | 3 | 3 |
| SW4 backward | 19 | 19 |

The shared forward/backward guard stays **8 for CK, 27 for JP8, 19 for SW4**. Eighteen of the 962 individual coefficients require one or two additional bits in the chosen reversed circuits, occurring in 21 CK, 4 JP8 and 5 SW4 additions per orientation.

For `t += (31/8)*s`, reverse NAF saves one real primitive but raises local depth from three to five. With `s=1`, halving rounded toward minus infinity at three fractional bits gives **4 instead of 31/8**. In the complete CK forward scalar program, native basis input 16 at three bits leaves errors `L43=-1/8`, `L422=+1/8`, `L425=+1/8`; four bits still fail, and five restore the exact endpoint. prs.title: Research: Gaussian E8 all-clique certificate ceiling is 40 (no new kappa)
prs.body:
**Research note / scoped negative result. No new kappa.** Nonnegative weighted-clique certificates on the fixed 60-line Gaussian E8 configuration cannot certify more than **40 Gaussian pairing-rank units**, even when every nonempty nonorthogonal clique is allowed.

PR770 proves ceiling 40 for inclusion-maximal cliques and expressly leaves non-maximal cliques outside its theorem. This package closes that certificate-domain gap. It preserves PR738's existing scalar decoder interval **[40,60]**; a cost-40 decoder remains unconstructed.

## New evidence

- The initial attempt to extend PR770's 900-pair dual fails on a singleton: 42 hits rather than the required 45. This is a failed extension hypothesis, not a defect in the predecessor's scoped theorem.
- An exact repaired dual retains the **180 ordered orthogonal-normal hyperplane pairs with six-line intersection**, each of Gaussian pairing rank two. Every nonempty clique Q meets both hyperplanes in at least `9 |Q|` of these pairs. Summing their local constraints gives `9 sum_Q |Q| w_Q <= 360`, hence ceiling 40 for arbitrary nonnegative clique weights.
- Complete enumeration covers **2,068,372 cliques**, without a size cutoff. A separately implemented Gaussian geometry/rank checker and Bron–Kerbosch/submask traversal agree on all counts, size minima, pairs and the complete clique-set digest.

# R439 phase-B block 508: 37 to 30 additions (no new kappa)

Finite bit-supplier construction. The tuned R439 phase-B block at frame 508

registers `[19, 27, 35, 43, 57, 65, 66, 74, 89, 97, 466]`) is replaced with a

literal reverse cleanup reduces the complete native word from **24,305 to
24,291 ADDs** (7 forward + 7 reverse).

| Quantity | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Block additions (frame 508) | 37 | **30** |

registers. Discovery (`search.py`, deterministic, no randomness) runs a
forward dynamic program over realized-register subsets: each register is
realized once, in some order, from already-realized rows or entry singletons,

minimum is 30 and the recovered witness achieves it.

prs.title: Research audit: quartic precision for balanced dirty cyclic inverses (no new kappa)
prs.body:
PR628's balanced dirty-array inverse uses a valid but conservative **O(p+d+r^5)** precision bound, charging growth across every leaf call. This **mathematical audit** gives a sufficient **O(p+d+r^4)** word-size bound for the **unchanged dispatcher and rounded leaves**, preserving arbitrary initial dirt, exact restoration, call count and storage. **No new κ.**

The improvement comes from complete recursive children restoring their workspace. Their ideal prefixes and inverse prefixes have norms at most `B=(1+K)^E(n)`, where

```text
E(1)=1
E(n)=n+max(floor(n/2)+E(ceil(n/2)), ceil(n/2)+E(floor(n/2))) <= 4n-3.
```

Every ideal interval then has norm at most `B^2`. For N complete leaf calls with error `a*u*(||source||+1)`, variation of constants gives execution error at most **`2*N*B^2*a*u*(B*D+1)`**, provided `N*B^2*a*u<=1/2`. prs.title: Scoped negative result: PR589's bit word is exactly frame-optimal (no new kappa)
prs.body:
**Scoped negative result; no new κ.** PR589's bit word is **exactly frame-optimal**. Keep its gate sequence, scalar program, start/final frames and COPY frames (decoder constant 63) fixed. Then no reassignment of gate frames, however many gates change at once, raises c = 0.001733427039589844234749. PR555's base word is frame-optimal too. PR589's tuner was greedy and made no optimality claim; this settles the frame-only part of that question exactly.

**Method** (standard library only, about 16 s):
1. **Bounds.** Forward least-frame and backward greatest-frame passes bound every legal frame. Only **159 of 5,472 gates** have any slack.
2. **Components.** Free gates couple only when consecutive on a register, giving **133 independent components** (largest has 5 gates). Each is enumerated exhaustively: 398 assignments, of which 55 fail nesting.
3. **Exact objective.** At z = c the moment is *linear* in the paid profile, so the sign of Σ n_d·d·(64/d)^c decides exactly whether c rises. Every strictly different alternative loses by at least 9.1e−4. Ten alternatives tie on the same profile.

**Positive control:** drop every free gate to its least frame. The optimiser finds 37 improving components and recovers **exactly** PR589's profile `{1:1323,2:1342,3:79,4:44,5:102,6:11,7:19}`.

```sh
bash research/bit589-frame-optimum/verify.sh   # → PASS_BIT589_FRAME_OPTIMUM
```

**Scope**
- Frame-only search class. Transports, Steinberg rewrites and different retained-total frames are outside it.
- C-gate frames are relaxed beyond H4, which only enlarges the search.
- The bit side does not bind κ. The practical conclusion: further bit headroom on this word must come from gate-order or structural moves.
- "No improvement" is proven only within this finite search class.

**Pins:** base `f567884a`. Inputs are the committed PR589 and PR555 words.

**Credit:** the PR589 word and tuner are by DreamingOfClouds, on eumemic's PR555 lineage. #815 and #864 give complex-side frame-optimality certificates by different methods. Assignment seed 16 (bit track).

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

[Review and scope](docs/research/community-frontier799-review.md) ·
[Selected record](certificates/selected-result.json) ·

[Integration receipt](docs/research/community-frontier799-integration.json) ·

```sh
python3 -m pip install numpy sympy scipy
make frontier799-verify
```

**Other reviewed work:** Chafik's #795 proves a fixed-profile owner optimum;
Tekalign's #777 independently reconstructs and verifies the parallel frame result.
Rohan Guliani's #806 traces historical provenance hashes, with its missing-payload
limits made explicit. Charles Bethin (#662/#707), mtpsl (#709), cxnmai (#721), and
Agastya Sondhi (#727) contribute exact verification accelerators and memory savings.

Alluri's [#681 circuit consolidation](docs/research/community-circuits681-review.md)
combines Ali Romman, mtpsl, Greer Guthrie, Sagar Thakrar and Scott Woolsey Biggart's
work. The individual #688/#691/#694/#696/#708/#713 reviews are now complete.

The composition of **DreamingOfClouds' [#276](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/276)**

T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{90446448750933}{125000000000000000}=0.000723571590007464.

DreamingOfClouds redesigned the local bit circuits to use fewer auxiliary

A signed paired-cube producer and coordinate-star centers complete the

`2^-11.0832`: above `2^-12` and below `2^-11`. It measures the asymptotic
exponent saving, not a practical runtime speedup.

## What changed

**Avi Eisenberg's interval strips and core-aware pair assembly (#62)** arrange
additions to allow more physical wire reuse. Combined with **eumemic's joint
frame compiler (#57)**, this yields the strongest finite network in this batch.
**Alejandro Zarzuelo Urdiales's exact parameter refinement and scoped Lean
certificate (#61)** supply that historical numerical value.

The bit network has m=575 and 137,151,806 physical roles; its certified recursive
saving is 102039046058023/2000000000000000000. The complex network retains saving
717/10^7. All recursive children, workspace restoration, copied centers and
endpoint costs remain charged. The seven final exponent margins are strictly positive.

The preceding combination of Avi's skip-prefix strips (#53), **Rohan Gupta's
dual-suffix layout (#55)**, eumemic's compiler and **Chafik Boukhalfa's composition
and ranked reclamation (#58/#60)** is also fully retained and reviewed.

Other reviewed contributions are retained even when their numerical witnesses
are superseded: **RaD's enlarged-frame and clone machinery (#51)**, **Rohan Arun's
positive-frame composition and order searches (#52/#56)**, **Rohan Gupta's parallel
order search (#50)**, **Chafik's original-envelope clones (#54)**, and **Rohan Garg's
split-pair recursion (#59)**. The review records the exact validation scope of each.

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

**Avi Eisenberg's interval strips and core-aware pair assembly (#62)** arrange
additions to allow more physical wire reuse. Combined with **eumemic's joint
frame compiler (#57)**, this yields the strongest finite network in this batch.

certificate (#61)** supply that historical numerical value.

The bit network has m=575 and 137,151,806 physical roles; its certified recursive
saving is 102039046058023/2000000000000000000. The complex network retains saving
717/10^7. All recursive children, workspace restoration, copied centers and
endpoint costs remain charged. The seven final exponent margins are strictly positive.

The preceding combination of Avi's skip-prefix strips (#53), **Rohan Gupta's
dual-suffix layout (#55)**, eumemic's compiler and **Chafik Boukhalfa's composition
and ranked reclamation (#58/#60)** is also fully retained and reviewed.

Other reviewed contributions are retained even when their numerical witnesses
are superseded: **RaD's enlarged-frame and clone machinery (#51)**, **Rohan Arun's
positive-frame composition and order searches (#52/#56)**, **Rohan Gupta's parallel
order search (#50)**, **Chafik's original-envelope clones (#54)**, and **Rohan Garg's

## Evidence and limits

The [round-two review](docs/research/community-round2-review.md) extends the
[previous follow-up audit](docs/research/community-followup-review.md) and
[PR #39 transfer review](docs/research/community-final-audit.md). The original
#109 framework and retained all-size interfaces remain assumptions. This is not
full formal verification, independent human peer review, a worldwide priority
claim, or a practical multiplication benchmark.

Fresh checks cover complete emitted words and dirty basis vectors, physical
frame transitions, exact fixed-basis profiles, all 4,073,300 data pairs for the
retained geometry, and independent rational recurrence/assembly arithmetic.
The formal packages verify their stated finite/arithmetic contracts. PR #61's
integrated axiom audit contains 169 distinct declarations, including 11 concrete
frontier theorems; its input rows are bound to the replayed finite profile.

fresh maintainer checks from contributor-supplied evidence. Earlier witnesses,
patches and attribution remain available. Submissions after #62 are outside this checkpoint's review; exact reviewed heads
are recorded in the ledger.

forks.readme:
# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

[Review and scope](docs/research/community-frontier799-review.md) ·
[Selected record](certificates/selected-result.json) ·
[Exact assembly](research/community-frontier799-audit/ASSEMBLY.json) ·
[Integration receipt](docs/research/community-frontier799-integration.json) ·

```sh

python3 -m pip install numpy sympy scipy
make frontier799-verify
```

**Other reviewed work:** Chafik's #795 proves a fixed-profile owner optimum;
Tekalign's #777 independently reconstructs and verifies the parallel frame result.
Rohan Guliani's #806 traces historical provenance hashes, with its missing-payload
limits made explicit. Charles Bethin (#662/#707), mtpsl (#709), cxnmai (#721), and
Agastya Sondhi (#727) contribute exact verification accelerators and memory savings.

Alluri's [#681 circuit consolidation](docs/research/community-circuits681-review.md)

work. The individual #688/#691/#694/#696/#708/#713 reviews are now complete.

`2^-11.0832`: above `2^-12` and below `2^-11`. It measures the asymptotic
exponent saving, not a practical runtime speedup.

## Historical reviewed community checkpoint

The reviewed community witness gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\boxed{\kappa=\frac{25508460085039}{500000000000000000}
=5.1016920170078\times10^{-5}>2^{-15}}.
$$

This is **23.71% above the preceding PR #49 release** and remains below 2^-14.
It is an improvement in the asymptotic exponent saving, not a measured runtime
speedup. The model and general reduction are inherited from OpenAI's
[*Integer multiplication below n log n*](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Integer-multiplication-below-n-log-n-September-23-2026).

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

The construction contributed by **[icekylinx](https://github.com/icekylinx)** in
[PR #144](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/144), building on
[PR #130](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/130), gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{4609169}{10000000000}=4.609169\times10^{-4}.
$$

A signed paired-cube producer and coordinate-star centers complete the
identity using the original source registers. Completed dirty cores reuse
one auxiliary bank across three orthogonal blocks, adopting an664's PR #128
sharing principle. The bit branch selects certified gauges from the retained
PR #97 / Swapnil word. All local transitions, copied centers, complement
calls, finite routers and rare-class fallback remain charged. The analytic,
uniform-recursion and fixed-tape hypotheses are retained.

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

```sh
python3 -m pip install numpy sympy scipy
```

**Other reviewed work:** Chafik's #795 proves a fixed-profile owner optimum;
Tekalign's #777 independently reconstructs and verifies the parallel frame result.
Rohan Guliani's #806 traces historical provenance hashes, with its missing-payload
limits made explicit. Charles Bethin (#662/#707), mtpsl (#709), cxnmai (#721), and
Agastya Sondhi (#727) contribute exact verification accelerators and memory savings.

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.

Rohan Guliani's #806 traces historical provenance hashes, with its missing-payload
limits made explicit. Charles Bethin (#662/#707), mtpsl (#709), cxnmai (#721), and

# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Community research maintained by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the original
OpenAI #109 framework.**

## Current reviewed result: read exchanges and enlarged frames

**Jeremy Kothe's [#799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799),
extending Chafik Boukhalfa's #741 frames and the earlier source-gauge construction,
with DreamingOfClouds' #589 bit improvement on eumemic's #555 supplier**, gives

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661634653669567}{1000000000000000000}=0.001661634653669567.
$$

This is approximately **0.026005% above the previous selected exponent saving**,
not a practical runtime claim. The [#741 checkpoint](certificates/checkpoints/frontier741.json)
is preserved. Four paired read exchanges improve the recursive rank profile
while retaining the helper endpoints and physical owners. The result builds on
icekylinx's source gauge, Rohan Arun's recurrence correction, and the cumulative
community construction and verification work. [Full contributor record](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

Fresh X4 scalar, frame, phase, owner, precision, moment and 47 strict assembly
checks pass, bound to rebuilt ancestral SW4 and bit suppliers. The public
wrapper supports either a full cold replay or explicitly verified ancestry
reuse. Integration Linux CI is tracked separately in the receipt.

All-size compilation, common-label/mutable-source realization, whole-call hosting,
precision/tape and analytic transfer remain conditional. These finite checks are
**not a complete Lean multiplication theorem**.
